canton-of-cartagena.t: The most durable of the 1873 Spanish cantons, which seized the navy's main base and held out for six months against the Republic.
canton-of-cartagena.o: On 12 July 1873 intransigent federalists led by [[e:antonio-galvez-arce|Antonio Gálvez Arce]], known as Antoñete, proclaimed the [[e:guangzhou|Canton]] of Cartagena. They seized the naval arsenal and much of the [[e:mediterranean|Mediterranean]] fleet, and a revolutionary junta called on other cities to join a Cantonal Federation.
canton-of-cartagena.r: The canton issued its own coins and newspaper and used the fleet, commanded by General [[e:juan-contreras-y-roman|Juan Contreras]], to raid [[e:alicante|Alicante]], [[e:almeria|Almería]] and other ports for supplies. The [[e:madrid|Madrid]] government declared its ships [[e:piracy|pirates]], and foreign warships seized some of them. Its leaders saw it as the seed of a federal [[e:spain|Spain]].
canton-of-cartagena.e: Government forces besieged Cartagena from the autumn of 1873. Weakened by bombardment and the explosion of its arsenal, it surrendered on 12 January 1874, and many leaders escaped to [[s:french-algeria|French Algeria]]. The rebellion helped discredit the [[s:spanish-first-republic|Spanish First Republic]].

county-of-aversa.t: The first Norman lordship in southern Italy, granted to mercenaries in 1030 and the springboard for the Norman conquest of the south.
county-of-aversa.o: In 1030 Duke [[e:sergius-iv-of-naples|Sergius IV]] of the [[s:duchy-of-naples|Duchy of Naples]] rewarded the Norman [[e:mercenary|mercenary]] leader [[e:rainulf-drengot|Rainulf Drengot]] with the town and district of Aversa, between [[e:naples|Naples]] and [[s:principality-of-capua|Capua]], to guard his frontier against the Principality of Capua. Rainulf's band became a magnet for further adventurers arriving from [[s:duchy-of-normandy|Normandy]].
county-of-aversa.r: Aversa was a military lordship in which a small warrior elite of French-speaking Normans ruled a [[e:kingdom-of-the-lombards|Lombard]] and Italo-Romance population. Its counts sold their swords to whichever of [[e:naples|Naples]], [[s:principality-of-capua|Capua]], [[s:principality-of-salerno|Salerno]] or the [[e:byzantine-empire|Byzantines]] paid best, gaining recognition from [[e:conrad-ii-holy-roman-emperor|Emperor Conrad II]] in 1038. A bishopric was established in the town in the mid-11th century, and the county drew in Norman knights who later served in [[e:apulia|Apulia]].
county-of-aversa.e: In 1058 Count [[e:richard-i-of-capua|Richard Drengot]] captured [[s:principality-of-capua|Capua]] and took the title of prince. Aversa was absorbed into the Principality of Capua, and its warriors had by then helped launch the conquests that created the [[s:duchy-of-apulia-and-calabria|Duchy of Apulia and Calabria]].

county-of-montbeliard.t: A French-speaking Lutheran enclave ruled by the dukes of Württemberg for four centuries before France annexed it in 1793.
county-of-montbeliard.o: Montbéliard guarded the [[e:belfort-gap|Belfort Gap]] between the [[e:jura-mountains|Jura]] and the [[e:vosges|Vosges]]. Around 1042 [[e:louis-of-mousson|Louis of Mousson]], who also held Bar through his wife [[e:sophie-of-bar|Sophie]], ruled it as count. Later houses of Montfaucon and Chalon held it, all within the [[s:kingdom-of-arles|Kingdom of Arles]] and so in the [[s:holy-roman-empire|Holy Roman Empire]].
county-of-montbeliard.r: In 1397 the heiress [[e:henriette-of-montbeliard|Henriette of Montbéliard]] was betrothed to [[e:eberhard-iv-count-of-wurttemberg|Eberhard IV of Württemberg]], and the county passed to the Württemberg dynasty. [[e:guillaume-farel|Guillaume Farel]] preached there in 1524–1525, and under the Württemberg rulers it later became Lutheran, an unusual Protestant enclave between Catholic [[s:free-county-of-burgundy|Franche-Comté]] and [[e:alsace|Alsace]]. [[e:frederick-i-duke-of-wurttemberg|Duke Frederick I]] ruled it from 1581 and brought in the architect [[e:heinrich-schickhardt|Heinrich Schickhardt]].
county-of-montbeliard.e: French troops occupied the county several times, and in 1793 the [[s:french-first-republic|French First Republic]] annexed it. Württemberg recognised the loss in 1796. The region kept its Lutheran heritage and later became the home of the [[e:peugeot|Peugeot]] industrial dynasty.

comtat-venaissin.t: A papal territory in Provence, governed from Carpentras for five centuries, where the popes lived at nearby Avignon in the 14th century.
comtat-venaissin.o: The Comtat had belonged to the counts of [[s:county-of-toulouse|Toulouse]]. By the [[e:treaty-of-paris-1229|Treaty of Paris]] of 1229 after the [[e:albigensian-crusade|Albigensian Crusade]], [[e:raymond-vii-count-of-toulouse|Raymond VII]] ceded it to the Church, but the French crown held it until [[e:philip-iii-of-france|Philip III]] handed it to [[e:pope-gregory-x|Pope Gregory X]] in 1274.
comtat-venaissin.r: The Comtat was governed by a papal rector at [[e:carpentras|Carpentras]], with its own estates. The [[e:papacy|papacy]] moved to neighbouring [[e:avignon|Avignon]] in 1309 and bought the city in 1348, and the region flourished during the Avignon papacy. [[e:jews|Jews]] expelled from [[e:france|France]] found refuge there as the '[[e:comtadin-jews|Pope's Jews]]', living in communities at Carpentras, [[e:cavaillon|Cavaillon]], Avignon and [[e:lisle-sur-la-sorgue|L'Isle-sur-la-Sorgue]].
comtat-venaissin.e: [[e:france|France]] occupied the territory several times in disputes with the popes. During the [[e:french-revolution|Revolution]], after local votes, the National Constituent Assembly annexed [[e:avignon|Avignon]] and the Comtat to France in 1791; the [[e:papacy|papacy]] accepted the loss in the [[e:treaty-of-tolentino|Treaty of Tolentino]] in 1797.

cerretani.t: The Pyrenean people of Cerdanya, famed in Roman times for their hams, whose name lives on in the Cerdanya valley.
cerretani.o: The Cerretani occupied the high Pyrenean valley of [[e:cerdanya|Cerdanya]] and the upper [[e:segre|Segre]], today divided between [[e:spain|Spain]], [[e:france|France]] and [[s:andorra|Andorra]]. They probably spoke an Iberian language, and are recorded from the late [[e:iron-age|Iron Age]].
cerretani.r: They lived from [[e:pastoralism|pastoralism]] and farming in the mountains, and [[e:strabo|Strabo]] noted that their hams were highly prized and profitable. Little is known of their political organisation. Their valley controlled routes across the [[e:pyrenees|Pyrenees]] between the [[e:ebro-river|Ebro]] basin and [[e:gaul|Gaul]].
cerretani.e: They came under Roman control in the 2nd century BCE as part of [[s:hispania-citerior|Hispania Citerior]]. [[e:pliny-the-elder|Pliny the Elder]] names the Roman town of [[e:llivia|Iulia Libica]], modern Llívia, in their territory, and the name of the people survives in the region of [[e:cerdanya|Cerdanya]].

comancheria.t: The domain of the Comanche, a horse-borne power of the southern Plains that dominated trade and raiding from Kansas to deep into Mexico.
comancheria.o: The [[e:comanche|Comanche]], or Numunuu, split from the [[e:shoshone|Shoshone]] in the Great Basin and moved onto the southern Plains in the early 18th century, first appearing in Spanish records at [[e:taos-new-mexico|Taos]] in 1706. Mastering the horse, they drove the [[e:apache|Apache]] south and by mid-century controlled a territory stretching across western [[e:texas|Texas]], [[e:oklahoma|Oklahoma]], [[e:kansas|Kansas]], eastern [[e:new-mexico|New Mexico]] and [[e:colorado|Colorado]].
comancheria.r: [[e:comanche|Comanche]] society was organised in independent divisions, among them the [[e:penateka|Penateka]], [[e:yamparika|Yamparika]], [[e:kotsoteka|Kotsoteka]], [[e:nokoni|Nokoni]] and [[e:kwahadi|Kwahadi]], each with its own chiefs, who met in councils. Vast horse herds and bison hunting underpinned an economy of trade and raiding, with captives, horses and robes exchanged at New Mexican fairs. In 1786 the chief [[e:ecueracapa|Ecueracapa]] made peace with [[s:santa-fe-de-nuevo-mexico|Santa Fe de Nuevo Mexico]], and raids into northern [[s:mexico|Mexico]] later reached as far as [[e:durango-city|Durango]].
comancheria.e: Epidemics, wars with Texans and the slaughter of the bison weakened the [[e:comanche|Comanche]]. After the [[e:red-river-war|Red River War]] of 1874 to 1875 the last [[e:kwahadi|Kwahadi]], led by [[e:quanah-parker|Quanah Parker]], surrendered at [[e:fort-sill|Fort Sill]], and the Comanche were settled on a reservation in [[e:indian-territory|Indian Territory]].

county-of-sobrarbe.t: A small Pyrenean county in northern Aragon, later the subject of the legend of the Fueros de Sobrarbe, the supposed oldest Aragonese laws.
county-of-sobrarbe.o: Sobrarbe, the valleys of the upper [[e:cinca|Cinca]] around Boltaña and [[e:ainsa|Aínsa]], emerged as a district in the 9th century under the shadow of Frankish power and of the neighbouring [[s:county-of-ribagorza|County of Ribagorza]]. Its early history is very poorly documented.
county-of-sobrarbe.r: Little is known of its government beyond its links with [[e:ribagorza|Ribagorza]] and the castles that defended it against the Muslim lords of [[e:barbastro|Barbastro]] and [[e:huesca|Huesca]]. Its people were herders and farmers in the mountain valleys.
county-of-sobrarbe.e: [[e:sancho-iii-of-navarre|Sancho III of Navarre]] took control in the early 11th century. On his death in 1035 Sobrarbe and [[e:ribagorza|Ribagorza]] went to his son Gonzalo, and after Gonzalo's murder around 1045 they passed to [[e:ramiro-i-of-aragon|Ramiro I of Aragon]], becoming part of the [[s:kingdom-of-aragon|Kingdom of Aragon]]. Later writers invented a Kingdom of Sobrarbe with ancient fueros.

county-of-hohengeroldseck.t: Tiny Black Forest lordship around the castle of Hohengeroldseck that Napoleon briefly made a sovereign principality of the von der Leyen family.
county-of-hohengeroldseck.o: The lords of Geroldseck built the castle of Hohengeroldseck on a ridge between the [[e:kinzig-rhine|Kinzig]] and Schutter valleys around 1250. They ruled a small lordship in the [[e:ortenau|Ortenau]] with villages such as Seelbach, held directly from the Empire, while other branches of the family held lands in [[e:alsace|Alsace]].
county-of-hohengeroldseck.r: The territory was tiny and rural, a cluster of farming and forest villages. The Geroldseck family was divided by inheritance disputes, and after their line died out in 1634 the lordship passed to the lords of Cronberg and then, in 1711, to the counts of von der Leyen, who governed it from [[e:koblenz|Koblenz]] and their [[e:saar-river|Saar]] estates. It remained Catholic.
county-of-hohengeroldseck.e: In 1806 [[e:napoleon|Napoleon]] made it a sovereign Principality of von der Leyen in the [[s:confederation-of-the-rhine|Confederation of the Rhine]], one of its smallest members. It was occupied by [[e:austria|Austria]] in 1814 and handed to [[e:baden|Baden]] in 1819. The ruins of Hohengeroldseck castle remain.

centralist-republic-of-mexico.t: Mexico's conservative centralist state of 1835 to 1846, during which Texas broke away, France attacked Veracruz and war with the United States began.
centralist-republic-of-mexico.o: In 1835 a conservative congress backed by [[e:antonio-lopez-de-santa-anna|Antonio López de Santa Anna]] abolished the federal system of the [[s:first-mexican-republic|First Mexican Republic]]. The [[e:siete-leyes|Siete Leyes]] of 1836 turned the states into [[e:departement|departments]] ruled from [[e:mexico-city|Mexico City]], limited voting by property and created a Supreme Conservative Power to check the other branches.
centralist-republic-of-mexico.r: Centralism provoked revolts across the north and south. [[e:texas|Texas]] won independence at [[e:battle-of-san-jacinto|San Jacinto]] in 1836, Yucatán declared itself a separate republic in 1841, and federalists proclaimed the [[s:republic-of-the-rio-grande|Republic of the Rio Grande]] in 1840. [[e:france|France]] blockaded [[e:veracruz-city|Veracruz]] in the [[e:pastry-war|Pastry War]] of 1838. Presidents changed often, among them [[e:anastasio-bustamante|Anastasio Bustamante]], [[e:antonio-lopez-de-santa-anna|Santa Anna]] and [[e:mariano-paredes|Mariano Paredes]], and the [[e:bases-organicas|Bases Orgánicas]] of 1843 replaced the [[e:siete-leyes|Siete Leyes]]. The treasury was always near bankruptcy.
centralist-republic-of-mexico.e: The [[s:united-states|United States]] annexed [[e:texas|Texas]] in 1845, and war broke out in 1846. In August 1846 a revolt restored the Constitution of 1824, creating the [[s:second-federal-republic-of-mexico|Second Federal Republic of Mexico]] as the country faced invasion.

commune-of-reggio.t: An Emilian city-republic between Parma and Modena that changed masters many times before passing finally to the Este in 1409.
commune-of-reggio.o: [[e:reggio-emilia|Reggio]], on the [[e:via-aemilia|Via Emilia]], had consuls by 1136, after the citizens took power from the [[e:bishop|bishop]] and from the lords of the Canossa lands. The commune extended its control into the Apennine foothills.
commune-of-reggio.r: The commune was governed by consuls, then a podestà and popular councils, and joined the [[s:lombard-league|Lombard League]] against [[e:frederick-barbarossa|Frederick Barbarossa]]. Its position between larger neighbours made it a pawn: the [[e:house-of-este|Este]] held it from 1289 to 1306, and in the 14th century it passed among various lords, including the [[e:house-of-gonzaga|Gonzaga]] under [[e:feltrino-gonzaga|Feltrino Gonzaga]] and then the Visconti. Factions of the Fogliani, Roberti and Canossa families divided the city.
commune-of-reggio.e: In 1409 [[e:niccolo-iii-deste|Niccolò III d'Este]] acquired [[e:reggio-emilia|Reggio]], which then remained an [[e:house-of-este|Este]] possession and part of the [[s:duchy-of-modena-and-reggio|Duchy of Modena and Reggio]] until 1859. In 1797 it hosted the congress of the [[s:cispadane-republic|Cispadane Republic]].

county-of-horne.t: A small county around Weert in the Maas valley, whose last notable count was beheaded with Egmont in Brussels in 1568.
county-of-horne.o: The lords of Horne held lands near [[e:roermond|Roermond]] and [[e:weert|Weert]] from the 12th century as [[e:vassal|vassals]] in the region between [[s:duchy-of-guelders|Guelders]], [[s:duchy-of-brabant|Brabant]] and [[s:prince-bishopric-of-liege|Liège]]. Around 1450 Jacob I of Horne was raised to the rank of count, and the county became an imperial fief.
county-of-horne.r: Horne was a rural county of heath and farmland, with its castle at Horn and its main town at [[e:weert|Weert]]. The counts served the Burgundian and [[s:county-of-habsburg|Habsburg]] courts. [[e:philip-de-montmorency-count-of-horn|Philip de Montmorency]], count of Horne, an admiral and knight of the [[e:order-of-the-golden-fleece|Golden Fleece]], joined the noble opposition to [[e:philip-ii-of-spain|Philip II]]'s policies in the [[s:kingdom-of-the-netherlands|Netherlands]].
county-of-horne.e: The [[e:fernando-alvarez-de-toledo-3rd-duke-of-alba|Duke of Alba]] had Horne and [[e:lamoral-count-of-egmont|Egmont]] beheaded in [[e:brussels|Brussels]] in 1568, a spark of the [[e:dutch-revolt|Dutch Revolt]]. The county passed to his relatives and in 1614 to the [[s:prince-bishopric-of-liege|Prince-Bishopric of Liège]]; it is now divided between the [[s:kingdom-of-the-netherlands|Netherlands]] and [[s:kingdom-of-belgium|Belgium]].
ru: Philip de Montmorency, Count of Horne

captaincy-of-goias.t: A gold-mining captaincy in the heart of Brazil, opened by Paulista bandeirantes, whose capital Vila Boa preserves its colonial character.
captaincy-of-goias.o: In 1722 the bandeirante [[e:bartolomeu-bueno-da-silva|Bartolomeu Bueno da Silva]], son of the explorer known as Anhanguera, led an expedition from [[e:sao-paulo|São Paulo]] into the central plateau and found gold along the Vermelho river in 1725. Mining camps grew up, and in 1744 the crown separated the region from the [[s:captaincy-of-sao-paulo|Captaincy of São Paulo]], with [[e:goias-velho|Vila Boa]], now Goiás Velho, as its capital.
captaincy-of-goias.r: The captaincy's economy was based on alluvial gold mined by enslaved Africans and taxed by the crown. Settlements were scattered and linked to the coast by long mule trails. Conflicts with indigenous peoples such as the [[e:kayapo|Kayapó]] and [[e:xavante|Xavante]] were frequent, and the government founded aldeias to settle them. By the late 18th century gold had run out, and [[e:cattle|cattle]] ranching became the mainstay.
captaincy-of-goias.e: [[e:goias-velho|Goiás]] became a province of [[s:new-republic-brazil|Brazil]] in 1821. In the 20th century its territory hosted the new national capital, [[e:brasilia|Brasília]], and the planned city of [[e:goiania|Goiânia]] replaced Goiás Velho as state capital. The old town became a [[e:unesco-world-heritage-site|UNESCO World Heritage Site]] in 2001.

colony-of-new-south-wales.t: The first British colony in Australia, founded as a penal settlement at Sydney Cove in 1788 and the parent of every other Australian colony.
colony-of-new-south-wales.o: After losing the American colonies as a destination for convicts, [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]] sent the First Fleet under [[e:arthur-phillip|Arthur Phillip]], which landed at [[e:sydney-cove|Sydney Cove]] in January 1788. The colony initially claimed the whole eastern half of the continent, from which [[s:colony-of-tasmania|Tasmania]], [[s:province-of-south-australia|South Australia]], [[s:colony-of-victoria|Victoria]], [[s:colony-of-queensland|Queensland]] and [[s:new-zealand|New Zealand]] were later separated.
colony-of-new-south-wales.r: Early New [[e:south-wales|South Wales]] was a military-run penal colony, troubled by famine and by the officers' rum trade that ended in the deposition of Governor [[e:william-bligh|William Bligh]] in 1808. [[e:lachlan-macquarie|Lachlan Macquarie]] built roads and public buildings and promoted freed convicts. Fine merino wool became the staple export, and the gold rush of 1851 brought free migrants. Expansion dispossessed [[e:aboriginal-australians|Aboriginal]] nations through violence and disease. [[e:penal-transportation|Transportation]] ended in 1840, and self-government came in 1856.
colony-of-new-south-wales.e: Under premiers such as [[e:henry-parkes|Henry Parkes]], a leading advocate of federation, New [[e:south-wales|South Wales]] joined the other colonies to form the [[s:commonwealth-of-australia|Commonwealth of Australia]] on 1 January 1901, becoming a state.

carantania.t: An early Slavic principality in the eastern Alps, ancestor of Carinthia, famous for its unusual ceremony of installing dukes on the Prince's Stone.
carantania.o: Alpine [[e:slavs|Slavs]] settled the eastern [[e:alps|Alps]] in the late 6th century under [[e:avars|Avar]] overlordship. After [[e:samo|Samo's]] death around 658 they formed an independent principality centred on the [[e:zollfeld|Zollfeld]] plain near [[e:karnburg|Karnburg]] in modern [[e:carinthia|Carinthia]]. A ruler named [[e:valuk|Valuk]] appears in [[e:chronicle-of-fredegar|Fredegar]] as 'duke of the [[e:wends|Wends]]' around 631.
carantania.r: Around 743 Prince [[e:borut|Borut]] sought Bavarian help against the [[e:avars|Avars]] and accepted Bavarian overlordship; his son [[e:gorazd-of-carantania|Gorazd]] and nephew [[e:hotimir|Hotimir]] were raised as Christians, and [[e:salzburg|Salzburg]] led the mission. Princes were installed on the [[e:princes-stone|Prince's Stone]] (Knežji kamen) in a ceremony led by a peasant speaking Slavic, a rite later used for dukes of [[e:carinthia|Carinthia]].
carantania.e: After a pagan revolt in the 770s, Carantania passed with [[e:bavaria|Bavaria]] under Frankish rule in 788. Following the uprising of [[e:ljudevit-posavski|Ljudevit Posavski]], the native princes were replaced by Frankish counts in 828. The land became the core of the later [[s:duchy-of-carinthia|Duchy of Carinthia]] and is a landmark in Slovene history.

canton-of-glarus.t: An Alpine valley canton that won its freedom from the Habsburgs at Näfels in 1388 and later divided its government between Catholics and Protestants.
canton-of-glarus.o: The [[e:linth|Linth]] valley belonged to the abbey of [[e:sackingen-abbey|Säckingen]], whose rights passed to the [[e:habsburg-dynasty|Habsburgs]]. In 1352 the valley joined the [[s:confederate-states-of-america|Confederacy]], though on unequal terms. The Glarners' victory over a [[s:county-of-habsburg|Habsburg]] army at [[e:battle-of-nafels|Näfels]] in 1388, still commemorated each April, secured their independence, and they gained full equality with the other cantons in 1473.
canton-of-glarus.r: [[e:sovereignty|Sovereignty]] lay with the [[e:landsgemeinde|Landsgemeinde]], the open-air assembly of all men, which still meets in Glarus. The valley lived from [[e:cattle|cattle]], [[e:mercenary|mercenary]] service and later textiles. [[e:huldrych-zwingli|Huldrych Zwingli]] was parish priest at Glarus before moving to [[s:canton-of-zurich|Zürich]]. The [[e:protestant-reformation|Reformation]] divided the canton, and from 1623 Catholics and Protestants kept separate assemblies and officials alongside a common government.
canton-of-glarus.e: The old canton dissolved in 1798 under the [[s:helvetic-republic|Helvetic Republic]], becoming part of the canton of [[e:linth|Linth]]. Restored in 1803, Glarus remains a Swiss canton and one of two still governed by a [[e:landsgemeinde|Landsgemeinde]].

coixtlahuaca.t: A powerful Chocho-Mixtec kingdom in north-western Oaxaca, controlling trade routes to the south, conquered by the Aztec Empire around 1458.
coixtlahuaca.o: Coixtlahuaca developed in a valley of the [[e:mixteca-alta|Mixteca Alta]] inhabited by [[e:chocho-people|Chocho]] (Ngiwa) and [[e:mixtecs|Mixtec]] people. By the 13th century it had become a powerful kingdom with a famous market, and pictorial [[e:manuscript|manuscripts]] known as the Lienzos of Coixtlahuaca record its rulers and boundaries.
coixtlahuaca.r: The kingdom drew wealth from its position on trade routes between the [[e:valley-of-mexico|Valley of Mexico]], the Gulf and [[e:oaxaca|Oaxaca]], and its market was frequented by merchants from many regions. According to [[e:mexica|Mexica]] accounts, the killing of Aztec merchants there provoked war. Its last independent ruler was Atonal.
coixtlahuaca.e: Around 1458 an army of the [[s:aztec-empire|Aztec Empire]] under [[e:moctezuma-i|Moctezuma I]] conquered Coixtlahuaca and executed Atonal, and the region became a tribute province. Under Spanish rule a large Dominican church was built there in the 16th century.

chenla.t: The Khmer kingdom that succeeded Funan in the 6th and 7th centuries, whose temples at Sambor Prei Kuk prefigure the art of Angkor.
chenla.o: Chenla first appears in Chinese sources as a [[e:vassal|vassal]] of [[s:funan|Funan]] in the middle [[e:mekong-river|Mekong]], possibly centred near [[e:wat-phu|Wat Phu]] in southern [[e:laos|Laos]]. In the late 6th century its kings [[e:bhavavarman-i|Bhavavarman I]] and [[e:mahendravarman-chenla|Chitrasena]], who took the name Mahendravarman, attacked Funan, and Ishanavarman I completed the takeover and built a capital at [[e:sambor-prei-kuk|Ishanapura]], now Sambor Prei Kuk.
chenla.r: Chenla's kings ruled through a network of local lords and temple foundations recorded in [[e:sanskrit|Sanskrit]] and [[e:old-khmer|Old Khmer]] inscriptions, the first substantial written records of the [[e:khmer-empire|Khmer]] language. [[e:shaivism|Shaivism]] dominated, with linga cults and [[e:harihara|Harihara]] images. [[e:sambor-prei-kuk|Sambor Prei Kuk]], with its octagonal brick towers, is now a [[e:unesco-world-heritage-site|World Heritage Site]].
chenla.e: After the death of [[e:jayavarman-i|Jayavarman I]] around 681 Chenla split, and Chinese sources speak of [[s:land-chenla|Land Chenla]] and [[s:water-chenla|Water Chenla]] from the early 8th century. In 802 [[e:jayavarman-ii|Jayavarman II]] proclaimed himself universal monarch on the [[e:phnom-kulen|Kulen hills]], founding the [[s:khmer-empire|Khmer Empire]].

county-of-girona.t: One of the first Frankish counties south of the Pyrenees, created when Girona surrendered to Charlemagne in 785.
county-of-girona.o: In 785 the people of [[e:girona|Girona]] handed their city to [[e:charlemagne|Charlemagne's]] forces, and a county was set up under Frankish rule as part of the frontier that became the [[s:marca-hispanica|Marca Hispanica]]. Its first known count was Rostany.
county-of-girona.r: Counts appointed by the Carolingian kings governed [[e:girona|Girona]] alongside its [[e:bishop|bishop]], defending the frontier against [[e:al-andalus|al-Andalus]]. The county included the plain around the city and controlled the road from [[e:gaul|Gaul]] to [[e:barcelona|Barcelona]]. It was often held together with Barcelona, and its counts were frequently [[e:goths|Goths]] of local or Septimanian origin.
county-of-girona.e: From 878 [[e:girona|Girona]] was held by [[e:wilfred-the-hairy|Wilfred the Hairy]] with [[e:barcelona|Barcelona]] and Osona. After his death in 897 it passed with Barcelona to his heirs and remained permanently part of the domains of the counts of Barcelona.

chuzan.t: The central kingdom of 14th-century Okinawa, which opened tribute relations with Ming China and under Sho Hashi united the island as the Ryukyu Kingdom.
chuzan.o: Chuzan emerged in central [[e:okinawa-island|Okinawa]] as one of three rival kingdoms that formed in the early 14th century, the traditional date being 1314. Its early seat was [[e:urasoe|Urasoe]] castle, and its rulers claimed descent from earlier legendary dynasties of [[e:shunten|Shunten]] and [[e:eiso|Eiso]].
chuzan.r: King [[e:satto|Satto]] opened tribute relations with [[e:ming-empire|Ming China]] in 1372, gaining access to Chinese trade and receiving skilled immigrants who settled at [[e:kumemura|Kume village]] near [[e:naha|Naha]]. Chuzan traded with [[e:japan|Japan]], [[e:korea|Korea]] and [[e:southeast-asia|Southeast Asia]], and its kings were overlords of local aji lords in their gusuku castles. In 1406 [[e:sho-shisho|Sho Shisho]] and his son [[e:sho-hashi|Sho Hashi]] overthrew King [[e:bunei|Bunei]] and moved the capital to Shuri.
chuzan.e: [[e:sho-hashi|Sho Hashi]] conquered [[s:hokuzan|Hokuzan]] in 1416 and [[s:nanzan|Nanzan]] in 1429, uniting [[e:okinawa-island|Okinawa]] as the [[s:ryukyu-kingdom|Ryukyu Kingdom]], whose kings kept the title King of Chuzan in their dealings with [[e:china|China]].

colony-of-british-columbia-1866-1871.t: The united Pacific colony of Vancouver Island and the mainland, which joined Canada in 1871 in return for a transcontinental railway.
colony-of-british-columbia-1866-1871.o: Debts left by the gold rushes and the cost of two administrations led [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]] to merge the [[s:colony-of-vancouver-island|Colony of Vancouver Island]] with the mainland [[s:colony-of-british-columbia-1858-1866|Colony of British Columbia]] (1858-1866) in November 1866, under Governor [[e:frederick-seymour|Frederick Seymour]]. [[e:new-westminster|New Westminster]] was the first capital, but after bitter rivalry [[s:colony-of-victoria|Victoria]] was chosen in 1868.
colony-of-british-columbia-1866-1871.r: The colony was governed by a governor and a partly elected legislative council. Its economy was depressed as [[e:cariboo|Cariboo]] gold declined, and its population of settlers was small next to the [[e:first-nations-in-canada|First Nations]] majority. After the [[e:alaska|Alaska]] Purchase of 1867, some residents favoured annexation to the [[s:united-states|United States]], while others, led by the journalist [[e:amor-de-cosmos|Amor De Cosmos]], campaigned to join [[s:canada|Canada]].
colony-of-british-columbia-1866-1871.e: Governor [[e:anthony-musgrave|Anthony Musgrave]], appointed in 1869, steered the colony towards Confederation. [[s:canada|Canada]] agreed to take over its debt and to begin a railway to the Pacific within two years, completing it within ten, and [[e:british-columbia|British Columbia]] became a province of [[e:canada|Canada]] on 20 July 1871.

commune-of-prato.t: A Tuscan wool-making city-republic, home of the merchant Francesco Datini, which was sold to Florence in 1351.
commune-of-prato.o: Prato grew around the castle of the Alberti counts and the parish church of [[e:prato-cathedral|Santo Stefano]], and consuls governed it by 1140. The commune developed in the shadow of [[s:duchy-of-florence|Florence]], a few miles away.
commune-of-prato.r: Prato was ruled by consuls and later a podestà, and its economy rested on wool cloth production, using the [[e:bisenzio|Bisenzio]] river to power fulling mills. The cathedral holds the relic of the Virgin's girdle, a major object of devotion. From the early 14th century the town placed itself under the Angevin kings of [[e:naples|Naples]] to keep its independence from [[s:duchy-of-florence|Florence]].
commune-of-prato.e: In 1351 [[e:joanna-i-of-naples|Queen Joanna I of Naples]] sold her rights over Prato to the [[s:republic-of-florence|Republic of Florence]], which ruled it from then on. The merchant [[e:francesco-di-marco-datini|Francesco Datini]], born there around 1335, made his fortune in [[e:avignon|Avignon]] before returning to Prato, where his huge archive survives.

chachapoya.t: Peoples of the cloud forests of northern Peru, builders of the great walled citadel of Kuélap and of cliffside tombs and sarcophagi.
chachapoya.o: The Chachapoya culture developed from around 800 in the montane forests between the [[e:maranon-river|Marañón]] and [[e:huallaga-river|Huallaga]] rivers, in present-day [[e:amazonas-region|Amazonas]] region of [[e:peru|Peru]]. Communities built circular stone houses on ridges and grew into a network of fortified settlements.
chachapoya.r: The Chachapoya were not a single state but a confederation of chiefdoms sharing culture and allying in war. Their most famous site, [[e:kuelap|Kuélap]], is a walled platform up to 20 metres high containing hundreds of round buildings. They placed their dead in cliffside mausoleums such as [[e:revash|Revash]] and in tall clay sarcophagi, the purunmachus of [[e:karajia|Karajía]]. Their stone buildings carry zigzag and rhomboid friezes.
chachapoya.e: The [[e:inca-empire|Incas]] conquered the Chachapoya around 1475 under [[e:tupac-inca-yupanqui|Túpac Inca Yupanqui]], facing repeated revolts and deporting many people. Some Chachapoya allied with the Spanish after 1532. Epidemics and colonial rule then depopulated the region, and many sites remained hidden in forest until modern times.

county-of-oettingen.t: A Swabian county in the Ries crater whose counts built a territory in the Nördlinger Ries before splitting into Protestant and Catholic lines.
county-of-oettingen.o: Count Ludwig of Oettingen appears around 1147, holding lands in the [[e:nordlinger-ries|Ries]], a fertile meteorite crater basin in Swabia. The counts were relatives of the [[e:hohenstaufen|Staufer]] and expanded their territory through purchases and offices, making it one of the larger counties in [[e:swabia|Swabia]].
county-of-oettingen.r: The counts ruled villages and small towns around Oettingen, [[e:wallerstein|Wallerstein]] and [[e:harburg-swabia|Harburg]], but the imperial city of [[s:free-imperial-city-of-nordlingen|Nördlingen]] in the middle of the [[e:nordlinger-ries|Ries]] stayed outside their control. The family later divided into several lines, and the [[e:protestant-reformation|Reformation]] split them by confession.
county-of-oettingen.e: In 1522 the county was divided between [[s:principality-of-oettingen-spielberg|Oettingen-Oettingen]], which turned Protestant, and Catholic [[s:principality-of-oettingen-wallerstein|Oettingen-Wallerstein]]. Later principalities, they were mediatised in 1806 and became part of [[e:bavaria|Bavaria]]. The princes of Oettingen-[[e:wallerstein|Wallerstein]] still live at [[e:harburg-swabia|Harburg]] and Wallerstein.

county-of-savoy.t: The Alpine county that controlled the Mont Cenis and Great St Bernard passes, the cradle of the house of Savoy and of later Italian kings.
county-of-savoy.o: [[e:humbert-i-count-of-savoy|Humbert White-Hands]], a noble of the [[s:kingdom-of-arles|Kingdom of Arles]], held counties around [[e:maurienne|Maurienne]] and [[s:duchy-of-savoy|Savoy]] from around 1003. His son [[e:odo-count-of-savoy|Odo]] married [[e:adelaide-of-susa|Adelaide of Turin]], bringing lands in [[e:piedmont|Piedmont]], so the dynasty straddled the [[e:alps|Alps]] from its beginnings.
county-of-savoy.r: The counts drew their power from controlling the main passes between [[e:france|France]] and [[e:italy|Italy]] and from tolls on the trade that crossed them. [[e:peter-ii-count-of-savoy|Peter II]], called the 'little [[e:charlemagne|Charlemagne]]', won the [[e:vaud|Vaud]] in the 13th century, and [[e:chambery|Chambéry]] became the capital in 1295. [[e:amadeus-vi-count-of-savoy|Amadeus VI]], the Green Count, led a [[e:crusade|crusade]] in 1366, and [[e:amadeus-vii-count-of-savoy|Amadeus VII]] acquired [[e:nice|Nice]] in 1388.
county-of-savoy.e: In 1416 [[e:sigismund-holy-roman-emperor|Emperor Sigismund]] raised [[e:amadeus-viii-duke-of-savoy|Amadeus VIII]] to the rank of duke, and the county became the [[s:duchy-of-savoy|Duchy of Savoy]]. The dynasty went on to rule [[e:sardinia|Sardinia]] and, from 1861, all [[e:italy|Italy]].

costoboci.t: Dacian people north of the Carpathians whose daring raid of 170 CE reached Greece and sacked the sanctuary of Eleusis.
costoboci.o: Known mainly from Roman sources, the Costoboci were a Dacian people living beyond Roman [[e:dacia|Dacia]], probably in the upper [[e:dniester|Dniester]] and [[e:prut|Prut]] region of modern [[e:ukraine|Ukraine]] and [[s:kingdom-of-romania|Romania]], in the 1st and 2nd centuries CE. An inscription in [[e:rome|Rome]] names a Costobocian king, Pieporus.
costoboci.r: Little is known of their society beyond Roman notices. During the [[e:marcomannic-wars|Marcomannic Wars]], in about 170 CE, they broke through the [[e:danube|Danube]] frontier, swept through [[e:moesia|Moesia]], [[e:thrace|Thrace]] and [[e:macedonia-region|Macedonia]], and plundered the mysteries sanctuary at [[e:eleusis|Eleusis]] near [[s:athens|Athens]].
costoboci.e: Soon after the raid they were attacked by the [[e:hasdingi|Asding]] [[e:vandals|Vandals]], who took their lands. They vanish from the record by the end of the 2nd century, probably absorbed by the [[s:carpi|Carpi]] and other neighbours.

chokwe-chiefdoms.t: Hunters, traders and artists of the upper Kasai whose 19th-century expansion overran the Lunda Empire and whose sculpture is world-famous.
chokwe-chiefdoms.o: The [[e:chokwe|Chokwe]] lived as hunters and farmers in the highlands of north-eastern [[s:portuguese-angola|Angola]], organised in chiefdoms whose rulers held titles derived from the [[s:lunda-empire|Lunda Empire]]. Their traditions link the chiefly line to [[e:lunda-empire|Lunda]] nobles who left the Lunda court around the 17th century.
chokwe-chiefdoms.r: [[e:chokwe|Chokwe]] chiefs ruled small, autonomous territories rather than a single kingdom. In the 19th century the Chokwe became leading traders in beeswax, [[e:ivory-trade|ivory]] and later wild [[e:rubber|rubber]], buying guns and absorbing captive women and dependants, which drove rapid population growth and expansion. Their carvers produced celebrated masks such as [[e:mwana-pwo|Mwana Pwo]] and figures of the hero [[e:chibinda-ilunga|Chibinda Ilunga]].
chokwe-chiefdoms.e: In 1887 [[e:chokwe|Chokwe]] forces sacked the [[e:lunda-empire|Lunda]] capital and briefly dominated the region. The collapse of the [[e:rubber|rubber]] trade and Portuguese and Belgian conquest brought the chiefdoms under colonial rule by about 1920. The Chokwe are now a major people of [[s:portuguese-angola|Angola]], [[e:zambia|Zambia]] and [[e:democratic-republic-of-the-congo|Congo]].

county-of-schaumburg.t: A Weser county whose counts also ruled Holstein for three centuries, later divided between Hesse and Lippe as the root of Schaumburg-Lippe.
county-of-schaumburg.o: The lords of Schauenburg appear around 1110 with a castle on the Nesselberg above the [[e:weser|Weser]] near [[e:rinteln|Rinteln]]. In 1111 [[e:lothair-iii-holy-roman-emperor|Duke Lothair of Saxony]] granted Adolf I of Schauenburg the [[s:county-of-holstein|County of Holstein]], beginning a long double rule over Holstein and the Weser lands.
county-of-schaumburg.r: The Schaumburg counts ruled a small, fertile territory on the [[e:weser|Weser]] while their [[s:county-of-holstein|Holstein]] branches became great Baltic lords. Count Ernst, who ruled from 1601, founded the university at [[e:rinteln|Rinteln]] in 1621, built the residence at [[e:buckeburg|Bückeburg]] and introduced Lutheran church order. [[e:stadthagen|Stadthagen]] held the counts' mausoleum.
county-of-schaumburg.e: The Schaumburg line died out with Otto V in 1640. The county was divided in 1647: the southern part went to [[s:electorate-of-hesse|Hesse-Kassel]], and the north to the counts of Lippe, forming [[s:principality-of-schaumburg-lippe|Schaumburg-Lippe]], which survived as a German state until 1946.

culhuacan.t: An ancient altepetl on the southern shore of Lake Texcoco, prized for its Toltec royal lineage, which passed legitimacy to the Mexica kings.
culhuacan.o: Culhuacan was settled in the Classic period and became a major city after the fall of Tula around 1150, when Toltec nobles were said to have established a dynasty there. It dominated the southern [[e:valley-of-mexico|Valley of Mexico]] in the 12th and 13th centuries.
culhuacan.r: Its rulers claimed direct Toltec descent, making Culhua lineage highly prestigious. In the early 14th century, according to [[e:mexica|Mexica]] tradition, the ruler [[e:coxcox|Coxcox]] allowed the wandering Mexica to settle at Tizaapan as [[e:vassal|vassals]]; they fought for him but were expelled after sacrificing a Culhua princess. The first Mexica king [[e:acamapichtli|Acamapichtli]] had Culhua royal ancestry.
culhuacan.e: Culhuacan was weakened by the [[s:tepanec-empire|Tepanec Empire]] and absorbed into the [[s:aztec-empire|Aztec Empire]] in the 15th century. It was conquered by the Spanish in 1521 and is now a district of [[e:mexico-city|Mexico City]].

crown-colony-of-sarawak.t: British colony in northern Borneo formed when the last White Rajah ceded Sarawak, despite strong local protest.
crown-colony-of-sarawak.o: After the [[s:japanese-occupation-of-british-borneo|Japanese occupation of British Borneo]], Rajah [[e:charles-vyner-brooke|Charles Vyner Brooke]] ceded the [[s:raj-of-sarawak|Raj of Sarawak]] to the British crown on 1 July 1946, arguing that he could not fund reconstruction. The cession was narrowly approved by the [[e:council-negri|Council Negri]] but opposed by many [[e:malays|Malays]] and members of the Brooke family.
crown-colony-of-sarawak.r: The colony was run by a governor with an appointed and later partly elected council. The anti-cession movement culminated in the assassination of Governor [[e:duncan-stewart-colonial-administrator|Duncan Stewart]] at [[e:sibu|Sibu]] by [[e:rosli-dhobi|Rosli Dhobi]] in December 1949. [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]] invested in schools, health and roads, and oil, [[e:rubber|rubber]], [[e:pepper|pepper]] and [[e:timber|timber]] exports grew. Communist influence spread among Chinese youth.
crown-colony-of-sarawak.e: After the [[e:cobbold-commission|Cobbold Commission]] found majority support, [[s:raj-of-sarawak|Sarawak]] joined [[s:malaysia|Malaysia]] on 16 September 1963 with safeguards on immigration, language and religion. The Indonesian Confrontation followed, and Sarawak remains a state of Malaysia.

cadurci.t: Gallic people of Quercy whose hill fort of Uxellodunum was the last stronghold to resist Caesar, in 51 BCE.
cadurci.o: The Cadurci lived in the valley of the Lot and its limestone plateaus, in the modern Lot. They were clients of the [[s:arverni|Arverni]] and produced linen famous in the Roman world.
cadurci.r: Their leader [[e:lucterius|Lucterius]] was one of the most active commanders of the revolt of 52 BCE, raising peoples of the south to threaten the Roman Province.
cadurci.e: In 51 BCE [[e:lucterius|Lucterius]] and the Senonian [[e:drappes|Drappes]] held [[e:siege-of-uxellodunum|Uxellodunum]], probably the Puy d'Issolud. Caesar cut off its water supply by tunnelling to the spring, and after the surrender he cut off the hands of the defenders as a warning. Under [[e:rome|Rome]] their town [[e:cahors|Divona]] became Cahors.

commune-of-bergamo.t: An Alpine-foothill city-republic in Lombardy, long torn between Guelph and Ghibelline clans before falling to Milan and then Venice.
commune-of-bergamo.o: Bergamo's [[e:bishop|bishops]] had held much of the city's authority, but consuls are recorded by 1098. The commune grew on wool, iron from the Bergamasque valleys and its position at the mouth of the Alpine valleys, and fought frequent border wars with [[s:commune-of-brescia|Brescia]].
commune-of-bergamo.r: [[e:consul|Consuls]] and later a podestà governed with a large council. Bergamo joined the [[s:lombard-league|Lombard League]] in 1167 against [[e:frederick-barbarossa|Frederick Barbarossa]], though it often leaned towards the emperors. In the 13th and 14th centuries the city was split between the Ghibelline Suardi and the Guelph Colleoni and Rivola families, whose feuds repeatedly invited outside lords into the upper town.
commune-of-bergamo.e: In 1332 [[e:azzone-visconti|Azzone Visconti]] took Bergamo into the [[s:lordship-of-milan|Lordship of Milan]]. The [[s:republic-of-venice|Republic of Venice]] conquered it in 1428 and held it until 1797, when it briefly became the [[s:republic-of-bergamo|Republic of Bergamo]].

castilla-de-oro.t: Spain's first mainland colony in the Americas, on the Isthmus of Panama, from which the Pacific was reached and the conquest of Peru launched.
castilla-de-oro.o: [[e:vasco-nunez-de-balboa|Vasco Núñez de Balboa]] founded Santa María la [[s:colony-of-antigua|Antigua]] del Darién in 1510 and crossed the isthmus to sight the Pacific in 1513. That year the Crown named the region Castilla de Oro and appointed [[e:pedrarias-davila|Pedrarias Dávila]] as governor; he arrived in 1514 with a large expedition.
castilla-de-oro.r: [[e:pedrarias-davila|Pedrarias]] ruled harshly, raiding indigenous communities for gold and slaves. Rivalry with [[e:vasco-nunez-de-balboa|Balboa]] ended with Balboa's execution in 1519. That year Pedrarias founded Panamá on the Pacific coast, which became the capital. Expeditions from [[s:republic-of-panama|Panama]] conquered [[s:republic-of-nicaragua|Nicaragua]] in 1524 and, under [[e:francisco-pizarro|Francisco Pizarro]], set out for [[e:peru|Peru]].
castilla-de-oro.e: The indigenous population of the isthmus collapsed. In 1538 the [[s:real-audiencia-of-panama|Real Audiencia of Panama]] was created, replacing the governorship as the main authority on the isthmus.

colla-kingdom.t: An Aymara kingdom on the northwestern shore of Lake Titicaca that rivalled the Lupaca and gave its name to the southern quarter of the Inca Empire.
colla-kingdom.o: The Colla, or Qolla, emerged as a leading power of the northern [[e:lake-titicaca|Titicaca]] basin around the 12th century, after the fall of [[s:tiwanaku|Tiwanaku]]. Their capital was [[e:hatuncolla|Hatuncolla]], near modern [[e:puno|Puno]], and their territory covered much of the plain between the lake and the Cordillera.
colla-kingdom.r: The Colla were ruled by powerful lords who controlled large herds of llamas and alpacas, a source of wool, meat and transport. They built fortified hilltop settlements and are known for chullpas, tall stone burial towers such as those at [[e:sillustani|Sillustani]], where elites were laid to rest. Colla lords fought the [[s:lupaca-kingdom|Lupaca Kingdom]] for control of the basin.
colla-kingdom.e: Around 1450 the Colla lord was defeated by the [[s:lupaca-kingdom|Lupaca]] and then by the [[e:inca-empire|Incas]] under [[e:pachacuti|Pachacuti]]. The Colla rebelled several times against Inca rule. Their name survived in [[e:collasuyu|Collasuyu]], the southern quarter of the [[s:inca-empire|Inca Empire]], and in the term Kolla for highland peoples of [[s:republic-of-bolivia|Bolivia]].

colony-of-new-zealand.t: The British colony founded after the Treaty of Waitangi, shaped by settler expansion and the New Zealand Wars, and first to give women the vote.
colony-of-new-zealand.o: After the [[e:treaty-of-waitangi|Treaty of Waitangi]] was signed with Māori chiefs in 1840, ending the [[s:united-tribes-of-new-zealand|United Tribes of New Zealand]], [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]] proclaimed [[e:sovereignty|sovereignty]] and governed [[s:new-zealand|New Zealand]] briefly as part of the [[s:colony-of-new-south-wales|Colony of New South Wales]]. It became a separate colony in 1841 under Governor [[e:william-hobson|William Hobson]], with [[e:auckland|Auckland]] as capital until [[e:wellington|Wellington]] replaced it in 1865.
colony-of-new-zealand.r: The [[s:new-zealand|New Zealand]] Company and church settlements brought British migrants, and the [[e:new-zealand-constitution-act-1852|Constitution Act]] of 1852 created a parliament and provinces. Disputes over land led to the [[e:new-zealand|New Zealand]] Wars from 1845 to 1872, followed by confiscations and the Native Land Court, which transferred most Māori land to settlers. Wool, gold from [[e:otago|Otago]] and, after 1882, refrigerated meat drove the economy. In 1893 it became the first self-governing country to give women the vote.
colony-of-new-zealand.e: [[e:richard-seddon|Richard Seddon's]] Liberal government, in office from 1893, pioneered [[e:social-insurance|old-age pensions]], compulsory labour arbitration and the purchase of large estates for small farmers. [[s:new-zealand|New Zealand]] declined to join the Australian federation and in 1907 became the [[s:dominion-of-new-zealand|Dominion of New Zealand]].

cherokee-nation.t: A Native American nation that adopted a written constitution and its own syllabary, and survived forced removal on the Trail of Tears to rebuild in Indian Territory.
cherokee-nation.o: After decades of war with colonists and the [[e:chickamauga-cherokee|Chickamauga]] resistance, [[e:cherokee|Cherokee]] towns in the southern [[e:appalachian-mountains|Appalachians]] made peace with the [[s:united-states|United States]] in 1794. Over the following years they centralised authority, creating a national council, a written legal code from 1808 and a capital at [[e:new-echota|New Echota]].
cherokee-nation.r: The 1827 constitution created a republic with a principal chief, a [[e:bicameral-legislature|bicameral legislature]] and courts. [[e:sequoyah|Sequoyah's]] syllabary, adopted in the 1820s, brought rapid literacy and the bilingual newspaper [[e:cherokee-phoenix|Cherokee Phoenix]]. Many [[e:cherokee|Cherokee]] farmed, and an elite owned plantations worked by enslaved Africans. Principal Chief [[e:john-ross-cherokee-chief|John Ross]] fought removal through petitions and lawsuits, and in [[e:worcester-v-georgia|Worcester v. Georgia]] in 1832 the Supreme Court ruled that [[e:georgia|Georgia's]] laws had no force in Cherokee territory, but the ruling went unenforced.
cherokee-nation.e: The disputed Treaty of New Echota led to forced removal in 1838 and 1839, the [[e:trail-of-tears|Trail of Tears]], in which thousands died. Rebuilt around [[e:tahlequah|Tahlequah]], the nation lost its government's powers when [[e:oklahoma|Oklahoma]] became a state in 1907; it was reconstituted in the 20th century.

county-of-coimbra.t: A frontier county of the Kingdom of Asturias and León created when Christian forces took Coimbra in 878, lost to Almanzor in 987.
county-of-coimbra.o: In 878 [[e:hermenegildo-gutierrez|Hermenegildo Gutiérrez]], a noble serving [[e:alfonso-iii-of-asturias|Alfonso III of Asturias]], captured [[e:coimbra|Coimbra]] on the [[e:mondego|Mondego]] from the [[s:emirate-of-cordoba|Emirate of Córdoba]]. The city became the centre of a frontier county stretching south from the [[e:douro|Douro]], settled by northern Christians and local [[e:mozarabs|Mozarabs]].
county-of-coimbra.r: The counts were military governors for the Asturian and Leonese kings, defending a vulnerable frontier and organising resettlement. Mozarabic Christians from [[e:al-andalus|al-Andalus]] brought Arabic culture and Visigothic church traditions, and monasteries such as [[e:lorvao-monastery|Lorvão]] became important landowners. Power passed among a few noble families who intermarried with the counts of Portugal.
county-of-coimbra.e: In 987 [[e:almanzor|Almanzor]] captured [[e:coimbra|Coimbra]], ending the county; the city was left largely deserted for a time. [[e:ferdinand-i-of-leon|Ferdinand I of León]] retook it in 1064, and in 1096 it was joined to the [[s:county-of-portugal|County of Portugal]], later becoming the first capital of the [[s:kingdom-of-portugal|Kingdom of Portugal]].

celtiberians.t: Celtic-speaking peoples of the central Iberian plateau whose long resistance to Rome ended with the fall of Numantia in 133 BCE.
celtiberians.o: The Celtiberians took shape from about the 6th century BCE in the upper [[e:ebro-river|Ebro]], [[e:douro|Douro]] and [[e:tagus|Tagus]] basins, in modern [[e:soria|Soria]], [[e:guadalajara-spain|Guadalajara]], [[e:zaragoza|Zaragoza]] and [[e:cuenca-spain|Cuenca]]. Ancient writers saw them as a mix of [[e:celts|Celts]] and [[e:iberians|Iberians]]; they spoke a Celtic language and included peoples such as the [[s:arevaci|Arevaci]], [[s:belli|Belli]], [[s:titti|Titti]] and [[s:lusones|Lusones]].
celtiberians.r: They lived in fortified hill towns, or oppida, governed by councils and assemblies, with strong warrior elites, client bonds and hospitality pacts recorded on bronze tablets. They wrote Celtiberian in an adapted Iberian script, as on the [[e:botorrita|Botorrita]] bronzes, and were famed for their swords, later adopted by the Roman army as the gladius hispaniensis.
celtiberians.e: [[e:rome|Rome]] fought the Celtiberian Wars from 181 to 133 BCE, ending with [[e:scipio-aemilianus|Scipio Aemilianus]]' siege and destruction of [[e:numantia|Numantia]]. Many later backed [[e:quintus-sertorius|Sertorius]], and after his death in 72 BCE they were absorbed into [[s:hispania-citerior|Hispania Citerior]] and Romanised.

colony-of-tobago.t: British sugar colony on Tobago, fought over with France until 1814, whose economic collapse led to its union with Trinidad in 1889.
colony-of-tobago.o: After a century of contest between the [[e:dutch|Dutch]], French, English and Courlanders, [[e:tobago|Tobago]] was ceded to [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]] by the [[e:treaty-of-paris-1763|Treaty of Paris]] in 1763. Settlers quickly cleared the forest for [[e:sugar-plantation|sugar]] estates, and [[e:scarborough-tobago|Scarborough]] became the capital. [[e:france|France]] captured the island in 1781 and held it until 1793, regained it briefly in 1802 and finally ceded it in 1814.
colony-of-tobago.r: [[e:tobago|Tobago]] had a governor, council and elected assembly of planters and, by the late 18th century, a population dominated by enslaved Africans on [[e:sugar-plantation|sugar]], [[e:cotton|cotton]] and [[e:indigo|indigo]] estates. After emancipation in 1834 to 1838 many freed people worked under the metairie, or sharecropping, system. Falling sugar prices, a hurricane in 1847 and the Belmanna riots of 1876, after which the assembly gave up its powers, marked its decline.
colony-of-tobago.e: The failure of the [[e:london|London]] firm Gillespie Brothers in 1884 ruined the [[e:sugar-plantation|sugar]] estates. [[e:tobago|Tobago]] was joined to [[e:trinidad|Trinidad]] in 1889 and became a ward of the [[s:colony-of-trinidad-and-tobago|Colony of Trinidad and Tobago]] in 1899, losing its separate administration.

cr.a: Thomas Bowen; derivative work by MagentaGreen

county-of-helfenstein.t: A Swabian county on the Swabian Jura whose counts controlled the trade route to Ulm before debts and extinction ended their line in 1627.
county-of-helfenstein.o: The lords of Helfenstein appear around 1100 with a castle on the [[e:swabian-jura|Swabian Jura]] above [[e:geislingen-an-der-steige|Geislingen an der Steige]]. The family rose under the [[e:hohenstaufen|Staufer]] and by the 14th century held a sizeable territory on the Alb and the [[e:fils-river|Fils]] valley, controlling the main road from [[e:stuttgart|Stuttgart]] to Ulm.
county-of-helfenstein.r: In 1396 the counts, deep in debt, sold most of their lands, including [[e:geislingen-an-der-steige|Geislingen]], to the imperial city of Ulm. They kept a smaller territory around Wiesensteig and became a modest family of Swabian counts who served the [[e:habsburg-dynasty|Habsburgs]]. Count [[e:ludwig-helferich-of-helfenstein|Ludwig Helferich of Helfenstein]] was killed in the [[e:weinsberg-massacre|Weinsberg massacre]] of the [[e:german-peasants-war|Peasants' War]] in 1525.
county-of-helfenstein.e: The last count, Rudolf, died in 1627. His territory around Wiesensteig passed through heiresses to the [[s:principality-of-furstenberg|Fürstenberg]] family and, in 1642, partly to [[e:bavaria|Bavaria]]. The ruins of Helfenstein castle still stand above [[e:geislingen-an-der-steige|Geislingen]].

county-of-toulouse.t: Great southern principality, heart of Occitan culture and troubadour poetry, destroyed by the Albigensian Crusade.
county-of-toulouse.o: [[e:charlemagne|Charlemagne]] appointed Chorson count of [[e:toulouse|Toulouse]] in 778, followed by [[e:william-of-gellone|William of Gellone]], later a saint. In the 9th century the county passed to a hereditary line known as the [[e:raymondines|Raymondines]], who extended their power over [[s:county-of-rodez|Rouergue]], [[e:quercy|Quercy]], [[e:albi|Albi]] and parts of [[e:languedoc|Languedoc]] and [[s:county-of-provence|Provence]].
county-of-toulouse.r: The counts ruled a loosely held territory of powerful [[e:vassal|vassals]] and self-governing towns, where [[e:toulouse|Toulouse]] was run by elected consuls. Count [[e:raymond-iv-of-toulouse|Raymond IV]] led a great army on the [[e:first-crusade|First Crusade]] and founded the [[s:county-of-tripoli|County of Tripoli]]. The court fostered troubadour poetry, and the [[e:catharism|Cathar]] heresy spread widely in its lands.
county-of-toulouse.e: The [[e:albigensian-crusade|Albigensian Crusade]] from 1209 brought northern French armies under [[e:simon-de-montfort-5th-earl-of-leicester|Simon de Montfort]], who defeated [[e:raymond-vi-count-of-toulouse|Raymond VI]] and [[e:peter-ii-of-aragon|Peter II of Aragon]] at [[e:battle-of-muret|Muret]] in 1213. By the [[e:treaty-of-paris-1229|Treaty of Paris]] in 1229 [[e:raymond-vii-count-of-toulouse|Raymond VII]]'s heiress [[e:joan-countess-of-toulouse|Joan]] married [[e:alphonse-count-of-poitiers|Alphonse of Poitiers]], and on their deaths in 1271 the county passed to the [[s:kingdom-of-france|Kingdom of France]].

county-of-osona.t: The Catalan county of the plain of Vic, resettled by Wilfred the Hairy, where the monasteries of Ripoll and Vic grew into centres of learning.
county-of-osona.o: Osona, named after the ancient [[s:ausetani|Ausetani]], came under Frankish rule around 798. After the revolt of [[e:aisso|Aissó]] in 826 it was largely abandoned. From about 879 [[e:wilfred-the-hairy|Wilfred the Hairy]] repopulated the plain of Vic, restored its bishopric in 886 and founded the monasteries of [[e:monastery-of-santa-maria-de-ripoll|Ripoll]] and [[e:monastery-of-sant-joan-de-les-abadesses|Sant Joan de les Abadesses]].
county-of-osona.r: Osona was a frontier county facing [[e:al-andalus|al-Andalus]], settled by free peasant colonists who cleared land and built castles. It was usually held by the counts of [[e:barcelona|Barcelona]] rather than having its own line. Its church centres flourished: [[e:monastery-of-santa-maria-de-ripoll|Ripoll]]'s library made it a hub of learning in the 10th century, where [[e:pope-sylvester-ii|Gerbert of Aurillac]] studied Arabic science.
county-of-osona.e: Osona remained in the hands of the [[e:house-of-barcelona|House of Barcelona]], briefly granted to younger sons, until it was fully merged with the [[s:county-of-barcelona|County of Barcelona]]. It became part of [[s:principality-of-catalonia|Catalonia]] and the [[s:crown-of-aragon|Crown of Aragon]], and Vic remains its centre.

chak-dynasty.t: The last independent dynasty of Kashmir, Shia rulers who held the valley for a quarter of a century before Akbar's conquest.
chak-dynasty.o: The Chaks were a Kashmiri military clan who rose to power as nobles under the [[s:kashmir-sultanate|Kashmir Sultanate]]. In 1561 [[e:ghazi-shah-chak|Ghazi Shah Chak]] deposed the last [[e:shah-mir|Shah Mir]] sultan and took the throne at Srinagar, founding the first Shia dynasty of [[e:kashmir|Kashmir]].
chak-dynasty.r: The Chak period was marked by noble feuds and religious tension between Shia and [[e:sunni-islam|Sunni]] factions. [[e:yusuf-shah-chak|Yusuf Shah Chak]], who reigned twice in the 1570s and 1580s, is remembered with his wife, the poet [[e:habba-khatun|Habba Khatun]], whose Kashmiri songs remain popular. The rulers struggled to resist Mughal pressure while sending envoys to [[e:akbar|Akbar]].
chak-dynasty.e: [[e:akbar|Akbar's]] forces invaded in 1586. [[e:yusuf-shah-chak|Yusuf Shah]] surrendered and was exiled to [[e:bihar|Bihar]], and his son [[e:yaqub-shah-chak|Yaqub Shah]] held out briefly. [[e:kashmir|Kashmir]] became a province of the [[s:mughal-empire|Mughal Empire]], ending its independence.

colony-of-newfoundland.t: England's oldest overseas colony in origin, a fishing outpost of the North Atlantic that chose to stay outside Canada for more than 80 years.
colony-of-newfoundland.o: [[e:john-cabot|John Cabot]] reached the region in 1497, and fishing fleets from [[e:england|England]], [[e:france|France]], Portugal and the Basque country worked its banks for a century before settlement. In 1610 [[e:john-guy|John Guy]] founded a colony at [[e:cupids|Cupids]] for the [[e:newfoundland-company|London and Bristol Company]], and other proprietary ventures followed, including [[e:george-calvert-1st-baron-baltimore|George Calvert]]'s Avalon at [[e:ferryland|Ferryland]] in 1621.
colony-of-newfoundland.r: For two centuries the migratory cod fishery from the West Country dominated, and fishing admirals and visiting naval officers kept order, while the French held [[s:plaisance|Plaisance]] until 1713. Settlers from [[e:england|England]] and Ireland gradually stayed year-round in outports along the coast, salting cod for markets in southern [[e:europe|Europe]] and the [[e:caribbean|Caribbean]]. [[s:dominion-of-newfoundland|Newfoundland]] became a formal crown colony in 1825, gained representative government in 1832 and responsible government in 1855 under [[e:philip-francis-little|Philip Francis Little]].
colony-of-newfoundland.e: Newfoundlanders rejected joining the new [[s:canada|Dominion of Canada]] in the 1869 election. The long dispute over French fishing rights on the French Shore was settled in 1904, and in 1907 the colony became the [[s:dominion-of-newfoundland|Dominion of Newfoundland]].

copan.t: The southernmost great Classic Maya kingdom, in western Honduras, famed for its sculpted stelae and the longest known Maya hieroglyphic text.
copan.o: The Copán valley had been farmed for centuries when, in 426 CE, [[e:kinich-yax-kuk-mo|K'inich Yax K'uk' Mo']], a lord with ties to [[s:teotihuacan|Teotihuacan]] and [[s:tikal|Tikal]], founded a dynasty that would rule for some four centuries. Successive temples were built over his tomb in the Acropolis.
copan.r: Sixteen kings ruled Copán. [[e:waxaklajuun-ubaah-kawiil|Waxaklajuun Ub'aah K'awiil]] (18 Rabbit) commissioned the deeply carved stelae of the Great Plaza before his capture by [[s:quirigua|Quiriguá]] in 738. The Hieroglyphic Stairway records dynastic history in some 2,200 glyphs, and Altar Q depicts all sixteen rulers. Nobles lived in sculpted compounds, and the city was a centre of scribal and astronomical learning.
copan.e: Under [[e:yax-pasaj-chan-yopaat|Yax Pasaj Chan Yopaat]] the valley was overpopulated and deforested, and royal rule ended around 820-830. Population dwindled over following centuries. Copán became a [[e:unesco-world-heritage-site|UNESCO World Heritage Site]] in 1980.

cr.a: Adalberto Hernandez Vega from Copan Ruinas, Honduras

canton-of-cadiz.t: A revolutionary canton proclaimed in the port city of Cádiz in July 1873, one of the first to be crushed by the Republic's army.
canton-of-cadiz.o: In July 1873 the federalists of Cádiz, a city with strong radical and republican traditions, declared a sovereign canton as part of the [[e:cantonal-rebellion|Cantonal Rebellion]] against the central government of the [[s:spanish-first-republic|Spanish First Republic]].
canton-of-cadiz.r: A revolutionary committee governed the city and its militias, but it had little support beyond Cádiz itself and almost no time to organise.
canton-of-cadiz.e: After crushing the [[s:canton-of-seville|Canton of Seville]], General [[e:manuel-pavia-y-rodriguez-de-alburquerque|Manuel Pavía]] advanced on Cádiz, which submitted in early August 1873 with little resistance.

chola-empire.t: The South Indian empire of Rajaraja and Rajendra, whose navy reached Southeast Asia and whose temples and bronzes are masterpieces of Indian art.
chola-empire.o: In 848 [[e:vijayalaya-chola|Vijayalaya]], a local chief descended from the [[s:early-cholas|Early Cholas]], took [[e:thanjavur|Thanjavur]] in the Kaveri delta. His son [[e:aditya-i|Aditya I]] defeated the [[s:pallava-dynasty|Pallava dynasty]] around 897, and [[e:parantaka-i|Parantaka I]] conquered the [[s:first-pandyan-empire|First Pandyan Empire]]. After a setback against the [[s:rashtrakuta-dynasty|Rashtrakutas]], [[e:rajaraja-i|Rajaraja I]], from 985, made the Cholas the greatest power of the south.
chola-empire.r: [[e:rajaraja-i|Rajaraja I]] conquered northern [[s:sri-lanka|Sri Lanka]] and the [[s:republic-of-maldives|Maldives]] and built the [[e:brihadishvara-temple|Brihadishvara]] temple at [[e:thanjavur|Thanjavur]]. [[e:rajendra-chola-i|Rajendra I]] marched to the [[e:ganges-plain|Ganges]], founded [[e:gangaikondacholapuram|Gangaikondacholapuram]] and launched a naval raid on [[e:srivijaya|Srivijaya]] in 1025. Villages were run by assemblies, recorded in the [[e:uttaramerur|Uttaramerur]] inscriptions, and land was carefully surveyed for revenue. Chola bronzes of [[e:nataraja|Shiva Nataraja]] and Tamil devotional literature flourished, and merchant [[e:guild|guilds]] traded with [[e:song-dynasty|Song China]].
chola-empire.e: From the late 12th century the empire was squeezed by the [[s:hoysala-empire|Hoysala Empire]] and a revived [[e:pandya-dynasty|Pandya]] kingdom. In 1279 the last Chola king, [[e:rajendra-chola-iii|Rajendra III]], was defeated by the [[s:later-pandyan-empire|Pandyas]], and Chola rule ended.

cook-islands.t: A Polynesian island group annexed by New Zealand in 1901 that has governed itself in free association with New Zealand since 1965.
cook-islands.o: With the consent of leading ariki, [[s:new-zealand|New Zealand]] annexed the islands of the [[s:cook-islands-federation|Cook Islands Federation]], together with [[e:niue|Niue]], on 11 June 1901. Niue was soon placed under a separate administration. A resident commissioner at [[e:avarua|Avarua]] on [[s:kingdom-of-rarotonga|Rarotonga]] governed on behalf of the [[e:new-zealand|New Zealand]] government.
cook-islands.r: Colonial administration was paternalistic, with the land court and island councils replacing the federation's institutions, and the islands depended on exports of citrus, copra and pearl shell to [[s:new-zealand|New Zealand]]. Cook Islanders served in the [[e:first-world-war|First World War]], and the 1918 influenza struck [[s:kingdom-of-rarotonga|Rarotonga]]. Large-scale emigration to [[e:new-zealand|New Zealand]] began after the [[e:second-world-war|Second World War]], and Cook Islanders are New Zealand citizens.
cook-islands.e: In 1965 the islands became self-governing in free association with [[s:new-zealand|New Zealand]] under Premier [[e:albert-henry|Albert Henry]], who was removed in 1978 for electoral fraud. The Cook Islands conducts much of its own foreign policy and relies on tourism, pearls and remittances.

county-of-wurttemberg.t: The Swabian county that grew from a single hilltop castle into the leading territory of south-west Germany, becoming a duchy in 1495.
county-of-wurttemberg.o: [[e:conrad-i-of-wurttemberg|Conrad of Wirtemberg]] is first mentioned in 1081 to 1083, with a castle on the Wirtemberg hill near [[e:stuttgart|Stuttgart]]. After the fall of the [[s:duchy-of-swabia|Duchy of Swabia]] in 1268, Count [[e:ulrich-i-count-of-wurttemberg|Ulrich I]] and his successors bought and seized many of its lands, building a compact territory on the [[e:neckar|Neckar]].
county-of-wurttemberg.r: [[e:eberhard-i-count-of-wurttemberg|Eberhard I]] fought the Swabian imperial cities and [[e:henry-vii-holy-roman-emperor|Emperor Henry VII]], and [[e:stuttgart|Stuttgart]] became the residence in the 14th century. The county was divided between [[e:bad-urach|Urach]] and Stuttgart lines in 1442. [[e:eberhard-i-duke-of-wurttemberg|Count Eberhard V the Bearded]] reunited it by the [[e:treaty-of-munsingen|Treaty of Münsingen]] in 1482 and founded the [[e:university-of-tubingen|University of Tübingen]] in 1477.
county-of-wurttemberg.e: In 1495 at the [[e:diet-of-worms-1495|Diet of Worms]], [[e:maximilian-i-holy-roman-emperor|Emperor Maximilian I]] raised Württemberg to a duchy under [[e:eberhard-i-duke-of-wurttemberg|Eberhard the Bearded]]. The [[s:duchy-of-wurttemberg|Duchy of Württemberg]] became an electorate in 1803 and a kingdom in 1806, and today forms part of the state of [[e:baden-wurttemberg|Baden-Württemberg]].

cispadane-republic.t: A short-lived French-backed republic south of the Po whose congress adopted the green, white and red tricolour, ancestor of the Italian flag.
cispadane-republic.o: In 1796 French victories ended Este rule in [[e:modena|Modena]] and papal rule in [[s:republic-of-bologna|Bologna]] and [[e:ferrara|Ferrara]]. Delegates of [[e:bologna|Bologna]], Ferrara, Modena and [[e:reggio-emilia|Reggio]] met in congress at Reggio and Modena, and in December 1796 proclaimed the Cispadane Republic.
cispadane-republic.r: On 7 January 1797 the congress at [[e:reggio-emilia|Reggio]] adopted the green, white and red tricolour as its flag, now celebrated as the birth of the Italian flag. The republic drafted a constitution modelled on the [[s:french-first-republic|French Directory]] and held elections in early 1797. It depended entirely on French protection, and [[s:republic-of-bologna|Bologna]] was its main centre.
cispadane-republic.e: Only months later, in July 1797, [[e:napoleon|Napoleon]] merged the Cispadane Republic with the [[s:transpadane-republic|Transpadane Republic]] to create the [[s:cisalpine-republic|Cisalpine Republic]].

county-of-flanders.t: Rich medieval county on the North Sea whose cloth towns of Bruges, Ghent and Ypres made it one of the wealthiest regions of Europe.
county-of-flanders.o: In 862 [[e:baldwin-i-of-flanders|Baldwin I]], called Iron Arm, eloped with [[e:judith-of-france|Judith]], daughter of [[e:charles-the-bald|Charles the Bald]], and was given lands around [[e:bruges|Bruges]] to defend against the [[e:vikings|Vikings]]. His descendants expanded the county from the [[e:scheldt|Scheldt]] to the [[e:canche|Canche]], holding most of it as [[e:vassal|vassals]] of the [[s:kingdom-of-france|Kingdom of France]] and a smaller part, [[e:imperial-flanders|Imperial Flanders]], from the [[s:holy-roman-empire|Holy Roman Empire]].
county-of-flanders.r: [[e:flanders|Flanders]] grew rich on weaving English wool into fine cloth, and its towns gained wide self-government and often defied the counts and the French kings. Count [[e:baldwin-i-latin-emperor|Baldwin IX]] became the first [[e:latin|Latin]] emperor of [[e:constantinople|Constantinople]] in 1204. In 1302 Flemish townsmen defeated French knights at the [[e:battle-of-the-golden-spurs|Battle of the Golden Spurs]] at [[e:kortrijk|Courtrai]].
county-of-flanders.e: In 1384 [[e:flanders|Flanders]] passed to [[e:philip-the-bold|Philip the Bold]] of [[s:duchy-of-burgundy|Burgundy]] and became part of the [[s:burgundian-state|Burgundian State]], then of the [[s:habsburg-netherlands|Habsburg Netherlands]] and the [[s:spanish-netherlands|Spanish Netherlands]]. [[e:france|France]] conquered its southern part in the 17th century, and the rest was annexed by France in 1795.

confederate-states-of-america.t: The breakaway republic of eleven slave-holding Southern states, whose defeat in the American Civil War ended slavery in the United States.
confederate-states-of-america.o: After [[e:abraham-lincoln|Abraham Lincoln]], who opposed the expansion of [[e:slavery|slavery]], won the 1860 election, [[e:south-carolina|South Carolina]] seceded from the [[s:united-states|United States]] in December. Six more Deep South states followed and formed the Confederacy at [[e:montgomery-alabama|Montgomery, Alabama]], in February 1861. After the attack on [[e:battle-of-fort-sumter|Fort Sumter]] in April, [[e:virginia|Virginia]], [[e:arkansas|Arkansas]], [[e:tennessee|Tennessee]] and North [[s:province-of-carolina|Carolina]] joined, and the capital moved to [[e:richmond-virginia|Richmond]].
confederate-states-of-america.r: The Confederate constitution copied much of the American one but explicitly protected [[e:slavery|slavery]]. President [[e:jefferson-davis|Jefferson Davis]] governed a weak central state that nonetheless introduced conscription in 1862, taxes in kind and [[e:paper-money|paper money]] that led to severe [[e:inflation|inflation]]. The Union [[e:naval-blockade|blockade]] throttled the [[e:cotton|cotton]] trade, and hopes of European recognition failed. [[e:robert-e-lee|Robert E. Lee's]] [[e:army-of-northern-virginia|Army of Northern Virginia]] won major victories until [[e:battle-of-gettysburg|Gettysburg]] in 1863.
confederate-states-of-america.e: With the fall of [[e:siege-of-vicksburg|Vicksburg]], William T. [[e:william-tecumseh-sherman|Sherman]]'s march through [[s:georgia|Georgia]] and the loss of [[e:richmond-virginia|Richmond]], [[e:robert-e-lee|Lee]] surrendered at [[e:battle-of-appomattox-court-house|Appomattox]] in April 1865 and [[e:jefferson-davis|Davis]] was captured in May. The [[e:thirteenth-amendment|Thirteenth Amendment]] abolished [[e:slavery|slavery]], and the Confederacy's memory remains bitterly contested.

county-of-aragon.t: The small Pyrenean county around Jaca that gave its name to the Kingdom and later the Crown of Aragon.
county-of-aragon.o: The county arose in the early 9th century in the upper valley of the river Aragón, around [[e:jaca|Jaca]], as a Frankish-backed frontier lordship. Its first known count, [[e:aznar-galindez-i|Aznar Galíndez I]], ruled in the 800s under Carolingian protection before being expelled by rivals allied with [[e:pamplona|Pamplona]].
county-of-aragon.r: Aragon was a mountain county of herders and small farmers, protected by castles and monasteries such as [[e:monastery-of-san-juan-de-la-pena|San Juan de la Peña]] and [[e:monastery-of-san-pedro-de-siresa|San Pedro de Siresa]]. Its native counts of the Galindo family kept close ties with [[e:pamplona|Pamplona]], and in the early 10th century the heiress [[e:andregoto-galindez|Andregoto Galíndez]] married [[e:garcia-sanchez-i-of-pamplona|García Sánchez I of Pamplona]], bringing the county under the Navarrese crown.
county-of-aragon.e: Aragon was ruled from [[e:pamplona|Pamplona]] until [[e:sancho-iii-of-navarre|Sancho III]] died in 1035 and left it to his son [[e:ramiro-i-of-aragon|Ramiro I]], who governed it as a separate realm, the beginning of the [[s:kingdom-of-aragon|Kingdom of Aragon]], which later grew into the [[s:crown-of-aragon|Crown of Aragon]].

cutch-state.t: The Jadeja Rajput kingdom of Kutch, a semi-island of salt marsh and desert between Sindh and Gujarat, with its own sea trade, coinage and court arts.
cutch-state.o: The [[e:jadeja|Jadeja Rajputs]] came from [[e:sindh|Sindh]] and settled in Kutch in the [[e:middle-ages|medieval period]]; the register's date reflects tradition rather than firm record. Several Jadeja branches competed until [[e:khengarji-i|Rao Khengarji]] I united the country in the mid-16th century and made [[e:bhuj|Bhuj]] his capital.
cutch-state.r: Kutch was cut off by the [[e:rann-of-kutch|Rann]] but faced the [[e:arabian-sea|Arabian Sea]], and its sailors and merchants traded with [[e:arabia|Arabia]] and [[e:east-africa|East Africa]] from [[e:mandvi-kutch|Mandvi]]. The state issued its own [[e:silver|silver]] kori coins. [[e:lakhpatji|Rao Lakhpatji]] (r. 1741–1761) patronised poets and craftsmen, and his reign produced the [[e:aina-mahal|Aina Mahal]] palace. The Rao ruled with powerful [[e:jadeja|Jadeja]] kinsmen holding estates.
cutch-state.e: Treaties with the British from 1816 made Kutch a protected state, and in 1819 a great earthquake struck. Kutch acceded to [[e:india|India]] in 1947 and in 1948 became a centrally governed province, later joining [[e:bombay-state|Bombay State]] and, in 1960, [[e:gujarat|Gujarat]].
