chosokabe-clan-domain.t: The domain of the Chosokabe of Tosa, whose lord Motochika conquered nearly all of Shikoku before Toyotomi Hideyoshi cut him back to his home province.
chosokabe-clan-domain.o: The Chosokabe were one of seven local warrior families of [[e:tosa-province|Tosa]], based at Okoh castle. [[e:chosokabe-kunichika|Chosokabe Kunichika]] rebuilt their power, and his son [[e:chosokabe-motochika|Motochika]], who succeeded in 1560, defeated rival families and the Ichijo governors to unify Tosa by 1575.
chosokabe-clan-domain.r: [[e:chosokabe-motochika|Motochika]] relied on part-time farmer-soldiers, the ichiryo gusoku, who kept their armour in the fields ready to fight. He overran [[e:awa-province-tokushima|Awa]], [[e:sanuki-province|Sanuki]] and [[e:iyo-province|Iyo]] and by 1585 controlled most of [[e:shikoku|Shikoku]]. He carried out a full land survey of [[e:tosa-province|Tosa]] and in 1597 issued a detailed house code, moving his seat to Urado on the coast.
chosokabe-clan-domain.e: Hideyoshi's invasion of [[e:shikoku|Shikoku]] in 1585 reduced [[e:chosokabe-motochika|Motochika]] to [[e:tosa-province|Tosa]], and his heir [[e:chosokabe-nobuchika|Nobuchika]] died in the [[e:kyushu|Kyushu]] campaign in 1586. His son [[e:chosokabe-morichika|Morichika]] joined the western army at [[e:battle-of-sekigahara|Sekigahara]] in 1600 and lost Tosa, which passed to [[e:yamauchi-kazutoyo|Yamauchi Kazutoyo]] as the [[s:tosa-domain|Tosa Domain]].

contestani.t: The Iberian people of Alicante and Murcia whose sculptors produced the Lady of Elche, the masterpiece of Iberian art.
contestani.o: The Contestani occupied the coast and hinterland of south-east [[e:spain|Spain]], roughly the modern provinces of [[e:alicante|Alicante]] and parts of [[e:murcia|Murcia]] and [[e:valencia|Valencia]], from the 5th century BCE. They grew out of earlier Iberian communities in close contact with Phoenician and Greek traders.
contestani.r: Their towns, such as [[e:la-alcudia-elche|Ilici]] (La Alcudia, [[e:elche|Elche]]), La Serreta near [[e:alcoy|Alcoy]] and [[e:lucentum|Lucentum]], were centres of a refined Iberian culture. The stone bust of the [[e:lady-of-elche|Lady of Elche]], carved around the 4th century BCE, comes from their territory. They wrote their Iberian language in a Greek-derived alphabet, recorded on lead tablets, and traded [[e:olive-oil|olive oil]], wine and esparto.
contestani.e: After Carthaginian control under [[s:barcid-iberia|Barcid Iberia]], the region passed to [[e:rome|Rome]] when [[e:scipio-africanus|Scipio]] captured [[e:carthago-nova|Carthago Nova]] in 209 BCE, and was pacified by 197 BCE. [[e:la-alcudia-elche|Ilici]] became a Roman colony, and the Contestani merged into [[s:hispania-citerior|Hispania Citerior]].

chichen-itza.t: The dominant city of northern Yucatán in the Terminal Classic and Early Postclassic, whose Castillo pyramid and Great Ballcourt are icons of Maya civilisation.
chichen-itza.o: Chichen Itza grew around two natural sinkholes (cenotes) in north-central [[e:yucatan-peninsula|Yucatán]]. Inscriptions show it was an important centre by the 9th century, when the lord [[e:kakupakal|K'ak'upakal]] was active, and it rose to dominate the north as Classic cities declined.
chichen-itza.r: Chichen Itza seems to have been governed by a council of nobles rather than a single divine king. Its art combined Maya traditions with central Mexican features such as feathered serpents, warrior columns and chacmool figures, once explained as a Toltec conquest but now seen as wider interaction. It controlled coastal trade in salt and other goods. The [[e:sacred-cenote|Sacred Cenote]] received offerings of gold, jade and [[e:human-sacrifice|human sacrifice]].
chichen-itza.e: Chichen Itza lost its political dominance around 1200, and the [[s:league-of-mayapan|League of Mayapan]] took its place, though pilgrims still visited the [[e:sacred-cenote|Sacred Cenote]] at the Spanish conquest. It became a [[e:unesco-world-heritage-site|UNESCO World Heritage Site]] in 1988.

corsican-republic.t: Pasquale Paoli's independent Corsica, whose written constitution of 1755 made it one of the first modern republics and inspired admirers across Europe.
corsican-republic.o: After decades of rebellion against [[s:republic-of-genoa|Genoa]], the Corsican assembly elected [[e:pasquale-paoli|Pasquale Paoli]] as General of the Nation in July 1755. In November he gave the island a constitution establishing a national assembly elected by male heads of family, with [[e:corte|Corte]] as the capital.
corsican-republic.r: Paoli built a state from the interior, founding a university at [[e:corte|Corte]] in 1765, a mint, a navy and the port of [[e:lile-rousse|L'Île-Rousse]]. Justice was reformed to curb vendettas. James Boswell's [[e:an-account-of-corsica|Account of Corsica]] of 1768 made Paoli famous in [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]] and among [[e:age-of-enlightenment|Enlightenment]] writers, but [[s:republic-of-genoa|Genoa]] still held the main ports.
corsican-republic.e: In 1768, by the [[e:treaty-of-versailles|Treaty of Versailles]], [[s:republic-of-genoa|Genoa]] ceded its rights over [[e:corsica|Corsica]] to [[e:france|France]]. French troops defeated the Corsicans at [[e:battle-of-ponte-novu|Ponte Novu]] in May 1769, Paoli went into exile in [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]], and the island became part of the [[s:kingdom-of-france|Kingdom of France]].

changbhakar-state.t: A small forested state on the northern edge of Chhattisgarh, separated from Korea State in the late 18th century.
changbhakar-state.o: Changbhakar was formed around 1790 when a junior branch of the [[e:chauhan|Chauhan]] family ruling [[s:korea-state|Korea State]] received its own share of territory, with its seat at [[s:bharatpur-state|Bharatpur]] in the hills of north-western [[e:chhattisgarh|Chhattisgarh]].
changbhakar-state.r: The state was thinly populated, heavily forested and largely Adivasi. It was a feudatory state of the [[e:chota-nagpur-plateau|Chota Nagpur]] and later [[e:chhattisgarh|Chhattisgarh]] groups under British supervision. Little else is recorded.
changbhakar-state.e: Changbhakar acceded to [[e:india|India]] and on 1 January 1948 was merged into the [[e:central-provinces|Central Provinces and Berar]]. Its lands are now in [[e:chhattisgarh|Chhattisgarh]].

county-of-champagne.t: The county of the great Champagne fairs, where Flemish cloth met Italian merchants and the court of Troyes nurtured Chrétien de Troyes.
county-of-champagne.o: The counties of [[e:troyes|Troyes]] and [[e:meaux|Meaux]] were built up in the 10th century by the counts of [[s:county-of-vermandois|Vermandois]], descendants of [[e:herbert-ii-count-of-vermandois|Herbert II]], and passed around 1022 to [[e:odo-ii-of-blois|Odo II of Blois]]. A younger branch of the [[s:county-of-blois|Blois]] family took Troyes, and Count Hugh was styled count of Champagne by around 1102. [[e:theobald-ii-count-of-champagne|Theobald II]] reunited Blois and Champagne in the 12th century.
county-of-champagne.r: The counts protected the cycle of fairs at [[e:troyes|Troyes]], [[e:provins|Provins]], [[e:lagny-sur-marne|Lagny]] and [[e:bar-sur-aube|Bar-sur-Aube]], which made Champagne the commercial crossroads of 12th- and 13th-century [[e:europe|Europe]]. [[e:henry-i-count-of-champagne|Henry the Liberal]] and [[e:marie-countess-of-champagne|Marie de Champagne]] made Troyes a literary centre, home of [[e:chretien-de-troyes|Chrétien de Troyes]]. Count [[e:theobald-i-of-navarre|Theobald IV]], a trouvère poet, became king of [[e:kingdom-of-navarre|Navarre]] in 1234.
county-of-champagne.e: Countess [[e:joan-i-of-navarre|Joan I]] married [[e:philip-iv-of-france|Philip IV]] in 1284, and when their son Louis X became king in 1314, Champagne passed into the royal domain of the [[s:kingdom-of-france|Kingdom of France]]. The fairs had already declined as sea routes to [[s:county-of-flanders|Flanders]] opened.

chikinchel.t: A Maya province on the northern coast of Yucatán whose salt beds supplied a wide trade, conquered by the Spanish in 1543-44.
chikinchel.o: Chikinchel emerged after the fall of the [[s:league-of-mayapan|League of Mayapan]] around 1441 along the north coast between [[s:ah-kin-chel|Ah Kin Chel]] and [[s:ecab|Ecab]]. Its main town was Chauaca, and its territory included extensive coastal salt flats.
chikinchel.r: Salt from its lagoons, among the most productive in [[e:mesoamerica|Mesoamerica]], was traded by canoe and porters to distant regions, alongside [[e:cotton|cotton]] and fish. The province's towns were governed by local lords, but little is recorded of its political organisation.
chikinchel.e: [[e:francisco-de-montejo-the-nephew|Francisco de Montejo the Nephew]] conquered Chikinchel in 1543-44 and founded the first [[e:valladolid-yucatan|Valladolid]] at Chauaca, moving it to Saci in 1545. The province became part of the [[s:province-of-yucatan|Province of Yucatán]].

county-of-konigsegg.t: Upper Swabian county of the Königsegg family, imperial counts who served the Habsburgs as soldiers and diplomats.
county-of-konigsegg.o: The Königsegg family, Swabian ministerials named after a castle near Saulgau, accumulated lordships around Aulendorf and in the [[e:allgau|Allgäu]]. In 1629 they were raised to imperial counts, and the lands were divided between the lines of Königsegg-Aulendorf and Königsegg-Rothenfels, the latter centred on Immenstadt.
county-of-konigsegg.r: The counties were small Catholic territories held within the [[e:swabian-circle|Swabian Circle]], administered from Aulendorf Castle. Members of the family pursued careers in [[s:county-of-habsburg|Habsburg]] service: Lothar Joseph Dominik von Königsegg-Rothenfels was an imperial field marshal and diplomat, and [[e:maximilian-friedrich-von-konigsegg-rothenfels|Maximilian Friedrich von Königsegg-Rothenfels]] became archbishop-elector of [[s:free-imperial-city-of-cologne|Cologne]] in 1761.
county-of-konigsegg.e: Königsegg-Rothenfels was exchanged with [[e:austria|Austria]] for estates in [[e:hungary|Hungary]] in 1804. Königsegg-Aulendorf was mediatised in 1806 and placed under the [[s:kingdom-of-wurttemberg|Kingdom of Württemberg]], the family keeping its estates and castle.

cantabri.t: The mountain people of northern Spain whose resistance in the Cantabrian Wars of 29 to 19 BCE brought Augustus himself to Iberia.
cantabri.o: The Cantabri lived in the Cantabrian mountains and coast of northern [[e:spain|Spain]], in modern [[e:cantabria|Cantabria]] and parts of [[e:burgos|Burgos]], [[e:palencia|Palencia]] and León, from about the 4th century BCE. They were a Celtic-speaking people organised in clans, living in hillforts.
cantabri.r: Their mountain economy was based on herding goats and [[e:cattle|cattle]], acorn bread and limited farming, and [[e:strabo|Strabo]] noted customs in which daughters inherited and husbands brought dowries. Their warriors raided the plains and served as [[e:mercenary|mercenaries]]; their cavalry manoeuvre, the Cantabrian circle, was adopted by the [[e:roman-empire|Romans]]. They were never united under a single ruler.
cantabri.e: Augustus opened the [[e:cantabrian-wars|Cantabrian Wars]] in 29 BCE, campaigning in person in 26 BCE, but conquest was completed only by [[e:marcus-vipsanius-agrippa|Agrippa]] in 19 BCE, after [[e:deportation|mass deportations]]. The land became part of [[s:hispania-tarraconensis|Hispania Tarraconensis]]; the name later reappeared in the [[s:duchy-of-cantabria|Duchy of Cantabria]].

cayuga-nation.t: One of the five founding nations of the Iroquois Confederacy, whose homeland around Cayuga Lake in New York was lost after the American Revolution.
cayuga-nation.o: The Cayuga lived in the Finger Lakes region of central [[e:new-york|New York]], chiefly around [[e:cayuga-lake|Cayuga Lake]] between the lands of the [[s:onondaga-nation|Onondaga]] and the [[s:seneca-nation|Seneca]]. According to [[s:iroquois-confederacy|Haudenosaunee]] tradition they accepted the [[e:great-law-of-peace|Great Law of Peace]] in the mid-15th century, joining the [[s:mohawk-nation|Mohawk]], [[s:oneida-nation|Oneida]], Onondaga and Seneca in the Iroquois [[s:confederate-states-of-america|Confederacy]].
cayuga-nation.r: The Cayuga sent ten chiefs to the [[e:grand-council-qing|Grand Council]], where they sat with the [[s:oneida-nation|Oneida]] as the younger brothers. Their villages of longhouses stood among orchards and fields of [[e:maize|maize]], beans and squash, which by the 18th century were extensive enough to impress American soldiers. Clan mothers held the right to choose and depose chiefs. In the [[e:beaver-wars|Beaver Wars]] and later colonial conflicts Cayuga warriors fought alongside the other nations.
cayuga-nation.e: Most Cayuga supported [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]] in the [[e:american-revolution|American Revolution]], and the Sullivan expedition burned their towns in 1779. After the war they ceded their lands to [[e:new-york|New York]] and scattered to [[e:buffalo-creek-reservation|Buffalo Creek]], the [[e:grand-river-ontario|Grand River]] in [[e:ontario|Ontario]] and [[e:ohio|Ohio]], from where some reached [[e:oklahoma|Oklahoma]]. A [[e:cayuga-people|Cayuga Nation]] survives in New [[e:york-maine|York]].

choshu-domain.t: The Mori domain at the western tip of Honshu that led the radical movement against the shogunate and supplied many leaders of Meiji Japan.
choshu-domain.o: After the Mori led the losing side at [[e:battle-of-sekigahara|Sekigahara]] in 1600, [[e:tokugawa-ieyasu|Tokugawa Ieyasu]] reduced their lands to the provinces of [[e:suo-province|Suo]] and [[e:nagato-province|Nagato]]. [[e:mori-terumoto|Mori Terumoto's]] son Hidenari ruled from Hagi castle, built from 1604, and the family's grievance against the Tokugawa was said to be kept alive for generations.
choshu-domain.r: [[e:choshu-domain|Choshu]] developed paper, salt and wax and reformed its finances under [[e:murata-seifu|Murata Seifu]] in the 1840s. [[e:yoshida-shoin|Yoshida Shoin's]] private school at Hagi trained young [[e:samurai|samurai]] who embraced the slogan revere the emperor, expel the barbarians. In 1863 Choshu fired on foreign ships at [[e:shimonoseki|Shimonoseki]], moved its seat to [[e:yamaguchi-city|Yamaguchi]] and was bombarded by Western fleets in 1864.
choshu-domain.e: Defeated in [[e:kyoto|Kyoto]] in 1864, [[e:choshu-domain|Choshu]] was rebuilt by radicals around [[e:takasugi-shinsaku|Takasugi Shinsaku's]] mixed militia, beat the [[e:shogun|shogunate]]'s army in 1866 and allied with [[e:satsuma-domain|Satsuma]]. Its men, [[e:kido-takayoshi|Kido Takayoshi]], [[e:ito-hirobumi|Ito Hirobumi]] and [[e:yamagata-aritomo|Yamagata Aritomo]], led [[e:empire-of-japan|Meiji Japan]]; it became [[e:yamaguchi-prefecture|Yamaguchi Prefecture]] in 1871.

county-of-poitou.t: County centred on Poitiers whose counts became dukes of Aquitaine and passed their lands to Eleanor of Aquitaine and the Plantagenets.
county-of-poitou.o: Carolingian counts ruled [[e:poitiers|Poitiers]] from the late 8th century. In the 9th century the [[e:ramnulfids|Ramnulfid]] family made the office hereditary, and in the 10th century [[e:william-iii-duke-of-aquitaine|Count William III]], called Towhead, took the title of Duke of [[s:duchy-of-aquitaine|Aquitaine]], after which the two titles were held together.
county-of-poitou.r: The counts ruled from [[e:poitiers|Poitiers]] over a land of abbeys, castles and salt-producing coasts. [[e:william-ix-duke-of-aquitaine|Duke William IX]], the first known troubadour, wrote poetry in Occitan, and his granddaughter [[e:eleanor-of-aquitaine|Eleanor of Aquitaine]] carried the county first to [[e:louis-vii-of-france|Louis VII]] of the [[s:kingdom-of-france|Kingdom of France]] and then to [[e:henry-ii-of-england|Henry II of England]].
county-of-poitou.e: [[e:philip-ii-of-france|Philip II]] seized Poitou from [[e:john-king-of-england|King John]] from 1204, and [[e:louis-viii-of-france|Louis VIII]] completed the conquest in 1224. It became an [[e:appanage|appanage]] for [[e:alphonse-count-of-poitiers|Alphonse of Poitiers]] and later for [[e:john-duke-of-berry|John, Duke of Berry]], on whose death in 1416 it returned to the crown.

chalcis.t: Euboean city on the Euripus strait that pioneered Greek colonisation in Italy, Sicily and the Chalcidice and spread its alphabet to the Etruscans and Romans.
chalcis.o: Chalcis grew on the narrowest point of the [[e:euripus-strait|Euripus]] channel between [[e:euboea|Euboea]] and mainland [[e:greece|Greece]]. Ionian in dialect, it was an early trading power by the 8th century BCE. Its long rivalry with nearby [[s:eretria|Eretria]] for the Lelantine plain, the [[e:lelantine-war|Lelantine War]], drew in allies from much of Greece.
chalcis.r: With [[s:eretria|Eretria]], Chalcidians founded [[e:pithekoussai|Pithekoussai]] and [[s:cumae|Cumae]] in [[e:italy|Italy]]; alone they founded [[s:naxos|Naxos]], [[s:leontini|Leontini]] and [[s:catana|Catana]] in [[e:sicily|Sicily]], [[s:rhegion|Rhegium]] and many towns in the [[e:chalcidice|Chalcidice]]. Their version of the alphabet passed to the [[e:etruscans|Etruscans]] and [[e:latin|Latins]]. Chalcis was governed by a landowning aristocracy, the hippobotai, or horse-breeders.
chalcis.e: [[s:athens|Athens]] defeated Chalcis in 506 BCE and settled colonists on its land. After revolts against the [[s:delian-league|Delian League]] it became a Macedonian stronghold, one of the 'fetters of [[e:greece|Greece]]', and [[e:aristotle|Aristotle]] died there in 322 BCE. [[e:rome|Rome]] sacked it in 146 BCE for joining the [[s:achaean-league|Achaean League]]'s war.

chhatarpur-state.t: A Bundelkhand state ruled by a Ponwar family, whose lands included the temples of Khajuraho.
chhatarpur-state.o: Chhatarpur town was founded by [[e:chhatrasal|Maharaja Chhatrasal]], but around 1785 [[e:soni-shah|Soni Shah]], a Ponwar who had served the [[e:bundela|Bundelas]], seized it from Chhatrasal's descendants and established his own state. The British confirmed the family's possession by sanad in 1806.
chhatarpur-state.r: Chhatarpur was an 11-gun salute state of the [[e:bundelkhand-agency|Bundelkhand Agency]] ruled by a [[e:maharaja|Maharaja]]. Its territory included the Chandela temples of [[e:khajuraho|Khajuraho]]. Maharaja Vishwanath Singh is portrayed in [[e:j-r-ackerley|J. R. Ackerley's]] memoir [[e:hindoo-holiday|Hindoo Holiday]], written after Ackerley served as his secretary in the 1920s.
chhatarpur-state.e: After independence Chhatarpur was merged into [[s:vindhya-pradesh|Vindhya Pradesh]] in 1948 and joined [[e:madhya-pradesh|Madhya Pradesh]] in 1956; it is now Chhatarpur district.

county-of-lippe.t: A Westphalian lordship around the Teutoburg Forest whose rulers founded Lippstadt and Lemgo and survived as a German state until 1947.
county-of-lippe.o: Bernhard I appears as lord of Lippe in 1123, holding lands on the Lippe river. His grandson [[e:bernhard-ii-of-lippe|Bernhard II]], a companion of [[e:henry-the-lion|Henry the Lion]], founded [[e:lippstadt|Lippstadt]] around 1185 and [[e:lemgo|Lemgo]], before becoming a crusader [[e:bishop|bishop]] in [[s:livonian-confederation|Livonia]]. The lordship developed between the bishoprics of [[e:paderborn|Paderborn]] and [[e:minden|Minden]].
county-of-lippe.r: Lippe was a rural territory of small towns and farms in the hills of the [[e:teutoburg-forest|Teutoburg Forest]]. The lords were raised to counts in 1528 and introduced the [[e:protestant-reformation|Reformation]], the Reformed faith following in 1605. [[e:detmold|Detmold]] became the main residence. Branches split off, including [[s:principality-of-schaumburg-lippe|Schaumburg-Lippe]] in 1647.
county-of-lippe.e: Count [[e:simon-august-count-of-lippe-detmold|Simon August]]'s successor Leopold I was raised to prince in 1789, making the county the [[s:principality-of-lippe|Principality of Lippe]]. It joined the [[s:confederation-of-the-rhine|Confederation of the Rhine]] and the [[s:german-empire|German Empire]], and became a Free State in 1918 before merging into [[e:north-rhine-westphalia|North Rhine-Westphalia]] in 1947.

confederation-of-the-equator.t: A republican revolt in northeastern Brazil against Emperor Pedro I's authoritarian constitution, crushed within months in 1824.
confederation-of-the-equator.o: In 1823 [[e:pedro-i-of-brazil|Pedro I]] dissolved [[e:brazil|Brazil's]] Constituent Assembly, and in 1824 he imposed a constitution that gave the emperor a moderating power. [[s:captaincy-of-pernambuco|Pernambuco]], already the home of the [[s:republic-of-pernambuco|Republic of Pernambuco]], rejected it. On 2 July 1824 its president, [[e:manuel-de-carvalho-pais-de-andrade|Manuel de Carvalho Pais de Andrade]], proclaimed the Confederation of the Equator in [[e:recife|Recife]].
confederation-of-the-equator.r: The confederation invited the northeastern provinces to form a federal republic modelled on the Colombian constitution, and parts of [[e:paraiba|Paraíba]], [[e:rio-grande-do-norte|Rio Grande do Norte]] and [[e:ceara|Ceará]] joined. The friar [[e:frei-caneca|Joaquim do Amor Divino Caneca]], known as Frei Caneca, was its leading ideologue through his newspaper. Divisions over ending the [[e:atlantic-slave-trade|slave trade]] weakened the movement.
confederation-of-the-equator.e: Imperial forces under [[e:francisco-de-lima-e-silva|Francisco de Lima e Silva]] and a fleet under [[e:thomas-cochrane-10th-earl-of-dundonald|Lord Cochrane]] took [[e:recife|Recife]] in September 1824, and resistance ended by November. [[e:frei-caneca|Frei Caneca]] and other leaders were executed in 1825, and [[s:captaincy-of-pernambuco|Pernambuco]] was punished by losing territory.
ru: Manuel de Carvalho Pais de Andrade

cauci.t: People of Ireland's east coast recorded only in Ptolemy's 2nd-century Geography, whose name echoes the Chauci of northern Germany.
cauci.o: The Cauci are known solely from [[e:geography-ptolemy|Ptolemy's Geography]] of about 150, which drew on earlier reports by merchants and sailors. He places them on the east coast of Ireland, between the [[s:eblani|Eblani]] to the north and the [[s:manapii|Manapii]] to the south, roughly in the area of modern [[e:dublin|Dublin]] and [[e:county-wicklow|Wicklow]].
cauci.r: Nothing is recorded of their rulers, settlements or way of life. Their name closely resembles that of the [[s:chauci|Chauci]], a Germanic people of the [[e:north-sea|North Sea]] coast, which has prompted speculation about settlers or traders from the Continent, but most scholars treat the likeness as coincidence or a copying error.
cauci.e: No later source mentions them, and Irish tradition preserves no matching name. Their region later formed part of the [[s:kingdom-of-leinster|Kingdom of Leinster]].

chanka-confederation.t: A confederation of highland peoples whose attack on Cusco, according to Inca tradition, triggered the rise of the Inca Empire.
chanka-confederation.o: The Chanka, or Chanca, occupied the highlands of [[e:apurimac-region|Apurímac]] and [[e:ayacucho|Ayacucho]], west of [[e:cusco|Cusco]], after the collapse of the [[s:wari-empire|Wari Empire]]. From around 1100 they lived in fortified hilltop settlements and formed a loose confederation of chiefdoms based around [[e:andahuaylas|Andahuaylas]].
chanka-confederation.r: Archaeology shows small fortified villages on high ridges rather than a centralised state, suggesting a warlike society of local chiefs who joined forces for war. They herded llamas and alpacas and farmed tubers. Chanka groups claimed descent from the lake of [[e:lake-choclococha|Choclococha]] and worshipped mountain spirits. The Chanka are remembered chiefly through [[e:inca-empire|Inca]] tradition, which portrayed them as fierce rivals.
chanka-confederation.e: According to [[e:inca-empire|Inca]] accounts, around 1438 the Chanka besieged [[e:cusco|Cusco]]. Prince [[e:pachacuti|Cusi Yupanqui]] defeated them, took the name Pachacuti and began the expansion that created the [[s:inca-empire|Inca Empire]]. Historians now treat this story partly as Inca propaganda. The Chanka were absorbed into the empire.

cape-colony.t: Britain's colony at the tip of Africa, whose frontier wars, abolition of slavery and Boer emigration shaped modern South Africa.
cape-colony.o: British forces took the [[s:dutch-cape-colony|Dutch Cape Colony]] in 1795, after the [[e:battle-of-muizenberg|Battle of Muizenberg]], to keep the sea route to [[e:india|India]] out of French hands. It was handed back to the [[s:batavian-republic|Batavian Republic]] in 1803 under the [[e:treaty-of-amiens|Peace of Amiens]], reoccupied after the [[e:battle-of-blaauwberg|Battle of Blaauwberg]] in 1806 and formally ceded by the [[s:kingdom-of-the-netherlands|Netherlands]] in 1814.
cape-colony.r: Governors such as [[e:lord-charles-somerset|Lord Charles Somerset]] at first ruled almost absolutely. English became the official language, the 1820 Settlers arrived in the [[e:eastern-cape|Eastern Cape]] and [[e:slavery|slavery]] ended in 1834, one cause of the [[e:great-trek|Great Trek]] of Dutch-speaking farmers. Frontier wars pushed the border eastwards into [[e:xhosa-people|Xhosa]] land. A parliament elected on a property-based, not racial, franchise came in 1853, and responsible government in 1872. Diamonds at [[e:kimberley|Kimberley]] and politicians like [[e:cecil-rhodes|Cecil Rhodes]] tied the colony to the mining economy of the interior.
cape-colony.e: After the [[e:second-boer-war|Second Boer War]] the Cape joined [[s:natal-colony|Natal]], the [[s:south-african-republic|Transvaal]] and the [[s:orange-river-colony|Orange River Colony]] in the [[s:union-of-south-africa|Union of South Africa]] in 1910, becoming the [[e:cape-province|Cape Province]]. Its qualified non-racial franchise was gradually stripped away by later governments, and [[e:cape-town|Cape Town]] remained the seat of the national parliament.

county-of-nice.t: The Riviera county that chose Savoy over Provence in 1388, gave the Savoyards their outlet to the sea and passed to France in 1860.
county-of-nice.o: During the war of succession that followed Queen [[e:joanna-i-of-naples|Joanna I]]'s death, [[e:nice|Nice]] and its hinterland rejected the Angevin claimant and in 1388, in the act known as the [[e:dedition-of-nice-to-savoy|Dedition]], placed themselves under [[e:amadeus-vii-count-of-savoy|Amadeus VII of Savoy]]. Nice thus left the [[s:county-of-provence|County of Provence]] and became Savoy's outlet to the [[e:mediterranean|Mediterranean]].
county-of-nice.r: The county was governed by Savoyard officials and later a senate at [[e:nice|Nice]], with [[e:villefranche-sur-mer|Villefranche]] as the dukes' naval base. In 1543 a [[e:franco-ottoman-alliance|Franco-Ottoman]] fleet besieged Nice, an event remembered through the heroine Catherine Ségurane. The people spoke [[e:nicard-dialect|Niçard Occitan]], while Italian was the language of administration. [[e:giuseppe-garibaldi|Giuseppe Garibaldi]] was born there in 1807.
county-of-nice.e: [[e:france|France]] occupied [[e:nice|Nice]] from 1792 to 1814. Under the [[e:treaty-of-turin-1860|Treaty of Turin]] of 1860, [[e:victor-emmanuel-ii|Victor Emmanuel II]] ceded it to [[e:napoleon-iii|Napoleon III's]] [[s:second-french-empire|Second French Empire]] in return for help in [[e:italian-unification|Italian unification]], ratified by a plebiscite.

commune-of-pistoia.t: A Tuscan city-republic with some of Italy's oldest communal statutes, where the feud of Black and White Guelphs began before spreading to Florence.
commune-of-pistoia.o: Pistoia, at the foot of the [[e:apennines|Apennines]] between [[s:duchy-of-florence|Florence]] and [[s:republic-of-lucca|Lucca]], had consuls by 1105. Its early statutes, from the 12th century, are among the oldest surviving communal law codes in [[e:italy|Italy]].
commune-of-pistoia.r: The commune was governed by consuls, then a podestà and a captain of the people. Pistoia was known for banking and metalwork and for the [[e:silver|silver]] altar of Saint James in its cathedral. Around 1300 a feud within the Cancellieri family split the [[e:guelphs-and-ghibellines|Guelphs]] into [[e:black-and-white-guelphs|Blacks and Whites]], a quarrel exported to [[s:duchy-of-florence|Florence]] that led to [[e:dante-alighieri|Dante's]] exile. [[e:florence|Florence]] and [[s:republic-of-lucca|Lucca]] besieged and took Pistoia in 1305–1306.
commune-of-pistoia.e: [[e:castruccio-castracani|Castruccio Castracani]] of [[s:republic-of-lucca|Lucca]] seized the city in 1325. [[s:duchy-of-florence|Florence]] later imposed a [[e:protectorate|protectorate]] and gradually tightened control, formally annexing Pistoia in 1401, after which it remained part of the [[s:republic-of-florence|Republic of Florence]].

county-of-ponthieu.t: A small county at the mouth of the Somme where Harold Godwinson was held captive and where the English won at Crécy.
county-of-ponthieu.o: Ponthieu emerged around 980 when Hugh, a castellan of [[e:abbeville|Abbeville]], married a daughter of [[e:hugh-capet|Hugh Capet]] and was recognised as count. Abbeville became the seat of a modest dynasty on the coast between [[s:duchy-of-normandy|Normandy]] and [[s:county-of-flanders|Flanders]].
county-of-ponthieu.r: The counts profited from the Somme estuary and the cloth and [[e:salt-trade|salt trades]]. In 1064 Count [[e:guy-i-count-of-ponthieu|Guy I]] captured the shipwrecked [[e:harold-godwinson|Harold Godwinson]] and handed him to [[e:william-the-conqueror|William of Normandy]], as shown on the [[e:bayeux-tapestry|Bayeux Tapestry]]. In 1279 the county passed through [[e:eleanor-of-castile|Eleanor of Castile]] to her husband [[e:edward-i-of-england|Edward I of England]].
county-of-ponthieu.e: The English kings held Ponthieu as [[e:vassal|vassals]] of [[e:france|France]]; [[e:edward-iii-of-england|Edward III]] fought at [[e:battle-of-crecy|Crécy]], inside the county, in 1346, and the [[e:treaty-of-bretigny|Treaty of Brétigny]] of 1360 gave it to him in full [[e:sovereignty|sovereignty]]. French forces reconquered it in 1369, and it joined the [[s:kingdom-of-france|Kingdom of France]], later passing briefly to [[s:duchy-of-burgundy|Burgundy]].

chauci.t: A Germanic seafaring people of the North Sea coast who lived on raised mounds amid the tides and later raided Roman Gaul by sea.
chauci.o: The Chauci lived along the [[e:north-sea|North Sea]] coast between the Ems and the [[e:elbe|Elbe]]. They enter Roman history in 12 BCE, when [[e:nero-claudius-drusus|Drusus]] led a naval expedition along their coast and made them allies. They supported [[e:rome|Rome]] against [[e:arminius|Arminius]], but kept their independence after Roman forces withdrew from [[e:germany|Germany]].
chauci.r: [[e:pliny-the-elder|Pliny the Elder]], who saw their land, describes people living on artificial mounds ([[e:terp|terpen]] or Wurten) among tidal flats, fishing and burning peat for fuel. [[e:tacitus|Tacitus]] praises them as the noblest of the Germans, preferring justice to plunder. Their coastal position made them skilled seafarers, and they raided the coast of [[e:gaul|Gaul]] in 41 and again in 47, the second time led by [[e:gannascus|Gannascus]], a Cananefate by birth.
chauci.e: Chaucian sea raids continued into the late 2nd century. The name vanishes in the 3rd century, when the coastal peoples between Ems and [[e:elbe|Elbe]] merged with others into the [[s:saxons|Saxons]], who took up the same raiding along the coasts of [[e:gaul|Gaul]] and [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]].

canton-of-bern.t: Aristocratic city-republic that grew into the largest state of the Swiss Confederacy, ruling from the Aare to Lake Geneva until 1798.
canton-of-bern.o: Duke [[e:berthold-v-duke-of-zahringen|Berthold V of Zähringen]] founded Bern on a loop of the [[e:aare|Aare]] in 1191. When the [[e:house-of-zahringen|Zähringen]] line died out in 1218 the town became an imperial city. It expanded by buying and conquering lands, defeated a coalition of nobles at [[e:battle-of-laupen|Laupen]] in 1339, and joined the [[s:old-swiss-confederacy|Old Swiss Confederacy]] in 1353.
canton-of-bern.r: A narrow circle of patrician families ruled through the Great and Small Councils. Bern conquered the [[e:aargau|Aargau]] from the [[e:habsburg-dynasty|Habsburgs]] in 1415 and [[e:vaud|Vaud]] from [[s:duchy-of-savoy|Savoy]] in 1536, creating the largest city-state north of the [[e:alps|Alps]]. It led the Swiss against [[s:duchy-of-burgundy|Burgundy]], with [[e:adrian-von-bubenberg|Adrian von Bubenberg]] holding [[e:battle-of-morat|Murten]] in 1476. Bern adopted the [[e:protestant-reformation|Reformation]] in 1528, and its finances drew on farming and [[e:mercenary|mercenary]] service.
canton-of-bern.e: French troops defeated Bern at [[e:battle-of-grauholz|Grauholz]] in 1798, and it was absorbed into the [[s:helvetic-republic|Helvetic Republic]], losing [[e:vaud|Vaud]] and [[e:aargau|Aargau]]. It re-emerged as a canton in 1803 and became the federal city of [[s:swiss-confederation|Switzerland]] in 1848.

county-of-lantaron.t: A small frontier county of the Kingdom of Asturias and León in the Ebro gorges, between Castile and Álava.
county-of-lantaron.o: Lantarón, near the [[e:ebro-river|Ebro]] gorges on the borders of Álava and [[e:burgos|Burgos]], became a county at the end of the 9th century, when Count Gonzalo Téllez is recorded as ruling Lantarón and Cerezo. It was one of several frontier counties defending the eastern flank of the [[s:kingdom-of-asturias|Kingdom of Asturias]].
county-of-lantaron.r: The counts were military governors for the kings of [[e:asturias|Asturias]] and León, holding castles such as Cerezo against raids from the [[s:banu-qasi|Banu Qasi]] and [[e:cordoba|Córdoba]]. The population of the area was a mix of Basque and Romance speakers living in small villages.
county-of-lantaron.e: In the 930s the county was absorbed by [[e:fernan-gonzalez-of-castile|Fernán González]] into the growing [[s:county-of-castile|County of Castile]], and Lantarón ceased to be a separate county.

county-of-habsburg.t: The modest Swiss county around Habsburg Castle in the Aargau, the ancestral home of the dynasty that came to rule Austria, Spain and much of Europe.
county-of-habsburg.o: Around 1020 to 1030 [[e:radbot-of-klettgau|Radbot]], a count in the [[s:landgraviate-of-klettgau|Klettgau]], and [[e:bishop|Bishop]] [[e:werner-i-of-strasbourg|Werner of Strasbourg]] built [[e:habsburg-castle|Habichtsburg]] ('hawk's castle') on a hill above the [[e:aare|Aare]] near [[e:brugg|Brugg]]. Radbot's descendants took the name [[e:habsburg-dynasty|Habsburg]] and built up lands in the [[e:aargau|Aargau]], [[e:alsace|Alsace]] and around Zurich, founding the family monastery of [[e:muri-abbey|Muri]] in 1027.
county-of-habsburg.r: The counts combined allodial land, advocacies over monasteries and comital rights in the [[e:aargau|Aargau]], [[e:thurgau|Thurgau]] and [[e:zurichgau|Zürichgau]]. They inherited much of the [[s:county-of-kyburg|County of Kyburg]] in 1264. Count [[e:rudolf-i-of-germany|Rudolf IV]] was elected King of the [[e:roman-empire|Romans]] in 1273 as Rudolf I and in 1278 defeated [[e:ottokar-ii-of-bohemia|Ottokar II of Bohemia]], gaining [[e:austria|Austria]] and [[e:styria|Styria]].
county-of-habsburg.e: After 1282 the family centred on [[e:vienna|Vienna]], and the Swiss lands slipped away to the [[s:old-swiss-confederacy|Swiss Confederacy]], notably after defeats at [[e:battle-of-morgarten|Morgarten]] in 1315 and [[e:battle-of-sempach|Sempach]] in 1386. In 1415, when [[e:frederick-iv-duke-of-austria|Duke Frederick IV]] was outlawed, Bern conquered the [[e:aargau|Aargau]], including [[e:habsburg-castle|Habsburg Castle]] itself.

collique.t: A lordship of the lower Chillón valley that controlled water and farmland north of modern Lima before falling to the Incas.
collique.o: Collique, or the Señorío de Colli, was one of several lordships that emerged on the central coast of [[e:peru|Peru]] after the decline of Wari influence around 1100. It controlled the lower and middle [[e:chillon-river|Chillón]] valley, with a fortified centre at Collique in the modern district of [[e:comas-district|Comas]].
collique.r: The lords of Collique controlled key irrigation canals in the [[e:chillon-river|Chillón]] valley and fortified their centre with walls. Their territory bordered [[s:ychsma|Ychsma]] to the south. The economy relied on irrigation farming of [[e:maize|maize]], [[e:cotton|cotton]] and fruits and on exchange with highland groups such as the Canta, with whom they fought for control of coca fields at Quivi.
collique.e: Around 1470 the [[e:inca-empire|Incas]] conquered Collique after a siege, and its lord was reportedly killed. The valley was then governed through Inca administration and later became part of Spanish [[e:lima|Lima]].

county-of-novellara.t: A tiny Emilian county ruled for over three centuries by a cadet branch of the Gonzaga family.
county-of-novellara.o: After losing the lordship of [[e:reggio-emilia|Reggio]] in 1371, [[e:feltrino-gonzaga|Feltrino Gonzaga]], of the family that ruled [[s:duchy-of-mantua|Mantua]], kept the small territory of Novellara and [[e:bagnolo-in-piano|Bagnolo]] in the plain north of Reggio. His descendants ruled it as an imperial fief, later recognised as a county.
county-of-novellara.r: The counts of Novellara governed a few villages and a fortified town from their castle, the Rocca. They lived from farming the rich plain and from service at larger courts, and maintained a modest [[e:renaissance|Renaissance]] court; the painter [[e:lelio-orsi|Lelio Orsi]] worked for them in the 16th century. The state survived by careful loyalty to the emperors and good relations with the [[e:house-of-este|Este]] and [[e:house-of-gonzaga|Gonzaga]].
county-of-novellara.e: The line of [[e:house-of-gonzaga|Gonzaga]]-Novellara died out in 1728. After disputes over the succession, the emperor granted the county to [[e:rinaldo-d-este-duke-of-modena|Rinaldo d'Este]] in 1737, and it became part of the [[s:duchy-of-modena-and-reggio|Duchy of Modena and Reggio]].

colony-of-nova-scotia.t: The British colony formed from French Acadia, scene of the Acadian expulsion, and the first colony in the British Empire to win responsible government.
colony-of-nova-scotia.o: The [[e:treaty-of-utrecht|Treaty of Utrecht]] of 1713 ceded peninsular [[s:acadia|Acadia]] to [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]], which renamed it [[e:nova-scotia|Nova Scotia]], reviving an earlier Scottish claim. For decades a small garrison at [[e:annapolis-royal|Annapolis Royal]] ruled a population of French-speaking [[e:acadians|Acadians]] and [[e:mikmaq|Mi'kmaq]]. In 1749 [[e:edward-cornwallis|Edward Cornwallis]] founded [[e:halifax-nova-scotia|Halifax]] as a naval base and new capital.
colony-of-nova-scotia.r: Doubting the [[e:acadians|Acadians]]' loyalty, governor [[e:charles-lawrence|Charles Lawrence]] began their [[e:deportation|deportation]] in 1755, and [[e:new-england|New England]] Planters took their farms. [[e:nova-scotia|Nova Scotia's]] assembly, first elected in 1758, was the oldest in what is now [[s:province-of-canada|Canada]]. After 1783 tens of thousands of Loyalists arrived, including [[e:black-loyalists|Black Loyalists]] at [[e:birchtown|Birchtown]], and [[s:colony-of-new-brunswick|New Brunswick]] was split off in 1784. Fishing, shipbuilding and [[e:timber|timber]] drove the economy, and in 1848 [[e:joseph-howe|Joseph Howe's]] reformers won responsible government.
colony-of-nova-scotia.e: In 1867 [[e:nova-scotia|Nova Scotia]] joined [[s:colony-of-new-brunswick|New Brunswick]] and the [[s:province-of-canada|Province of Canada]] to form the [[s:canada|Dominion of Canada]], of which it remains a province. Union was unpopular at first, and [[e:joseph-howe|Howe]] led a campaign for repeal before accepting better financial terms in 1869.

canton-of-basel.t: The Rhine-knee city of the Council of Basel and the humanist printers, which joined the Swiss Confederacy in 1501.
canton-of-basel.o: Basel was ruled by the [[s:prince-bishopric-of-basel|Prince-Bishopric of Basel]], but from the late 13th century the city council steadily acquired the [[e:bishop|bishop]]'s rights, buying [[e:kleinbasel|Kleinbasel]] across the [[e:rhine|Rhine]] in 1392, and by the end of the 14th century it was in effect a free city of the empire. It allied with the Confederates and in 1501 joined them as the eleventh canton.
canton-of-basel.r: A council in which the [[e:guild|guilds]] dominated governed the city and its rural territory. The [[e:council-of-basel|Council of Basel]] met there from 1431 to 1449, and the university, the oldest in [[s:swiss-confederation|Switzerland]], was founded in 1460. Printers such as [[e:johann-froben|Johann Froben]] made Basel a centre of humanism, and [[e:erasmus|Erasmus]] lived there. The city adopted the Reformed faith in 1529, and [[e:silk|silk]] ribbons, trade and banking later enriched it.
canton-of-basel.e: Its [[e:guild|guild]] oligarchy gave way in 1798 to the [[s:helvetic-republic|Helvetic Republic]]. Restored in 1803, the canton split in 1833 after civil conflict into [[e:basel-stadt|Basel-Stadt]] and [[e:basel-landschaft|Basel-Landschaft]], which remain separate half-cantons.

cisrhenian-republic.t: Brief project for a Rhineland sister republic of France, proclaimed in 1797 but abandoned within months.
cisrhenian-republic.o: After French armies occupied the left bank of the [[e:rhine|Rhine]], local supporters of the Revolution in towns such as [[e:bonn|Bonn]], [[e:koblenz|Koblenz]], [[s:free-imperial-city-of-cologne|Cologne]] and [[s:free-imperial-city-of-aachen|Aachen]] proclaimed a Cisrhenian Republic in September 1797, with the encouragement of General [[e:lazare-hoche|Lazare Hoche]], who favoured a separate state allied to [[e:france|France]].
cisrhenian-republic.r: The republic never had a functioning government or capital; it consisted of declarations, liberty trees and a movement led by young intellectuals, among them [[e:joseph-gorres|Joseph Görres]] in [[e:koblenz|Koblenz]]. Its supporters wanted independence from the princes and from direct French rule, but most of the population showed little support.
cisrhenian-republic.e: [[e:lazare-hoche|Hoche]] died in September 1797, and the [[e:treaty-of-campo-formio|Treaty of Campo Formio]] the following month opened the way for French annexation. The left bank was organised into French [[e:departement|departments]] from 1798, ending the project; [[e:joseph-gorres|Görres]] later became a leading German Catholic publicist.

cortona.t: Etruscan hill city above the Val di Chiana, known for its monumental tumuli and the Tabula Cortonensis, one of the longest Etruscan texts.
cortona.o: [[s:lordship-of-cortona|Cortona]], Etruscan Curtun, sits high on a spur of Monte Sant'Egidio overlooking the [[e:val-di-chiana|Val di Chiana]] and [[e:lake-trasimeno|Lake Trasimeno]]. Greek and Roman writers credited it with legendary origins, linking it to [[e:dardanus|Dardanus]] or to Pelasgian settlers. Archaeologically it developed into a city in the 7th and 6th centuries BCE, when its first walls were built.
cortona.r: Cortona's elite built the great 'Melone' tumuli at Sodo below the town, one with a monumental stepped altar decorated with sphinxes devouring warriors. Its bronzes include a famous hanging lamp with sixteen burners. The [[e:tabula-cortonensis|Tabula Cortonensis]], a bronze tablet of about 200 BCE found in 1992, records a land transaction among named families and is a key source for the Etruscan language and law.
cortona.e: [[e:livy|Livy]] names [[s:lordship-of-cortona|Cortona]] with [[s:perusia|Perusia]] and [[s:arretium|Arretium]] among the cities that made a thirty-year truce with [[e:rome|Rome]] in 310 BCE. It gradually became a Roman ally and later a municipium, overshadowed by Arretium. The Etruscan walls still underlie the medieval town.

chenani-state.t: A small Rajput hill state north of Jammu that survived as an autonomous fief within the Dogra kingdom of Jammu and Kashmir.
chenani-state.o: Chenani's rulers claimed [[e:rajputs|Rajput]] descent, and tradition dates the state to around 1100. It lay on the Tawi river on the route from [[e:jammu|Jammu]] towards [[e:kashmir|Kashmir]].
chenani-state.r: Few details of Chenani's early history are recorded. In the 19th century its Rajas became tributaries of [[e:gulab-singh|Gulab Singh of Jammu]] and kept internal autonomy as a [[e:jagir|jagir]] within [[s:jammu-and-kashmir-princely-state|Jammu and Kashmir (princely state)]].
chenani-state.e: Its special status lapsed after [[e:indian-independence|Indian independence]], when it was absorbed into [[s:jammu-and-kashmir-princely-state|Jammu and Kashmir]]. Chenani is now a town in [[e:udhampur|Udhampur]] district, known for the [[e:chenani-nashri-tunnel|Chenani-Nashri]] road tunnel.

cayman-islands.t: Three low islands south of Cuba, long a sleepy dependency of Jamaica, now a British Overseas Territory and one of the world's largest offshore financial centres.
cayman-islands.o: [[e:christopher-columbus|Columbus]] sighted the islands in 1503, and they were visited by turtle hunters and [[e:piracy|pirates]] for over a century. [[e:spain|Spain]] ceded them, with [[s:jamaica|Jamaica]], to [[e:england|England]] in the [[e:treaty-of-madrid-1670|Treaty of Madrid]] in 1670. Permanent settlement on [[e:grand-cayman|Grand Cayman]] began only around the 1730s, with settlers from [[e:jamaica|Jamaica]] and the enslaved people they brought.
cayman-islands.r: For most of their history the islands were a dependency of [[s:jamaica|Jamaica]], managed locally by a justice of the peace and, from 1831, an elected assembly of vestrymen. Islanders lived by turtling, shipbuilding, rope making and seafaring, and many men worked abroad as sailors. The Wreck of the Ten Sail in 1794 is a celebrated local tradition. Presbyterian missions shaped religious life.
cayman-islands.e: When [[s:jamaica|Jamaica]] became independent in 1962, the Caymans chose to remain British and became a separate crown colony. Tax-neutral finance laws from the 1960s, tourism and diving transformed the economy, and the islands are today a prosperous [[e:british-overseas-territories|British Overseas Territory]] governed from [[e:george-town-cayman-islands|George Town]].

czechoslovakia.t: Central European state of Czechs and Slovaks that went from democracy to Nazi occupation and communism before splitting peacefully in 1993.
czechoslovakia.o: As [[e:austro-hungarian-empire|Austria-Hungary]] collapsed, Czech leaders proclaimed independence in [[e:prague|Prague]] on 28 October 1918, and Slovak leaders joined two days later. [[e:tomas-garrigue-masaryk|Tomáš Masaryk]], who had campaigned for the state abroad, became president. The new republic included [[s:kingdom-of-bohemia|Bohemia]], [[s:margraviate-of-moravia|Moravia]], part of [[s:duchy-of-silesia|Silesia]], [[e:slovakia|Slovakia]] and [[s:carpatho-ukraine|Subcarpathian Ruthenia]].
czechoslovakia.r: The [[s:french-first-republic|First Republic]] was a parliamentary democracy and industrial power, but had large German and Hungarian minorities. The [[e:munich-agreement|Munich Agreement]] of 1938 forced it to cede the [[e:sudetenland|Sudetenland]], and in 1939 [[e:germany|Germany]] occupied the rest. Restored in 1945, it expelled most Germans, and the communists seized power in 1948. The [[e:prague-spring|Prague Spring]] reforms of [[e:alexander-dubcek|Alexander Dubček]] were crushed by a [[e:warsaw-pact-invasion-of-czechoslovakia|Warsaw Pact invasion]] in 1968.
czechoslovakia.e: The [[e:velvet-revolution|Velvet Revolution]] of 1989 ended communist rule and made [[e:vaclav-havel|Václav Havel]] president. Differences between Czech and Slovak politicians led to a peaceful dissolution on 31 December 1992 into the [[e:czech-republic|Czech Republic]] and [[e:slovakia|Slovakia]].

county-of-barby.t: A small county on the Elbe near Magdeburg, ruled by the counts of Barby until their line died out in 1659.
county-of-barby.o: The lords of Barby held lands on the [[e:elbe|Elbe]] near the mouth of the [[e:saale|Saale]], between [[e:magdeburg|Magdeburg]] and [[s:principality-of-anhalt|Anhalt]], from the 12th century. In 1497 [[e:maximilian-i-holy-roman-emperor|Emperor Maximilian I]] raised them to imperial counts, though much of their territory was held in fief from the [[s:archbishopric-of-magdeburg|Archbishopric of Magdeburg]] and from [[e:saxony|Saxony]].
county-of-barby.r: The counts ruled a few small towns and villages, including Barby, Rosenburg and Mühlingen, from their castle at Barby. They introduced the [[e:protestant-reformation|Lutheran Reformation]] in the 1540s. The territory lived from farming in the fertile Elbe-[[e:saale|Saale]] plain and from river trade.
county-of-barby.e: When the last count, August Ludwig, died in 1659, the county was divided among his overlords: most of it went to the [[e:saxons|Saxon]] dukes of the [[s:duchy-of-saxe-weissenfels|Duchy of Saxe-Weissenfels]], and some lands to [[s:principality-of-anhalt-zerbst|Anhalt-Zerbst]]. Barby became part of [[e:kingdom-of-prussia|Prussia]] in 1815.

county-of-katzenelnbogen.t: A Rhineland county rich from tolls on the Rhine and the earliest Riesling vineyards, whose inheritance made the landgraves of Hesse a major power.
county-of-katzenelnbogen.o: The counts of Katzenelnbogen first appear around 1095 as advocates of the [[e:bishopric-of-worms|Bishopric of Worms]] and the abbey of [[e:lorsch|Lorsch]]. They built Katzenelnbogen castle in the [[e:taunus|Taunus]] and expanded into the [[e:rhine|Rhine]] valley, acquiring lands on both banks and the area of [[e:darmstadt|Darmstadt]].
county-of-katzenelnbogen.r: The counts became wealthy from [[e:rhine|Rhine]] tolls collected at castles such as [[e:rheinfels-castle|Rheinfels]] above [[e:sankt-goar|Sankt Goar]], built in 1245, and [[e:burg-katz|Burg Katz]]. Count [[e:john-iv-count-of-katzenelnbogen|Johann IV]] is linked with the first recorded mention of [[e:riesling|Riesling]] grapes, in 1435. Their lands stretched from the Rhine into the upper Rhine plain.
county-of-katzenelnbogen.e: When [[e:philip-i-count-of-katzenelnbogen|Philipp the Elder]], the last count, died in 1479, his daughter's husband, Landgrave [[e:henry-iii-landgrave-of-hesse|Henry III of Hesse]], inherited the county. Its rich tolls helped make [[e:hesse|Hesse]] a significant power; the upper county around [[e:darmstadt|Darmstadt]] later became the core of [[s:grand-duchy-of-hesse|Hesse-Darmstadt]].

cornavii-caithness.t: People of Caithness at the northern tip of mainland Britain, recorded by Ptolemy and named after their headlands.
cornavii-caithness.o: [[e:geography-ptolemy|Ptolemy's Geography]] of about 150 places the Cornavii in the far north-east of mainland [[e:scotland|Scotland]], in modern [[e:caithness|Caithness]]. Their name, from a Celtic word for horn, probably means 'people of the promontory', referring to headlands such as [[e:duncansby-head|Duncansby Head]] or [[e:dunnet-head|Dunnet Head]]; the same name was borne by the [[s:cornovii|Cornovii]] of the [[e:midlands|English Midlands]] and by the people of [[e:cornwall|Cornwall]].
cornavii-caithness.r: Nothing is recorded of their rulers. [[e:caithness|Caithness]] has one of the densest concentrations of brochs in [[e:scotland|Scotland]], tall drystone towers built in the last centuries BCE, which point to a society of powerful local families controlling fertile farmland and coastal resources.
cornavii-caithness.e: The Cornavii do not appear after Ptolemy. [[e:caithness|Caithness]] later formed part of the lands of the northern [[e:picts|Picts]] before falling under Norse rule as part of the earldom of [[e:orkney|Orkney]] in the 9th and 10th centuries.

colony-of-grenada.t: British colony on Grenada, the Isle of Spice, shaken by Fédon's rebellion and capital of the Windward Islands, independent since 1974.
colony-of-grenada.o: [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]] captured [[s:french-grenada|French Grenada]] in 1762 and received it by the [[e:treaty-of-paris-1763|Treaty of Paris]] in 1763. Many French planters stayed, and British attempts to restrict Catholic rights caused lasting tension. [[e:france|France]] retook the island in 1779 but returned it in 1783. Under British rule [[e:st-georges-grenada|Fort Royal]] became St George's.
colony-of-grenada.r: [[e:sugar-plantation|Sugar]] estates worked by enslaved Africans dominated until emancipation. In 1795 to 1796 [[e:julien-fedon|Julien Fédon]], a free coloured planter inspired by revolutionary [[e:france|France]], led a rebellion that held most of the island and killed the lieutenant governor. In the 19th century [[e:nutmeg|nutmeg]] and [[e:cacao|cacao]] replaced sugar, giving [[s:grenada|Grenada]] its spice reputation, and from 1885 [[e:st-georges-grenada|St George's]] housed the governor of the [[s:british-windward-islands|British Windward Islands]]. [[e:crown-colony|Crown colony]] rule replaced the assembly in 1877.
colony-of-grenada.e: [[e:eric-gairy|Eric Gairy's]] labour movement of 1951 brought mass politics. [[s:grenada|Grenada]] joined the [[s:west-indies-federation|West Indies Federation]], became an [[e:west-indies-associated-states|Associated State]] in 1967 and, despite strikes and protests against Gairy, gained independence as Grenada on 7 February 1974.

charkhari-state.t: A Bundela Rajput state of Bundelkhand known for its lakes and hill fort, whose Raja stood by the British during the revolt of 1857.
charkhari-state.o: Charkhari was founded around 1765 by [[e:khuman-singh-of-charkhari|Khuman Singh]], a descendant of [[e:chhatrasal|Maharaja Chhatrasal]] through the [[s:jaitpur-state|Jaitpur]] branch, who received a share of the family lands. The British confirmed the state by sanad in 1804.
charkhari-state.r: Charkhari was an 11-gun salute state of the [[e:bundelkhand-agency|Bundelkhand Agency]] ruled by a [[e:maharaja|Maharaja]] from the hill fort of Mangalgarh, ringed by artificial lakes. In 1857 Raja [[e:ratan-singh-of-charkhari|Ratan Singh]] remained loyal to the British and was besieged by the rebel leader [[e:tatya-tope|Tantia Tope]], for which he was later rewarded.
charkhari-state.e: After independence Charkhari joined [[s:vindhya-pradesh|Vindhya Pradesh]] and was absorbed by 1950; the town is now in [[e:mahoba|Mahoba]] district of [[e:uttar-pradesh|Uttar Pradesh]].
