cananefates.t: Germanic people of the Dutch coast near The Hague, kin of the Batavi, who joined the Batavian revolt of 69 CE.
cananefates.o: [[e:tacitus|Tacitus]] says the Cananefates were related to the [[s:batavi|Batavi]] and equal to them in origin, language and courage, though fewer in number. They lived in the coastal dunes and peat lands of the western [[s:kingdom-of-the-netherlands|Netherlands]], between the [[e:rhine|Rhine]] mouth and the sea.
cananefates.r: Like the [[s:batavi|Batavi]] they supplied soldiers to [[e:rome|Rome]], including cavalry units. [[e:tacitus|Tacitus]] describes how in 69 CE they chose [[e:brinno|Brinno]] as their leader by raising him on a shield, the earliest recorded example of this Germanic custom.
cananefates.e: Under [[e:brinno|Brinno]] they attacked Roman forts on the coast at the start of the revolt of [[e:julius-civilis|Julius Civilis]]. After its defeat they returned to Roman rule, and their chief town became [[e:forum-hadriani|Forum Hadriani]] (Voorburg), granted market rights under Hadrian. Frankish raids in the 3rd century ended Roman life there.

chiefdom-of-nicoya.t: The leading chiefdom of the Chorotega people on the Nicoya peninsula of Costa Rica, met by Spanish explorers in 1522-23.
chiefdom-of-nicoya.o: The [[e:chorotega|Chorotega]], speakers of an [[e:oto-manguean-languages|Oto-Manguean]] language, are thought to have migrated from central [[s:mexico|Mexico]] to the Pacific coast of [[e:central-america|Central America]] around 800. They settled the Nicoya peninsula and the [[e:gulf-of-nicoya|Gulf of Nicoya]] area, where several chiefdoms emerged.
chiefdom-of-nicoya.r: Nicoya was ruled by a chief who bore the same name as his territory. Society was divided into nobles, commoners and slaves, and councils of elders advised the chief. The [[e:chorotega|Chorotega]] produced fine polychrome pottery and carved jade and stone metates, grew [[e:maize|maize]], [[e:cacao|cacao]] and [[e:cotton|cotton]], and used a ritual calendar of Mesoamerican type. They also made purple dye from shellfish.
chiefdom-of-nicoya.e: The Spanish expedition of [[e:gil-gonzalez-davila|Gil González Dávila]] reached Nicoya in 1522-23, and the chief accepted baptism. Colonial rule, slaving and disease devastated the population. Nicoya became an [[e:encomienda|encomienda]] and later part of [[s:republic-of-costa-rica|Costa Rica]].

commune-of-parma.t: An Emilian city-republic that defeated Emperor Frederick II's siege in 1248 and commissioned Benedetto Antelami's great baptistery.
commune-of-parma.o: Parma's citizens gradually took power from their [[e:bishop|bishops]], who had been counts of the city, and by 1149 consuls governed the commune. It controlled the [[e:via-aemilia|Via Emilia]] and a route across the [[e:apennines|Apennines]] to [[s:grand-duchy-of-tuscany|Tuscany]].
commune-of-parma.r: Governed by consuls, then a podestà and popular councils, [[s:duchy-of-parma-and-piacenza|Parma]] joined the [[s:lombard-league|Lombard League]]. In 1196 [[e:benedetto-antelami|Benedetto Antelami]] began its octagonal baptistery. Ghibelline at first, it turned Guelph in 1247 and withstood Frederick II's siege, destroying his camp-city of [[s:colony-of-victoria|Victoria]] in February 1248. The Rossi, [[s:principality-of-correggio|Correggio]] and Sanvitale families competed for power; [[e:giberto-da-correggio|Giberto da Correggio]] became lord in 1303.
commune-of-parma.e: After a succession of lords, [[e:obizzo-iii-deste|Obizzo III d'Este]] sold the city to [[e:luchino-visconti-lord-of-milan|Luchino Visconti]] in 1346, and it joined the [[s:lordship-of-milan|Lordship of Milan]]. In 1545 it became the capital of the [[s:duchy-of-parma-and-piacenza|Duchy of Parma and Piacenza]].

chutu-dynasty.t: A successor dynasty of the Satavahanas in the western Deccan, ruling from Banavasi before the Kadambas.
chutu-dynasty.o: As the [[s:satavahana-dynasty|Satavahana dynasty]] declined in the 2nd and 3rd centuries, local rulers called Chutus took over the region around [[e:banavasi|Banavasi]] in northern [[e:karnataka|Karnataka]] and parts of the coast. They styled themselves Satakarni like their former overlords and may have been Satavahana feudatories or relatives.
chutu-dynasty.r: The dynasty is known from coins bearing the name Chutukadananda and from a few [[e:prakrit|Prakrit]] inscriptions at [[e:banavasi|Banavasi]] and Kanheri recording gifts to Buddhist monasteries, including one by the king Haritiputra Vishnukada Chutukulananda Satakarni. Nothing more is known of their government.
chutu-dynasty.e: The Chutus were followed by the [[s:pallava-dynasty|Pallava dynasty]], which briefly controlled the area, and then by the [[s:kadamba-dynasty|Kadamba dynasty]] founded by [[e:mayurasharma|Mayurasharma]] in the mid-4th century, which made [[e:banavasi|Banavasi]] its capital.

commune-of-milan.t: The leading city-republic of Lombardy, razed by Frederick Barbarossa in 1162 and then at the head of the league that defeated him at Legnano.
commune-of-milan.o: [[e:milan|Milan's]] archbishops had long dominated the city, but by 1097 consuls drawn from nobles and citizens were governing it. The young commune extended its power over the surrounding countryside and over neighbours such as [[e:lodi-dynasty|Lodi]] and Como, whose complaints drew [[e:frederick-barbarossa|Emperor Frederick Barbarossa]] into [[e:italy|Italy]].
commune-of-milan.r: Government passed from consuls to a podestà, usually an outsider, alongside councils and the popular credenza di Sant'Ambrogio. [[s:duchy-of-milan|Milan]] was a manufacturing centre for wool cloth and arms, with its own Ambrosian liturgy. [[e:frederick-barbarossa|Barbarossa]] destroyed the city in 1162, but it was rebuilt, joined the [[s:lombard-league|Lombard League]] and helped defeat the emperor at [[e:battle-of-legnano|Legnano]] in 1176, winning self-government at the [[e:peace-of-constance|Peace of Constance]] in 1183.
commune-of-milan.e: Rivalry between nobles and the popular party opened the way to strongmen. In 1259 [[e:martino-della-torre|Martino della Torre]] was made lord of the people, and the commune gave way to the [[s:lordship-of-milan|Lordship of Milan]], later dominated by the Visconti.

county-of-manderscheid-blankenheim.t: An Eifel county of the counts of Manderscheid, centred on Blankenheim castle at the source of the Ahr.
county-of-manderscheid-blankenheim.o: The lords of Manderscheid in the [[e:eifel|Eifel]] acquired Blankenheim and its castle by marriage in the 15th century and were raised to counts in 1457. In 1488 their lands were divided, creating the Manderscheid-Blankenheim line alongside other branches such as Manderscheid-Schleiden.
county-of-manderscheid-blankenheim.r: The counts ruled a small, wooded territory in the [[e:eifel|Eifel]] with iron mining and smelting, and belonged to the [[e:lower-rhenish-westphalian-circle|Lower Rhenish-Westphalian Circle]]. They remained Catholic, and [[e:johann-of-manderscheid-blankenheim|Johann of Manderscheid-Blankenheim]] served as [[e:bishop|bishop]] of [[s:free-imperial-city-of-strasbourg|Strasbourg]] from 1569. The later counts gathered a notable library and collection of Roman antiquities at Blankenheim.
county-of-manderscheid-blankenheim.e: The male line died out in 1780, and the lands passed by marriage to the [[e:house-of-sternberg|Sternberg]] family of [[s:kingdom-of-bohemia|Bohemia]]. French occupation of the left bank of the [[e:rhine|Rhine]] in 1794 ended the county, which later became part of [[e:kingdom-of-prussia|Prussia]].

chetumal.t: A Maya province on Chetumal Bay, rich in cacao, where the Spanish castaway Gonzalo Guerrero became a Maya war leader against his countrymen.
chetumal.o: Chetumal (Chactemal) emerged as a powerful province after the fall of the [[s:league-of-mayapan|League of Mayapan]] around 1441, on the bay shared today by [[s:mexico|Mexico]] and [[s:belize|Belize]]. Its fertile lands produced [[e:cacao|cacao]] and honey, and its towns were linked by trade to [[s:republic-of-honduras|Honduras]] and the north.
chetumal.r: Chetumal was ruled by the lord [[e:nachan-kaan|Nachan Kaan]] at the time of the conquest. [[e:gonzalo-guerrero|Gonzalo Guerrero]], shipwrecked in 1511, married his daughter, adopted Maya customs and led its warriors against the Spanish; he died in [[s:republic-of-honduras|Honduras]] around 1536. The province defeated [[e:alonso-davila|Alonso Dávila's]] attempt to found a settlement in 1531.
chetumal.e: In 1544 [[e:gaspar-pacheco|Gaspar]] and [[e:melchor-pacheco|Melchor Pacheco]] conquered Chetumal brutally, and it was absorbed into the [[s:province-of-yucatan|Province of Yucatán]]. The modern city of Chetumal, capital of [[e:quintana-roo|Quintana Roo]], was founded in 1898.

carolingian-kingdom-of-italy.t: The former Lombard kingdom under Charlemagne's dynasty, which made Italy part of the Frankish world and linked its crown to the imperial title.
carolingian-kingdom-of-italy.o: [[e:charlemagne|Charlemagne]] conquered the [[s:kingdom-of-the-lombards|Lombard Kingdom]] in 774 and took the title [[e:king-of-the-lombards|King of the Lombards]]. In 781 Pope Hadrian I crowned his young son [[e:pepin-of-italy|Pepin]] King of [[e:italy|Italy]], creating a subordinate kingdom with its capital at [[s:commune-of-pavia|Pavia]], covering northern and central Italy apart from [[e:venice|Venice]] and the papal lands.
carolingian-kingdom-of-italy.r: The [[e:carolingian-empire|Carolingians]] kept [[e:kingdom-of-the-lombards|Lombard]] law and the palace at [[s:commune-of-pavia|Pavia]] but installed Frankish counts and [[e:bishop|bishops]], issued [[e:capitulary|capitularies]] for [[e:italy|Italy]] and supported monasteries such as [[e:bobbio-abbey|Bobbio]] and [[e:nonantola-abbey|Nonantola]]. [[e:pepin-of-italy|Pepin]]'s son Bernard rebelled in 817 and was blinded in 818, dying of his injuries. [[e:lothair-i|Lothair I]] and his son [[e:louis-ii-of-italy|Louis II]] ruled Italy as emperors; Louis II spent decades fighting Arab raiders in the south and recovered [[s:principality-of-bari|Bari]] in 871.
carolingian-kingdom-of-italy.e: After [[e:louis-ii-of-italy|Louis II]] died in 875, the crown passed among [[e:charles-the-bald|Charles the Bald]], [[e:carloman-of-bavaria|Carloman]] and [[e:charles-the-fat|Charles the Fat]], who was deposed in 887 and died in 888. Italian nobles then chose their own kings, beginning with [[e:berengar-i-of-italy|Berengar of Friuli]], and the [[s:kingdom-of-italy|Kingdom of Italy]] continued under them.

colony-of-british-columbia-1858-1866.t: A mainland British colony created in haste in 1858 to control the tens of thousands of miners drawn by the Fraser River gold rush.
colony-of-british-columbia-1858-1866.o: When gold was found on the [[e:fraser-river|Fraser River]] in 1858, some 30,000 miners, mostly from [[e:california|California]], poured into territory held only by [[e:hudsons-bay-company|Hudson's Bay Company]] posts. To assert British [[e:sovereignty|sovereignty]], Parliament created the colony of [[e:british-columbia|British Columbia]] in August 1858. [[e:james-douglas-governor|James Douglas]], governor of the [[s:colony-of-vancouver-island|Colony of Vancouver Island]], also became its governor after cutting his ties with the Company.
colony-of-british-columbia-1858-1866.r: Royal Engineers under [[e:richard-clement-moody|Richard Clement Moody]] surveyed the land and founded [[e:new-westminster|New Westminster]] as capital in 1859. Judge [[e:matthew-baillie-begbie|Matthew Baillie Begbie]] enforced law in the mining camps. The [[e:cariboo|Cariboo]] gold rush from 1862 led to the building of the [[e:cariboo-wagon-road|Cariboo Wagon Road]]. Miners' violence against [[e:nlakapamux|Nlaka'pamux]] villages in the [[e:fraser-canyon-war|Fraser Canyon War]] of 1858 and the [[e:tsilhqotin-war|Tsilhqot'in War]] of 1864 marked relations with [[e:first-nations-in-canada|First Nations]].
colony-of-british-columbia-1858-1866.e: [[e:james-douglas-governor|Douglas]] retired in 1864 and was succeeded by [[e:frederick-seymour|Frederick Seymour]]. Costly road building left heavy debts as gold output fell, and in 1866 [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]] united the mainland with [[s:colony-of-vancouver-island|Vancouver Island]] as the [[s:colony-of-british-columbia-1866-1871|Colony of British Columbia]].

commune-of-kotor.t: Self-governing Adriatic port of Kotor between the fall of Serbian rule and Venetian annexation, trading under shifting Hungarian and Bosnian protection.
commune-of-kotor.o: Kotor, a Romance-speaking port at the head of its deep bay, had long enjoyed self-government under the [[e:nemanjic-dynasty|Nemanjić]] rulers of [[s:serbia|Serbia]]. As the [[s:serbian-empire|Serbian Empire]] disintegrated, the city accepted the protection of [[e:louis-i-of-hungary|Louis I of Hungary]] in 1371 and ran its own affairs.
commune-of-kotor.r: A council of nobles governed the commune under its own statutes, with a Catholic [[e:bishop|bishop]] and the [[e:cathedral-of-saint-tryphon|cathedral of Saint Tryphon]] at its centre. Kotor lived from sea trade and from carrying goods to and from the Balkan interior, rivalling [[s:republic-of-ragusa|Ragusa]]. Its protectors changed often: [[e:hungary|Hungary]], [[e:tvrtko-i-of-bosnia|Tvrtko]] I of the [[s:kingdom-of-bosnia|Kingdom of Bosnia]] from 1385, and pressure from [[s:zeta-under-the-balsici|Zeta under the Balšići]].
commune-of-kotor.e: Facing threats from the [[e:balsic-noble-family|Balšići]] and the [[e:ottoman-empire|Ottomans]], Kotor placed itself under [[e:venice|Venice]] in 1420. It remained Venetian until 1797, and its walls and old town are now a [[e:unesco-world-heritage-site|World Heritage Site]] in [[s:montenegro|Montenegro]].

croton.t: Achaean Greek city of southern Italy famed for its athletes, its doctors and Pythagoras, which destroyed Sybaris in 510 BCE.
croton.o: Achaean colonists led by [[e:myscellus-of-rhypes|Myscellus of Rhypes]] founded Croton around 710 BCE on the Ionian coast of [[e:calabria|Calabria]], reportedly on the advice of the Delphic oracle. It had a good harbour and a broad territory, and became one of the major powers of [[e:magna-graecia|Magna Graecia]].
croton.r: Croton produced more Olympic victors than any other city in some periods, above all the wrestler [[e:milo-of-croton|Milo]]. It was renowned for medicine, with [[e:democedes|Democedes]] and [[e:alcmaeon-of-croton|Alcmaeon]]. Around 530 BCE [[e:pythagoras|Pythagoras]] settled there, and his followers dominated politics for a time before being violently overthrown. The sanctuary of [[e:temple-of-hera-lacinia|Hera Lacinia]] at [[e:capo-colonna|Capo Colonna]] was a religious centre for the Italiote [[e:greeks|Greeks]]. After defeat by [[s:locri-epizephyrii|Locri]] at the [[e:battle-of-the-sagra|Sagras]] river, Croton crushed [[s:sybaris|Sybaris]] in 510 BCE.
croton.e: In the 4th century Croton suffered from [[e:dionysius-i-of-syracuse|Dionysius I]], who held it from 379 BCE, and from the [[s:bruttii|Bruttians]] and [[e:agathocles-of-syracuse|Agathocles]]. During the war with [[e:pyrrhus-of-epirus|Pyrrhus]] it was taken by [[e:rome|Rome]] in 277 BCE. A Roman colony was founded there in 194 BCE, and the town survives as [[e:crotone|Crotone]].

centrocaspian-dictatorship.t: An anti-Bolshevik government that briefly held Baku in 1918 with British help before the city fell to the Ottoman Army of Islam.
centrocaspian-dictatorship.o: On 31 July 1918, after the [[s:baku-commune|Baku Soviet]] voted to invite British troops against the advancing Ottoman forces, the Bolshevik-led [[e:baku|Baku]] Commune resigned. [[e:socialist-revolutionary-party|Socialist Revolutionaries]], [[e:mensheviks|Mensheviks]] and [[e:armenian-revolutionary-federation|Armenian Dashnaks]] formed a new government, named after the Centrocaspian committee of sailors of the [[e:caspian-flotilla|Caspian Fleet]].
centrocaspian-dictatorship.r: The Dictatorship relied on the [[e:caspian-flotilla|Caspian Fleet]], Armenian militia and a small British force, [[e:dunsterforce|Dunsterforce]], under General [[e:lionel-dunsterville|Lionel Dunsterville]], which arrived in August 1918. It tried to defend [[e:baku|Baku]] and its oil fields, but the defence was poorly coordinated, and relations between the British and local leaders were strained.
centrocaspian-dictatorship.e: [[e:dunsterforce|Dunsterforce]] withdrew on 14 September 1918, and the next day the Ottoman-led [[e:caucasus-army-of-islam|Army of Islam]] captured [[e:baku|Baku]], followed by massacres of [[e:armenians|Armenians]]. The city became the capital of the [[s:azerbaijan-democratic-republic|Azerbaijan Democratic Republic]].

colony-of-trinidad-and-tobago.t: British colony joining Trinidad and Tobago from 1889, transformed by oil, labour revolt, calypso and steelpan before independence in 1962.
colony-of-trinidad-and-tobago.o: [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]] joined struggling [[e:tobago|Tobago]] to the [[s:colony-of-trinidad|Colony of Trinidad]] in 1889, and in 1899 Tobago became a ward of the combined colony, ruled from [[e:port-of-spain|Port of Spain]]. The union was administrative, and Tobagonians often felt neglected by the larger island.
colony-of-trinidad-and-tobago.r: [[e:crown-colony|Crown colony]] government left power with the governor and nominated officials. Commercial oil production began in southern [[e:trinidad|Trinidad]] in the 1900s, and asphalt from the [[e:pitch-lake|Pitch Lake]] was exported worldwide. [[e:arthur-cipriani|Arthur Cipriani]] led a reform movement in the 1920s, and the 1937 oilfield strikes and riots, inspired by [[e:uriah-butler|Uriah Butler]], led to unions and reform. In 1941 the [[s:united-states|United States]] built bases at [[e:chaguaramas|Chaguaramas]]. [[e:trinidad-and-tobago-carnival|Carnival]], calypso and the steelpan flourished among a population of African and Indian descent.
colony-of-trinidad-and-tobago.e: [[e:universal-suffrage|Universal suffrage]] came in 1946. [[e:eric-williams|Eric Williams]] founded the [[e:peoples-national-movement|People's National Movement]] in 1956 and became chief minister. [[e:port-of-spain|Port of Spain]] hosted the [[s:west-indies-federation|West Indies Federation]], and after it collapsed the colony became independent as [[s:trinidad-and-tobago|Trinidad and Tobago]] on 31 August 1962.

caliphate-of-ibn-al-zubayr.t: A rival caliphate based in Mecca that, during the Second Fitna, was recognised across much of the Islamic world before the Umayyads crushed it.
caliphate-of-ibn-al-zubayr.o: [[e:abd-allah-ibn-al-zubayr|Abd Allah ibn al-Zubayr]], son of a [[e:companions-of-the-prophet|Companion of the Prophet]] and grandson of [[e:abu-bakr-al-siddiq|Abu Bakr]], refused to recognise the [[e:umayyad-caliphate|Umayyad]] [[e:caliphate|caliph]] [[e:yazid-i|Yazid I]] and took refuge in [[e:mecca|Mecca]]. When Yazid died in 683 and his son soon after, Ibn al-Zubayr proclaimed himself caliph and was accepted in the [[s:kingdom-of-hejaz|Hejaz]], [[e:iraq|Iraq]], [[e:egypt|Egypt]], [[s:republic-of-yemen|Yemen]] and much of [[s:syrian-arab-republic|Syria]].
caliphate-of-ibn-al-zubayr.r: He governed from [[e:mecca|Mecca]], where he rebuilt the [[e:kaaba|Kaaba]] after it was damaged in an [[e:umayyad-caliphate|Umayyad]] siege, while his brother [[e:musab-ibn-al-zubayr|Mus'ab]] ruled [[e:iraq|Iraq]] from [[e:basra|Basra]]. His authority depended on governors and tribal allies, and he faced revolts from the [[e:kharijites|Kharijites]] of the [[s:najdiyya|Najdiyya]] and from [[e:al-mukhtar-al-thaqafi|al-Mukhtar]]'s pro-[[e:alids|Alid]] movement at [[e:kufa|Kufa]], which Mus'ab defeated in 687.
caliphate-of-ibn-al-zubayr.e: The [[e:umayyad-caliphate|Umayyad]] victory at [[e:battle-of-marj-rahit-684|Marj Rahit]] in 684 kept [[s:syrian-arab-republic|Syria]], Marwan I retook [[e:egypt|Egypt]] in 685, and [[e:abd-al-malik-ibn-marwan|Abd al-Malik]] reconquered [[e:iraq|Iraq]], where [[e:musab-ibn-al-zubayr|Mus'ab]] was killed in 691. In 692 [[e:al-hajjaj-ibn-yusuf|al-Hajjaj]] besieged and bombarded [[e:mecca|Mecca]]; [[e:abd-allah-ibn-al-zubayr|Ibn al-Zubayr]] died fighting and the [[s:umayyad-caliphate|Umayyad Caliphate]] was reunited.

cornouaille.t: Breton kingdom of south-western Brittany, founded by settlers from Britain and centred on Quimper.
cornouaille.o: From the 5th and 6th centuries migrants from western [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]] settled the Armorican peninsula, once the land of the [[s:osismii|Osismii]]. Those in the south-west named their territory after [[e:cornwall|Cornwall]]: Kernev in Breton, Cornubia in [[e:latin|Latin]]. Its early history is known mainly from saints' lives and legends, such as that of [[e:gradlon|King Gradlon]] and the drowned city of Ys.
cornouaille.r: The kingdom was ruled by local Breton dynasties and organised around monasteries and the see of [[e:quimper|Quimper]], traditionally founded by [[e:saint-corentin|Saint Corentin]]. The abbey of [[e:landevennec-abbey|Landévennec]], founded by [[e:winwaloe|Saint Guénolé]], was its chief religious centre and produced important [[e:manuscript|manuscripts]].
cornouaille.e: In the 9th century Cornouaille was drawn into the unified [[s:kingdom-of-brittany|Kingdom of Brittany]] under [[e:nominoe|Nominoe]] and [[e:erispoe|Erispoe]]. It survived as a county whose counts later became dukes of [[s:duchy-of-brittany|Brittany]] in the 11th century, and the name remains in use for the region around [[e:quimper|Quimper]].

county-of-wied-neuwied.t: Rhineland county whose capital, Neuwied, was founded as a haven of religious tolerance and became famous for fine furniture.
county-of-wied-neuwied.o: Count [[e:frederick-iii-of-wied|Frederick III of Wied]] founded the town of [[e:neuwied|Neuwied]] on the [[e:rhine|Rhine]] in 1653, inviting settlers with promises of religious freedom. In 1698 the Wied lands were divided between Wied-Runkel and Wied-Neuwied, the latter ruling from the new town.
county-of-wied-neuwied.r: [[e:neuwied|Neuwied]] welcomed [[e:mennonites|Mennonites]], [[e:moravian-church|Moravian Brethren]], Catholics, [[e:jews|Jews]] and Reformed Christians, each with its own congregation. The cabinetmakers [[e:abraham-roentgen|Abraham]] and [[e:david-roentgen|David Roentgen]] built a workshop there whose marquetry furniture was sold to the courts of [[e:paris|Paris]] and [[e:saint-petersburg|St Petersburg]]. The counts were raised to princes in 1784. [[e:prince-maximilian-of-wied-neuwied|Prince Maximilian of Wied-Neuwied]] later became known for expeditions to [[s:new-republic-brazil|Brazil]] and [[e:north-america|North America]].
county-of-wied-neuwied.e: Wied-[[e:neuwied|Neuwied]] was mediatised in 1806 and placed under the [[s:duchy-of-nassau|Duchy of Nassau]], then in 1815 under [[e:kingdom-of-prussia|Prussia]] as part of the [[e:rhine-province|Rhine Province]]. The princely family kept its palace in Neuwied.

county-of-edessa.t: The first Crusader state, founded on the upper Euphrates; its fall to Zengi in 1144 launched the Second Crusade.
county-of-edessa.o: In 1098 [[e:baldwin-i-of-jerusalem|Baldwin of Boulogne]] left the main army of the [[e:first-crusade|First Crusade]] and went east at the invitation of [[e:thoros-of-edessa|Thoros]], the Armenian ruler of Edessa, who adopted him as son and heir. Weeks later Thoros was killed in a riot and Baldwin took the city, founding the first [[e:latin|Latin]] state in the East.
county-of-edessa.r: The county stretched across the [[e:euphrates|Euphrates]], with [[e:turbessel|Turbessel]] west of the river and Edessa east of it. A small Frankish elite ruled a population of [[e:armenians|Armenians]] and [[e:syriac-christians|Syriac Christians]] and relied on intermarriage with Armenian nobility. Its counts, [[e:baldwin-ii-of-jerusalem|Baldwin II]], [[e:joscelin-i-count-of-edessa|Joscelin I]] and [[e:joscelin-ii-of-edessa|Joscelin II]], were exposed on every side; the defeat at [[e:harran|Harran]] in 1104 halted their advance towards [[e:mesopotamia|Mesopotamia]].
county-of-edessa.e: [[e:imad-al-din-zengi|Imad al-Din Zengi]] took Edessa on 24 December 1144 while [[e:joscelin-ii-of-edessa|Joscelin II]] was absent, provoking the [[e:second-crusade|Second Crusade]]. Joscelin was captured by [[e:nur-al-din|Nur al-Din]] in 1150, and his wife Beatrice sold the remaining fortresses to [[s:byzantium|Byzantium]], which soon lost them.
county-of-edessa.re: Latin Christianity, Armenian and Syriac Christianity

colony-of-western-australia.t: The vast western colony that began as a struggling free settlement on the Swan River and was transformed by the gold rushes of the 1890s.
colony-of-western-australia.o: Fearing French claims, [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]] established a garrison at [[e:king-george-sound|King George Sound]] in 1826 and in 1829 founded the Swan River Colony under Captain [[e:james-stirling-royal-navy-officer|James Stirling]], with [[e:perth|Perth]] as capital and [[e:fremantle|Fremantle]] as port. Unlike [[s:colony-of-new-south-wales|New South Wales]], it was meant for free settlers, who received land in proportion to the capital they brought.
colony-of-western-australia.r: Poor soils, scattered settlement and labour shortages kept the colony small for decades, and in 1850 it began accepting convicts, about 9,700 of them by 1868. Wool, sandalwood and pearling were important, and pastoralists pushed into [[e:aboriginal-australians|Aboriginal]] lands in the north. Self-government came only in 1890, with [[e:john-forrest|John Forrest]] as premier. The gold discoveries at [[e:coolgardie|Coolgardie]] and [[e:kalgoorlie|Kalgoorlie]] in 1892 and 1893 brought a population boom.
colony-of-western-australia.e: After hesitating, Western [[s:commonwealth-of-australia|Australia]] voted in 1900 to join the federation and became a state of the Commonwealth of [[e:australia|Australia]] in 1901. Resentment of federal policies produced a vote for secession in 1933, which [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]] declined to act on.

cr.a: Original: Ivor Evans, Leslie John Hawkins, Egbert John Nuttall, Annie Dorrington and William Stevens Vector: Ian Fieggen

crown-domain-of-the-nguyen-dynasty.t: A special status zone of 1950 to 1955 placing Vietnam's Central Highlands and some upland areas under Bao Dai's personal authority.
crown-domain-of-the-nguyen-dynasty.o: In April 1950 [[e:bao-dai|Bao Dai]], head of the [[s:state-of-vietnam|State of Vietnam]], decreed that the Central Highlands and other upland areas inhabited mainly by ethnic minorities would form the Hoang trieu Cuong tho, Crown Domain, directly under the Nguyen crown rather than the ordinary government. The [[e:nung-people|Nung]] and Tai areas of the north were also attached.
crown-domain-of-the-nguyen-dynasty.r: The domain was administered from [[e:buon-ma-thuot|Ban Me Thuot]] under a separate statute that protected highland peoples' land and customs, limited lowland Vietnamese settlement and kept French military and planter influence strong. [[e:bao-dai|Bao Dai]] used the highlands for hunting and as a personal power base, with residences at [[e:da-lat|Da Lat]] and Ban Me Thuot.
crown-domain-of-the-nguyen-dynasty.e: After the [[s:republic-of-geneva|Geneva]] Accords of 1954 and [[e:bao-dai|Bao Dai's]] deposition by [[e:ngo-dinh-diem|Ngo Dinh Diem]] in 1955, the Crown Domain was abolished, and the highlands were integrated into the [[s:republic-of-vietnam|Republic of Vietnam]], opening them to large-scale Vietnamese settlement.

co-operative-republic-of-guyana.t: The only English-speaking country in South America, independent since 1966 and transformed in the 2020s by offshore oil.
co-operative-republic-of-guyana.o: [[s:british-guiana|British Guiana]] became independent as Guyana on 26 May 1966, with [[e:forbes-burnham|Forbes Burnham]] of the [[e:peoples-national-congress|People's National Congress]] as prime minister. On 23 February 1970, the anniversary of the [[s:berbice|Berbice]] uprising, it became the Co-operative Republic of Guyana.
co-operative-republic-of-guyana.r: [[e:forbes-burnham|Burnham]] pursued co-operative socialism, nationalising the bauxite and [[e:sugar-plantation|sugar]] industries, and ruled through manipulated elections until his death in 1985. Politics remained divided along ethnic lines between the largely Afro-Guyanese [[e:peoples-national-congress|PNC]] and the Indo-Guyanese [[e:peoples-progressive-party-guyana|People's Progressive Party]]. In 1978 the mass deaths at the [[e:jonestown|Jonestown]] commune of an American cult drew world attention. [[e:cheddi-jagan|Cheddi Jagan]] won free elections in 1992.
co-operative-republic-of-guyana.e: [[e:exxonmobil|ExxonMobil]] discovered large offshore oil fields in 2015, and production began in 2019, making Guyana one of the world's fastest-growing economies. Venezuela's claim to the [[s:essequibo|Essequibo]] region, two thirds of Guyana's territory, remains a source of tension.

capua.t: The great city of Campania, Etruscan in origin and later Oscan, whose defection to Hannibal in 216 BCE ended in harsh Roman punishment.
capua.o: [[s:principality-of-capua|Capua]] lay in the fertile Campanian plain near the [[e:volturno|Volturno]], on the site of modern [[e:santa-maria-capua-vetere|Santa Maria Capua Vetere]]. The [[e:etruscans|Etruscans]] developed it into a city in the 7th and 6th centuries BCE as the centre of their Campanian holdings. Around 423 BCE [[e:oscan-language|Oscan]]-speaking [[s:samnite-league|Samnites]] seized it, and its people became known as Campani.
capua.r: [[s:principality-of-capua|Capua]] grew rich on grain, wine, [[e:bronze-working|bronze-working]] and perfumes, and [[e:roman-empire|Romans]] saw it as a centre of luxury. It was governed by a chief magistrate, the meddix tuticus, and a senate. Threatened by the [[s:samnite-league|Samnites]], it appealed to [[e:rome|Rome]] in 343 BCE, triggering the [[e:first-samnite-war|First Samnite War]], and from 338 BCE its citizens held Roman citizenship without the vote. Its Mother Goddess sanctuary yielded hundreds of stone statues of women with infants.
capua.e: After [[e:battle-of-cannae|Cannae]] in 216 BCE [[s:principality-of-capua|Capua]] went over to [[e:hannibal|Hannibal]]. [[e:rome|Rome]] besieged it and took it in 211 BCE, executed its leaders, confiscated its land and abolished its self-government. It recovered as a Roman colony and later saw the slave revolt of [[e:spartacus|Spartacus]] begin in its gladiator school in 73 BCE.

captaincy-general-of-venezuela.t: The Spanish colonial unit that first united the provinces of Venezuela under Caracas and became the starting point of Bolívar's revolution.
captaincy-general-of-venezuela.o: On 8 September 1777 [[e:charles-iii-of-spain|Charles III]] united the provinces of [[s:venezuela|Venezuela]], [[e:cumana|Cumaná]], [[e:guayana-province|Guayana]], [[e:maracaibo|Maracaibo]], [[e:trinidad|Trinidad]] and [[e:margarita-island|Margarita]] under the captain-general in [[e:caracas|Caracas]], separating them from the [[s:viceroyalty-of-new-granada|Viceroyalty of New Granada]] for military and financial purposes. It built on the old [[s:province-of-venezuela|Province of Venezuela]].
captaincy-general-of-venezuela.r: An intendancy for finance was created in 1776, an [[e:audiencia|Audiencia]] at [[e:caracas|Caracas]] in 1786 and a merchant [[e:guild|guild]] in 1793, giving Caracas real autonomy. [[e:cacao|Cacao]], [[e:indigo|indigo]] and [[e:coffee-economy|coffee]] were exported by a [[e:criollo-people|Creole]] planter elite using enslaved labour. Revolutionary ideas spread, and [[e:francisco-de-miranda|Francisco de Miranda]] led a failed invasion in 1806. [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]] took [[e:trinidad|Trinidad]] in 1797.
captaincy-general-of-venezuela.e: On 19 April 1810 a junta in [[e:caracas|Caracas]] deposed the captain-general, and the [[s:first-republic-of-venezuela|First Republic of Venezuela]] declared independence on 5 July 1811. Years of war followed until [[e:simon-bolivar|Bolívar]]'s victory at [[e:battle-of-carabobo|Carabobo]] in 1821; the last royalists left [[e:puerto-cabello|Puerto Cabello]] in 1823.

county-of-sicily.t: The Norman county that conquered Muslim Sicily and built the multilingual, multi-faith government later inherited by the Kingdom of Sicily.
county-of-sicily.o: [[e:roger-i-of-sicily|Roger de Hauteville]], [[e:robert-guiscard|Robert Guiscard's]] youngest brother, crossed to [[e:sicily|Sicily]] in 1061 and took [[e:messina|Messina]]. With Guiscard he besieged [[e:palermo|Palermo]], which fell in early 1072, and Roger became count of Sicily under his brother's overlordship. The conquest of the [[s:emirate-of-sicily|Emirate of Sicily]] took thirty years, ending with the fall of [[e:noto-sicily|Noto]] in 1091, the year Roger also raided [[e:malta|Malta]].
county-of-sicily.r: Roger ruled a largely Muslim and Greek population with a thin Norman elite. He kept Arabic-speaking fiscal offices, recruited Muslim troops, refounded [[e:latin|Latin]] bishoprics and endowed Greek monasteries. In 1098 [[e:pope-urban-ii|Pope Urban II]] granted him unusual control over the Sicilian church. After his death in 1101, his widow [[e:adelaide-del-vasto|Adelaide del Vasto]] ruled as regent and moved the court to [[e:palermo|Palermo]].
county-of-sicily.e: [[e:roger-ii-of-sicily|Roger II]] came of age in 1112, absorbed the mainland [[s:duchy-of-apulia-and-calabria|Duchy of Apulia and Calabria]] in 1127 and was crowned king at [[e:palermo|Palermo]] on Christmas Day 1130. The county thus became the core of the [[s:kingdom-of-sicily|Kingdom of Sicily]].
county-of-sicily.re: Catholic Christianity, with Greek Orthodox Christianity and Sunni Islam
county-of-sicily.la: Arabic, Greek, Latin, Old Norman French

county-of-urgell.t: The longest-lasting Catalan county, ruled by the Ermengol counts from Balaguer, whose bishops became co-princes of Andorra.
county-of-urgell.o: Urgell, in the upper [[e:segre|Segre]] valley, was taken by the [[s:franks|Franks]] around 798 and organised as a county of the [[s:marca-hispanica|Marca Hispanica]], often joined with [[e:cerdanya|Cerdanya]]. [[e:wilfred-the-hairy|Wilfred the Hairy]] ruled it from 870. In 992 it passed to Ermengol I, son of [[e:borrell-ii-of-barcelona|Borrell II of Barcelona]], founding a dynasty that lasted over two centuries.
county-of-urgell.r: The counts of Urgell, nearly all named Ermengol, pushed south against [[e:al-andalus|al-Andalus]] and conquered [[e:balaguer|Balaguer]] in 1105, making it their capital. The [[e:bishop|bishops]] of [[e:la-seu-durgell|La Seu d'Urgell]] held great influence, and an agreement of 1278 with the counts of Foix made them co-lords of [[s:andorra|Andorra]]. Later the county passed to a branch of the royal [[e:house-of-barcelona|House of Barcelona]].
county-of-urgell.e: Count [[e:james-ii-of-urgell|James II]] claimed the throne of Aragon in 1410, but the [[e:compromise-of-caspe|Compromise of Caspe]] of 1412 chose [[e:ferdinand-i-of-aragon|Ferdinand of Antequera]]. James rebelled, was besieged in [[e:balaguer|Balaguer]] in 1413 and imprisoned, and the county was confiscated. The [[e:bishop|bishop]] of Urgell remains co-prince of [[s:andorra|Andorra]].

crimean-socialist-soviet-republic.t: A Bolshevik republic in the Crimea in spring 1919, headed by Lenin's brother Dmitry Ulyanov and ended by the White advance.
crimean-socialist-soviet-republic.o: In April 1919 the [[e:red-army|Red Army]] broke into the [[e:crimea|Crimea]], ending the [[s:crimean-regional-government|Crimean Regional Government]], and the Bolsheviks proclaimed the Crimean Socialist Soviet Republic. [[e:dmitry-ulyanov|Dmitry Ulyanov]], [[e:vladimir-lenin|Lenin]]'s younger brother, became deputy chairman and effective head of its council of people's commissars.
crimean-socialist-soviet-republic.r: The republic was intended partly to reassure the [[e:crimean-tatars|Crimean Tatars]] and the [[e:allies|Allies]] that the [[e:crimea|Crimea]] had its own government. It nationalised land, banks and industry and set up a [[e:red-army|Red Army]] of the Crimea. Allied warships and White troops still held the [[e:kerch|Kerch]] peninsula, so its control was never complete.
crimean-socialist-soviet-republic.e: In June 1919 [[e:anton-denikin|Denikin]]'s [[e:armed-forces-of-south-russia|Armed Forces of South Russia]] landed and advanced into the [[e:crimea|Crimea]], and the Soviet government withdrew. The Crimea remained in White hands until November 1920, when the Bolsheviks returned for good.

california-republic.t: The Bear Flag Republic, a 25-day revolt by American settlers in Mexican California whose flag became the state flag of California.
california-republic.o: In June 1846, as war between the [[s:united-states|United States]] and [[s:mexico|Mexico]] began, American settlers in the [[e:sacramento-valley|Sacramento Valley]] feared expulsion by Mexican authorities in [[s:alta-california|Alta California]]. Encouraged by the explorer [[e:john-c-fremont|John C. Frémont]], about 30 of them seized the town of [[e:sonoma-california|Sonoma]] on 14 June and took the local commander, [[e:mariano-guadalupe-vallejo|Mariano Guadalupe Vallejo]], prisoner.
california-republic.r: The rebels proclaimed a [[e:california|California]] Republic, with [[e:william-b-ide|William B. Ide]] as their leader, and raised a flag with a grizzly bear, a star and the words 'California Republic', painted by William Todd. The republic had no real institutions and controlled little beyond [[e:sonoma-california|Sonoma]] and the [[e:sacramento-valley|Sacramento Valley]]. [[e:john-c-fremont|Frémont]] took command of its forces, the [[e:california-battalion|California Battalion]], in early July.
california-republic.e: On 7 July 1846 Commodore [[e:john-d-sloat|John Sloat]] raised the American flag at [[e:monterey-california|Monterey]], and the Stars and Stripes replaced the Bear Flag at [[e:sonoma-california|Sonoma]] on 9 July. The republic dissolved into the [[e:occupation-of-japan|American occupation]]. [[e:california|California]] became a state in 1850, adopting a version of the bear flag in 1911.

cessetani.t: The Iberian people of the Tarragona area, in whose land the Romans probably won their first battle in Iberia, at Cissa in 218 BCE.
cessetani.o: The Cessetani, or Cosetani, inhabited the [[e:camp-de-tarragona|Camp de Tarragona]] and the lower [[e:penedes|Penedès]] in southern [[s:principality-of-catalonia|Catalonia]] from about the 5th century BCE. Their main settlement was Kese, usually located at or near [[e:tarragona|Tarragona]].
cessetani.r: Their territory had fortified settlements such as Alorda Park at [[e:calafell|Calafell]] and lived from farming and trade along the coast. Kese minted widely circulated coins with an Iberian legend. Their political structure is not recorded, but they were prosperous enough for both [[e:carthage|Carthage]] and [[e:rome|Rome]] to value the area.
cessetani.e: In 218 BCE [[e:gnaeus-cornelius-scipio-calvus|Gnaeus Scipio]] defeated the Carthaginian commander Hanno near [[e:battle-of-cissa|Cissa]], a town sometimes identified with Kese, and the [[e:roman-empire|Romans]] established their base at [[e:tarraco|Tarraco]]. The region thus became [[e:rome|Rome's]] first foothold in [[e:iberia|Iberia]], and Tarraco grew into the capital of [[s:hispania-citerior|Hispania Citerior]] and later [[s:hispania-tarraconensis|Tarraconensis]].

county-of-oldenburg.t: A North Sea county whose counts supplied kings to Denmark, Norway and Sweden, raised in 1774 to the Duchy of Oldenburg.
county-of-oldenburg.o: Count Elimar I appears in 1108, and his family built Oldenburg castle on the [[e:hunte|Hunte]]. The counts expanded over the marshes towards the [[e:weser|Weser]] and the Jade, fighting the free Frisian peasants of [[e:stedingen|Stedingen]], who were crushed in a [[e:crusade|crusade]] in 1234.
county-of-oldenburg.r: In 1448 Count [[e:christian-i-of-denmark|Christian of Oldenburg]] was elected King of [[e:denmark|Denmark]] as Christian I, founding the [[e:house-of-oldenburg|House of Oldenburg]], which later ruled Denmark, [[e:norway|Norway]], [[e:sweden|Sweden]], [[e:russia|Russia]] and [[e:greece|Greece]] in its various branches. Count [[e:anton-gunther-count-of-oldenburg|Anton Günther]] kept Oldenburg out of the [[e:thirty-years-war|Thirty Years' War]] and was famous for [[e:horse-breeding|horse breeding]]. The economy relied on [[e:cattle|cattle]] and dyke-building.
county-of-oldenburg.e: After [[e:anton-gunther-count-of-oldenburg|Anton Günther]] died in 1667, Oldenburg passed to the Danish crown. In 1773 [[e:denmark|Denmark]] exchanged it with [[e:russia|Russia]], which gave it to [[e:frederick-augustus-i-duke-of-oldenburg|Frederick August]] of [[s:duchy-of-holstein-gottorp|Holstein-Gottorp]], and in 1774 it was raised to a duchy. It later became a grand duchy and now part of [[e:lower-saxony|Lower Saxony]].

canton-of-lucerne.t: The first city to ally with the Swiss forest cantons, in 1332, and later the leading Catholic power of the Confederacy.
canton-of-lucerne.o: Lucerne grew around the monastery of Saint [[e:leodegar|Leodegar]] where the [[e:reuss-river|Reuss]] leaves [[e:lake-lucerne|Lake Lucerne]], and boomed after the opening of the [[e:gotthard-pass|Gotthard]] route in the 13th century. Sold to the [[e:habsburg-dynasty|Habsburgs]] in 1291, the town allied with the [[s:canton-of-uri|Canton of Uri]], the [[s:canton-of-schwyz|Canton of Schwyz]] and the [[s:canton-of-unterwalden|Canton of Unterwalden]] in 1332, and the Swiss victory at [[e:battle-of-sempach|Sempach]] in 1386 freed it from [[s:county-of-habsburg|Habsburg]] rule.
canton-of-lucerne.r: A small council of patrician families governed the city and a large rural territory acquired in the 15th century. Lucerne lived from [[e:gotthard-pass|Gotthard]] transit trade and [[e:mercenary|mercenary]] contracts. It led the Catholic cantons during the [[e:protestant-reformation|Reformation]], hosted the papal nuncio from 1586, and with its allies crushed the great [[e:swiss-peasant-war-of-1653|Peasants' War]] of 1653.
canton-of-lucerne.e: The patrician regime abdicated in 1798 as French troops invaded, and Lucerne briefly served as capital of the [[s:helvetic-republic|Helvetic Republic]]. Restored as a canton in 1803, it remains a member of the [[s:swiss-confederation|Swiss Confederation]].

cooch-behar-state.t: The western successor of the Koch kingdom of northern Bengal, a princely state renowned for its cultured Maharajas until it joined India in 1949.
cooch-behar-state.o: The Koch kingdom rose under [[e:biswa-singha|Biswa Singha]] in the early 16th century and reached its height under [[e:nara-narayan|Nara Narayan]]. After a division of the realm in the 1580s, the western half, Koch [[e:bihar|Bihar]], continued under [[e:nara|Nara]] Narayan's line, while the eastern [[s:koch-hajo|Koch Hajo]] fell to the [[e:mughal-empire|Mughals]] and [[e:ahom-people|Ahoms]].
cooch-behar-state.r: The [[e:maharaja|Maharajas]] ruled the plains between the [[e:teesta-river|Teesta]] and [[e:sankosh-river|Sankosh]] rivers, at times in conflict with [[s:zhabdrung-bhutan|Bhutan]] and the [[e:mughal-empire|Mughals]]. A 1773 treaty with the [[e:east-india-company|East India Company]] against Bhutanese incursions made it a tributary state. [[e:nripendra-narayan|Nripendra Narayan]], married to [[e:suniti-devi|Suniti Devi]], daughter of the reformer [[e:keshab-chandra-sen|Keshab Chandra Sen]], built the [[e:cooch-behar-palace|Cooch Behar Palace]] and modernised the administration.
cooch-behar-state.e: [[e:maharaja|Maharaja]] [[e:jagaddipendra-narayan|Jagaddipendra Narayan]] signed a merger agreement with [[e:india|India]] in August 1949, and Cooch Behar became a district of [[e:west-bengal|West Bengal]] in January 1950. [[e:gayatri-devi|Gayatri Devi]], later Maharani of [[e:jaipur|Jaipur]], was born into its royal family.

county-palatine-of-chester.t: A Norman marcher earldom on the Welsh border whose earls ruled Cheshire almost as independent princes.
county-palatine-of-chester.o: After crushing northern and Mercian resistance, [[e:william-the-conqueror|William the Conqueror]] gave the earldom of [[e:chester|Chester]] to [[e:gerbod-the-fleming|Gerbod the Fleming]] and then, in 1071, to [[e:hugh-davranches-earl-of-chester|Hugh d'Avranches]]. Its purpose was to guard the northern Welsh border and push into [[s:kingdom-of-gwynedd|Gwynedd]].
county-palatine-of-chester.r: The earls held nearly all of [[e:cheshire|Cheshire]], with their own courts, sheriff and barons, and royal writs did not normally run there, a status later called palatine. Hugh and his cousin [[e:robert-of-rhuddlan|Robert of Rhuddlan]] advanced along the north Welsh coast. [[e:ranulf-de-gernon-4th-earl-of-chester|Ranulf de Gernon]] and [[e:ranulf-de-blondeville-6th-earl-of-chester|Ranulf de Blondeville]] were major figures in the wars of Stephen and John; Ranulf III built [[e:beeston-castle|Beeston Castle]].
county-palatine-of-chester.e: When [[e:john-of-scotland-earl-of-huntingdon|John the Scot]], the last earl of the line, died childless in 1237, [[e:henry-iii-of-england|Henry III]] took the earldom into royal hands. From 1301 it was given to the heir to the throne, and [[e:cheshire|Cheshire]] kept palatine institutions until 1830.

chiefdom-of-maui.t: The Hawaiian chiefdom of Maui, which under Kahekili II briefly dominated most of the islands before falling to Kamehameha I.
chiefdom-of-maui.o: Around 1500 the chief Piʻilani united the districts of [[e:maui|Maui]] under a single rule, and his reign is remembered as a time of peace and building. Tradition credits him and his son [[e:kihapiilani|Kihapiʻilani]] with a paved trail around the island and with [[e:piilanihale|Piʻilanihale]], the largest temple platform in [[e:hawaii|Hawaii]]. [[e:wailuku|Wailuku]] became a principal royal seat.
chiefdom-of-maui.r: [[e:maui|Maui's]] aliʻi nui governed through district chiefs, priests and the kapu system, with irrigated taro in the valleys of west Maui and dryland farming on the slopes of [[e:haleakala|Haleakalā]]. Rulers fought frequent wars with the [[s:chiefdom-of-hawaii-island|Chiefdom of Hawaii Island]] over the Hāna district. In the 18th century [[e:kekaulike|Kekaulike]] strengthened the kingdom, and his son [[e:kahekili-ii|Kahekili II]], who ruled from about 1765, conquered the [[s:chiefdom-of-oahu|Chiefdom of Oahu]] in 1783 and controlled [[e:molokai|Molokaʻi]] and [[e:lanai|Lānaʻi]].
chiefdom-of-maui.e: [[e:kamehameha-i|Kamehameha I]] defeated [[e:maui|Maui's]] forces at [[e:iao-valley|ʻĪao Valley]] in 1790. After [[e:kahekili-ii|Kahekili]]'s death in 1794 his realm was divided, and in 1795 Kamehameha took Maui on his way to [[e:oahu|Oʻahu]]. [[e:lahaina|Lahaina]] later served as capital of the [[s:kingdom-of-hawaii|Kingdom of Hawaii]].

chincha-kingdom.t: A wealthy lordship of Peru's south coast whose merchants and seafarers traded spondylus shell and whose lord was carried in a litter alongside Atahualpa.
chincha-kingdom.o: The Chincha valley on the south coast of [[e:peru|Peru]] became the centre of a powerful lordship from around 1000, after the decline of Wari influence. Its capital at [[e:la-centinela|La Centinela]], with adobe pyramids and plazas, dominated the valley.
chincha-kingdom.r: Chincha society was highly specialised, with tens of thousands of farmers, fishermen and merchants according to a 16th-century account. Its merchants traded by sea northwards to [[s:republic-of-ecuador|Ecuador]] for spondylus shell and inland by llama caravan for [[e:copper|copper]] from the highlands. Chincha's wealth earned it a privileged position under the [[e:inca-empire|Incas]]: at [[e:cajamarca|Cajamarca]] in 1532, the lord of Chincha was the only lord besides [[e:atahualpa|Atahualpa]] carried in a litter, and he was killed in the attack.
chincha-kingdom.e: Chincha was incorporated into the [[s:inca-empire|Inca Empire]] around 1476 under [[e:tupac-inca-yupanqui|Túpac Inca Yupanqui]], and the [[e:inca-empire|Incas]] built a palace at [[e:la-centinela|La Centinela]]. After the Spanish conquest the population collapsed from disease, falling to a small fraction within decades.

colony-of-dominica.t: Mountainous British colony between Guadeloupe and Martinique, home of the last Kalinago community in the eastern Caribbean, independent since 1978.
colony-of-dominica.o: Dominica's rugged terrain had allowed the [[e:kalinago|Kalinago]] to hold it long after their neighbours fell, and [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]] and [[e:france|France]] agreed in 1748 to leave it neutral. French woodcutters and planters nevertheless settled there. The [[e:treaty-of-paris-1763|Treaty of Paris]] in 1763 gave it to [[e:britain|Britain]], though France occupied it again from 1778 to 1783.
colony-of-dominica.r: [[e:coffee-economy|Coffee]] and later [[e:sugar-plantation|sugar]], [[e:cacao|cacao]] and limes were grown on estates worked by enslaved Africans, while maroon bands held out in the interior until the campaigns of 1813 to 1814. In 1838 Dominica's assembly became the first in the British [[e:caribbean|Caribbean]] with a majority of men of colour. After the assembly was weakened, the island became a crown colony in 1898, and in 1903 a reserve was set aside for the [[e:kalinago|Kalinago]]. The French-based [[e:antillean-creole|Kwéyòl]] remained the people's everyday language.
colony-of-dominica.e: Part of the [[e:leeward-islands|Leeward Islands]] until 1940 and then of the [[s:british-windward-islands|British Windward Islands]], [[s:commonwealth-of-dominica|Dominica]] joined the [[s:west-indies-federation|West Indies Federation]], became an [[e:west-indies-associated-states|Associated State]] in 1967 and gained independence as the Commonwealth of Dominica on 3 November 1978.

county-of-blois.t: The Loire county of the Thibaudian counts, rivals of the early Capetians, whose family gave England King Stephen and later united with Champagne.
county-of-blois.o: [[e:theobald-i-of-blois|Theobald the Trickster]], a [[e:vassal|vassal]] of [[e:hugh-the-great|Hugh the Great]], held Blois, [[e:chartres|Chartres]] and [[e:tours|Tours]] by around 940 and founded a dynasty. His grandson [[e:odo-ii-of-blois|Odo II]] added [[e:troyes|Troyes]] and [[e:meaux|Meaux]] around 1022, encircling the Capetian royal domain and contending with [[s:county-of-anjou|Anjou]] for [[e:touraine|Touraine]], which was lost in 1044.
county-of-blois.r: The counts ruled a rich farming land of the [[e:loire|Loire]] and the [[e:beauce|Beauce]], with [[e:chartres|Chartres]] and its cathedral school a major centre of learning. Count [[e:stephen-count-of-blois|Stephen-Henry]], husband of [[e:adela-of-normandy|Adela of Normandy]], was a leader of the First Crusade, and their son Stephen became king of [[e:england|England]] in 1135. The family's [[s:county-of-champagne|Champagne]] branch, ruling the County of Champagne, became the more powerful line.
county-of-blois.e: From the 1230s the house of [[e:house-of-chatillon|Châtillon]] held Blois. The last count, [[e:guy-ii-of-blois|Guy II]], sold it to [[e:louis-i-duke-of-orleans|Louis of Orléans]] in 1391, with possession at his death in 1397. When Louis's grandson, born at Blois, became [[e:louis-xii-of-france|Louis XII]] in 1498, it joined the [[s:kingdom-of-france|Kingdom of France]].

carpetani.t: A people of the central Meseta around Toledo and Madrid, defeated by Hannibal on the Tagus before Rome absorbed their lands.
carpetani.o: The Carpetani occupied the upper and middle [[e:tagus|Tagus]] basin, in modern [[e:madrid|Madrid]], [[e:toledo|Toledo]] and [[e:ciudad-real|Ciudad Real]], from the second half of the first millennium BCE. Their language is thought to have been Celtic, though Iberian influences were strong.
carpetani.r: They lived in fortified towns such as [[e:toledo|Toletum]] and [[e:complutum|Complutum]], on a farming and herding economy of the open plateau. Their political organisation is little known, but they could field large armies. In 220 BCE [[e:hannibal|Hannibal]] defeated a coalition of Carpetani, [[s:olcades|Olcades]] and [[s:vaccaei|Vaccaei]] at the crossing of the [[e:tagus|Tagus]].
carpetani.e: [[e:rome|Rome]] reached their land in the early 2nd century BCE: [[e:marcus-fulvius-nobilior|Marcus Fulvius Nobilior]] won a battle near [[e:toledo|Toletum]] in 193 BCE and took the town in 192 BCE, and [[e:tiberius-sempronius-gracchus-consul-177-bc|Tiberius Sempronius Gracchus]] pacified the region by 179 BCE. They became part of [[s:hispania-citerior|Hispania Citerior]], and Toletum grew into Roman and later Visigothic Toledo.

canton-of-schaffhausen.t: A Rhine city above the great falls that regained its freedom from the Habsburgs in 1415 and joined the Swiss Confederacy in 1501.
canton-of-schaffhausen.o: Schaffhausen grew around the Benedictine abbey of All Saints, founded in 1049, at the point where [[e:rhine|Rhine]] boats had to unload above the falls. Pledged to the [[e:habsburg-dynasty|Habsburgs]] in 1330, it regained imperial status in 1415, when Duke [[e:frederick-iv-duke-of-austria|Frederick IV]] of [[e:austria|Austria]] was outlawed during the [[e:council-of-constance|Council of Constance]], and afterwards bought out the remaining claims.
canton-of-schaffhausen.r: The [[e:guild|guilds]] dominated the council from 1411. Schaffhausen lived from moving goods around the [[e:rhine|Rhine]] Falls, especially salt, wine and grain. It allied with the Confederates in 1454 and joined as the twelfth canton in 1501. It adopted the Reformed faith in 1529 and governed a rural territory north of the Rhine.
canton-of-schaffhausen.e: The old regime ended in 1798 with the [[s:helvetic-republic|Helvetic Republic]], and the canton was restored in 1803. It remains a Swiss canton, the only one lying almost entirely north of the [[e:rhine|Rhine]].

chen-dynasty.t: The last of the Southern Dynasties, ruling the lower Yangtze from Jiankang until the Sui conquest of 589 reunited China after nearly three centuries of division.
chen-dynasty.o: The [[s:liang-dynasty|Liang dynasty]] collapsed in the 550s under the [[e:hou-jing|Hou Jing]] rebellion and northern invasions. The general [[e:emperor-wu-of-chen|Chen Baxian]], who had defeated Hou Jing, gained control of [[e:jiankang|Jiankang]] and in 557 accepted the abdication of the boy Emperor Jing of [[s:liang-liang-shidu|Liang]], founding Chen with himself as [[e:emperor-wu-of-han|Emperor Wu]].
chen-dynasty.r: Chen was the smallest of the southern states, having lost [[e:sichuan|Sichuan]] and the lands north of the [[e:yangtze-river|Yangtze]], and it relied on local strongmen as much as on the old émigré aristocracy. [[e:jiankang|Jiankang]] remained a centre of Buddhist learning and courtly poetry. [[e:emperor-xuan-of-chen|Emperor Xuan]] recovered the Huai river region in 573 but lost it again to [[s:northern-zhou|Northern Zhou]] by 579.
chen-dynasty.e: The last ruler, [[e:chen-shubao|Chen Shubao]], became a byword for frivolous palace life. In 589 [[e:sui-dynasty|Sui]] armies crossed the [[e:yangtze-river|Yangtze]] and took [[e:jiankang|Jiankang]] with little resistance; Chen Shubao was taken to [[e:changan|Chang'an]] and lived out his life in comfortable captivity. [[e:china|China]] was united again under the [[s:sui-dynasty|Sui Dynasty]].

county-of-solms-braunfels.t: Hessian county on the Lahn ruled from Braunfels castle, whose family later sponsored the German settlement of New Braunfels in Texas.
county-of-solms-braunfels.o: The counts of Solms, named after a stream near [[s:free-imperial-city-of-wetzlar|Wetzlar]], divided their lands around 1258. One line took [[e:braunfels|Braunfels]] castle above the [[e:lahn|Lahn]] as its seat and became the counts of Solms-Braunfels, ruling lands between Wetzlar and the [[e:taunus|Taunus]], held directly from the Empire.
county-of-solms-braunfels.r: The county was small and rural, with farming, forests and some iron mining. Its counts, often serving as officers in foreign armies, inherited other Solms lands such as Greifenstein and Hungen. They adopted the [[e:calvinism|Reformed Protestant]] faith. In 1742 the head of the family, Friedrich Wilhelm, was raised to the rank of imperial prince.
county-of-solms-braunfels.e: Solms-[[e:braunfels|Braunfels]] was mediatised in 1806 and divided between [[s:county-of-nassau|Nassau]] and [[s:grand-duchy-of-hesse|Hesse-Darmstadt]], with the Nassau part passing to [[e:kingdom-of-prussia|Prussia]] in 1815. In 1845 [[e:prince-carl-of-solms-braunfels|Prince Carl of Solms-Braunfels]] led German settlers to [[e:texas|Texas]], founding [[e:new-braunfels|New Braunfels]].

crown-colony-of-labuan.t: Small British island colony off Borneo, founded as a coaling station and base against piracy in the South China Sea.
crown-colony-of-labuan.o: The [[s:brunei-sultanate|Brunei Sultanate]] ceded the island of Labuan to [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]] by treaty in 1846, under pressure after British naval action against Brunei. It was made a crown colony in 1848, with [[e:james-brooke|James Brooke]], the [[e:rajah-of-sarawak|Rajah of Sarawak]], as its first governor and [[e:hugh-low|Hugh Low]] as colonial secretary.
crown-colony-of-labuan.r: [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]] hoped Labuan would become a second [[s:singapore|Singapore]], a naval station supplied by local [[e:coal|coal]] and a base for suppressing piracy. Coal mines opened but repeatedly failed, the climate was unhealthy and trade stayed small. The colony was run by a governor and a handful of officials, with a mixed Malay, Chinese and Bruneian population.
crown-colony-of-labuan.e: Unable to pay its way, Labuan was handed to the [[e:british-north-borneo-company|British North Borneo Company]] to administer from 1890 to 1906. It then became part of the [[s:straits-settlements|Straits Settlements]], later of [[s:north-borneo|North Borneo]], and is today a federal territory of [[s:malaysia|Malaysia]].

cr.a: British Government, redraw by Ranking Update

county-of-hohenlohe.t: A Franconian county on the Kocher and Jagst rivers whose many branches of the Hohenlohe family ruled until mediatisation in 1806.
county-of-hohenlohe.o: The lords of [[e:weikersheim|Weikersheim]], later called Hohenlohe after a castle near Uffenheim, appear around 1153 as [[e:hohenstaufen|Staufer]] ministerials. They acquired lands on the [[e:tauber|Tauber]], [[e:kocher|Kocher]] and [[e:jagst|Jagst]], and in 1450 were recognised as counts of the Empire, building a territory centred on [[e:ohringen|Öhringen]], Weikersheim and Neuenstein.
county-of-hohenlohe.r: Hohenlohe was a rural land of farms, vineyards and small residence towns. The family split into numerous lines, divided between Lutheran Hohenlohe-Neuenstein and Catholic Hohenlohe-Waldenburg after the [[e:protestant-reformation|Reformation]]. [[e:weikersheim|Weikersheim]] castle, with its baroque garden, and Langenburg are among their residences. Several branches were raised to princes in the 18th century.
county-of-hohenlohe.e: In 1806 the Hohenlohe principalities were mediatised and divided between Württemberg and [[e:bavaria|Bavaria]]. The family remained prominent: [[e:chlodwig-zu-hohenlohe-schillingsfurst|Chlodwig zu Hohenlohe-Schillingsfürst]] served as German Chancellor from 1894 to 1900.

cochuah.t: A Maya province of eastern Yucatán centred on Tihosuco, conquered in 1544, whose region later became the cradle of the Caste War.
cochuah.o: Cochuah emerged after the collapse of the [[s:league-of-mayapan|League of Mayapan]] around 1441. It lay in the forests of east-central Yucatán, in what is now [[e:quintana-roo|Quintana Roo]], with [[e:tihosuco|Tihosuco]] and Ichmul among its main towns.
cochuah.r: Colonial sources describe Cochuah as a warlike province whose towns were governed by local lords. Its people farmed [[e:maize|maize]] and [[e:cotton|cotton]] and traded with the coastal provinces. Little else is recorded of its institutions.
cochuah.e: [[e:gaspar-pacheco|Gaspar]] and [[e:melchor-pacheco|Melchor Pacheco]] conquered Cochuah in 1544 with great violence, and it became part of the [[s:province-of-yucatan|Province of Yucatán]]. In 1847 the [[e:caste-war-of-yucatan|Caste War of Yucatán]], a long Maya uprising, broke out at nearby [[e:tepich|Tepich]] and centred on the [[e:tihosuco|Tihosuco]] district.

cumania.t: The vast steppe confederation of the Cumans or Polovtsians, partners and enemies of Rus', Hungary and Byzantium until the Mongols swept it away.
cumania.o: The [[e:cumans|Cumans]], called Polovtsians by the Rus' and [[e:kipchaks|Kipchaks]] in eastern sources, were Turkic nomads who moved west from the steppes of [[s:kazakhstan|Kazakhstan]] in the 11th century. Around 1060 they displaced the [[e:oghuz-turks|Oghuz]] and [[s:pechenegs|Pechenegs]] north of the [[e:black-sea|Black Sea]], and in 1068 they defeated the sons of [[e:yaroslav-the-wise|Yaroslav the Wise]] on the [[e:battle-of-the-alta-river-1068|Alta]] river.
cumania.r: Cumania was never a single state but a shifting union of tribes and clans under their own khans, such as [[e:boniak|Boniak]], [[e:sharukan|Sharukan]] and [[e:konchak|Konchak]]. They herded horses and sheep, traded through the Crimean ports and set up stone statues of ancestors on the steppe. Rus' princes fought them but also married their daughters and hired them in civil wars.
cumania.e: [[e:cumans|Cumans]] and Rus' were defeated together by the [[e:mongols|Mongols]] at the [[e:battle-of-the-kalka-river|Kalka]] in 1223, and the Mongol campaign of 1237 to 1241 conquered the steppe. Khan [[e:koten|Kotyan]] led thousands into [[e:hungary|Hungary]], and many [[e:kipchaks|Kipchaks]] were sold to [[e:egypt|Egypt]], where they became [[e:mamluk|Mamluks]]. Their language became the common speech of the [[s:golden-horde|Golden Horde]] and is recorded in the [[e:codex-cumanicus|Codex Cumanicus]].

cacicazgo-of-maguana.t: A Taíno chiefdom of central Hispaniola whose cacique Caonabo destroyed the first Spanish settlement, La Navidad, in 1493.
cacicazgo-of-maguana.o: Maguana occupied the mountainous centre of [[e:hispaniola|Hispaniola]], including the San Juan valley and the gold-bearing [[e:cibao|Cibao]] uplands. It was one of five principal chiefdoms on the island when the Spanish arrived in 1492, with roots in earlier [[e:taino|Taíno]] society.
cacicazgo-of-maguana.r: Its paramount cacique [[e:caonabo|Caonabo]], said by some sources to have come from the Lucayan islands, was a renowned war leader. His wife [[e:anacaona|Anacaona]] was the sister of [[e:bohechio|Bohechío]] of [[s:cacicazgo-of-jaragua|Jaragua]], linking the two chiefdoms. Its people farmed [[e:cassava|cassava]], held ballgames in plazas and worshipped zemís.
cacicazgo-of-maguana.e: [[e:caonabo|Caonabo]] destroyed the Spanish fort of [[e:la-navidad|La Navidad]] in 1493. In 1495 [[e:alonso-de-ojeda|Alonso de Ojeda]] captured him by a ruse, and he died at sea on the way to [[e:spain|Spain]]. Spanish forces then broke Maguana's resistance and imposed tribute in gold.

crown-of-aragon.t: A composite Mediterranean monarchy uniting Aragon, Catalonia, Valencia and Majorca, whose rule stretched to Sicily, Sardinia, Naples and Athens.
crown-of-aragon.o: The marriage of [[e:petronilla-of-aragon|Petronila]] of the [[s:kingdom-of-aragon|Kingdom of Aragon]] and [[e:ramon-berenguer-iv-count-of-barcelona|Ramon Berenguer IV of Barcelona]] united their lands, and their son [[e:alfonso-ii-of-aragon|Alfonso II]] inherited both in 1162. [[e:james-i-of-aragon|James I]] the Conqueror then took [[e:mallorca|Majorca]] in 1229 and [[e:valencia|Valencia]] in 1238, creating the [[s:kingdom-of-majorca|Kingdom of Majorca]] and the [[s:kingdom-of-valencia|Kingdom of Valencia]].
crown-of-aragon.r: The Crown was a federation: each realm kept its own laws, [[e:corte|Cortes]] and currency under a shared king. Catalan merchants and naval power drove expansion, with [[e:sicily|Sicily]] won in 1282, [[e:sardinia|Sardinia]] from 1323 and [[e:naples|Naples]] in 1442. After the [[e:compromise-of-caspe|Compromise of Caspe]] in 1412 the Castilian [[e:house-of-trastamara|Trastámara]] dynasty ruled.
crown-of-aragon.e: The marriage of [[e:ferdinand-ii-of-aragon|Ferdinand II]] and Isabella of [[s:kingdom-of-castile|Castile]] in 1469 joined the Crown to [[e:kingdom-of-castile|Castile]], later [[s:habsburg-spain|Habsburg Spain]]. The separate institutions survived until the [[e:nueva-planta-decrees|Nueva Planta decrees]] of 1707-1716 that followed the [[e:war-of-the-spanish-succession|War of the Spanish Succession]].

county-of-nassau-saarbrucken.t: A Nassau county on the Saar whose 18th-century princes made Saarbrücken a Baroque residence and an early centre of coal mining.
county-of-nassau-saarbrucken.o: The County of [[e:saarbrucken|Saarbrücken]] passed by marriage to the Walramian Nassaus when Count John I of the [[s:county-of-nassau-weilburg|County of Nassau-Weilburg]] married its heiress [[s:sultanate-of-anjouan|Johanna]]. In 1381 their son [[e:philip-i-count-of-nassau-saarbrucken|Philip I]] inherited it, and Saarbrücken became the seat of a [[s:county-of-nassau|Nassau]] line that ruled lands on the [[e:saar-river|Saar]] and in [[s:duchy-of-lorraine|Lorraine]].
county-of-nassau-saarbrucken.r: Elisabeth of [[s:duchy-of-lorraine|Lorraine]], wife of [[e:philip-i-count-of-nassau-saarbrucken|Philip I]], translated French chansons de geste into German prose in the 15th century. The counts introduced the [[e:protestant-reformation|Lutheran Reformation]] in 1575. In the 18th century Prince [[e:william-henry-prince-of-nassau-saarbrucken|William Henry]] and his son Louis made [[e:saarbrucken|Saarbrücken]] a [[e:baroque|Baroque]] residence, with buildings by [[e:friedrich-joachim-stengel|Friedrich Joachim Stengel]] including the [[e:ludwigskirche|Ludwigskirche]], and developed [[e:coal|coal]] mining and ironworks.
county-of-nassau-saarbrucken.e: French revolutionary troops occupied the county in 1793, and [[e:france|France]] annexed the left bank of the [[e:rhine|Rhine]] in 1797. In 1815 [[e:saarbrucken|Saarbrücken]] went to [[e:kingdom-of-prussia|Prussia]]; it is now the capital of the German state of [[e:saarland|Saarland]].

colonial-nigeria.t: The British colony formed in 1914 by joining the northern and southern protectorates, the most populous colony in Africa and independent as Nigeria in 1960.
colonial-nigeria.o: On 1 January 1914 [[e:frederick-lugard|Frederick Lugard]] amalgamated the [[s:protectorate-of-northern-nigeria|Protectorate of Northern Nigeria]] and the [[s:protectorate-of-southern-nigeria|Protectorate of Southern Nigeria]] into the Colony and [[e:protectorate|Protectorate]] of [[e:nigeria|Nigeria]], with its capital at [[s:kingdom-of-lagos|Lagos]]. The move mainly allowed the revenues of the south to cover the costs of the north; the two halves continued to be administered largely separately.
colonial-nigeria.r: British rule relied on [[e:indirect-rule|indirect rule]] through [[e:emir|emirs]] and chiefs, extended to the south through appointed warrant chiefs, a policy that provoked the [[e:aba-womens-war|Aba Women's War]] of 1929. [[e:nigeria|Nigeria]] exported [[e:palm-oil|palm oil]], cocoa, [[e:groundnut|groundnuts]], [[e:cotton|cotton]] and [[e:tin|tin]]. Nationalist politics grew around [[e:herbert-macaulay|Herbert Macaulay]] and [[e:nnamdi-azikiwe|Nnamdi Azikiwe]], and the constitutions of 1946, 1951 and 1954 created a federation of Northern, Western and Eastern regions.
colonial-nigeria.e: The regions became self-governing in the late 1950s, led by [[e:ahmadu-bello|Ahmadu Bello]], [[e:obafemi-awolowo|Obafemi Awolowo]] and [[e:nnamdi-azikiwe|Azikiwe]]. [[e:abubakar-tafawa-balewa|Abubakar Tafawa Balewa]] became federal prime minister in 1957, and [[e:nigeria|Nigeria]] became independent on 1 October 1960.

captaincy-general-of-chile.t: Spain's southernmost colony in the Americas, a frontier realm defined by a long war against the Mapuche and later the birthplace of the Chilean republic.
captaincy-general-of-chile.o: [[e:pedro-de-valdivia|Pedro de Valdivia]] led an expedition from [[e:peru|Peru]] and founded [[s:spanish-jamaica|Santiago]] in February 1541. He extended Spanish settlement south, founding [[e:concepcion-chile|Concepción]] and [[e:valdivia|Valdivia]], but was killed by [[e:mapuche|the Mapuche]] under [[e:lautaro|Lautaro]] at [[e:battle-of-tucapel|Tucapel]] in 1553. The territory was governed as the [[e:governorate|Governorate]] of [[s:republic-of-chile|Chile]] within the [[s:viceroyalty-of-peru|Viceroyalty of Peru]].
captaincy-general-of-chile.r: Chile's governor was also captain-general because of the [[e:arauco-war|Arauco War]] against [[e:mapuche|the Mapuche]]. After the [[s:araucania|Mapuche]] victory at [[e:battle-of-curalaba|Curalaba]] in 1598 destroyed the southern towns, the frontier settled on the [[e:biobio-river|Biobío]] river with a permanent army. The Royal [[e:audiencia|Audiencia]] sat at [[s:spanish-jamaica|Santiago]] from 1609. The economy rested on wheat, tallow and livestock sold to [[e:peru|Peru]], worked on large [[e:hacienda|haciendas]]. The [[e:bourbon-reforms|Bourbon reforms]] made [[s:republic-of-chile|Chile]] a captaincy general more independent of [[e:lima|Lima]] in 1798.
captaincy-general-of-chile.e: A [[e:criollo-people|Creole]] junta took power in 1810, opening the [[s:patria-vieja|Patria Vieja]]. Royalist forces regained control in 1814, but [[e:jose-de-san-martin|José de San Martín]] and [[e:bernardo-ohiggins|Bernardo O'Higgins]] won at [[e:battle-of-chacabuco|Chacabuco]] in 1817 and [[e:battle-of-maipu|Maipú]] in 1818, when [[s:republic-of-chile|Chile]] declared independence as the Republic of Chile.

county-of-hohenems.t: A small Vorarlberg county whose counts rose through papal patronage and whose palace library yielded two manuscripts of the Nibelungenlied.
county-of-hohenems.o: The lords of Ems held castles above the [[e:rhine|Rhine]] valley near [[e:dornbirn|Dornbirn]] from the 12th century. Wolf Dietrich of Ems married Chiara de Medici, whose brother became [[e:pope-pius-iv|Pope Pius IV]] in 1559; with papal backing their sons rose quickly, and in 1560 the family was made imperial counts of Hohenems.
county-of-hohenems.r: Count [[e:jakob-hannibal-i-of-hohenems|Jakob Hannibal I]] was a general in Spanish service, while his brother [[e:mark-sittich-von-hohenems-altemps|Mark Sittich]] became a cardinal. Count Kaspar built up the [[e:renaissance|Renaissance]] palace at Hohenems and in 1617 invited Jewish families to settle, founding a notable Jewish community. The counts also acquired the [[s:county-of-vaduz|County of Vaduz]] and the [[s:lordship-of-schellenberg|Lordship of Schellenberg]].
county-of-hohenems.e: Heavy debts forced the sale of [[s:county-of-vaduz|Vaduz]] and [[s:lordship-of-schellenberg|Schellenberg]] to [[s:principality-of-liechtenstein|Liechtenstein]]. When the male line died out in 1759, the county reverted to [[e:austria|Austria]] and became part of [[e:vorarlberg|Vorarlberg]]. Two [[e:manuscript|manuscripts]] of the [[e:nibelungenlied|Nibelungenlied]] were found in the palace library in 1755 and 1779.

cahokia.t: The largest city in North America north of Mexico before the 18th century, whose Monks Mound remains the largest prehistoric earthwork in the Americas.
cahokia.o: Around 1050 a cluster of villages on the American Bottom, the [[e:mississippi-river|Mississippi]] floodplain opposite modern St Louis, was rapidly rebuilt to a grand plan. Archaeologists call this sudden change the Big Bang: a central plaza was levelled, [[e:monks-mound|Monks Mound]] was raised, and thousands of people gathered in what was likely the first Mississippian capital.
cahokia.r: At its peak around 1100 Cahokia may have housed 10,000 to 20,000 people, fed by [[e:maize|maize]] farming. Rulers lived atop [[e:monks-mound|Monks Mound]], some 30 metres high, and circles of [[e:timber|timber]] posts, the so-called [[e:cahokia-woodhenge|Woodhenge]], marked solar events. Mound 72 held a high-status burial on a bed of 20,000 shell [[e:bead|beads]], with many sacrificed people. Cahokian pottery, stone figurines and the chunkey game spread Mississippian ideas across the [[e:midwestern-united-states|Midwest]] and South.
cahokia.e: Cahokia declined after about 1200, when a palisade was built around its core, and was largely abandoned by 1350; flooding, drought, exhausted resources and political strife have all been proposed. Its name comes from a later subgroup of the [[s:illinois-confederation|Illinois Confederation]]. It became a [[e:unesco-world-heritage-site|UNESCO World Heritage Site]] in 1982.

county-of-vermandois.t: A Picard county held by descendants of Charlemagne, whose counts were king-makers in 10th-century France before the land returned to the crown.
county-of-vermandois.o: Herbert I, a Carolingian descended from Bernard of [[e:italy|Italy]], became count of Vermandois around 896, with his seat at [[e:saint-quentin|Saint-Quentin]]. His family built up lands across [[e:picardy|Picardy]] and [[s:county-of-champagne|Champagne]] during the struggles between the Carolingian kings and the [[e:robertians|Robertians]].
county-of-vermandois.r: [[e:herbert-ii-count-of-vermandois|Herbert II]] was the most powerful lord of northern [[e:france|France]] in the 920s, holding [[e:charles-the-simple|King Charles the Simple]] prisoner at [[e:peronne|Péronne]] until the king's death in 929 and seizing the archbishopric of [[e:reims|Reims]] for his young son. Later counts were less prominent. Around 1080 the heiress [[e:adelaide-countess-of-vermandois|Adelaide]] married [[e:hugh-of-vermandois|Hugh of Vermandois]], brother of King Philip I and a leader of the [[e:first-crusade|First Crusade]].
county-of-vermandois.e: In the 12th century the county passed by marriage to [[e:philip-i-count-of-flanders|Philip of Alsace]], count of [[s:county-of-flanders|Flanders]], who lost much of it to [[e:philip-ii-of-france|Philip II of France]] in the [[e:treaty-of-boves|Treaty of Boves]] in 1185. After the death of Countess Eleanor in 1213 the rest was absorbed by the [[s:kingdom-of-france|Kingdom of France]].

chouchi.t: The mountain stronghold of the Di people's Yang clan in southern Gansu, which survived through the Sixteen Kingdoms by balancing northern and southern dynasties.
chouchi.o: In 296 [[e:yang-maosou|Yang Maosou]], chief of a Di clan from the upper [[e:han-river|Han River]] region, led his people to Chouchi, a flat-topped mountain near modern Xihe in southern [[e:gansu|Gansu]], whose natural defences made it a refuge during the collapse of the [[s:western-jin|Western Jin]].
chouchi.r: The Yang rulers took titles from whichever dynasty was strongest, Jin, [[s:former-qin|Former Qin]], [[s:northern-wei|Northern Wei]] or the southern courts, while governing their Di subjects by their own customs. Their realm in the hills between [[e:gansu|Gansu]], [[e:shaanxi|Shaanxi]] and [[e:sichuan|Sichuan]] controlled routes between north and south. It was destroyed by Former [[e:qin-dynasty|Qin]] in 371 and revived in 385, later as several related principalities centred on Wudu.
chouchi.e: Under pressure from the [[s:northern-wei|Northern Wei]] and the southern dynasties, the Yang principalities were absorbed one by one; the register follows the end of their independence in 506, when Northern Wei took Wuxing. Yang descendants kept local power in the region into the 6th century.

captaincy-of-rio-de-janeiro.t: The royal captaincy founded after the expulsion of the French from Guanabara Bay, which grew into the capital of Brazil and seat of a European monarchy.
captaincy-of-rio-de-janeiro.o: After Portuguese forces drove the French of [[s:france-antarctique|France Antarctique]] from [[e:guanabara-bay|Guanabara Bay]], the crown established the Captaincy of [[e:rio-de-janeiro|Rio de Janeiro]] in 1567 as a royal rather than hereditary captaincy. The city of São Sebastião do Rio de Janeiro, founded by [[e:estacio-de-sa|Estácio de Sá]] in 1565, was moved to the [[e:morro-do-castelo|Morro do Castelo]].
captaincy-of-rio-de-janeiro.r: [[e:rio-de-janeiro|Rio]] grew on [[e:sugar-plantation|sugar]] and as a port for trade with the [[e:rio-de-la-plata|River Plate]] and [[s:portuguese-angola|Angola]]. The Sá family, especially [[e:salvador-correia-de-sa-e-benevides|Salvador Correia de Sá]], dominated its politics in the 17th century. With the gold rush in [[s:captaincy-of-minas-gerais|Minas Gerais]] from the 1690s, Rio became the main outlet for gold and the main entry for enslaved Africans. French corsairs sacked it in 1711. In 1763 it replaced [[e:salvador|Salvador]] as capital of the [[s:state-of-brazil|State of Brazil]].
captaincy-of-rio-de-janeiro.e: In 1808 the Portuguese royal family arrived, making [[e:rio-de-janeiro|Rio]] the capital of the Portuguese empire and, from 1815, of the [[s:kingdom-of-brazil|Kingdom of Brazil]]. In 1821 the captaincy became a province, and in 1822 Rio was the capital of the independent [[e:brazilian-empire|Empire of Brazil]].

cr.a: Tonyjeff, based on ancient national symbol.

canton-of-uri.t: Alpine valley community guarding the Gotthard road, a founding member of the Swiss Confederacy and home of the William Tell legend.
canton-of-uri.o: In 853 [[e:louis-the-german|Louis the German]] gave the [[e:reuss-river|Reuss]] valley of Uri to the [[e:fraumunster|Fraumünster]] abbey of [[s:canton-of-zurich|Zürich]]. When the [[e:gotthard-pass|Gotthard Pass]] was opened to traffic in the early 13th century, the valley gained strategic value, and in 1231 King [[e:henry-vii-of-germany|Henry VII]] bought it back from the [[e:habsburg-dynasty|Habsburgs]] and granted it imperial immediacy. In 1291 Uri joined [[s:canton-of-schwyz|Schwyz]] and [[s:canton-of-unterwalden|Unterwalden]] in the [[e:federal-charter-of-1291|Federal Charter]].
canton-of-uri.r: Free peasants governed themselves through the [[e:landsgemeinde|Landsgemeinde]], the assembly of all men, which elected a [[e:landammann|Landammann]]. Wealth came from [[e:cattle|cattle]], transport across the [[e:gotthard-pass|Gotthard]] and [[e:mercenary|mercenary]] service. Uri expanded southwards over the pass, taking the [[e:leventina|Leventina]] valley in the 15th century. The legend of [[e:william-tell|William Tell]] is set in [[e:altdorf-uri|Altdorf]]. The canton stayed Catholic during the [[e:protestant-reformation|Reformation]].
canton-of-uri.e: The French invasion of 1798 brought Uri into the [[s:helvetic-republic|Helvetic Republic]]. It was restored as a canton in 1803 and remains a canton of [[s:swiss-confederation|Switzerland]], crossed by the [[e:gotthard-pass|Gotthard]] road and railway tunnels.

county-of-henneberg.t: A Franconian county in the Thuringian Forest whose princely counts ruled from Schleusingen until their line died out in 1583.
county-of-henneberg.o: The Henneberg family appears in the late 11th century; its counts held the burgraviate of [[e:wurzburg|Würzburg]] and built Henneberg castle south of the [[e:thuringian-forest|Thuringian Forest]]. Their lands lay between [[e:franconia|Franconia]] and [[e:thuringia|Thuringia]], around [[e:meiningen|Meiningen]], [[e:schmalkalden|Schmalkalden]] and [[e:schleusingen|Schleusingen]].
county-of-henneberg.r: The counts divided into several lines, including Henneberg-[[e:schleusingen|Schleusingen]], raised to princely count in 1310. [[e:berthold-vii-count-of-henneberg-schleusingen|Berthold VII]] was an important adviser to [[e:louis-iv-holy-roman-emperor|Emperor Louis IV]]. The counts adopted [[e:lutheranism|Lutheranism]], and Count [[e:george-ernest-count-of-henneberg-schleusingen|George Ernest]] founded a [[e:gymnasium|gymnasium]] at Schleusingen in 1577.
