county-of-henneberg.e: A treaty of 1554 settled inheritance on the [[e:house-of-wettin|Wettins]], and when [[e:george-ernest-count-of-henneberg-schleusingen|George Ernest]] died without heirs in 1583, the county passed to the Ernestine and Albertine branches of [[e:saxony|Saxony]], with parts to [[e:hesse|Hesse]]. Its lands later formed parts of Saxe-[[e:meiningen|Meiningen]] and [[e:thuringia|Thuringia]].

cambay-state.t: A Muslim-ruled port state on the Gulf of Khambhat, founded by the last Mughal governors of Gujarat as the old harbour silted up.
cambay-state.o: [[e:momin-khan-i|Mirza Ja'far Najm-ud-daula]], titled Momin Khan I, was a Mughal official of Persian descent in [[e:gujarat|Gujarat]]. As imperial authority collapsed he made himself master of the ancient port of [[e:khambhat|Cambay]] (Khambhat) around 1730, founding a line of Nawabs who survived [[e:maratha-empire|Maratha]] pressure by paying them a share of the revenue.
cambay-state.r: [[e:khambhat|Cambay]] had been one of [[e:india|India's]] great ports, but silting of the gulf reduced it to a modest town known for agate and cornelian working, textiles and salt. The Nawabs, who were Shia, ruled a mostly [[e:hinduism|Hindu]] population and accepted British protection in the late 18th century, later belonging to the [[e:gujarat-states-agency|Gujarat States Agency]] with an 11-gun salute.
cambay-state.e: The last Nawab acceded to [[e:india|India]], and in 1948 [[e:khambhat|Cambay]] was merged into [[e:bombay-state|Bombay State]]. Since 1960 Khambhat has been part of [[e:gujarat|Gujarat's]] [[e:anand-district|Anand district]].

chios.t: Rich Ionian island state, famed for its wine and mastic, a major naval power and home of the Homeridae who claimed descent from Homer.
chios.o: [[e:ionia|Ionian Greeks]] settled Chios, a large island off the [[s:erythrae|Erythrae]] peninsula, c. 1000 BCE, and it became one of the twelve members of the [[s:ionian-league|Ionian League]]. By the 6th century BCE it was a wealthy trading state; an inscribed law of c. 575 to 550 BCE mentions a popular council.
chios.r: Chios exported wine and mastic and was said to be the first Greek state to buy slaves. The [[e:homeridae|Homeridae]] [[e:guild|guild]] of poets claimed descent from [[e:homer|Homer]]. It sent 100 ships to the [[e:battle-of-lade|Battle of Lade]] in 494 BCE. In the [[s:delian-league|Delian League]] it kept its own fleet, before revolting in 412 BCE and later leaving the [[s:second-athenian-league|Second Athenian League]] in the [[e:social-war-357-355-bce|Social War]] of 357 BCE.
chios.e: In 86 BCE [[e:mithridates-vi-of-pontus|Mithridates]] of the [[s:kingdom-of-pontus|Kingdom of Pontus]] deported the Chians to the [[e:black-sea|Black Sea]]; [[e:sulla|Sulla]] restored them and [[e:rome|Rome]] confirmed their freedom. The island stayed prosperous under Roman rule and later Genoese and Ottoman masters.

canton-of-granada.t: A short-lived federalist canton proclaimed in Granada in July 1873 and ended by General Pavía's troops in August.
canton-of-granada.o: On 20 July 1873 the federalists of [[e:granada|Granada]] proclaimed a sovereign canton, part of the [[e:cantonal-rebellion|Cantonal Rebellion]] that swept southern and eastern [[e:spain|Spain]] against the government of the [[s:spanish-first-republic|Spanish First Republic]].
canton-of-granada.r: A cantonal junta took over the city, organised militias and proposed radical measures, including the demolition of some old fortifications and the taxing of the wealthy. It had little time and few resources to carry them out.
canton-of-granada.e: After crushing the cantons of [[e:seville|Seville]] and Cádiz, General [[e:manuel-pavia-y-rodriguez-de-alburquerque|Manuel Pavía's]] forces entered [[e:granada|Granada]] on 12 August 1873, and the canton dissolved without serious resistance.

county-palatine-of-cephalonia-and-zakynt.t: Ionian island county ruled by the Orsini and Tocco families for three centuries, a link between Italy, the Frankish Morea and Epirus.
county-palatine-of-cephalonia-and-zakynt.o: In 1185 the Norman admiral [[e:margaritus-of-brindisi|Margaritus of Brindisi]] took [[e:kefalonia|Cephalonia]] and [[e:zakynthos|Zakynthos]] from [[s:byzantium|Byzantium]] for [[e:william-ii-of-sicily|William II of Sicily]]. By about 1195 the islands were held by [[e:matthew-orsini|Matthew Orsini]], of an Apulian family, who founded a hereditary lordship and placed himself in turn under the protection of the Pope, [[e:venice|Venice]] and the [[s:principality-of-achaea|Principality of Achaea]].
county-palatine-of-cephalonia-and-zakynt.r: The counts ruled a Greek [[e:eastern-orthodox-church|Orthodox]] population through Italian and Greek officials, with a [[e:latin|Latin]] [[e:bishop|bishop]] alongside the Orthodox clergy. The Orsini intermarried with the rulers of the [[s:despotate-of-epirus|Despotate of Epirus]] and later acquired it. In 1357 the county passed to [[e:leonardo-i-tocco|Leonardo I Tocco]], and his son [[e:carlo-i-tocco|Carlo I Tocco]] extended [[e:tocco-family|Tocco]] power to [[e:ioannina|Ioannina]] and Arta.
county-palatine-of-cephalonia-and-zakynt.e: [[e:leonardo-iii-tocco|Leonardo III Tocco]] lost his mainland lands to the [[e:ottoman-empire|Ottomans]] and in 1479 the islands as well, fleeing to [[e:italy|Italy]]. [[e:venice|Venice]] won [[e:zakynthos|Zakynthos]] in 1485 and [[e:kefalonia|Cephalonia]] in 1500, making them part of the [[s:venetian-ionian-islands|Venetian Ionian Islands]].

colony-of-martinique.t: French Caribbean sugar colony, birthplace of the Empress Joséphine and later of the négritude movement, which became an overseas department of France in 1946.
colony-of-martinique.o: [[e:pierre-belain-desnambuc|Pierre Belain d'Esnambuc]] landed at [[e:saint-pierre-martinique|Saint-Pierre]] in 1635 and claimed the island for the [[e:compagnie-des-iles-de-lamerique|Compagnie des Îles d'Amérique]]. The [[e:kalinago|Kalinago]] were pushed to the east and then expelled by 1660. Martinique came under direct royal rule in 1674 and became the seat of the governor-general of the French [[e:windward-islands|Windward Islands]].
colony-of-martinique.r: Planter society was built on [[e:sugar-plantation|sugar]], [[e:coffee-economy|coffee]] and [[e:cacao|cacao]] estates worked by enslaved Africans under the [[e:code-noir|Code Noir]]. [[e:saint-pierre-martinique|Saint-Pierre]] was the commercial and cultural centre, while [[e:fort-de-france|Fort-Royal]], later Fort-de-[[e:france|France]], held the administration. [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]] occupied Martinique several times, notably during 1794 to 1802, which kept [[e:slavery|slavery]] in force there during the revolutionary abolition. [[e:josephine-de-beauharnais|Joséphine de Beauharnais]] was born at [[e:les-trois-ilets|Trois-Îlets]] in 1763.
colony-of-martinique.e: [[e:slavery|Slavery]] ended in 1848 after a rising in [[e:saint-pierre-martinique|Saint-Pierre]]. The eruption of [[e:mount-pelee|Mount Pelée]] in 1902 destroyed Saint-Pierre and killed about 28,000 people. Under a 1946 law championed by [[e:aime-cesaire|Aimé Césaire]], Martinique became an overseas [[e:departement|department]] of [[e:france|France]], as it remains.

cyme-aeolis.t: The largest of the Aeolian cities on the Anatolian coast, home of Hesiod's father and the historian Ephorus.
cyme-aeolis.o: [[e:aeolians|Aeolian Greeks]] founded Cyme on the coast north of the [[e:gediz-river|Hermus]], near modern [[e:aliaga|Aliağa]], c. 1000 BCE. It became the leading city of the Aeolian dodecapolis, and tradition held that [[e:hesiod|Hesiod's]] father sailed from Cyme to [[e:boeotia|Boeotia]]. A Cymaean princess was said to have married [[e:midas|King Midas]] of [[s:kingdom-of-phrygia|Phrygia]].
cyme-aeolis.r: Cyme was a commercial port, minting coins from the 6th century BCE. It fell to the [[s:kingdom-of-lydia|Kingdom of Lydia]] and then the [[s:achaemenid-empire|Achaemenid Empire]]; its tyrant [[e:aristagoras-of-cyme|Aristagoras]] was among those guarding Darius's bridge over the [[e:danube|Danube]] c. 513 BCE. The city joined the [[e:ionian-revolt|Ionian Revolt]] and later the [[s:delian-league|Delian League]], and the historian [[e:ephorus|Ephorus]] was born there in the 4th century BCE.
cyme-aeolis.e: In the [[e:hellenistic-period|Hellenistic period]] Cyme passed between [[e:seleucid-empire|Seleucid]] and [[e:pergamenes|Pergamene]] control and kept its civic institutions. It came under [[e:rome|Rome]] when the province of Asia was organised in 129 BCE, and remained a modest city into late antiquity.

cenel-loairn.t: A leading kindred of Dal Riata in northern Argyll, rivals of Cenel nGabrain, whose descendants may later have ruled Moray.
cenel-loairn.o: Cenel Loairn claimed descent from [[e:loarn-mac-eirc|Loarn mac Eirc]], said to be a brother of [[e:fergus-mor|Fergus Mor]], the legendary founder of [[s:dal-riata|Dal Riata]]. By the 7th century it controlled [[e:lorn|Lorn]], [[e:isle-of-mull|Mull]] and neighbouring districts in northern [[e:argyll|Argyll]], with its main stronghold at [[e:dunollie|Dunollie]] near [[e:oban|Oban]].
cenel-loairn.r: Like other Dal Riatan kindreds it owed naval service and tribute recorded in the [[e:senchus-fer-n-alban|Senchus fer nAlban]]. Its kings competed with [[s:cenel-ngabrain|Cenel nGabrain]] for the kingship of all [[s:dal-riata|Dal Riata]], and in the late 7th and early 8th centuries [[e:ferchar-fota|Ferchar Fota]] and his son [[e:selbach-mac-ferchair|Selbach]] held that position. Selbach burned [[e:dunollie|Dunollie]] in 701 and later rebuilt it.
cenel-loairn.e: [[e:selbach-mac-ferchair|Selbach]]'s defeat at sea in 719 and Pictish conquest under [[e:oengus-i-of-the-picts|Oengus son of Fergus]] in the 730s broke Cenel Loairn's power. Later Scottish genealogies traced the rulers of the [[s:kingdom-of-moray|Kingdom of Moray]], including [[e:macbeth-king-of-scotland|Macbeth]], to this kindred, though the link is debated.

commune-of-rome.t: A medieval Roman republic that revived the Senate on the Capitol in 1144 and briefly challenged the popes' rule over their own city.
commune-of-rome.o: In 1143–1144 the citizens of [[e:rome|Rome]] rebelled against [[e:pope-innocent-ii|Pope Innocent II]] and his aristocratic allies, revived the Senate on the [[e:capitoline-hill|Capitoline Hill]] and dated their documents from the 'renewal of the Senate'. [[e:giordano-pierleoni|Giordano Pierleoni]] was named patrician.
commune-of-rome.r: The commune was governed by an elected Senate of up to 56 members, drawing on memories of ancient [[e:rome|Rome]]. From 1145 the reformer [[e:arnold-of-brescia|Arnold of Brescia]] preached against papal temporal power and supported the republic. It struggled against the popes and the [[s:papal-states|Papal States]], and was opposed by [[e:frederick-barbarossa|Frederick Barbarossa]], who handed Arnold over for execution in 1155. Rome also fought neighbouring towns such as [[s:tibur|Tivoli]].
commune-of-rome.e: In 1188 a pact with [[e:pope-clement-iii|Pope Clement III]] recognised the Senate in return for papal [[e:sovereignty|sovereignty]]. Around 1193 [[e:benedetto-carushomo|Benedetto Carushomo]] replaced the many senators with a single senator, and the commune's independent phase ended, though the [[e:roman-senate|Roman Senate]] continued as a city office under the popes.

cynetes.t: The people of the Algarve, named by Herodotus as the westernmost inhabitants of Europe and linked to the enigmatic south-western script.
cynetes.o: The Cynetes, or Conii, lived in the far south of modern Portugal, in the [[e:algarve|Algarve]] and lower [[e:alentejo|Alentejo]]. [[e:herodotus|Herodotus]] in the 5th century BCE called them the most westerly people of [[e:europe|Europe]], beyond the [[e:celts|Celts]]. Their lands lay on the Atlantic routes that connected [[s:tartessos|Tartessos]] with the north.
cynetes.r: Their region holds most of the inscribed stone stelae in the south-western script, the oldest writing in [[e:iberia|Iberia]], dated to the 7th to 5th centuries BCE; the language they record is undeciphered and debated. Little is known of their political organisation, though Appian names a town, Conistorgis, as their chief place.
cynetes.e: In 153 BCE [[s:lusitanians|Lusitanians]] raiding Roman territory captured Conistorgis, then held by allies of [[e:rome|Rome]]. The Cynetes were absorbed into the Roman province of [[s:hispania-ulterior|Hispania Ulterior]] and later [[s:lusitania|Lusitania]], and their name disappears from the record.

catuvellauni.t: The leading power of late Iron Age Britain, whose king Cunobelinus ruled much of the south-east and whose sons led resistance to the Roman invasion of 43.
catuvellauni.o: The Catuvellauni held the lands north of the [[e:river-thames|Thames]] around [[e:hertfordshire|Hertfordshire]]. [[e:cassivellaunus|Cassivellaunus]], who commanded British resistance to [[e:julius-caesar|Julius Caesar]] in 54 BCE, is usually thought to have been their leader, with his stronghold perhaps at Wheathampstead. By the late 1st century BCE their king [[e:tasciovanus|Tasciovanus]] was minting coins at [[e:verulamium|Verlamion]], near modern [[e:st-albans|St Albans]].
catuvellauni.r: Their rulers issued abundant gold coinage, some styled with the [[e:latin|Latin]] REX, and imported wine, [[e:silver|silver]] and fine pottery from the Roman world, as rich burials at Welwyn and Folly Lane show. [[e:cunobelinus|Cunobelinus]], ruling from about 9 to 40 CE from [[e:camulodunum|Camulodunum]], which he took from the [[s:trinovantes|Trinovantes]], extended influence over Kent and much of the south-east; [[e:suetonius|Suetonius]] called him king of the [[e:britons-celtic-people|Britons]].
catuvellauni.e: After [[e:cunobelinus|Cunobelinus]] died, his sons [[e:togodumnus|Togodumnus]] and [[e:caratacus|Caratacus]] provoked [[e:rome|Rome]] by attacking the [[s:atrebates-britain|Atrebates (Britain)]]. [[e:claudius|Claudius]] invaded in 43; Togodumnus was killed and Caratacus fled west to fight on among the [[s:silures|Silures]] and [[s:ordovices|Ordovices]] until 51. The tribe became the civitas Catuvellaunorum, centred on [[e:verulamium|Verulamium]], in [[s:roman-britain|Roman Britain]].

cholula.t: A great holy city of the Puebla valley, home to the largest pyramid by volume in the world and a centre of the cult of Quetzalcoatl.
cholula.o: Cholula was inhabited from the Preclassic, and its [[e:great-pyramid-of-cholula|Great Pyramid]], Tlachihualtepetl, was built in stages from about 200 BCE. Traditions in the [[e:historia-tolteca-chichimeca|Historia Tolteca-Chichimeca]] say Tolteca-[[e:chichimeca|Chichimeca]] groups took control of the city in 1168, founding the Postclassic state.
cholula.r: Postclassic Cholula was ruled by two high priests and a council of nobles rather than a king. It was a famous pilgrimage centre of [[e:quetzalcoatl|Quetzalcoatl]] and a market city, known for fine polychrome pottery. Cholula had shifting alliances with [[s:tlaxcala|Tlaxcala]] and [[s:huexotzinco|Huexotzinco]] and at times with the [[s:aztec-empire|Aztec Empire]].
cholula.e: In 1519 [[e:hernan-cortes|Hernán Cortés]] and his Tlaxcalan allies massacred thousands of Cholulans in the main temple precinct. The Spanish built churches over its shrines, including one atop the [[e:great-pyramid-of-cholula|Great Pyramid]], and Cholula became a Spanish town.

chahamanas-of-shakambhari.t: The Chauhan Rajput dynasty of Sambhar and Ajmer, whose king Prithviraj Chauhan fought Muhammad of Ghor at Tarain.
chahamanas-of-shakambhari.o: Tradition names Vasudeva, said to have discovered the [[e:sambhar-salt-lake|Sambhar]] salt lake, as the dynasty's founder in the 7th century. The early [[e:chauhan|Chahamanas]] ruled the Sapadalaksha country around Shakambhari, modern Sambhar in [[e:rajasthan|Rajasthan]], as feudatories of the [[s:gurjara-pratihara|Gurjara-Pratihara]]. [[e:vigraharaja-ii|Vigraharaja II]] asserted independence in the 10th century, as recorded in the [[e:harsha|Harsha]] inscription of 973.
chahamanas-of-shakambhari.r: [[e:ajayaraja-ii|Ajayaraja]] founded [[e:ajmer|Ajmer]] around 1113 and made it the capital, and [[e:arnoraja|Arnoraja]] built the [[e:ana-sagar-lake|Ana Sagar]] lake. [[e:vigraharaja-iv|Vigraharaja IV]] took [[e:delhi|Delhi]] from the Tomara dynasty and wrote a [[e:sanskrit|Sanskrit]] play inscribed on stone in Ajmer. The [[e:chauhan|Chahamanas]] fought the [[s:paramara-dynasty|Paramara dynasty]], the [[s:chaulukya-dynasty|Chaulukya dynasty]] and the [[s:ghaznavid-empire|Ghaznavids]]. Their state rested on a warrior nobility, revenue from agriculture and the [[e:sambhar-salt-lake|Sambhar]] [[e:salt-trade|salt trade]].
chahamanas-of-shakambhari.e: [[e:prithviraj-chauhan|Prithviraja III]] defeated [[e:muhammad-of-ghor|Muhammad of Ghor]] at the [[e:first-battle-of-tarain|first battle of Tarain]] in 1191, but lost the second in 1192 and was executed. A relative ruled [[e:ajmer|Ajmer]] under Ghurid protection until 1194, and the branch at [[e:ranthambore-fort|Ranthambore]] continued. Prithviraj became a hero of [[e:rajputs|Rajput]] legend through the [[e:prithviraj-raso|Prithviraj Raso]].

corinth.t: Wealthy trading city on the Isthmus, founder of Syracuse and Corcyra and a leading power of Archaic Greece, destroyed by Rome in 146 BCE.
corinth.o: Corinth grew in the early [[e:iron-age|Iron Age]] on the Isthmus linking the [[e:peloponnese|Peloponnese]] to central [[e:greece|Greece]], below the fortress hill of [[e:acrocorinth|Acrocorinth]]. Dorian settlers formed the city, and from the 8th century BCE it was governed by the [[e:bacchiadae|Bacchiad]] clan, who founded [[s:corcyra|Corcyra]] and [[s:syracuse|Syracuse]] in 733 BCE.
corinth.r: [[e:cypselus|Cypselus]] overthrew the [[e:bacchiadae|Bacchiads]] c. 657 BCE, and his son [[e:periander|Periander]] made Corinth a major power. Corinthian pottery dominated [[e:mediterranean|Mediterranean]] markets in the 7th century BCE, and the diolkos let ships be dragged across the Isthmus. After the tyranny an oligarchy ruled, and Corinth was a key ally in the [[s:peloponnesian-league|Peloponnesian League]]; its quarrels with [[s:corcyra|Corcyra]] and [[s:athens|Athens]] helped start the [[e:peloponnesian-war|Peloponnesian War]].
corinth.e: Corinth fought [[s:sparta|Sparta]] in the [[e:corinthian-war|Corinthian War]] of 395 to 387 BCE. Macedonian kings garrisoned [[e:acrocorinth|Acrocorinth]] until [[e:aratus-of-sicyon|Aratus]] took it for the [[s:achaean-league|Achaean League]] in 243 BCE. [[e:lucius-mummius-achaicus|Lucius Mummius]] destroyed Corinth in 146 BCE; [[e:julius-caesar|Julius Caesar]] refounded it as a Roman colony in 44 BCE.
corinth.re: Greek religion; cults of Poseidon and Aphrodite

chersonesus-taurica.t: Democratic Greek city in south-western Crimea, colony of Heraclea Pontica, whose ruins near Sevastopol preserve a whole ancient landscape of farm plots.
chersonesus-taurica.o: Colonists from [[s:heraclea-pontica|Heraclea Pontica]], joined according to tradition by settlers from [[s:delos|Delos]], founded Chersonesus in 422-421 BCE on a small bay in the south-west of [[e:crimea|Crimea]], perhaps on the site of an earlier trading post. Over the 4th century BCE the city took control of the Heracleian peninsula and parts of the north-west Crimean coast.
chersonesus-taurica.r: Chersonesus was a democracy whose citizens swore an oath, preserved in a 3rd-century BCE inscription, to defend the city and never betray it. Its farmland was divided into regular rectangular plots, many planted with vineyards, and wine, fish and grain were its main exports. Its patron deity was the [[e:parthenos-chersonesus|Maiden]] (Parthenos).
chersonesus-taurica.e: Pressed by the [[e:scythians|Scythians]] of [[e:crimea|Crimea]] under [[e:scilurus|Scilurus]] and [[e:palakus|Palacus]], the city appealed to [[e:mithridates-vi-of-pontus|Mithridates VI of Pontus]] c. 110 BCE; his general [[e:diophantus-general|Diophantus]] defended it, and it passed under Pontic and later Roman protection. As Byzantine Cherson it survived into the [[e:middle-ages|Middle Ages]], where tradition places the baptism of [[e:vladimir-the-great|Vladimir of Kiev]] in 988.

candarids.t: A long-lived Turkish beylik of the Black Sea region, ruling Kastamonu and Sinop until the Ottomans took it in 1461.
candarids.o: Shams al-Din Yaman Candar, a Turkish commander in Ilkhanid service, was granted the district of Eflani in the 1290s. His son [[e:suleyman-pasha-candarid|Suleyman Pasha]] took [[e:kastamonu|Kastamonu]] from the [[s:chobanids-of-kastamonu|Chobanids of Kastamonu]] in 1309 and [[s:sinope|Sinop]] from the [[s:pervaneids|Pervaneids]] around 1322.
candarids.r: The [[e:beylik|beylik]] controlled the [[e:copper|copper]] mines of [[e:kure-kastamonu|Kure]] and the port of [[s:sinope|Sinop]], which traded with Genoese colonies across the [[e:black-sea|Black Sea]]. [[e:ibn-battuta|Ibn Battuta]] stayed in [[e:kastamonu|Kastamonu]] in the 1330s. The rulers patronised Turkish literature and built mosques in Kastamonu. Under [[e:isfendiyar-bey|Isfendiyar Bey]], after whom the family was also called, they survived the Ottoman advance by alliances and ceding territory.
candarids.e: [[e:bayezid-i|Bayezid I]] annexed [[e:kastamonu|Kastamonu]] in 1392, but [[e:timur|Timur]] restored the family in 1402. [[e:mehmed-ii|Mehmed II]] took [[s:sinope|Sinop]] from [[e:ismail-bey-of-candar|Ismail Bey]] in 1461 on the way to [[s:empire-of-trebizond|Trebizond]], ending the [[e:beylik|beylik]].

cr.a: self- based on WP locator maps

crusader-smyrna.t: A Latin outpost in the harbour of Smyrna, seized by a crusade in 1344 and held by the Knights Hospitaller until Timur destroyed it.
crusader-smyrna.o: To stop the raids of [[e:umur-bey|Umur Bey]] of the [[s:aydinids|Aydinids]], [[e:pope-clement-vi|Pope Clement VI]] organised a naval league with [[e:venice|Venice]], [[e:cyprus|Cyprus]] and the [[e:knights-hospitaller|Knights Hospitaller]]. In October 1344 its fleet captured the harbour castle of [[s:smyrna|Smyrna]], while the Turks kept the upper citadel on [[e:mount-pagus|Mount Pagus]].
crusader-smyrna.r: The colony was a fortified enclave held by a mixed garrison under a papal captain, supplied by sea and constantly under pressure from the Turks above. [[e:umur-bey|Umur Bey]] was killed attacking it in 1348, and [[e:humbert-ii-of-viennois|Humbert II of Viennois]] led a further expedition in 1345-1347. From 1374 the pope entrusted [[s:smyrna|Smyrna]] to the [[e:knights-hospitaller|Hospitallers]], who held it as an outpost of their state on [[s:rhodes|Rhodes]].
crusader-smyrna.e: In December 1402 [[e:timur|Timur]] besieged the castle after defeating the [[e:ottoman-empire|Ottomans]] at [[e:ankara|Ankara]]. He took it within about two weeks and massacred the defenders who did not escape by sea, ending the [[e:latin|Latin]] presence.

cacicazgo-of-guaynia.t: The leading Taíno chiefdom of Puerto Rico, in the south of the island, whose caciques Agüeybaná I and II met and then fought the Spanish.
cacicazgo-of-guaynia.o: Guaynía occupied the southern coast of [[e:puerto-rico|Puerto Rico]] (Borikén) around the Guayanilla area. It developed within [[e:taino|Taíno]] society over the centuries before Spanish arrival and by 1500 was the most powerful of the island's chiefdoms, with other caciques recognising its leader.
cacicazgo-of-guaynia.r: Its paramount cacique [[e:agueybana-i|Agüeybaná I]] welcomed [[e:juan-ponce-de-leon|Juan Ponce de León]] in 1508 and allowed the Spanish to settle. [[e:taino|Taíno]] villages centred on ceremonial plazas, such as those at [[e:tibes-indigenous-ceremonial-center|Tibes]] and [[e:caguana-ceremonial-site|Caguana]], and farmed [[e:cassava|cassava]] and [[e:maize|maize]]. Under the [[e:encomienda|encomienda]] system the Taíno were forced to work in gold mining.
cacicazgo-of-guaynia.e: After [[e:agueybana-i|Agüeybaná I]] died around 1510, his brother [[e:agueybana-ii|Agüeybaná II]] led a general [[e:taino|Taíno]] uprising in 1511. It was crushed, Agüeybaná II was probably killed in the fighting, and the Taíno population collapsed under war, forced labour and disease.

captaincy-of-bahia.t: The captaincy around the Bay of All Saints that became the seat of colonial Brazil's government and the heart of its sugar and slave economy.
captaincy-of-bahia.o: In 1534 [[e:john-iii-of-portugal|King John III]] granted the Captaincy of the [[e:bay-of-all-saints|Bay of All Saints]] to [[e:francisco-pereira-coutinho|Francisco Pereira Coutinho]]. His settlement failed, and he was killed by the [[e:tupinamba|Tupinambá]] in 1547. The crown bought back the captaincy, and in 1549 [[e:tome-de-sousa|Tomé de Sousa]] founded [[e:salvador|Salvador]] there as the capital of the [[s:state-of-brazil|State of Brazil]].
captaincy-of-bahia.r: [[e:salvador|Salvador]] was the seat of [[e:brazil|Brazil's]] governors-general and [[e:viceroy-of-india|viceroys]] until 1763 and the first bishopric, from 1551. The [[e:reconcavo|Recôncavo]] around the bay was filled with [[e:sugar-plantation|sugar]] plantations and tobacco farms, and Salvador was one of the main ports of the [[e:atlantic-slave-trade|Atlantic slave trade]], giving [[e:bahia|Bahia]] a strong African culture. The [[e:dutch|Dutch]] briefly took Salvador in 1624 and 1625.
captaincy-of-bahia.e: The capital moved to [[e:rio-de-janeiro|Rio de Janeiro]] in 1763. [[e:bahia|Bahia]] became a province of the [[e:brazilian-empire|Empire of Brazil]], though Portuguese troops held [[e:salvador|Salvador]] until 2 July 1823, still celebrated as Bahia's independence day.

caledonii.t: Confederation of the Scottish Highlands that fought Agricola at Mons Graupius and Septimius Severus, and gave its name to Caledonia.
caledonii.o: The Caledonii were a people of the central and northern Highlands, named by Ptolemy and others; Roman writers used [[s:new-caledonia-darien|Caledonia]] for northern [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]] as a whole. They first appear in history when the governor [[e:gnaeus-julius-agricola|Agricola]] marched north, and [[e:tacitus|Tacitus]] says a host of Caledonian peoples gathered under [[e:calgacus|Calgacus]] to meet him at [[e:battle-of-mons-graupius|Mons Graupius]] in 83 or 84.
caledonii.r: [[e:roman-empire|Romans]] describe them as a warrior society of clans and chiefs, without towns or coinage, living by herding and farming in a landscape of roundhouses, crannogs and brochs further north. [[e:cassius-dio|Cassius Dio]] later portrays the Caledonians and [[s:maeatae|Maeatae]] as the two main groupings beyond the walls, and tells of the Caledonian [[e:argentocoxus|Argentocoxus]], whose wife bantered with the empress [[e:julia-domna|Julia Domna]].
caledonii.e: Defeated at [[e:battle-of-mons-graupius|Mons Graupius]] but never conquered, the Caledonians bought peace or raided as Roman power allowed. [[e:septimius-severus|Septimius Severus]] campaigned against them from 208 to 211, and after his death [[e:rome|Rome]] withdrew. By the late 3rd century Roman writers spoke instead of the [[e:picts|Picts]], whose [[s:kingdom-of-the-picts|Kingdom of the Picts]] absorbed the Caledonian peoples.

colony-of-singapore.t: British crown colony created when Singapore was separated from the Straits Settlements, and the stage for its path to self-rule.
colony-of-singapore.o: When [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]] dissolved the [[s:straits-settlements|Straits Settlements]] in 1946, it kept [[s:singapore|Singapore]] apart from the new [[s:malayan-union|Malayan Union]] because of its Chinese majority and its value as a naval base. The Colony of [[e:singapore|Singapore]] was established on 1 April 1946 under a governor.
colony-of-singapore.r: The post-war years brought labour unrest, communist activity and the [[e:malayan-emergency|Malayan Emergency]]. The [[e:rendel-constitution|Rendel Constitution]] of 1955 created a partly elected legislature, and [[e:david-marshall|David Marshall]] became chief minister. Full internal self-government came in 1959 as the State of [[s:singapore|Singapore]], with [[e:lee-kuan-yew|Lee Kuan Yew]] of the [[e:peoples-action-party|People's Action Party]] as prime minister, while [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]] kept defence and foreign affairs.
colony-of-singapore.e: [[e:lee-kuan-yew|Lee]] pursued merger with [[s:federation-of-malaya|Malaya]] to end colonial rule and gain an economic hinterland. [[s:singapore|Singapore]] joined [[s:malaysia|Malaysia]] on 16 September 1963, but political and racial tensions led to separation in 1965, creating the independent [[e:singapore|Singapore]].
colony-of-singapore.re: Buddhism, Chinese folk religion, Sunni Islam, Christianity, Hinduism

commonwealth-of-england.t: The republic that replaced the monarchy after the execution of Charles I in 1649, the only period without a king in English history.
commonwealth-of-england.o: After Parliament's victory in the Civil Wars, Charles I was tried and executed in January 1649. The Rump Parliament abolished the monarchy and the House of Lords and declared [[e:england|England]] a Commonwealth governed without a king. [[e:oliver-cromwell|Cromwell]] then conquered Ireland and [[e:scotland|Scotland]], which were joined to it.
commonwealth-of-england.r: Power lay with the Rump, its [[e:english-council-of-state|Council of State]] and the New Model Army. The regime passed the [[e:navigation-acts|Navigation Act]] of 1651, fought the [[e:first-anglo-dutch-war|First Anglo-Dutch War]] and allowed some religious toleration while repressing [[e:levellers|Levellers]] and royalists. [[e:oliver-cromwell|Cromwell]] expelled the Rump in 1653, and the nominated [[e:barebones-parliament|Barebone's Parliament]] failed, leading to the [[e:protectorate|Protectorate]].
commonwealth-of-england.e: After the [[e:protectorate|Protectorate]] collapsed in 1659 the restored Rump briefly revived the Commonwealth. General [[e:george-monck|George Monck]] marched from [[e:scotland|Scotland]], the [[e:convention-parliament-1660|Convention Parliament]] invited [[e:charles-ii-of-england|Charles II]] back, and the monarchy was restored in May 1660 in the [[s:kingdom-of-england|Kingdom of England]].

carthaginiensis.t: The late Roman province of central and south-eastern Hispania, named after its capital Carthago Nova, modern Cartagena.
carthaginiensis.o: Carthaginiensis was created around 293 by [[e:diocletian|Diocletian]], who divided [[s:hispania-tarraconensis|Hispania Tarraconensis]]. It took in the south-east coast and much of the central [[e:meseta-central|Meseta]], including [[e:toledo|Toletum]], with [[e:carthago-nova|Carthago Nova]] as capital. The [[e:balearic-islands|Balearic Islands]] belonged to it until about 369.
carthaginiensis.r: A governor administered it within the [[s:diocese-of-hispania|Diocese of Hispania]]. [[e:carthago-nova|Carthago Nova]] remained a port for esparto, fish sauce and the remains of its [[e:silver|silver]] trade, while inland cities such as [[e:toledo|Toletum]] and [[e:complutum|Complutum]] grew in importance. Christian communities were well established, and the [[e:council-of-elvira|Council of Elvira]] of around 305 drew [[e:bishop|bishops]] from the region.
carthaginiensis.e: After 409 the [[s:alans|Alans]] and [[e:vandals|Vandals]] overran the province, and Roman control was patchy. In 460 the emperor Majorian's fleet, gathered on its coast to attack the Vandals in [[e:africa|Africa]], was destroyed. The region fell to the [[e:visigoths|Visigoths]], and later [[s:byzantine-spania|Byzantine Spania]] held its coast.

colony-of-new-brunswick.t: A British colony created for Loyalist refugees in 1784, whose timber and shipbuilding made it a founding province of Canada.
colony-of-new-brunswick.o: After the [[e:american-revolution|American Revolution]] about 14,000 Loyalists settled along the [[e:saint-john-river|Saint John River]] in what was then part of the [[s:colony-of-nova-scotia|Colony of Nova Scotia]]. Wanting a government of their own, they won partition in 1784, and [[e:thomas-carleton|Thomas Carleton]] became the first governor. [[e:fredericton|Fredericton]], inland and safer from attack, was chosen as capital over the port of Saint John.
colony-of-new-brunswick.r: The colony had an elected assembly from 1786 and won responsible government in 1848. Its economy depended on cutting pine for masts and [[e:timber|timber]] exported to [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]], and on building wooden ships. Irish immigration in the 1840s, [[e:acadians|Acadians]] returning to the north and east, and [[e:maliseet|Wolastoqiyik]] and [[e:mikmaq|Mi'kmaq]] communities shaped a mixed society. A boundary dispute with [[s:county-of-maine|Maine]] was settled by the [[e:webster-ashburton-treaty|Webster-Ashburton Treaty]] of 1842.
colony-of-new-brunswick.e: Railway hopes and fear of American invasion after the Civil War persuaded New [[e:brunswick|Brunswick]] to join Confederation. It became one of the four original provinces of [[s:province-of-canada|Canada]] on 1 July 1867.

county-of-barcelona.t: The leading Catalan county, whose counts united Catalonia and, through marriage with Aragon in 1137, founded the Crown of Aragon.
county-of-barcelona.o: [[e:louis-the-pious|Louis the Pious]], king of [[s:duchy-of-aquitaine|Aquitaine]], captured [[e:barcelona|Barcelona]] from the Muslims in 801 after a long siege, and [[e:charlemagne|Charlemagne]] made it the main county of the [[s:marca-hispanica|Marca Hispanica]]. Its first count, the Goth [[e:bera-count-of-barcelona|Bera]], was deposed in 820. In 878 [[e:wilfred-the-hairy|Wilfred the Hairy]] received it, and after his death in 897 his heirs inherited it without royal appointment.
county-of-barcelona.r: The counts gradually gathered [[e:girona|Girona]], Osona and other counties into their hands. After [[e:almanzor|Almanzor]] sacked [[e:barcelona|Barcelona]] in 985, [[e:borrell-ii-of-barcelona|Borrell II]] stopped seeking Frankish protection. [[e:ramon-berenguer-i-count-of-barcelona|Ramon Berenguer I]] is traditionally credited with the first [[e:usatges-of-barcelona|Usatges of Barcelona]], the core of Catalan law, and bought rights over [[e:carcassonne|Carcassonne]]. [[e:ramon-berenguer-iii-of-barcelona|Ramon Berenguer III]] gained [[s:county-of-provence|Provence]] by marriage, and the city prospered through trade and tribute from the [[e:taifa|taifas]].
county-of-barcelona.e: In 1137 [[e:ramon-berenguer-iv-count-of-barcelona|Ramon Berenguer IV]] was betrothed to [[e:petronilla-of-aragon|Petronilla]], heiress of Aragon, and governed both lands. Their son [[e:alfonso-ii-of-aragon|Alfonso II]] succeeded in [[e:barcelona|Barcelona]] in 1162 and in Aragon in 1164, and the county became the core of the [[s:crown-of-aragon|Crown of Aragon]].

county-of-ziegenhain.t: A Hessian county in the Schwalm valley whose counts held a moated castle and whose extinction in 1450 enlarged the landgraviate of Hesse.
county-of-ziegenhain.o: The counts of Ziegenhain appear around 1144, with a moated castle in the marshy [[e:schwalm|Schwalm]] valley. Through marriage they also acquired the County of [[e:nidda|Nidda]] in the [[e:wetterau|Wetterau]] in the 12th century. Their lands lay between the [[s:landgraviate-of-hesse|Landgraviate of Hesse]] and the abbeys of [[e:fulda|Fulda]] and Hersfeld.
county-of-ziegenhain.r: The counts were advocates of [[e:fulda-abbey|Fulda Abbey]] and often in conflict with the landgraves of [[e:hesse|Hesse]]. Their territory was rural, centred on the small town of Ziegenhain and the castle at [[e:nidda|Nidda]]. Little is known of their administration in detail.
county-of-ziegenhain.e: The last count, John II, died in 1450, and both Ziegenhain and [[e:nidda|Nidda]] passed to the landgraves of [[e:hesse|Hesse]]. Landgrave [[e:philip-i-landgrave-of-hesse|Philip the Magnanimous]] later turned Ziegenhain into a fortress, used as a prison in later centuries.

congo-free-state.t: King Leopold II's personal colony in the Congo basin, whose forced rubber collection became an international scandal.
congo-free-state.o: Through his International African Association and the expeditions of [[e:henry-morton-stanley|Henry Morton Stanley]] from 1879, King [[e:leopold-ii|Leopold II]] of the Belgians gathered treaties with Congolese chiefs. The [[e:berlin-conference|Berlin Conference]] of 1884-1885 recognised his claims, and in 1885 he proclaimed the Congo Free State, a state he ruled personally, not as a Belgian colony, with [[e:boma|Boma]] as its capital.
congo-free-state.r: Leopold declared vacant land state property and granted concessions to companies. The [[e:force-publique|Force Publique]], African soldiers under European officers, defeated rivals such as the [[s:yeke-kingdom|Yeke Kingdom]] and [[s:tippu-tips-state|Tippu Tip's State]], and enforced quotas of wild [[e:rubber|rubber]] through hostage-taking, flogging and the cutting off of hands. Millions died from violence, famine and disease, though exact figures are debated.
congo-free-state.e: Reports by [[e:roger-casement|Roger Casement]] and the campaign of [[e:e-d-morel|E. D. Morel's]] [[e:congo-reform-association|Congo Reform Association]] forced action. [[s:kingdom-of-belgium|Belgium]] annexed the territory in November 1908 as the [[s:belgian-congo|Belgian Congo]]. The scandal became a landmark in the history of international human rights campaigning.

cr.a: See file history below for details.

county-of-la-marche.t: A border county between Poitou and the Limousin, held by the Lusignans at the height of their power and later by Armagnac and Bourbon princes.
county-of-la-marche.o: La [[e:marche|Marche]] took its name from its position as a frontier zone, or march, of the duchy of [[s:duchy-of-aquitaine|Aquitaine]]. Around 958 [[e:boso-the-old|Boso the Old]], a lord of [[e:charroux|Charroux]], held comital authority there, and his descendants ruled both La Marche and the neighbouring [[s:county-of-perigord|Périgord]].
county-of-la-marche.r: A poor upland county of pasture and woodland, La [[e:marche|Marche]] mattered for its strategic place between the [[e:house-of-plantagenet|Plantagenet]] and Capetian spheres. From 1199 the [[e:house-of-lusignan|Lusignans]] held it; Hugh X married [[e:isabella-of-angouleme|Isabella of Angoulême]], widow of [[e:john-king-of-england|King John]], and joined a failed revolt against [[e:louis-ix-of-france|Louis IX]] in 1242. [[e:gueret|Guéret]] and [[e:charroux|Charroux]] were its main centres.
county-of-la-marche.e: After the Lusignan line ended in 1308, [[e:philip-iv-of-france|Philip IV]] took the county. It passed to the [[e:house-of-bourbon|Bourbons]], the [[e:house-of-armagnac|Armagnacs]] and back to the Bourbons as an [[e:appanage|appanage]], until [[e:francis-i|Francis I]] confiscated the lands of [[e:charles-iii-duke-of-bourbon|Constable Charles of Bourbon]] in 1523. It was united with the [[s:kingdom-of-france|Kingdom of France]] in 1527.

colony-of-fiji.t: A British colony for nearly a century that protected Fijian land and chiefly rule while bringing Indian labour for sugar, shaping modern Fiji's divided politics.
colony-of-fiji.o: [[e:fiji|Fiji's]] chiefs ceded the islands to [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]] on 10 October 1874, ending the [[s:kingdom-of-fiji|Kingdom of Fiji]]. A [[e:measles|measles]] epidemic in 1875 killed perhaps a third of the Fijian population. The first governor, [[e:arthur-hamilton-gordon-1st-baron-stanmore|Sir Arthur Gordon]], laid down the colony's lasting system, and the capital moved from [[e:levuka|Levuka]] to [[e:suva|Suva]] in 1882.
colony-of-fiji.r: [[e:arthur-hamilton-gordon-1st-baron-stanmore|Gordon]] ruled indirectly through chiefs and a Great Council of Chiefs, and forbade the further sale of Fijian land, most of which remains communally owned. To work [[e:sugar-plantation|sugar]] plantations, run largely by the [[e:colonial-sugar-refining-company|Colonial Sugar Refining Company]], about 60,000 indentured labourers came from [[e:india|India]] between 1879 and 1916. [[e:ratu-sir-lala-sukuna|Ratu Sir Lala Sukuna]] was the leading Fijian statesman of the colonial era, and Fijian soldiers fought in the [[e:solomon|Solomon]] Islands during the [[e:second-world-war|Second World War]].
colony-of-fiji.e: [[e:fiji|Fiji]] became independent on 10 October 1970, with [[e:ratu-sir-kamisese-mara|Ratu Sir Kamisese Mara]] as prime minister. Tensions between indigenous Fijians and [[e:indo-fijians|Indo-Fijians]], rooted in colonial policy, contributed to coups in 1987 and later.

county-of-sponheim.t: A Rhineland county between the Nahe and the Moselle, divided into two halves whose rulers died out in 1437, leaving the land to shared lordship.
county-of-sponheim.o: The counts of Sponheim appear in 1044 near the [[e:nahe|Nahe]] in the [[e:hunsruck|Hunsrück]], with their castle at Sponheim and a family monastery founded there. A related branch became dukes of [[e:carinthia|Carinthia]] from 1122. In the 13th century the [[e:rhineland|Rhineland]] county was divided into the Front County, centred on [[e:bad-kreuznach|Kreuznach]], and the Rear County, centred on [[e:traben-trarbach|Trarbach]].
county-of-sponheim.r: The counts ruled villages, vineyards and castles across the [[e:hunsruck|Hunsrück]] and the lower [[e:nahe|Nahe]] and [[e:moselle|Moselle]], balancing between the archbishops of [[e:trier|Trier]] and [[e:mainz|Mainz]] and the [[s:electoral-palatinate|Electoral Palatinate]]. The abbey of Sponheim later had the humanist [[e:johannes-trithemius|Johannes Trithemius]] as abbot from 1483.
county-of-sponheim.e: Countess [[e:loretta-of-sponheim|Loretta of Sponheim]] famously captured Archbishop Baldwin of [[e:trier|Trier]] in 1328. The last ruler of the Front County, Countess Elisabeth, died in 1417 and the last of the Rear County, Count John V, in 1437. The lands passed to the margraves of [[e:baden|Baden]] and the counts of [[s:county-of-veldenz|Veldenz]], then the [[s:electoral-palatinate|Palatinate]], under shared rule until 1776.

chhota-udaipur-state.t: A Chauhan Rajput state of eastern Gujarat whose rulers traced their line to the medieval kings of Pavagadh and Champaner.
chhota-udaipur-state.o: When [[e:sultan|Sultan]] [[e:mahmud-begada|Mahmud Begada]] of [[e:gujarat|Gujarat]] took [[e:champaner|Champaner]] in 1484, members of the Khichi [[e:chauhan|Chauhan]] ruling family fled east and founded the states of [[e:chhota-udaipur|Chhota Udaipur]] and Baria. Chhota [[e:udaipur|Udaipur]] emerged as a separate state around 1743.
chhota-udaipur-state.r: The state lay in forested hill country with a largely Adivasi population of [[e:rathwa|Rathwa]], [[e:bhils|Bhil]] and other communities. It paid tribute to the [[e:gaekwads|Gaekwads]] of [[s:baroda-state|Baroda State]] and later belonged to the [[e:rewa-kantha-agency|Rewa Kantha Agency]], ruled by a Maharawal. [[e:timber|Timber]] and forest produce were important; the Rathwa [[e:pithora-painting|Pithora paintings]] come from this area.
chhota-udaipur-state.e: After accession to [[e:india|India]], [[e:chhota-udaipur|Chhota Udaipur]] was merged into [[e:bombay-state|Bombay State]] in 1948 and became part of [[e:gujarat|Gujarat]] in 1960, now as Chhota [[e:udaipur|Udaipur]] district.

cr.a: The original uploader was Nataraja at French Wikipedia.

commune-of-asti.t: A Piedmontese city-republic whose merchants and money-lenders spread across France and Flanders, giving the 'Lombard' bankers their name in the north.
commune-of-asti.o: Asti had long been ruled by its [[e:bishop|bishops]], but consuls representing the citizens are recorded in 1095, making it one of the earliest communes in [[e:piedmont|Piedmont]]. It grew rich on the trade route between [[e:lombardy|Lombardy]], the Alpine passes and [[e:france|France]], and resisted both its bishop and the [[s:march-of-montferrat|March of Montferrat]].
commune-of-asti.r: The commune was run by consuls and later a podestà, with powerful merchant families building tower houses in the city. Asti's financiers set up pawn and loan banks across [[e:france|France]], [[s:county-of-savoy|Savoy]], the [[e:low-countries|Low Countries]] and the [[e:rhineland|Rhineland]]. [[e:frederick-barbarossa|Frederick Barbarossa]] burned the city in 1155, but it recovered and won a wide rural territory. The [[e:palio-of-asti|Palio of Asti]] horse race is first recorded in 1275.
commune-of-asti.e: Faction strife between the Solaro and de Castello families led the city to submit to outside lords, including the [[e:capetian-house-of-anjou|Angevins]], and in 1342 to [[e:luchino-visconti-lord-of-milan|Luchino Visconti]] of the [[s:lordship-of-milan|Lordship of Milan]]. Asti later passed as a dowry to the [[e:orleans|Orléans]] and then to the [[s:duchy-of-savoy|Duchy of Savoy]].

calusa.t: A powerful chiefdom of south-western Florida, unusual in building a complex, tribute-taking society on fishing rather than farming, which resisted Spain for two centuries.
calusa.o: The Calusa grew out of the fishing and shell-gathering cultures of the Gulf coast estuaries around [[e:charlotte-harbor|Charlotte Harbor]] and [[e:estero-bay|Estero Bay]]. By around 1000 they were building large shell mounds, ridges and canals, and their capital, [[e:mound-key|Calos]], on Mound Key, became the centre of a paramount chiefdom that dominated much of southern [[e:florida|Florida]].
calusa.r: Without [[e:maize|maize]] agriculture, the Calusa lived on fish, shellfish and plants from rich estuaries, yet supported a hereditary paramount chief, priests and warriors. Subject towns, among them the [[e:tequesta|Tequesta]] and others around [[e:lake-okeechobee|Lake Okeechobee]], sent tribute. They dug canoe canals, notably across Pine Island, and carved fine wooden masks and figures like those found at [[e:key-marco|Key Marco]]. In 1566 the chief known to the Spanish as Carlos met [[e:pedro-menendez-de-aviles|Pedro Menéndez de Avilés]], who founded a short-lived [[e:jesuits|Jesuit]] mission.
calusa.e: The Calusa wounded [[e:juan-ponce-de-leon|Juan Ponce de León]] fatally in 1521 and kept Spanish missions out. Epidemics and, after 1700, slave raids by [[e:muscogee|Muscogee]] and [[e:yamasee|Yamasee]] allies of English [[s:province-of-carolina|Carolina]] destroyed them. Survivors fled to the [[e:florida-keys|Keys]] and to [[e:cuba|Cuba]], the last leaving in 1760.

county-of-valentinois.t: A Rhône valley county around Valence and Die held by the Poitiers family, later turned into a duchy for Cesare Borgia and Diane de Poitiers.
county-of-valentinois.o: In the early 12th century the [[e:poitiers|Poitiers]] family, of uncertain origin, established itself as counts in the [[e:valentinois|Valentinois]], the lands around [[e:valence|Valence]] on the left bank of the [[e:rhone|Rhône]]. By the 13th century they had also acquired the [[e:diois|Diois]] to the east, forming the united county of Valentinois and Diois.
county-of-valentinois.r: The counts ruled a land of river trade, vineyards and Alpine valleys, holding their lands within the [[s:kingdom-of-arles|Kingdom of Arles]]. Much of their energy went into long struggles with the [[e:bishop|bishops]] of [[e:valence|Valence]] and Die, who claimed lordship over the cities, and with the neighbouring dauphins of [[s:dauphine-of-viennois|Viennois]].
county-of-valentinois.e: The last count, [[e:louis-ii-of-poitiers|Louis II of Poitiers]], bequeathed the county to the [[e:dauphin-of-france|Dauphin of France]], and it passed to the crown in 1419 despite claims by [[s:county-of-savoy|Savoy]]. [[e:louis-xii-of-france|Louis XII]] later made it a duchy for [[e:cesare-borgia|Cesare Borgia]] in 1498, and [[e:henry-ii-of-france|Henry II]] gave it to [[e:diane-de-poitiers|Diane de Poitiers]].

captaincy-of-sao-vicente.t: The first Portuguese settlement in Brazil with a proper town council, whose highland outpost of São Paulo became the base of the bandeirantes.
captaincy-of-sao-vicente.o: [[e:martim-afonso-de-sousa|Martim Afonso de Sousa]] founded São Vicente on the coast of modern [[e:sao-paulo|São Paulo]] state in 1532, the first permanent Portuguese town in [[s:new-republic-brazil|Brazil]]. In 1534 [[e:john-iii-of-portugal|King John III]] granted him the hereditary Captaincy of São Vicente, one of the original captaincies, covering a long section of the southern coast.
captaincy-of-sao-vicente.r: The captaincy grew from [[e:sugar-plantation|sugar]] mills on the coast, but its future lay on the plateau, where the [[e:jesuits|Jesuits]] [[e:manuel-da-nobrega|Manuel da Nóbrega]] and [[e:jose-de-anchieta|José de Anchieta]] founded [[e:sao-paulo|São Paulo]] in 1554. Society was poor and heavily mixed with the [[e:tupi|Tupi]], and língua geral was widely spoken. From the late 16th century bandeirante expeditions set out to capture indigenous slaves and search for gold, pushing far beyond the [[e:treaty-of-tordesillas|Tordesillas]] line.
captaincy-of-sao-vicente.e: After the gold discoveries, the crown bought the captaincy back from its heirs and in 1709 created the [[s:captaincy-of-sao-paulo|Captaincy of São Paulo and Minas de Ouro]], which absorbed São Vicente.

crown-of-castile.t: The union of Castile and León that conquered most of al-Andalus, sent Columbus across the Atlantic and formed the core of the Spanish monarchy.
crown-of-castile.o: In 1230 Ferdinand III, king of the [[s:kingdom-of-castile|Kingdom of Castile]], inherited the [[s:kingdom-of-leon|Kingdom of León]], permanently uniting the two crowns. He then conquered [[e:cordoba|Córdoba]] in 1236, [[e:jaen|Jaén]] in 1246 and [[e:seville|Seville]] in 1248, leaving the [[s:emirate-of-granada|Emirate of Granada]] as the main surviving Muslim state.
crown-of-castile.r: [[e:kingdom-of-castile|Castile's]] [[e:cortes|Cortes]], wool trade dominated by the [[e:mesta|Mesta]], towns and military orders shaped its society. [[e:alfonso-x-of-castile|Alfonso X]] sponsored law codes and translations at [[e:toledo|Toledo]]. The [[e:house-of-trastamara|Trastámara]] dynasty took power in 1369. Isabella I and [[e:ferdinand-ii-of-aragon|Ferdinand II]], who had set up the [[e:portuguese-inquisition|Inquisition]] in 1478, conquered [[e:granada|Granada]] in 1492, the year [[e:christopher-columbus|Columbus]] sailed and the [[e:jews|Jews]] were expelled.
crown-of-castile.e: From 1516 [[s:kingdom-of-castile|Castile]] was the heartland of [[s:habsburg-spain|Habsburg Spain]], supplying its taxes, soldiers and American empire. After the [[e:war-of-the-spanish-succession|War of the Spanish Succession]], the [[e:nueva-planta-decrees|Nueva Planta decrees]] imposed Castilian institutions on [[e:kingdom-of-aragon|Aragon]], and the Crown merged into a unified Spanish state.

colony-of-jamaica.t: Britain's most valuable Caribbean colony for much of the 18th century, a sugar island built on slavery that became independent in 1962.
colony-of-jamaica.o: An English expedition under [[e:sir-william-penn|William Penn]] and [[e:robert-venables|Robert Venables]], part of [[e:oliver-cromwell|Oliver Cromwell's]] Western Design, failed against [[e:santo-domingo|Santo Domingo]] and seized lightly defended [[s:spanish-jamaica|Spanish Jamaica]] in 1655. [[e:spain|Spain]] ceded the island by the [[e:treaty-of-madrid-1670|Treaty of Madrid]] in 1670. Port Royal, base of buccaneers such as [[e:henry-morgan|Henry Morgan]], flourished until an earthquake destroyed it in 1692.
colony-of-jamaica.r: A governor ruled with an elected planter assembly, from [[e:spanish-town|Spanish Town]] until [[e:kingston-jamaica|Kingston]] became capital in 1872. [[e:sugar-plantation|Sugar]] estates using enslaved Africans made [[s:jamaica|Jamaica]] enormously profitable. Resistance was constant, from [[e:tackys-revolt|Tacky's Revolt]] of 1760 to the [[e:baptist-war|Baptist War]] of 1831 to 1832 led by [[e:samuel-sharpe|Samuel Sharpe]], which hastened emancipation in 1834 to 1838. After the [[e:morant-bay-rebellion|Morant Bay rebellion]] of 1865 the assembly was abolished and crown colony rule imposed.
colony-of-jamaica.e: Labour unrest in 1938 gave rise to trade unions and parties led by [[e:alexander-bustamante|Alexander Bustamante]] and [[e:norman-manley|Norman Manley]]. [[e:universal-suffrage|Universal suffrage]] came in 1944. [[s:jamaica|Jamaica]] joined the [[s:west-indies-federation|West Indies Federation]] in 1958 but left after a 1961 referendum and became independent as [[e:jamaica|Jamaica]] on 6 August 1962.

commune-of-pavia.t: The old Lombard royal capital turned city-republic, a loyal imperial ally and Milan's bitter rival until the Visconti took it in 1359.
commune-of-pavia.o: Pavia had been the capital of the [[s:kingdom-of-the-lombards|Kingdom of the Lombards]] and the coronation city of the [[s:kingdom-of-italy-medieval|Kingdom of Italy (medieval)]]. Around 1100 its citizens organised a commune under consuls, inheriting the city's royal palace traditions and a renowned school of law.
commune-of-pavia.r: [[e:consul|Consuls]] and later a podestà ruled the city, which stood firmly with the emperors against [[s:duchy-of-milan|Milan]], fighting it repeatedly in the 12th and 13th centuries. Pavia controlled the confluence of the [[e:ticino-river|Ticino]] and the Po and much of the [[e:lomellina|Lomellina]]. Its churches, such as [[e:san-michele-maggiore-pavia|San Michele Maggiore]] where kings were crowned and [[e:san-pietro-in-ciel-doro|San Pietro in Ciel d'Oro]] with [[e:augustine-of-hippo|Saint Augustine's]] tomb, reflected its royal past. The Beccaria family dominated in the 14th century.
commune-of-pavia.e: [[e:galeazzo-ii-visconti|Galeazzo II Visconti]] captured Pavia in 1359 after a long siege, absorbing it into the [[s:lordship-of-milan|Lordship of Milan]]. The Visconti built a castle there, founded the university in 1361 and later the [[e:certosa-di-pavia|Certosa di Pavia]].

carpi.t: Free Dacian people east of the Carpathians who raided Roman Dacia and Moesia throughout the 3rd century until Rome resettled them inside the empire.
carpi.o: The [[s:lordship-of-carpi|Carpi]] lived in [[s:principality-of-moldavia|Moldavia]], east of the [[e:carpathian-mountains|Carpathians]] and outside Roman [[e:dacia|Dacia]], from the 2nd century CE. They are usually identified with the Poienești archaeological culture of farming villages and cremation cemeteries, and are considered a Dacian people.
carpi.r: They lived in unfortified villages under tribal leaders, farming and herding. In the crisis of the 3rd century they joined the [[e:goths|Goths]] in raids across the [[e:danube|Danube]], besieging [[e:marcianopolis|Marcianopolis]] and attacking [[e:dacia|Dacia]]. The emperor [[e:philip-the-arab|Philip the Arab]] defeated them in 247, and several emperors took the victory title Carpicus.
carpi.e: Aurelian, and then [[e:diocletian|Diocletian]] and [[e:galerius|Galerius]] around 295–305, defeated them and moved large numbers into [[e:pannonia|Pannonia]] and [[e:moesia|Moesia]]. The last mention comes under Constantine around 318, after which the remaining [[s:lordship-of-carpi|Carpi]] merged into the Gothic and Roman worlds.

cozumel.t: An island Maya chiefdom off the east coast of Yucatán, home to a pilgrimage shrine of the goddess Ix Chel and the first landfall of Cortés in 1519.
cozumel.o: Cozumel (Cuzamil) was settled for centuries and became an important trading and religious centre in the Postclassic period. After the fall of the [[s:league-of-mayapan|League of Mayapan]] around 1441 it was an independent chiefdom, with [[e:san-gervasio|San Gervasio]] as a main centre.
cozumel.r: The island was a major port of call for seagoing traders who carried salt, [[e:cotton|cotton]], honey and [[e:cacao|cacao]] around the peninsula. Pilgrims came from across [[e:yucatan-peninsula|Yucatán]] to consult the oracle of [[e:ix-chel|Ix Chel]], goddess of childbirth and the moon. Small shrines and coastal structures dotted the island.
cozumel.e: [[e:juan-de-grijalva|Grijalva]] landed in 1518 and Cortés in 1519, smashing idols and recovering the castaway [[e:jeronimo-de-aguilar|Jerónimo de Aguilar]]. [[e:smallpox|Smallpox]] struck in 1520, and the population plummeted. The island submitted to [[e:francisco-de-montejo|Montejo]] in 1527 and was formally under Spanish control by the 1540s.

colony-of-saint-lucia.t: British colony on Saint Lucia after 1814, with French law and Kwéyòl culture, a coaling station for the Royal Navy and home of two Nobel laureates.
colony-of-saint-lucia.o: After about fourteen changes of ownership between [[e:france|France]] and [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]], [[s:saint-lucia|Saint Lucia]] was finally ceded to [[e:britain|Britain]] by the [[e:treaty-of-paris-1814|Treaty of Paris]] in 1814. The British kept much of the French legal system and Catholic church organisation that they found, and [[e:castries|Castries]] remained the capital.
colony-of-saint-lucia.r: As a crown colony [[s:saint-lucia|Saint Lucia]] had no elected assembly for most of the 19th century, and the [[e:custom-of-paris|Coutume de Paris]] remained the basis of [[e:civil-law|civil law]] until a new code in 1879. [[e:sugar-plantation|Sugar]] declined after emancipation; Indian indentured workers arrived from 1859. [[e:castries|Castries]] became a major coaling station for steamships from the 1880s. From 1838 the island belonged to the [[s:british-windward-islands|British Windward Islands]]. Bananas became the main export after the [[e:second-world-war|Second World War]].
colony-of-saint-lucia.e: [[s:saint-lucia|Saint Lucia]] joined the [[s:west-indies-federation|West Indies Federation]], became an [[e:west-indies-associated-states|Associated State]] in 1967 and gained independence as Saint Lucia on 22 February 1979. The economist [[e:w-arthur-lewis|Arthur Lewis]] and the poet [[e:derek-walcott|Derek Walcott]], both born under colonial rule, later won [[e:nobel-prize|Nobel Prizes]].

caliphate-of-cordoba.t: The Umayyad caliphate of al-Andalus, which made Córdoba the largest city in western Europe and a centre of learning before collapsing in 1031.
caliphate-of-cordoba.o: [[e:abd-al-rahman-iii|Abd al-Rahman III]], emir from 912, restored Umayyad control over the rebellious regions of [[e:al-andalus|al-Andalus]]. In 929 he proclaimed himself [[e:caliphate|caliph]], challenging both the [[e:abbasid-caliphate|Abbasids]] and the new Fatimid caliphate in [[e:north-africa|North Africa]], and took [[e:ceuta|Ceuta]] and other ports across the Strait.
caliphate-of-cordoba.r: The [[e:caliphate|caliphate]] was a centralised state with a professional army, a strong navy and a wealthy treasury. [[e:abd-al-rahman-iii|Abd al-Rahman III]] built the palace city of [[e:madinat-al-zahra|Madinat al-Zahra]], and [[e:al-hakam-ii|al-Hakam II]] gathered a vast library and enlarged the [[e:mosque-cathedral-of-cordoba|Great Mosque]]. Muslims, Christians and [[e:jews|Jews]] took part in a flourishing culture of science, medicine and poetry. From 978 the hajib [[e:almanzor|Almanzor]] ruled for the weak [[e:hisham-ii|Hisham II]] and raided the Christian north, sacking [[s:spanish-jamaica|Santiago]] in 997.
caliphate-of-cordoba.e: After [[e:almanzor|Almanzor's]] sons died, civil war broke out in 1009, [[e:madinat-al-zahra|Madinat al-Zahra]] was sacked, and [[e:caliphate|caliphs]] followed in quick succession. In 1031 the Córdoban notables abolished the caliphate, and [[e:al-andalus|al-Andalus]] split into the [[e:taifa|taifa]] kingdoms.

county-of-boulogne.t: A Channel-coast county whose counts fought at Hastings, ruled Crusader Jerusalem and married into the English throne.
county-of-boulogne.o: [[e:boulogne-sur-mer|Boulogne]] took shape in the late 9th and early 10th centuries under counts linked to the house of [[s:county-of-flanders|Flanders]]; [[e:adalulf-count-of-boulogne|Adalulf]], a son of [[e:baldwin-ii-margrave-of-flanders|Baldwin II of Flanders]], held it in the 910s. The port's position on the shortest crossing to [[e:england|England]] shaped its history from the start.
county-of-boulogne.r: The counts drew wealth from the port, cross-[[e:english-channel|Channel]] trade and lands in [[e:england|England]]. [[e:eustace-ii-count-of-boulogne|Eustace II]] fought for [[e:william-the-conqueror|William the Conqueror]] at [[e:battle-of-hastings|Hastings]] in 1066, and his sons [[e:godfrey-of-bouillon|Godfrey of Bouillon]] and Baldwin I led the First Crusade and ruled [[e:jerusalem|Jerusalem]]. [[e:matilda-i-countess-of-boulogne|Countess Matilda]] married [[e:stephen-king-of-england|Stephen of England]]. Count [[e:renaud-de-dammartin|Renaud de Dammartin]] fought against [[e:philip-ii-of-france|Philip II]] at [[e:battle-of-bouvines|Bouvines]] in 1214 and lost his lands.
county-of-boulogne.e: The county passed through the houses of [[s:county-of-auvergne|Auvergne]] and [[e:house-of-la-tour-dauvergne|La Tour]] before the [[s:burgundian-state|Burgundian State]] took it in 1435. After [[e:charles-the-bold|Charles the Bold's]] death, [[e:louis-xi|Louis XI]] seized it in 1477 and placed it under the Virgin of [[e:boulogne-sur-mer|Boulogne]], holding it directly for the [[s:kingdom-of-france|Kingdom of France]].

confederate-ireland.t: The Catholic government formed at Kilkenny during the Irish Confederate Wars, which ruled most of Ireland in the 1640s until Cromwell's conquest.
confederate-ireland.o: The rebellion of October 1641 by Catholic Irish [[e:gentry|gentry]] spread across the island. In 1642 Catholic clergy and lords formed the Confederation of Kilkenny, a government loyal to Charles I but demanding Catholic rights and self-government for Ireland.
confederate-ireland.r: A General Assembly and a [[e:supreme-council-of-the-irish-confederation|Supreme Council]] governed, raising taxes and armies. Its motto was 'Irishmen united for God, King and country'. The papal nuncio Rinuccini divided the Confederates over peace with the king. [[e:owen-roe-oneill|Owen Roe O'Neill]] won the [[e:battle-of-benburb|Battle of Benburb]] in 1646, while [[e:thomas-preston-1st-viscount-tara|Thomas Preston]] led the [[s:kingdom-of-leinster|Leinster]] army.
confederate-ireland.e: The Confederation dissolved itself in 1649 to ally with the royalists under [[e:james-butler-1st-duke-of-ormonde|Ormond]]. [[e:oliver-cromwell|Oliver Cromwell's]] campaign from 1649 and the surrender of the last Irish forces in 1652 ended it, followed by massive land confiscation under the [[s:commonwealth-of-england|Commonwealth of England]].

commune-of-novara.t: A Piedmontese city-republic between Milan and Vercelli, caught for two centuries between its larger neighbours until absorbed by the Visconti.
commune-of-novara.o: Novara, an old Roman town on the road from [[s:duchy-of-milan|Milan]] to [[e:turin|Turin]], had a commune governed by consuls by 1116, gradually taking power from its [[e:bishop|bishops]] and the counts of Biandrate.
commune-of-novara.r: The commune was governed by consuls and later a podestà. It joined the [[s:lombard-league|Lombard League]] against [[e:frederick-barbarossa|Frederick Barbarossa]], but its position between [[s:duchy-of-milan|Milan]] and [[s:commune-of-vercelli|Vercelli]] made it a frequent battleground. Grain farming in its countryside and traffic on the road to the western [[e:alps|Alps]] supported the town. In the 13th and 14th centuries the Tornielli and Brusati families led rival factions.
commune-of-novara.e: In 1332 Novara submitted to [[e:azzone-visconti|Azzone Visconti]] and became part of the [[s:lordship-of-milan|Lordship of Milan]]. It remained [[s:duchy-of-milan|Milanese]] until passing to the [[s:kingdom-of-sardinia|Kingdom of Sardinia]] in 1738.

county-of-schwarzburg.t: A Thuringian county whose counts briefly gave Germany a rival king and whose two branches survived as principalities until 1918.
county-of-schwarzburg.o: [[e:sizzo-iii-of-schwarzburg|Sizzo III]], who held lands in the [[e:thuringian-forest|Thuringian Forest]], called himself count of Schwarzburg in 1123 after the castle on the [[e:schwarza-saale|Schwarza]] river. The family held scattered lands in [[e:thuringia|Thuringia]] around [[e:arnstadt|Arnstadt]], [[e:rudolstadt|Rudolstadt]] and [[e:sondershausen|Sondershausen]], expanding through marriage and purchase.
county-of-schwarzburg.r: The counts were among the leading Thuringian nobles alongside the [[e:house-of-wettin|Wettins]]. In 1349 Count [[e:gunther-von-schwarzburg|Günther XXI of Schwarzburg]] was elected anti-king against Charles IV but resigned within months and died the same year. The family split into many lines, including [[e:arnstadt|Arnstadt]] and [[e:sondershausen|Sondershausen]]. [[e:lutheranism|Lutheranism]] was adopted in the 16th century.
county-of-schwarzburg.e: In 1599 the [[e:treaty-of-stadtilm|Treaty of Stadtilm]] divided the lands into [[s:principality-of-schwarzburg-rudolstadt|Schwarzburg-Rudolstadt]] and [[s:principality-of-schwarzburg-sondershausen|Schwarzburg-Sondershausen]], which became principalities in 1697 and 1710. Both lasted until 1918 and became part of the state of [[e:thuringia|Thuringia]] in 1920.

canton-of-zug.t: A small lakeside canton that joined the Swiss Confederacy in 1352 and remained a Catholic stronghold of central Switzerland.
canton-of-zug.o: Zug was a [[s:county-of-habsburg|Habsburg]] town on the [[e:lake-zug|Lake of Zug]], surrounded by rural communities. In 1352 Confederate forces besieged it, and the town and countryside joined the alliance of the [[s:canton-of-zurich|Canton of Zürich]] and the forest cantons, though [[e:habsburg-dynasty|Habsburg]] influence lingered until the Swiss victory at [[e:battle-of-sempach|Sempach]] in 1386. Zug counted among the eight old cantons.
canton-of-zug.r: Government was unusually shared between the town of Zug and three rural communes, [[e:ageri|Ägeri]], [[e:menzingen|Menzingen]] and [[e:baar-switzerland|Baar]], which met together in the [[e:landsgemeinde|Landsgemeinde]] and rotated offices. The economy rested on farming, fishing, trade and [[e:mercenary|mercenary]] service. Zug remained Catholic in the [[e:protestant-reformation|Reformation]] and fought on the Catholic side at [[e:battle-of-kappel|Kappel]] in 1531.
canton-of-zug.e: The old order ended with the French invasion of 1798 and the [[s:helvetic-republic|Helvetic Republic]]. Restored as a canton in 1803, Zug remains part of the [[s:swiss-confederation|Swiss Confederation]] and is now known as a low-tax business centre.

captaincy-general-of-santo-domingo.t: Spain's first colony in the Americas, on Hispaniola, from which the conquest of the Caribbean and mainland was launched.
captaincy-general-of-santo-domingo.o: [[e:christopher-columbus|Columbus]] founded [[e:la-isabela|La Isabela]] on the north coast of [[e:hispaniola|Hispaniola]] in 1493, and [[e:santo-domingo|Santo Domingo]] was established on the south coast in 1496-98. Under [[e:nicolas-de-ovando|Nicolás de Ovando]], governor from 1502, the [[e:taino|Taíno]] chiefdoms were destroyed and the island became the base of Spanish power in the [[e:caribbean|Caribbean]].
captaincy-general-of-santo-domingo.r: [[e:santo-domingo|Santo Domingo]] received the first [[e:audiencia|Audiencia]] in the [[e:americas|Americas]] in 1511, the first cathedral and, in 1538, a university. Gold mining using [[e:taino|Taíno]] forced labour gave way to [[e:sugar-plantation|sugar]] and [[e:cattle|cattle]] ranching worked by enslaved Africans. As [[e:spain|Spain's]] attention turned to [[s:mexico|Mexico]] and [[e:peru|Peru]], the colony declined. The 'devastations' of 1605-06 depopulated the north and west to stop smuggling.
captaincy-general-of-santo-domingo.e: French buccaneers settled the empty west, which [[e:spain|Spain]] recognised as [[s:saint-domingue|Saint-Domingue]] in 1697. By the Peace of [[s:canton-of-basel|Basel]] in 1795 Spain ceded the rest of the island to [[e:france|France]]. The former colony later became the [[s:first-dominican-republic|Dominican Republic]].

cisplatina.t: The province of Uruguay under Portuguese and then Brazilian rule, whose struggle for freedom led to the independence of Uruguay.
cisplatina.o: Portuguese forces from [[s:new-republic-brazil|Brazil]] invaded the [[s:eastern-province|Banda Oriental]] in 1816 to crush [[e:jose-gervasio-artigas|José Artigas]], and General [[e:carlos-frederico-lecor|Carlos Frederico Lecor]] entered [[e:montevideo|Montevideo]] in January 1817, ending the Eastern Province. In 1821 a congress in Montevideo, under Portuguese pressure, voted to annex the territory as the Cisplatine Province.
cisplatina.r: [[e:carlos-frederico-lecor|Lecor]] governed with the support of [[e:montevideo|Montevideo's]] merchants and landowners. When [[s:new-republic-brazil|Brazil]] declared independence in 1822, Cisplatina passed to the [[e:brazilian-empire|Empire of Brazil]] after Portuguese troops in Montevideo were expelled in 1824. In 1825 the [[e:thirty-three-orientals|Thirty-Three Orientals]] led by [[e:juan-antonio-lavalleja|Juan Antonio Lavalleja]] landed and declared union with the [[s:united-provinces-of-the-rio-de-la-plata|United Provinces of the Río de la Plata]], sparking the [[e:cisplatine-war|Cisplatine War]].
cisplatina.e: Neither side could win: [[e:argentina|Argentina's]] victory at [[e:battle-of-ituzaingo|Ituzaingó]] in 1827 was offset by a Brazilian [[e:naval-blockade|blockade]]. Through British mediation, the [[e:preliminary-peace-convention|Preliminary Peace Convention]] of 1828 created the independent [[s:oriental-republic-of-uruguay|Oriental Republic of Uruguay]].

cr.a: Variant of the flag designed by José Gervasio Artigas and José María de Roo

county-of-zeeland.t: The island county at the mouths of the Scheldt, Maas and Rhine, disputed by Holland and Flanders and later a stronghold of the Dutch Revolt.
county-of-zeeland.o: The islands of Zeeland had long been disputed between the counts of [[s:county-of-flanders|Flanders]] and the counts of Holland, who shared them in a complex arrangement. By the Treaty of Paris in 1323 [[e:flanders|Flanders]] gave up its claims, and Zeeland became a county ruled by the counts of Holland, with [[e:middelburg|Middelburg]] as its main town.
county-of-zeeland.r: Zeeland was a land of reclaimed islands, dykes and seaports. [[e:middelburg|Middelburg]], [[e:zierikzee|Zierikzee]], [[e:veere|Veere]] and [[e:vlissingen|Flushing]] traded in wine, salt, cloth and fish, and the islands were vulnerable to great floods. The county had its own estates but shared rulers with the [[s:county-of-holland|County of Holland]], passing with it to the [[e:house-of-wittelsbach|Wittelsbachs]], the [[s:burgundian-state|Burgundian State]] and the [[e:habsburg-dynasty|Habsburgs]].
county-of-zeeland.e: In 1572 the [[e:sea-beggars|Sea Beggars]] took [[e:vlissingen|Flushing]], and Zeeland became, with Holland, the core of the [[e:dutch-revolt|Dutch Revolt]]. It joined the [[e:union-of-utrecht|Union of Utrecht]] in 1579, and after the [[e:act-of-abjuration|Act of Abjuration]] of 1581 it was a province of the [[s:dutch-republic|Dutch Republic]].

commune-of-brescia.t: A combative Lombard city-republic, home of the reformer Arnold of Brescia, that withstood a siege by Emperor Frederick II in 1238.
commune-of-brescia.o: [[e:brescia|Brescia's]] citizens took power from their [[e:bishop|bishop]] in the late 11th and early 12th centuries, and the commune was governed by consuls by around 1100. It controlled a rich territory of valleys, iron mines and lakes between [[e:lake-garda|Lake Garda]] and [[e:lake-iseo|Lake Iseo]].
commune-of-brescia.r: The commune was run by consuls and later a podestà. The preacher [[e:arnold-of-brescia|Arnold of Brescia]], who attacked clerical wealth, came from the city. [[e:brescia|Brescia]] joined the [[s:lombard-league|Lombard League]] against [[e:frederick-barbarossa|Frederick Barbarossa]], resisted a long siege by Frederick II in 1238 and another by [[e:henry-vii-holy-roman-emperor|Henry VII]] in 1311. It was famed for iron working and arms making, and its Old Cathedral, the [[e:old-cathedral-brescia|Rotonda]], dates from this era.
commune-of-brescia.e: Exhausted by faction, [[e:brescia|Brescia]] accepted the [[e:scaliger|Scaliger]] lords of [[s:commune-of-verona|Verona]] and then in 1337 submitted to [[e:azzone-visconti|Azzone Visconti]], joining the [[s:lordship-of-milan|Lordship of Milan]]. The [[s:republic-of-venice|Republic of Venice]] took it in 1426.

county-of-kladsko.t: A mountain-ringed county on the Bohemian-Silesian border, created by George of Poděbrady in 1459 and won by Prussia in 1742.
county-of-kladsko.o: The [[e:klodzko|Kłodzko]] (Glatz) Land, a basin enclosed by the [[e:sudetes|Sudeten]] mountains, had long belonged to [[s:kingdom-of-bohemia|Bohemia]], though at times it was held by Silesian dukes. In 1459 [[e:george-of-podebrady|George of Poděbrady]], king of the Kingdom of [[e:bohemia|Bohemia]], raised it to a county and granted it to his sons, who also held the [[s:duchy-of-ziebice|Duchy of Ziębice]].
county-of-kladsko.r: The county passed through several hands before coming under the [[e:habsburg-dynasty|Habsburgs]] in the 16th century. Its fortress at [[e:klodzko|Kłodzko]] guarded the road from [[s:duchy-of-silesia|Silesia]] into [[s:kingdom-of-bohemia|Bohemia]]. [[e:lutheranism|Lutheranism]] spread widely until the [[e:counter-reformation|Counter-Reformation]] restored [[e:catholicism|Catholicism]] after 1622. [[e:glassmaking|Glassmaking]], linen weaving and spa towns such as [[e:kudowa-zdroj|Kudowa]] and Duszniki supported the economy.
county-of-kladsko.e: In 1742 [[e:frederick-the-great|Frederick II of Prussia]] annexed the county with most of [[s:duchy-of-silesia|Silesia]], and it was incorporated into Prussian Silesia. After the [[e:second-world-war|Second World War]] it became part of [[e:poland|Poland]], and its German population was expelled.

canton-military-government.t: The rival government that Sun Yat-sen set up in Guangzhou to defend the constitution against Beijing's warlords, the cradle of the Nationalist revolution.
canton-military-government.o: In 1917 Premier [[e:duan-qirui|Duan Qirui]] of the [[s:beiyang-government|Beiyang government]] refused to restore the dissolved parliament. [[e:sun-yat-sen|Sun Yat-sen]] launched the Constitutional Protection Movement, and members of parliament who had followed him to [[e:guangzhou|Guangzhou]] elected him generalissimo of a military government, with support from southern warlords.
canton-military-government.r: The government depended on [[e:guangxi|Guangxi]] and [[e:yunnan|Yunnan]] generals, who forced Sun out in 1918 and ruled through a directorate under [[e:cen-chunxuan|Cen Chunxuan]]. [[e:chen-jiongming|Chen Jiongming]] brought Sun back in 1920, and in 1921 he became extraordinary president, but Chen turned against him in 1922. Returning in 1923, Sun accepted Soviet aid, admitted Communists to his party and founded the [[e:whampoa-military-academy|Whampoa Military Academy]] under [[e:chiang-kai-shek|Chiang Kai-shek]] in 1924.
canton-military-government.e: Sun died in [[e:beijing|Beijing]] in March 1925 while negotiating with the northern warlords. In July 1925 the regime was reorganised as the [[s:nationalist-government|Nationalist government]], which launched the [[e:northern-expedition|Northern Expedition]] the following year and went on to rule [[e:china|China]] from [[e:nanjing|Nanjing]].

cimmerians.t: Horse-riding raiders of the Pontic steppe whose attacks shook Urartu, Phrygia and Lydia in the 8th and 7th centuries BCE.
cimmerians.o: The Cimmerians are known almost entirely from outside sources: Assyrian letters calling them Gimirri, a line in [[e:homer|Homer]] and the later accounts of [[e:herodotus|Herodotus]], who placed their [[e:bantustan|homeland]] north of the [[e:black-sea|Black Sea]]. Archaeologists still debate which steppe cultures belonged to them. They appear in history around 714 BCE, when they defeated the army of [[s:kingdom-of-urartu|Urartu]].
cimmerians.r: They were mounted nomads led by war chiefs, apparently speaking an Iranian language. Pushed south of the [[e:caucasus|Caucasus]], according to [[e:herodotus|Herodotus]] by the [[e:scythians|Scythians]], they became [[e:mercenary|mercenaries]] and raiders across [[e:anatolia|Anatolia]]. They overran [[s:kingdom-of-phrygia|Phrygia]] around 696 BCE, when [[e:midas|King Midas]] is said to have killed himself, and later sacked [[e:sardis|Sardis]], killing [[e:gyges-of-lydia|Gyges of Lydia]] around 644 BCE.
cimmerians.e: Their leader [[e:dugdamme|Dugdamme]], the Lygdamis of Greek sources, died campaigning against [[e:assyrian-empire|Assyria]] around 640 BCE, and [[e:alyattes|Alyattes of Lydia]] finally drove the remaining bands out of [[e:anatolia|Anatolia]]. Survivors merged with neighbouring peoples. Their name lived on in Greek legend, in the [[e:kerch-strait|Cimmerian Bosporus]] and, through Welsh antiquarians, in the mistaken idea that they were ancestors of the [[e:welsh-people|Cymry]].

chiefdom-of-oahu.t: The Hawaiian chiefdom of Oʻahu, centred on Waikīkī, whose conquest by Kamehameha I at the Battle of Nuʻuanu in 1795 created the Kingdom of Hawaii.
chiefdom-of-oahu.o: [[e:oahu|Oʻahu's]] districts were drawn under a single ruling line by around 1400. Tradition remembers the 16th-century aliʻi nui [[e:kakuhihewa|Kākuhihewa]] as presiding over a peaceful, prosperous island, and chiefly residences clustered at [[e:waikiki|Waikīkī]], with its fishponds and coconut groves, and at sacred sites such as [[e:kukaniloko|Kūkaniloko]], the royal birthplace in central Oʻahu.
chiefdom-of-oahu.r: The aliʻi nui ruled through priests, district chiefs and the kapu system, and the island's fertile valleys supported intensive taro terraces and large fishponds. In 1773 the chiefs chose [[e:kahahana|Kahahana]] as ruler, but in 1783 [[e:kahekili-ii|Kahekili II]] of the [[s:chiefdom-of-maui|Chiefdom of Maui]] conquered [[e:oahu|Oʻahu]] and ruled it until his death in 1794. His son [[e:kalanikupule|Kalanikūpule]] defeated [[e:kaeokulani|Kaʻeokulani]] of [[e:kauai|Kauaʻi]] that year with the help of the British trader [[e:william-brown-sea-captain|William Brown]].
chiefdom-of-oahu.e: In 1795 [[e:kamehameha-i|Kamehameha I]] landed at [[e:waikiki|Waikīkī]] and defeated [[e:kalanikupule|Kalanikūpule]] at the [[e:battle-of-nuuanu|Battle of Nuʻuanu]], where many defenders were driven over the Pali cliffs. [[e:oahu|Oʻahu]] became part of the [[s:kingdom-of-hawaii|Kingdom of Hawaii]], and [[e:honolulu|Honolulu]] later grew into its capital.

colony-of-antigua.t: English and later British sugar colony that hosted the Royal Navy's main Leeward Islands base and became independent as Antigua and Barbuda in 1981.
colony-of-antigua.o: English colonists from [[s:colony-of-saint-christopher|Saint Kitts]] under [[e:edward-warner|Edward Warner]] settled Antigua in 1632. The French briefly occupied it in 1666, but the [[e:treaty-of-breda-1667|Treaty of Breda]] in 1667 restored English rule. [[e:christopher-codrington-1640-1698|Christopher Codrington]] began large-scale [[e:sugar-plantation|sugar]] planting in 1674, and the island was soon covered with plantations and windmills.
colony-of-antigua.r: Antigua had its own governor, council and assembly, and [[e:st-johns-antigua-and-barbuda|St John's]] served as capital of the wider [[s:leeward-islands-colony|Leeward Islands colony]] for long periods. [[e:sugar-plantation|Sugar]] estates relied on enslaved Africans, and a planned rising in 1736 was crushed with savage executions. English Harbour, later [[e:nelsons-dockyard|Nelson's Dockyard]], was the [[e:royal-navy|Royal Navy's]] chief base in the [[e:leeward-islands|Leewards]]. Antigua freed its enslaved people in 1834 without the apprenticeship system used elsewhere.
colony-of-antigua.e: After emancipation the island remained poor and dependent on [[e:sugar-plantation|sugar]].
