Labour activism led by [[e:vere-bird|Vere Bird]] built a political movement in the mid-20th century. Antigua became an [[e:west-indies-associated-states|Associated State]] in 1967 and gained independence, together with [[e:barbuda|Barbuda]] and [[e:redonda|Redonda]], as [[s:antigua-and-barbuda|Antigua and Barbuda]] on 1 November 1981.

chionites.t: Hunnic invaders of Bactria in the 4th century who fought both against and alongside Sasanian Persia, including at the siege of Amida in 359.
chionites.o: The Chionites, Xionites in [[e:latin|Latin]] and Xiyon in [[e:middle-persian|Middle Persian]], appear in Roman and Persian sources from the mid-4th century as nomads who moved into [[e:transoxiana|Transoxiana]] and [[s:greco-bactrian-kingdom|Bactria]] from the north, threatening the [[s:kushano-sasanian-kingdom|Kushano-Sasanian Kingdom]]. Their exact origin and relation to the European [[e:huns|Huns]] are debated.
chionites.r: [[e:shapur-ii|Shapur II]] fought them on his eastern frontier around 350 before making an alliance, and [[e:ammianus-marcellinus|Ammianus Marcellinus]] describes their king [[e:grumbates|Grumbates]] leading Chionite troops alongside the [[e:persians|Persians]] at the siege of the Roman city of [[e:amida|Amida]] in 359, where Grumbates' son was killed. Little is known of their internal organisation beyond rule by kings over mounted warrior bands.
chionites.e: The Chionites appear to have given rise to, or been absorbed by, the later Hunnic dynasties of the region, notably the [[s:kidarite-kingdom|Kidarite Kingdom]] and the [[s:alchon-huns|Alchon Huns]], by the early 5th century.

captaincy-general-of-the-philippines.t: Spain's colony in the Philippines from 1565 to 1898, governed from Manila and linked to the Americas by the Manila galleon.
captaincy-general-of-the-philippines.o: [[e:miguel-lopez-de-legazpi|Miguel Lopez de Legazpi]] arrived from [[s:new-spain|New Spain]] in 1565, founded a settlement at [[e:cebu|Cebu]] and in 1571 took the [[s:kingdom-of-maynila|Kingdom of Maynila]], making [[e:manila|Manila]] the capital. The islands, named after [[e:philip-ii-of-spain|Philip II]], were administered through the [[e:viceroyalty-of-new-spain|Viceroyalty of New Spain]] until Mexican independence in 1821.
captaincy-general-of-the-philippines.r: A governor-general ruled with the Real [[e:audiencia|Audiencia]], while friars of the religious orders converted most lowland Filipinos to [[e:catholicism|Catholicism]] and wielded great local power. The [[e:manila-galleon|Manila galleons]] carried Chinese [[e:silk|silk]] and [[e:porcelain|porcelain]] to [[e:acapulco|Acapulco]] for Mexican [[e:silver|silver]] from 1565 to 1815. Governor [[e:jose-basco-y-vargas|Jose Basco y Vargas]] introduced the tobacco monopoly in 1782. Muslim [[e:mindanao|Mindanao]] and Sulu resisted conquest.
captaincy-general-of-the-philippines.e: [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]] occupied [[e:manila|Manila]] in 1762 to 1764. [[e:nationalism|Nationalism]] grew after the Cavite mutiny of 1872, and the execution of [[e:jose-rizal|Jose Rizal]] in 1896 fed the [[e:philippine-revolution|Philippine Revolution]]. [[e:spain|Spain]] ceded the islands to the [[s:united-states|United States]] in the [[e:treaty-of-paris-1898|Treaty of Paris]] of 1898.

cr.a: previous version Ignaciogavira; current version HansenBCN, designs from SanchoPanzaXXI

chalcidian-league.t: Federation of the Greek towns of Chalcidice centred on Olynthus, the strongest power of the northern Aegean until Philip II of Macedon destroyed it.
chalcidian-league.o: In 432 BCE the Chalcidian towns, persuaded by [[e:perdiccas-ii-of-macedon|Perdiccas II of Macedon]], revolted from the [[s:delian-league|Delian League]], and many of their people moved into [[s:olynthus|Olynthus]]. From this union grew a federal state calling itself 'the Chalcidians'. With help from the Spartan [[e:brasidas|Brasidas]] in 424 BCE it secured its independence from [[s:athens|Athens]].
chalcidian-league.r: Member towns shared citizenship, laws on marriage and property and a common [[e:silver|silver]] coinage showing [[e:apollo|Apollo]] and his lyre, among the finest of the age. In the early 4th century BCE the league grew aggressively, absorbing [[s:potidaea|Potidaea]] and even occupying [[s:pella|Pella]], the Macedonian capital, during the troubles of [[e:amyntas-iii-of-macedon|Amyntas III]].
chalcidian-league.e: Appeals from [[e:acanthus-greece|Acanthus]] and Apollonia brought a Spartan war (382-379 BCE) that forced the league to dissolve. It revived, allied first with [[e:philip-ii-of-macedon|Philip II]] and then with [[s:athens|Athens]], but Philip besieged [[s:olynthus|Olynthus]] and destroyed it in 348 BCE, ending the league and annexing [[e:chalcidice|Chalcidice]] to [[e:kingdom-of-macedon|Macedon]].

chan-santa-cruz.t: Independent Maya state in eastern Yucatán, led in the name of a Talking Cross, that resisted Mexico for half a century during the Caste War.
chan-santa-cruz.o: The [[e:caste|Caste]] War broke out in Yucatán in 1847. When Maya rebels were driven back into the eastern forests, a cross appeared in 1850 at a cenote near the settlement of [[e:felipe-carrillo-puerto-quintana-roo|Chan Santa Cruz]] and began to speak, guiding them in war. [[e:jose-maria-barrera|José María Barrera]], a rebel leader, promoted the cult, and the town became the rebels' sacred capital.
chan-santa-cruz.r: The Cruzob, people of the cross, combined Maya and Catholic belief in a military theocracy. The cross's orders were conveyed through officials such as the [[e:tatich|Tatich]], or Patron of the Cross, and the Interpreter, and the population was organised in military companies that guarded the shrine. The state traded [[e:timber|timber]] and captured goods for guns and powder with [[s:british-honduras|British Honduras]], which helped it survive.
chan-santa-cruz.e: After [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]] agreed a border treaty with [[s:mexico|Mexico]] in 1893 and arms supplies dwindled, Mexican troops under General [[e:ignacio-bravo|Ignacio Bravo]] took [[e:felipe-carrillo-puerto-quintana-roo|Chan Santa Cruz]] in 1901. The town was renamed and is now Felipe Carrillo Puerto. Some Cruzob communities held out until the 1930s and still keep the cross's shrines.
chan-santa-cruz.re: Cult of the Talking Cross (Maya Christianity)

commune-of-lodi.t: A Lombard city-republic refounded on a new site by Frederick Barbarossa in 1158 after Milan had destroyed the old town.
commune-of-lodi.o: [[s:duchy-of-milan|Milan]] destroyed the old town of [[e:lodi-dynasty|Lodi]] in 1111 and again in 1158. That year [[e:frederick-barbarossa|Emperor Frederick Barbarossa]], whom the Lodigiani had appealed to, refounded the city on a new site on the [[e:adda|Adda]], a few miles from the old one, now [[e:lodi-vecchio|Lodi Vecchio]]. The new commune grew under imperial protection.
commune-of-lodi.r: The commune was governed by consuls and later a podestà. Although founded as an imperial ally, [[e:lodi-dynasty|Lodi]] joined the [[s:lombard-league|Lombard League]] in 1167. The cathedral was begun in the year of its refoundation. The town lived from farming and river trade, but was always overshadowed by [[s:duchy-of-milan|Milan]]. In the 13th and 14th centuries the Fissiraga and Vistarini families competed for control.
commune-of-lodi.e: In 1335 [[e:lodi-dynasty|Lodi]] submitted to [[e:azzone-visconti|Azzone Visconti]] and became part of the [[s:lordship-of-milan|Lordship of Milan]]. The Peace of Lodi of 1454 between [[s:duchy-of-milan|Milan]] and [[e:venice|Venice]] was later signed there.

county-of-jaffa-and-ascalon.t: A Crusader county on the southern coast of the Kingdom of Jerusalem, often held by royal princes and later by the jurist John of Ibelin.
county-of-jaffa-and-ascalon.o: [[e:jaffa|Jaffa]], the port of [[e:jerusalem|Jerusalem]], was occupied by the crusaders in 1099. It became a county in the early 12th century under the Le Puiset family, until [[e:hugh-ii-of-jaffa|Hugh II]] revolted against [[e:fulk-king-of-jerusalem|King Fulk]] in 1134 and was exiled. [[e:baldwin-iii-of-jerusalem|Baldwin III]] captured [[e:ashkelon|Ascalon]] from the [[e:fatimid-caliphate|Fatimids]] in 1153, and the combined county was given to his brother [[e:amalric-i-of-jerusalem|Amalric]].
county-of-jaffa-and-ascalon.r: The county was frequently held by members of the royal family, including [[e:amalric-i-of-jerusalem|Amalric]] and later [[e:guy-of-lusignan|Guy of Lusignan]], and its revenues came from the port and coastal farmland. [[e:richard-i-of-england|Richard I of England]] fought at [[e:jaffa|Jaffa]] in 1192, and the [[e:treaty-of-jaffa-1192|Treaty of Jaffa]] ended the [[e:third-crusade|Third Crusade]] there. In the 13th century it passed to the [[e:house-of-brienne|Brienne]] family and then to [[e:john-of-ibelin-count-of-jaffa|John of Ibelin]], author of the main legal treatise of the kingdom.
county-of-jaffa-and-ascalon.e: [[e:ashkelon|Ascalon]] was lost in 1187 and later dismantled. [[e:baybars|Baybars]] captured [[e:jaffa|Jaffa]] in March 1268, ending the county.

county-of-nassau-dillenburg.t: Ottonian Nassau county in the Siegerland and Dill valley, birthplace of William the Silent and the root of the Dutch royal house of Orange-Nassau.
county-of-nassau-dillenburg.o: In 1255 the counts of [[s:county-of-nassau|Nassau]] divided their lands along the [[e:lahn|Lahn]]. [[e:walram-ii-count-of-nassau|Walram]] took the south, while [[e:otto-i-duke-of-brunswick-gottingen|Otto I]] received the northern lands with [[e:siegen|Siegen]], [[e:dillenburg|Dillenburg]] and [[e:herborn|Herborn]], founding the Ottonian line. His descendants ruled these lands as counts of Nassau-Dillenburg, repeatedly dividing and reuniting them.
county-of-nassau-dillenburg.r: The county was hilly and wooded, rich in iron ore from the [[e:siegerland|Siegerland]]. Count [[e:engelbert-i-of-nassau|Engelbert I]] acquired [[e:breda|Breda]] through marriage in 1403, linking the family to the [[s:kingdom-of-the-netherlands|Netherlands]]. [[e:william-i-count-of-nassau-siegen|William the Rich]] introduced the [[e:protestant-reformation|Reformation]]; his son [[e:william-the-silent|William the Silent]], born at [[e:dillenburg|Dillenburg]] in 1533, inherited [[s:principality-of-orange|Orange]]. [[e:john-vi-count-of-nassau-dillenburg|John VI]] adopted [[e:calvinism|Reformed Protestantism]] and founded the [[e:herborn-academy|Herborn Academy]] in 1584.
county-of-nassau-dillenburg.e: The lands were divided among several lines, including [[s:principality-of-nassau-siegen|Nassau-Siegen]], Nassau-[[e:diez|Dietz]] and [[s:principality-of-nassau-hadamar|Nassau-Hadamar]]. When the [[e:dillenburg|Dillenburg]] line died out in 1739, its lands passed to Nassau-Dietz, whose prince [[e:william-iv-prince-of-orange|William IV]] became stadtholder of the [[s:dutch-republic|Dutch Republic]], ancestor of the [[e:dutch|Dutch]] royal house.

county-of-foix.t: A Pyrenean county that sheltered Cathars, produced the hunter-prince Gaston Fébus and passed through Navarre to Henry IV.
county-of-foix.o: Around 1012 the lands of the count of [[e:carcassonne|Carcassonne]] were divided, and his son [[e:bernard-roger-of-foix|Bernard-Roger]] received the region around Foix, which became a separate county under the castle above the [[e:ariege-river|Ariège]]. His son Roger I is the first to be called count of Foix.
county-of-foix.r: The counts ruled a mountainous land of pasture and iron mines. Count [[e:raymond-roger-of-foix|Raymond-Roger]] fought the crusaders in the [[e:albigensian-crusade|Albigensian Crusade]], and many of his family supported the [[e:catharism|Cathars]]. In 1290 the counts inherited [[s:viscounty-of-bearn|Béarn]], and [[e:gaston-iii-of-foix|Gaston III Fébus]] ruled both from [[e:orthez|Orthez]] as a near-sovereign prince and wrote a famous hunting book.
county-of-foix.e: The house of Foix inherited the throne of [[e:kingdom-of-navarre|Navarre]] in 1479, then passed to the [[e:house-of-albret|Albrets]]. Through [[e:jeanne-dalbret|Jeanne d'Albret]] it reached [[e:henry-iv-of-france|Henry IV]], who in 1607 united his personal lands, including Foix, with the [[s:kingdom-of-france|Kingdom of France]].

champa.t: A string of Cham kingdoms along the central Vietnamese coast for some 1,600 years, rich from maritime trade and famous for its red-brick Hindu temples.
champa.o: Chinese sources record that around 192 a local official in the Han commandery of Rinan rebelled and founded the kingdom of Linyi, usually seen as the origin of Champa. The [[e:cham|Cham]], an Austronesian-speaking people, built a series of polities along the coast from [[e:quang-binh-province|Quang Binh]] to [[e:phan-thiet|Phan Thiet]], using the name Champa in [[e:sanskrit|Sanskrit]] inscriptions from the 7th century.
champa.r: Champa was less a single state than a federation of regions such as [[e:indrapura-champa|Indrapura]], Amaravati, [[e:vijaya-champa|Vijaya]], [[e:kauthara|Kauthara]] and [[e:panduranga|Panduranga]], each with its own centre. Kings patronised [[e:shiva|Shiva]] worship, building temple complexes like [[e:my-son|My Son]] and Po [[s:nagar|Nagar]], and drew wealth from sea trade in aloeswood, [[e:spice-trade|spices]] and ceramics. Champa fought often with the [[s:khmer-empire|Khmer Empire]], sacking [[e:angkor|Angkor]] in 1177, and with [[s:ly-dynasty|Dai Viet]].
champa.e: [[s:ly-dynasty|Dai Viet]]'s southward push captured [[e:vijaya-champa|Vijaya]] in 1471, leaving only [[e:panduranga|Panduranga]] in the far south. This rump survived as a [[e:vassal|vassal]] until the [[s:nguyen-dynasty|Nguyen dynasty]] under [[e:minh-mang|Minh Mang]] abolished it in 1832. Many [[e:cham|Cham]], now largely Muslim, live in [[s:socialist-republic-of-vietnam|Vietnam]] and [[s:kingdom-of-cambodia-1953-1970|Cambodia]] today.

cait.t: A Pictish province in the far north of mainland Scotland, whose name survives in Caithness and in Gaelic Cataibh for Sutherland.
cait.o: Cait is one of the seven Pictish provinces named after the legendary sons of [[e:cruithne-legendary-king|Cruithne]]. The name, perhaps 'cat people', survives in [[e:caithness|Caithness]], the Norse 'headland of the Cats', and Gaelic Cataibh, the name for [[e:sutherland|Sutherland]].
cait.r: Nothing reliable is known of its government or rulers. [[e:broch|Broch]] towers and later Pictish symbol stones show a long-settled farming and seafaring population in the region.
cait.e: From the 9th century Norse settlers from [[e:orkney|Orkney]] took over [[e:caithness|Caithness]], which came under the [[s:earldom-of-orkney|Earldom of Orkney]]. The area was gradually brought into the [[s:kingdom-of-scotland|Kingdom of Scotland]] in the 12th and 13th centuries.

cisalpine-republic.t: Napoleon's largest Italian sister republic, uniting Lombardy, Emilia and Romagna, and an early laboratory for a modern Italian state.
cisalpine-republic.o: On 29 June 1797 [[e:napoleon|Napoleon]] proclaimed the Cisalpine Republic, merging the [[s:transpadane-republic|Transpadane Republic]] with territories that soon included the [[s:cispadane-republic|Cispadane Republic]], [[e:romagna|Romagna]], the [[e:valtellina|Valtellina]] and the former Venetian cities of [[s:commune-of-bergamo|Bergamo]], [[s:commune-of-brescia|Brescia]] and [[e:crema|Crema]]. The [[e:treaty-of-campo-formio|Treaty of Campo Formio]] confirmed it in October 1797.
cisalpine-republic.r: The republic had a constitution modelled on the [[s:french-first-republic|French Directory]], with [[s:duchy-of-milan|Milan]] as capital. It reorganised its territory into [[e:departement|departments]], sold church lands and built a national guard, but the French made and unmade its governments and drew heavy contributions. Debate about Italian identity flourished in [[e:milan|Milan]].
cisalpine-republic.e: An Austro-Russian offensive overthrew the republic in 1799. Restored after [[e:napoleon|Napoleon's]] victory at [[e:battle-of-marengo|Marengo]] in 1800, it was transformed at the [[e:consulta-of-lyon|Consulta of Lyon]] in January 1802 into the [[s:italian-republic-1802-1805|Italian Republic]] (1802–1805).

county-of-veldenz.t: A small Moselle and Palatinate county whose heiress carried it to the Wittelsbachs, founding the line of Palatinate-Zweibrücken.
county-of-veldenz.o: The counts of Veldenz appear around 1112 as a branch of the Nahegau counts, taking their name from Veldenz castle above the [[e:moselle|Moselle]] near [[e:bernkastel-kues|Bernkastel]]. Their lands lay scattered in the [[e:hunsruck|Hunsrück]], along the Moselle and in the western [[s:electoral-palatinate|Palatinate]] around [[e:meisenheim|Meisenheim]] and [[e:lauterecken|Lauterecken]].
county-of-veldenz.r: The county was modest in size, living from vineyards and farming in the hill country, and was held as a fief of the [[s:prince-bishopric-of-verdun|Bishopric of Verdun]]. A second line of counts from the [[s:county-of-hohengeroldseck|Geroldseck]] family ruled from 1259. In 1437 the counts also inherited part of the [[s:county-of-sponheim|County of Sponheim]].
county-of-veldenz.e: Count Frederick III died in 1444 without sons; his daughter Anna had married Stephen, son of [[e:rupert-of-germany|King Rupert]] of the [[s:electoral-palatinate|Palatinate]]. Their heirs formed the house of [[s:palatinate-zweibrucken|Palatinate-Zweibrücken]], ancestors of the later kings of [[e:bavaria|Bavaria]] and of [[e:sweden|Sweden's]] Charles X.

cr.a: Gustav Droysen; derivative work by Beckstet

confederation-of-the-rhine.t: Napoleon's league of German client states, whose creation in 1806 brought the end of the Holy Roman Empire.
confederation-of-the-rhine.o: On 12 July 1806 sixteen German states, including [[e:bavaria|Bavaria]], Württemberg and [[e:baden|Baden]], signed the [[e:rhine-confederation-act|Rhine Confederation Act]] in [[e:paris|Paris]], leaving the [[s:holy-roman-empire|Holy Roman Empire]] under [[e:napoleon|Napoleon's]] protection. [[e:francis-ii|Emperor Francis II]] abdicated as [[e:holy-roman-emperor|Holy Roman Emperor]] on 6 August 1806. [[e:saxony|Saxony]], [[e:westphalia|Westphalia]] and many smaller states joined later, bringing it to some 39 members.
confederation-of-the-rhine.r: [[e:napoleon|Napoleon]] was its protector and [[e:karl-theodor-von-dalberg|Karl Theodor von Dalberg]] its prince-primate. A federal diet in [[e:frankfurt|Frankfurt]] was planned but never met. Members were bound to a military alliance with [[e:france|France]] and had to supply contingents, notably for the 1812 Russian campaign. Within their borders many states introduced Napoleonic reforms, ended [[e:serfdom|serfdom]] and absorbed mediatised lands.
confederation-of-the-rhine.e: After [[e:napoleon|Napoleon's]] defeat at [[e:leipzig|Leipzig]] in October 1813, its members changed sides one by one and the confederation dissolved. The [[e:congress-of-vienna|Congress of Vienna]] replaced it in 1815 with the [[s:german-confederation|German Confederation]].
