castilian-almeria.t: The great Muslim port of Almería under Christian rule for a decade after its capture by a Castilian-led crusade in 1147.
castilian-almeria.o: In 1147 [[e:alfonso-vii-of-leon-and-castile|Alfonso VII of Castile]], styled Emperor of [[e:spain|Spain]], led a coalition including [[s:republic-of-genoa|Genoa]], [[e:pisa|Pisa]], [[e:ramon-berenguer-iv-count-of-barcelona|Ramon Berenguer IV of Barcelona]] and [[e:garcia-ramirez-of-navarre|García Ramírez of Navarre]] against [[e:almeria|Almería]], then a corsair base. The city fell in October 1147, and the Genoese received a share of it.
castilian-almeria.r: [[e:almeria|Almería]] was held as an isolated outpost far from Castilian territory, garrisoned by Castilian troops while [[s:republic-of-genoa|Genoa]] sought trading privileges. Much of the Muslim population had been killed, enslaved or had fled, and the economy declined. The conquest was celebrated in the [[e:latin|Latin]] [[e:poem-of-almeria|Poem of Almería]].
castilian-almeria.e: In 1157 the [[e:almohad-caliphate|Almohads]] besieged and recaptured the city. [[e:alfonso-vii-of-leon-and-castile|Alfonso VII]], failing to relieve it, died on his way home. [[e:almeria|Almería]] remained Muslim until 1489, when it surrendered to the Catholic Monarchs.

colonial-brazil.t: Portugal's vast South American colony, built on sugar, gold and the labour of millions of enslaved Africans, from which modern Brazil grew.
colonial-brazil.o: [[e:pedro-alvares-cabral|Pedro Álvares Cabral]] reached the coast of [[s:new-republic-brazil|Brazil]] in April 1500 and claimed it for Portugal under the Treaty of Tordesillas. Early decades were dominated by the trade in [[e:brazilwood|brazilwood]]. From 1534 the crown divided the coast into hereditary captaincies, and in 1549 [[e:tome-de-sousa|Tomé de Sousa]] founded [[e:salvador|Salvador]] as the seat of the [[s:state-of-brazil|State of Brazil]].
colonial-brazil.r: The colony was governed from [[e:lisbon|Lisbon]] through governors-general and later [[e:viceroy-of-india|viceroys]], and the [[e:jesuits|Jesuits]] ran missions among the indigenous peoples. [[e:sugar-plantation|Sugar plantations]] in [[s:captaincy-of-pernambuco|Pernambuco]] and [[e:bahia|Bahia]] relied on enslaved Africans, and [[s:new-republic-brazil|Brazil]] became the largest destination of the [[e:atlantic-slave-trade|Atlantic slave trade]]. Bandeirantes from [[e:sao-paulo|São Paulo]] pushed into the interior, and gold was found in [[s:captaincy-of-minas-gerais|Minas Gerais]] in the 1690s, moving the centre of gravity south. [[e:rio-de-janeiro|Rio de Janeiro]] became the capital in 1763.
colonial-brazil.e: In 1808 the Portuguese court fled [[e:napoleon|Napoleon's]] invasion to [[e:rio-de-janeiro|Rio de Janeiro]], opening [[e:brazil|Brazil's]] ports. In 1815 it was raised to the [[s:kingdom-of-brazil|Kingdom of Brazil]] within a [[s:united-kingdom-of-great-britain-and-ireland|United Kingdom]] with Portugal, ending its colonial status.

colony-of-saint-vincent.t: British colony on Saint Vincent, taken from its Garifuna inhabitants by war and deportation, known for arrowroot, breadfruit and La Soufrière volcano.
colony-of-saint-vincent.o: [[e:saint-vincent-island|Saint Vincent]] was largely held by the [[e:garifuna|Garifuna]] and [[e:kalinago|Kalinago]] until the [[e:treaty-of-paris-1763|Treaty of Paris]] of 1763 granted it to [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]]. Surveyors began dividing land for plantations, provoking the [[e:first-carib-war|First Carib War]] of 1772 to 1773. [[e:france|France]] occupied the island from 1779 to 1783, and in 1795 to 1796 the Garifuna rose again before their [[e:deportation|deportation]] in 1797.
colony-of-saint-vincent.r: A governor, council and assembly ruled from [[e:kingstown|Kingstown]], while [[e:sugar-plantation|sugar]], [[e:cotton|cotton]] and later arrowroot were grown on estates worked by enslaved Africans. The botanic garden founded in 1765 is among the oldest in the [[e:americas|Americas]] and received [[e:william-bligh|William Bligh's]] breadfruit in 1793. After emancipation, indentured workers came from [[e:madeira|Madeira]] and [[e:india|India]]. The assembly gave way to crown colony rule in 1877, and [[e:la-soufriere-saint-vincent|La Soufrière]]'s eruption in 1902 killed about 1,600 people.
colony-of-saint-vincent.e: [[e:saint-vincent-island|Saint Vincent]] belonged to the [[s:british-windward-islands|British Windward Islands]], then joined the [[s:west-indies-federation|West Indies Federation]]. It became an [[e:west-indies-associated-states|Associated State]] in 1969 and gained independence, with the northern [[e:grenadines|Grenadines]], as [[s:saint-vincent-and-the-grenadines|Saint Vincent and the Grenadines]] on 27 October 1979.

cacicazgo-of-magua.t: A Taíno chiefdom in the fertile Vega Real of north-central Hispaniola, ruled by Guarionex, which rose against Spanish rule in 1497.
cacicazgo-of-magua.o: Maguá was one of the five principal chiefdoms (cacicazgos) into which [[e:hispaniola|Hispaniola]] was divided when [[e:christopher-columbus|Columbus]] arrived in 1492. Its origins lie in the [[e:taino|Taíno]] society that developed on the island in the centuries before, and it was centred on the [[e:vega-real|Vega Real]] valley.
cacicazgo-of-magua.r: Maguá was led by the paramount cacique [[e:guarionex|Guarionex]], to whom lesser caciques owed allegiance. Its people lived in villages around central plazas and ballcourts (bateyes), grew [[e:cassava|cassava]], [[e:maize|maize]] and [[e:sweet-potato|sweet potatoes]] in mounded fields (conucos), and venerated spirits (zemís). The Spanish built forts such as [[e:concepcion-de-la-vega|Concepción de la Vega]] in its territory.
cacicazgo-of-magua.e: Burdened by tribute in gold and food, [[e:guarionex|Guarionex]] led a revolt in 1497-98, but he was captured and later drowned in 1502 when the ship taking him to [[e:spain|Spain]] sank. The chiefdom disappeared under colonial rule and disease.

commune-of-vercelli.t: A Piedmontese city-republic on the road to France that founded one of Italy's earliest universities in 1228.
commune-of-vercelli.o: Vercelli's powerful [[e:bishop|bishops]] held comital rights over the city, but citizens governed through consuls by around 1120. The commune expanded across the plain of the [[e:sesia|Sesia]], competing with [[s:commune-of-novara|Novara]], [[e:casale-monferrato|Casale]] and the [[s:march-of-montferrat|March of Montferrat]].
commune-of-vercelli.r: [[e:consul|Consuls]] and later a podestà ran the commune, which joined the [[s:lombard-league|Lombard League]] against [[e:frederick-barbarossa|Frederick Barbarossa]]. In 1228 it agreed with students and masters from [[s:commune-of-padua|Padua]] to found a studium, one of the earliest Italian universities. Cardinal [[e:guala-bicchieri|Guala Bicchieri]], papal legate in [[e:england|England]], founded the abbey of [[e:basilica-of-santandrea-vercelli|Sant'Andrea]], a Gothic landmark begun in 1219. The rival Avogadro and Tizzoni families split the city.
commune-of-vercelli.e: In 1335 Vercelli accepted [[e:azzone-visconti|Azzone Visconti]] and became part of the [[s:lordship-of-milan|Lordship of Milan]]. It passed to the [[s:duchy-of-savoy|Duchy of Savoy]] in 1427.

cyprus-under-isaac-komnenos.t: Breakaway Byzantine realm on Cyprus ruled by the self-proclaimed emperor Isaac Komnenos until Richard the Lionheart conquered the island in 1191.
cyprus-under-isaac-komnenos.o: [[e:isaac-komnenos-of-cyprus|Isaac Komnenos]], a great-nephew of Emperor Manuel I, had been governor in [[e:cilicia|Cilicia]] and a prisoner of the [[e:armenians|Armenians]]. After his ransom he arrived in [[e:cyprus|Cyprus]] in 1184 with forged imperial letters, took over the government and proclaimed himself emperor, refusing to recognise Andronikos I in [[e:constantinople|Constantinople]].
cyprus-under-isaac-komnenos.r: Isaac ruled from [[e:nicosia|Nicosia]] with [[e:mercenary|mercenaries]] and was remembered by Cypriots as harsh and grasping, seizing property and abusing local nobles. He secured his position by allying with [[e:william-ii-of-sicily|William II of Sicily]], whose fleet defeated a Byzantine expedition sent by [[e:isaac-ii-angelos|Isaac II Angelos]] in 1186-1187, and reportedly with [[e:saladin|Saladin]]. The island remained Greek [[e:eastern-orthodox-church|Orthodox]] and Greek-speaking.
cyprus-under-isaac-komnenos.e: In May 1191 ships of the [[e:third-crusade|Third Crusade]] carrying [[e:richard-i-of-england|Richard I's]] sister and his betrothed [[e:berengaria-of-navarre|Berengaria]] were stranded at [[e:limassol|Limassol]]. Isaac's mistreatment of them gave Richard a pretext: he conquered [[e:cyprus|Cyprus]] within weeks and held Isaac in [[e:silver|silver]] chains. Richard soon sold the island to the [[e:knights-templar|Knights Templar]].

canton-of-malaga.t: A federalist canton proclaimed in Málaga during the Cantonal Rebellion of 1873, one of the last in Andalusia to dissolve.
canton-of-malaga.o: In July 1873 the federal republicans of Málaga, a city with a strong radical movement, declared it a sovereign canton, joining the wave of cantonal risings against the central government of the [[s:spanish-first-republic|Spanish First Republic]].
canton-of-malaga.r: Local federalists ran the city through a cantonal committee and volunteer militias. The canton avoided open battle with the government and was torn by quarrels among its own factions over how far to break with [[e:madrid|Madrid]].
canton-of-malaga.e: As the government regained control of [[e:andalusia|Andalusia]] after General Pavía's campaign against the [[s:canton-of-seville|Canton of Seville]] and the [[s:canton-of-cadiz|Canton of Cádiz]], the Málaga canton dissolved without a major fight in the late summer of 1873.

colony-of-the-bahamas.t: British island colony that began as a refuge for Puritan dissenters, became a notorious pirate haven, and grew into the independent Commonwealth of The Bahamas.
colony-of-the-bahamas.o: In 1648 the Eleutheran Adventurers, Puritan settlers from [[e:bermuda|Bermuda]] led by [[e:william-sayle|William Sayle]], founded a colony on [[e:eleuthera|Eleuthera]]. Settlement spread to [[e:new-providence|New Providence]], where [[s:county-of-nassau|Nassau]] grew up. In 1670 [[e:charles-ii-of-england|Charles II]] granted the islands to the Lords Proprietors of [[s:province-of-carolina|Carolina]], whose weak rule left Nassau open to Spanish raids and, by the early 18th century, to [[e:piracy|pirates]].
colony-of-the-bahamas.r: The crown took direct control in 1718, when [[e:woodes-rogers|Woodes Rogers]] arrived as royal governor and suppressed the [[e:piracy|pirates]]; an elected House of Assembly followed in 1729. Loyalists from the American colonies arrived after 1783 with enslaved workers to plant [[e:cotton|cotton]], which soon failed. Wrecking, salt raking, sponging and later [[e:naval-blockade|blockade]] running in the [[e:american-civil-war|American Civil War]] and rum running during [[e:prohibition-in-the-united-states|Prohibition]] sustained the economy. A small white merchant elite, the [[e:bay-street-boys|Bay Street Boys]], dominated politics.
colony-of-the-bahamas.e: Internal self-government came in 1964, and majority rule followed in 1967 under [[e:lynden-pindling|Lynden Pindling's]] [[e:progressive-liberal-party|Progressive Liberal Party]], after a long campaign by the black majority. The colony became independent as the [[s:bahamas|Bahamas]] on 10 July 1973, by then reliant on tourism and offshore finance.

commune-of-vicenza.t: A Veneto city-republic that founded a short-lived university and spent much of its history under the rule of stronger neighbours.
commune-of-vicenza.o: [[e:vicenza|Vicenza]], between [[s:commune-of-verona|Verona]] and [[s:commune-of-padua|Padua]], had consuls by 1147 after its citizens took power from the [[e:bishop|bishop]]. It joined the [[s:veronese-league|Veronese League]] in 1164 and then the [[s:lombard-league|Lombard League]] against [[e:frederick-barbarossa|Frederick Barbarossa]].
commune-of-vicenza.r: The commune was governed by consuls and later a podestà. A university was founded in 1204 but soon faded. From the 1230s the city came under [[e:ezzelino-iii-da-romano|Ezzelino III da Romano]], and after his fall [[s:commune-of-padua|Padua]] controlled [[e:vicenza|Vicenza]] from 1266. Wool and [[e:silk|silk]] were its main trades, and its noble families held castles in the surrounding hills and the Berici hills to the south. Like its neighbours, it was split by feuds between Guelph and Ghibelline families.
commune-of-vicenza.e: In 1311 [[e:cangrande-i-della-scala|Cangrande della Scala]] took [[e:vicenza|Vicenza]], and it became part of the [[s:lordship-of-verona|Lordship of Verona]]. In 1404 it submitted to the [[s:republic-of-venice|Republic of Venice]], which ruled it until 1797.

crimean-khanate.t: The Tatar khanate of the Giray dynasty, an Ottoman ally whose raiders terrorised Poland-Lithuania and Russia for three centuries.
crimean-khanate.o: As the [[s:golden-horde|Golden Horde]] fell apart, [[e:haci-i-giray|Haci Giray]], a descendant of [[e:genghis-khan|Genghis Khan]], established an independent khanate in the [[e:crimea|Crimea]] and the neighbouring steppe around 1441, with support from [[s:grand-duchy-of-lithuania|Lithuania]]. His son [[e:menli-i-giray|Mengli Giray]] became a [[e:vassal|vassal]] of the [[s:ottoman-empire|Ottoman Empire]] after the Ottoman conquest of the Crimean coast in 1475 and destroyed the remnant of the [[s:great-horde|Great Horde]] in 1502.
crimean-khanate.r: The khans ruled from the palace at [[e:bakhchysarai|Bakhchysarai]] with the help of powerful clan chiefs, and the [[e:ottoman-empire|Ottomans]] controlled the southern coast. The economy depended heavily on raids into Poland-[[e:lithuania|Lithuania]] and [[e:russia|Russia]], which took hundreds of thousands of captives for the slave markets of [[s:genoese-gazaria|Caffa]]. In 1571 [[e:devlet-i-giray|Devlet Giray]] burned [[e:moscow|Moscow]].
crimean-khanate.e: Russian victories over the [[e:ottoman-empire|Ottomans]] led to the [[e:treaty-of-kucuk-kaynarca|Treaty of Kuchuk Kainarji]] in 1774, which made the khanate nominally independent. [[e:catherine-the-great|Catherine II]] annexed it to the [[s:russian-empire|Russian Empire]] in 1783, and many [[e:crimean-tatars|Crimean Tatars]] emigrated to Ottoman lands.

cherusci.t: The Germanic people of Arminius, whose ambush of three Roman legions in the Teutoburg Forest in 9 CE ended Rome's plan to rule Germany to the Elbe.
cherusci.o: The Cherusci lived in the region of the middle [[e:weser|Weser]] and the [[e:harz|Harz]] foothills. Caesar mentions them in 53 BCE as neighbours of the [[s:suebi|Suebi]]. After the campaigns of [[e:nero-claudius-drusus|Drusus]] from 12 BCE they became Roman allies, and their noble sons, among them [[e:arminius|Arminius]], served in the Roman army and received Roman citizenship.
cherusci.r: Cheruscan society was led by noble families competing for power and Roman favour; [[e:arminius|Arminius]]' rival [[e:segestes|Segestes]] stayed loyal to [[e:rome|Rome]]. In 9 CE Arminius led a coalition that destroyed the legions of [[e:publius-quinctilius-varus|Publius Quinctilius Varus]]. He then fought [[e:germanicus|Germanicus]] to a standstill in 15 to 16 and defeated [[e:maroboduus|Maroboduus]] in 17, before being murdered by kinsmen around 21.
cherusci.e: Internal feuding weakened the Cherusci; in 47 [[e:rome|Rome]] sent [[e:arminius|Arminius]]' nephew [[e:italicus-cheruscan-king|Italicus]] to rule them. [[e:tacitus|Tacitus]], writing around 98, describes them as worn down and overshadowed by the [[s:chatti|Chatti]]. They disappear soon afterwards, probably absorbed into the peoples who later formed the [[s:saxons|Saxons]].

county-of-angouleme.t: Medieval county of the Charente whose heiress Isabella married King John of England and whose lords included the Lusignans.
county-of-angouleme.o: In 866 [[e:charles-the-bald|Charles the Bald]] appointed his kinsman [[e:vulgrin-i-count-of-angouleme|Vulgrin I]] count of [[e:angouleme|Angoulême]] and [[s:county-of-perigord|Périgord]] to defend the region against [[e:vikings|Viking]] raids. His descendants, called the Taillefer line after the nickname of [[e:william-i-of-angouleme|Count William I Taillefer]], held Angoulême for more than three centuries.
county-of-angouleme.r: The counts were [[e:vassal|vassals]] of the dukes of [[s:duchy-of-aquitaine|Aquitaine]] and controlled the [[e:charente|Charente]] valley, with [[e:angouleme|Angoulême]] on its fortified hill. The cathedral of [[e:angouleme-cathedral|Saint-Pierre]], rebuilt in the 12th century, shows the domed [[e:romanesque-architecture|Romanesque]] style of the region.
county-of-angouleme.e: [[e:isabella-of-angouleme|Isabella of Angoulême]] married [[e:john-king-of-england|King John]] of [[e:england|England]] in 1200 and later Hugh X of Lusignan, whose family then held the county. On the death of the last Lusignan heir in 1308 it passed to the French crown. It was later an [[e:appanage|appanage]] of the [[e:house-of-valois-angouleme|Valois-Angoulême]] branch, which gave [[e:france|France]] [[e:francis-i|Francis I]].

chitradurga-nayakas.t: Poligar chiefs who ruled the fortress of Chitradurga in Karnataka, remembered for the legend of Onake Obavva.
chitradurga-nayakas.o: The [[e:nayaka|Nayakas]] of [[e:chitradurga|Chitradurga]] were Beda chiefs who served the [[s:vijayanagara-empire|Vijayanagara Empire]] as local military governors. After Vijayanagara's defeat in 1565 they gained autonomy, and by the 1580s they ruled from the hill fortress of Chitradurga, whose seven concentric walls were extended by successive rulers.
chitradurga-nayakas.r: The [[e:nayaka|Nayakas]], also called [[e:palayakkarar|Palegars]], ruled a dry upland territory of central [[e:karnataka|Karnataka]] through warrior clans and revenue from farming and herding. They made shifting alliances with the [[s:keladi-nayaka-kingdom|Keladi Nayaka kingdom]], the [[s:kingdom-of-mysore-1399-1799|Kingdom of Mysore]], the [[e:mughal-empire|Mughals]] and the [[e:maratha-empire|Marathas]]. [[e:madakari-nayaka-v|Madakari Nayaka V]], the last ruler, is a folk hero in Karnataka.
chitradurga-nayakas.e: [[e:hyder-ali|Hyder Ali]] of the [[s:kingdom-of-mysore-1399-1799|Kingdom of Mysore]] besieged [[e:chitradurga|Chitradurga]], and the fort fell in 1779 after a long resistance; [[e:madakari-nayaka-v|Madakari Nayaka]] died in captivity. Legend says [[e:onake-obavva|Onake Obavva]], a guard's wife, killed many attackers with a pestle in an earlier siege.

cr.a: H. SHASHIDHAR of the Indian Administrative Service and N. SREENIVASA MURTHY Geographer of the DCD, Karnataka DIRECTOR...

champoton.t: A Maya province on the Campeche coast whose warriors killed the first Spanish expedition's leader in 1517, later Montejo's base for conquering Yucatán.
champoton.o: Champotón, the Chakanputun of the Maya chronicles, was an ancient coastal town associated with the [[e:itza-people|Itza]] before their rise at [[s:chichen-itza|Chichen Itza]]. After the fall of the [[s:league-of-mayapan|League of Mayapan]] around 1441 it emerged as an independent province on the western coast of the [[e:yucatan-peninsula|Yucatán]] peninsula.
champoton.r: The province was ruled by the [[s:kowoj|Couoh]] lineage from the town of Champotón at the mouth of a river, which lived from fishing, salt and coastal trade. In 1517 its lord [[e:moch-couoh|Moch Couoh]] led warriors who defeated [[e:francisco-hernandez-de-cordoba-founder-of-nicaragua|Francisco Hernández de Córdoba's]] expedition, mortally wounding him. [[e:juan-de-grijalva|Grijalva]]'s expedition fought there again in 1518.
champoton.e: In 1537 [[e:francisco-de-montejo-the-younger|Francisco de Montejo the Younger]] established a Spanish base at Champotón, from which the conquest of [[e:yucatan-peninsula|Yucatán]] was launched. The province was absorbed into the [[s:province-of-yucatan|Province of Yucatán]], and the town survives in [[e:campeche|Campeche]] state.

cacicazgo-of-marien.t: A Taíno chiefdom of north-western Hispaniola whose cacique Guacanagarí befriended Columbus in 1492 and hosted the first Spanish fort.
cacicazgo-of-marien.o: Marién occupied the north-western part of [[e:hispaniola|Hispaniola]], today's northern [[s:first-empire-of-haiti|Haiti]]. It was one of the island's five principal chiefdoms when [[e:christopher-columbus|Columbus]] arrived in December 1492, rooted in [[e:taino|Taíno]] society of the preceding centuries.
cacicazgo-of-marien.r: Its cacique [[e:guacanagari|Guacanagarí]] helped the Spanish salvage the wreck of the [[e:santa-maria-ship|Santa María]] on Christmas Day 1492, and [[e:christopher-columbus|Columbus]] built the fort of [[e:la-navidad|La Navidad]] with its [[e:timber|timbers]] in his territory. Marién's people lived in villages with plazas, farmed [[e:cassava|cassava]] and fished, and its chief ranked with the other great caciques of the island.
cacicazgo-of-marien.e: [[e:la-navidad|La Navidad]] was destroyed by [[e:caonabo|Caonabo of Maguana]] in 1493. [[e:guacanagari|Guacanagarí]] remained allied with the Spanish but saw his people subjected to tribute and forced labour; he fled into the mountains and died there. The chiefdom vanished with the [[e:taino|Taíno]] collapse.

company-rule-in-rhodesia.t: The era when Cecil Rhodes's British South Africa Company governed the lands that became Zimbabwe and Zambia.
company-rule-in-rhodesia.o: In 1889 the [[e:british-south-africa-company|British South Africa Company]] of [[e:cecil-rhodes|Cecil Rhodes]] received a royal charter, based on the [[e:rudd-concession|Rudd Concession]] from the [[e:ndebele-kingdom|Ndebele]] king [[e:lobengula|Lobengula]]. Its Pioneer Column marched into [[e:mashonaland|Mashonaland]] and raised the flag at [[e:harare|Fort Salisbury]] in September 1890. In 1893 the company conquered the [[s:ndebele-kingdom|Ndebele Kingdom]].
company-rule-in-rhodesia.r: The company ruled through administrators such as [[e:leander-starr-jameson|Leander Starr Jameson]] and [[e:william-milton|William Milton]], granting land and mining claims to settlers in hope of a second [[e:witwatersrand|Witwatersrand]] that never appeared. The [[e:ndebele-kingdom|Ndebele]] and [[e:shona|Shona]] risings of 1896-1897, the [[e:first-chimurenga|first Chimurenga]], were suppressed. North of the [[e:zambezi|Zambezi]] it governed [[s:north-western-rhodesia|North-Western Rhodesia]] and [[s:north-eastern-rhodesia|North-Eastern Rhodesia]], later [[s:northern-rhodesia|Northern Rhodesia]].
company-rule-in-rhodesia.e: Settlers resented company rule. In a 1922 referendum they rejected union with [[s:republic-of-south-africa|South Africa]], and in 1923 [[s:southern-rhodesia|Southern Rhodesia]] became a self-governing British colony; [[s:northern-rhodesia|Northern Rhodesia]] passed to the [[e:colonial-office|Colonial Office]] in 1924, though the company kept mineral rights.

county-of-auvergne.t: The county of the volcanic Massif Central, centred on Clermont, where Pope Urban II preached the First Crusade in 1095.
county-of-auvergne.o: Auvergne was ruled in the late 9th century by [[e:william-i-duke-of-aquitaine|William the Pious]] as part of his Aquitanian power. In the later 10th century the viscounts of [[e:clermont-ferrand|Clermont]] took the comital title, and by around 980 they governed the county as hereditary counts under the loose overlordship of the dukes of [[s:duchy-of-aquitaine|Aquitaine]].
county-of-auvergne.r: The county was a land of uplands, pasture and [[e:romanesque-architecture|Romanesque]] churches, with the [[e:bishop|bishops]] of [[e:clermont-ferrand|Clermont]] a rival power in the city. In 1095 [[e:pope-urban-ii|Urban II]] proclaimed the First Crusade at the [[e:council-of-clermont|Council of Clermont]]. In the 12th century a family dispute split off the [[s:dauphine-of-viennois|Dauphiné]] of Auvergne, and [[e:philip-ii-of-france|Philip II]]'s campaigns from 1209 seized much of the county for the crown.
county-of-auvergne.e: The remaining county, centred on [[e:vic-le-comte|Vic-le-Comte]], passed to the [[e:house-of-la-tour-dauvergne|La Tour]] family and through [[e:madeleine-de-la-tour-dauvergne|Madeleine de la Tour d'Auvergne]] to her daughter [[e:catherine-de-medici|Catherine de' Medici]]. The royal lands of Auvergne, held by the [[e:house-of-bourbon|Bourbons]], were confiscated after 1523 and united with the [[s:kingdom-of-france|Kingdom of France]] in 1531.

commune-of-perugia.t: A proud Umbrian hill-city republic, nominally papal but largely independent for four centuries, until crushed in the Salt War of 1540.
commune-of-perugia.o: Perugia, an ancient Etruscan city, had consuls by 1139. Though within the lands claimed by the [[s:papal-states|Papal States]], it governed itself and conquered much of central [[e:umbria|Umbria]], including rival [[e:assisi|Assisi]] and [[e:foligno|Foligno]].
commune-of-perugia.r: The commune was usually [[e:guelphs-and-ghibellines|Guelph]] and allied with the [[e:papacy|papacy]], but guarded its autonomy. Elected priors ruled from the [[e:palazzo-dei-priori-perugia|Palazzo dei Priori]], and the [[e:fontana-maggiore|Fontana Maggiore]] by [[e:nicola-pisano|Nicola]] and [[e:giovanni-pisano|Giovanni Pisano]] was completed in 1278. The university was founded in 1308. In the 15th century the condottiere [[e:braccio-da-montone|Braccio da Montone]] ruled the city, and later the Baglioni family dominated it. The painter [[e:perugino|Perugino]] worked there.
commune-of-perugia.e: In 1540 Perugia rebelled against a new salt tax imposed by [[e:pope-paul-iii|Pope Paul III]]. Papal troops crushed the Salt War, and the pope built the [[e:rocca-paolina|Rocca Paolina]] fortress over the Baglioni houses, ending the city's autonomy.

chobanids-of-kastamonu.t: A Turkish frontier dynasty that ruled Kastamonu for the Seljuks and led their naval expedition across the Black Sea to the Crimea.
chobanids-of-kastamonu.o: [[e:husam-al-din-choban|Husam al-Din Choban]] was a commander of the [[s:sultanate-of-rum|Sultanate of Rum]] who was given the frontier district of [[e:kastamonu|Kastamonu]], facing Byzantine and later Komnenian lands to the north, in the early 13th century. His family held it as a hereditary march.
chobanids-of-kastamonu.r: Around 1220-1221 [[e:husam-al-din-choban|Choban]] led a Seljuk expedition by sea from [[s:sinope|Sinop]] to [[e:sudak|Sudak]] in the [[e:crimea|Crimea]], an event recorded by the historian [[e:ibn-bibi|Ibn Bibi]]. His successors ruled as marcher lords, leading [[e:turkmen|Turkmen]] warriors in raids on Byzantine territory. Under Muzaffar al-Din Yavlak Arslan the family acted increasingly independently as Seljuk power declined under the [[e:mongols|Mongols]].
chobanids-of-kastamonu.e: In 1309 [[e:suleyman-pasha-candarid|Suleyman Pasha]], from the [[s:candarids|Candarids]], killed the last Chobanid ruler Mahmud and took [[e:kastamonu|Kastamonu]], which became the Candarid capital.

catepanate-of-italy.t: Byzantine province of southern Italy governed from Bari by a catepan, the last stronghold of the Eastern Empire in Italy until the Normans took Bari in 1071.
catepanate-of-italy.o: Around 965–970 the [[e:byzantine-empire|Byzantines]] combined the [[e:theme-system|themes]] of [[s:theme-of-longobardia|Longobardia]], [[e:calabria|Calabria]] and [[e:lucania|Lucania]] under a single high-ranking governor, the catepan, based at [[s:principality-of-bari|Bari]]. The change answered threats from [[e:otto-i|Otto I's]] campaigns in the south and from Arab raids.
catepanate-of-italy.r: The catepanate governed a mixed population of Latin-speaking [[e:lombards|Lombards]] and [[e:greeks|Greeks]], with Greek monasteries flourishing in [[e:calabria|Calabria]]. Local revolts were frequent: [[e:melus-of-bari|Melus of Bari]] rebelled in 1009 and again in 1017 with Norman [[e:mercenary|mercenaries]], but the catepan [[e:basil-boioannes|Basil Boioannes]] crushed them at Cannae in 1018 and founded new towns such as [[e:troia-apulia|Troia]]. The province also served as a base for [[e:george-maniakes|George Maniakes's]] expedition to [[e:sicily|Sicily]] in 1038.
catepanate-of-italy.e: The Normans, first hired as [[e:mercenary|mercenaries]], conquered the province piece by piece from the 1040s. [[e:robert-guiscard|Robert Guiscard]] took [[s:principality-of-bari|Bari]] in April 1071 after a long siege, ending Byzantine rule in [[e:italy|Italy]]. Greek religious and cultural influence lasted much longer in [[e:calabria|Calabria]] and [[e:salento|Salento]].

county-of-nassau-weilburg.t: A Walramian county of the house of Nassau on the Lahn, whose line later ruled the Duchy of Nassau and inherited Luxembourg.
county-of-nassau-weilburg.o: The Walramian line of the house of [[s:county-of-nassau|Nassau]] held lands south of the [[e:lahn|Lahn]], and a partition in 1344 gave Count [[e:john-i-count-of-nassau-weilburg|John I]] a share centred on [[e:weilburg|Weilburg]]. John acquired [[e:saarbrucken|Saarbrücken]] by marriage, and the family built up scattered territories across the middle [[e:rhine|Rhine]] and [[e:saar-river|Saar]].
county-of-nassau-weilburg.r: The counts ruled small, scattered lands from [[e:weilburg|Weilburg]] castle, rebuilt in [[e:renaissance|Renaissance]] style in the 16th century, and introduced the [[e:protestant-reformation|Lutheran Reformation]]. Repeated partitions and reunions created the [[s:county-of-nassau-saarbrucken|County of Nassau-Saarbrücken]] and the [[s:principality-of-nassau-usingen|Principality of Nassau-Usingen]] among other branches, and in the 18th century the Weilburg counts used the title of prince.
county-of-nassau-weilburg.e: Nassau-[[e:weilburg|Weilburg]] survived the end of the empire by joining the [[s:confederation-of-the-rhine|Confederation of the Rhine]]. In 1806 it united with [[s:principality-of-nassau-usingen|Nassau-Usingen]] to form the [[s:duchy-of-nassau|Duchy of Nassau]], and after [[e:usingen|Usingen's]] extinction in 1816 the Weilburg line ruled it alone. Annexed by [[e:kingdom-of-prussia|Prussia]] in 1866, the family inherited the [[s:grand-duchy-of-luxembourg|Grand Duchy of Luxembourg]] in 1890.

county-palatine-of-durham.t: The palatinate where the bishops of Durham ruled as prince-bishops for more than seven centuries, guarding England's northern frontier.
county-palatine-of-durham.o: The [[e:bishop|bishops]] of [[e:durham-england|Durham]] inherited the lands and prestige of the community of [[e:saint-cuthbert|Saint Cuthbert]], whose shrine moved to Durham in 995. [[e:william-the-conqueror|William the Conqueror]] appointed [[e:walcher-bishop-of-durham|Walcher of Lorraine]] bishop in 1071 and gave him the earldom of [[s:kingdom-of-northumbria|Northumbria]] in 1075, joining spiritual and secular power on the Scottish border.
county-palatine-of-durham.r: The [[e:bishop|bishops]] had their own courts, chancery, mint, sheriff and army, and royal writs did not normally run between the [[e:river-tyne|Tyne]] and the [[e:river-tees|Tees]]. [[e:durham-castle|Durham Castle]], begun in 1072, and the cathedral, begun in 1093, expressed their power. Bishops such as [[e:antony-bek|Antony Bek]] and [[e:thomas-langley|Thomas Langley]] were leading royal servants. [[e:coal|Coal]] and lead mining added to their wealth.
county-palatine-of-durham.e: The Tudors curbed the palatinate's independence in 1536. The [[e:durham-university|University of Durham]] was founded in 1832 with part of the [[e:bishop|bishops]]' endowment, and the [[e:durham-england|Durham]] (County Palatine) Act of 1836 transferred the remaining secular powers to the crown.

county-of-tyrol.t: An Alpine county controlling the Brenner Pass that became a jewel of the Habsburg lands and is today divided between Austria and Italy.
county-of-tyrol.o: The counts of [[e:tyrol|Tyrol]], named after [[e:tyrol-castle|Tyrol Castle]] near [[e:merano|Merano]], appear around 1140 as advocates of the bishoprics of [[e:brixen|Brixen]] and [[e:trento|Trent]]. [[e:albert-iv-count-of-tyrol|Albert IV]], the last of this line, left his lands in 1253 to the counts of [[e:gorizia|Gorizia]]; [[e:meinhard-ii-of-gorizia-tyrol|Meinhard II]] built a unified territory from Merano to the [[e:inn-river|Inn]] valley.
county-of-tyrol.r: [[e:tyrol|Tyrol's]] estates, including peasants, had a voice in government, unusually. [[e:margaret-maultasch|Margaret Maultasch]] handed the county to the [[e:habsburg-dynasty|Habsburgs]] in 1363. [[e:silver|Silver]] mining at [[e:schwaz|Schwaz]] made Tyrol rich, and [[e:maximilian-i-holy-roman-emperor|Maximilian I]] ruled from [[e:innsbruck|Innsbruck]]. The [[e:landlibell|Landlibell of 1511]] set out the estates' defence obligations.
county-of-tyrol.e: [[e:tyrol|Tyrol]] remained a [[s:county-of-habsburg|Habsburg]] crown land, fighting the [[e:bavarians|Bavarians]] and French under [[e:andreas-hofer|Andreas Hofer]] in 1809. After the [[e:first-world-war|First World War]], the south, including [[e:bolzano|Bolzano]] and [[s:prince-bishopric-of-trent|Trento]], went to [[e:italy|Italy]] in 1919, while North and [[e:east-tyrol|East Tyrol]] remain an Austrian state.

coosa-chiefdom.t: A paramount chiefdom of the South-East whose lord, when de Soto came in 1540, held sway over towns stretching from eastern Tennessee into central Alabama.
coosa-chiefdom.o: Coosa formed in the 14th and 15th centuries among Mississippian towns along the [[e:coosawattee-river|Coosawattee River]] in north-west [[s:georgia|Georgia]], with its capital probably at the Little [[e:egypt|Egypt]] site near modern Carters. Through alliance and conquest its paramount chief drew in neighbouring chiefdoms, including the declining [[s:etowah-chiefdom|Etowah chiefdom]], creating one of the largest polities in the region.
coosa-chiefdom.r: Spanish chroniclers of [[e:hernando-de-soto|Hernando de Soto's]] expedition in 1540 describe the chief of Coosa carried in a litter, surrounded by attendants, and receiving tribute from subject chiefs along a corridor some 400 kilometres long. Towns had mounds, plazas and palisades, and [[e:maize|maize]], beans and squash grew in wide valley fields. When soldiers of the [[e:tristan-de-luna-y-arellano|Tristán de Luna]] expedition returned in 1560, Coosa was already smaller and fighting rebellious tributaries.
coosa-chiefdom.e: Epidemics and political fragmentation broke up the paramount chiefdom by about 1600. Its people moved down the [[e:coosa-river|Coosa River]] into [[e:alabama|Alabama]], where the town of Coosa became a leading town of the Upper [[e:muscogee|Muscogee]], part of the [[s:muscogee-confederacy|Muscogee Confederacy]].

connecticut-colony.t: The Puritan river colony centred on Hartford, whose Fundamental Orders of 1639 are often called the first written constitution in America.
connecticut-colony.o: In 1636 the minister [[e:thomas-hooker|Thomas Hooker]] led his congregation from [[s:province-of-massachusetts-bay|Massachusetts]] to [[e:hartford-connecticut|Hartford]] on the [[e:connecticut-river|Connecticut River]], joining settlers at [[e:windsor-connecticut|Windsor]] and [[e:wethersfield-connecticut|Wethersfield]]. The new towns fought the [[e:pequot-war|Pequot War]] in 1637 alongside the [[e:mohegan|Mohegan]], destroying the [[s:pequot-nation|Pequot Nation]], and in 1639 adopted the [[e:fundamental-orders-of-connecticut|Fundamental Orders]] as their frame of government.
connecticut-colony.r: [[e:connecticut|Connecticut]] was a Puritan commonwealth like [[s:province-of-massachusetts-bay|Massachusetts]], but the [[e:fundamental-orders-of-connecticut|Fundamental Orders]] did not require church membership for voting. The colony bought [[s:saybrook-colony|Saybrook Colony]] in 1644, and [[e:john-winthrop-the-younger|John Winthrop the Younger]] won a royal charter in 1662 that also absorbed the [[s:new-haven-colony|New Haven Colony]]. Legend says the charter was hidden in the Charter Oak in 1687 to keep it from the [[s:dominion-of-new-england|Dominion of New England]]. [[e:yale-university|Yale College]] was founded in 1701.
connecticut-colony.e: Under governor [[e:jonathan-trumbull|Jonathan Trumbull]], the only colonial governor to back independence, [[e:connecticut|Connecticut]] supplied the Continental Army so generously it was called the Provisions State. It became a state of the [[s:united-states|United States]] in 1776, keeping its charter as constitution until 1818.

courland-tobago.t: Caribbean colony of the Duchy of Courland on Tobago, settled in 1654 and fought over with the Dutch until abandoned near the end of the century.
courland-tobago.o: [[e:jacob-kettler|Duke Jacob Kettler]] of the [[s:duchy-of-courland-and-semigallia|Duchy of Courland and Semigallia]] sent settlers to [[e:tobago|Tobago]] in 1654 aboard the ship Das Wappen der Herzogin von Kurland. They landed at what became [[e:great-courland-bay|Great Courland Bay]], built Fort Jacobus and the settlement of Jacobusstadt, and named the island New [[e:courland|Courland]].
courland-tobago.r: The colonists, including Latvian peasants and German officers, tried to grow [[e:sugar-plantation|sugar]], tobacco and other tropical crops with enslaved African labour. A [[e:dutch|Dutch]] settlement on the other side of the island, backed by the Lampsins brothers, competed with the Courlanders, and both struggled with disease and shortage of settlers.
courland-tobago.e: The [[e:dutch|Dutch]] took over in 1659 while [[e:jacob-kettler|Duke Jacob]] was a Swedish prisoner. [[e:courland|Courland]] regained the claim and resettled the island in the 1680s, but the colony was abandoned by about 1690. [[e:tobago|Tobago]] later became British; [[e:great-courland-bay|Great Courland Bay]] keeps the name.

chupanids.t: A Mongol family of the Suldus clan that dominated north-western Iran after the Ilkhanate collapsed, ruling Tabriz through puppet khans.
chupanids.o: [[e:chupan|Amir Chupan]] was the most powerful commander of the [[s:ilkhanate|Ilkhanate]] under [[e:oljeitu|Öljeitü]] and [[e:abu-said-bahadur-khan|Abu Sa'id]] until Abu Sa'id had him killed in 1327. After Abu Sa'id's death in 1335, Chupan's grandson [[e:hasan-kuchak|Hasan Kuchak]] ('Little Hasan') seized [[s:azerbaijan|Azerbaijan]] and set up puppet khans, such as [[e:sati-beg|Sati Beg]] and Sulayman Khan, to legitimise his rule.
chupanids.r: The Chupanids fought the [[s:jalayirids|Jalayirids]] for control of the Ilkhanid heartland around [[e:tabriz|Tabriz]]. [[e:hasan-kuchak|Hasan Kuchak]] was murdered by his wife in 1343, and his brother [[e:malik-ashraf|Malik Ashraf]] ruled Tabriz with notorious cruelty and extortion, causing many scholars and merchants to flee. Their rule was military, relying on Mongol and Turkish troops, with little stable administration.
chupanids.e: In 1357 [[e:jani-beg|Jani Beg]], khan of the [[s:golden-horde|Golden Horde]], invaded [[s:azerbaijan|Azerbaijan]] at the invitation of exiles, captured [[e:malik-ashraf|Malik Ashraf]] and executed him, ending the dynasty. [[e:azerbaijan|Azerbaijan]] soon passed to the [[s:jalayirids|Jalayirids]].

catana.t: Chalcidian Greek city at the foot of Mount Etna, home of the lawgiver Charondas, which was twice emptied of its people by Sicilian tyrants.
catana.o: Chalcidian colonists from [[s:naxos|Naxos]] founded [[e:catania|Catana]] in 729 BCE, led by Euarchus, on the coast south of [[e:mount-etna|Mount Etna]], in a fertile plain watered by the [[e:simeto|Simeto]]. The site had a good harbour and access to the [[e:sicels|Sicel]] interior.
catana.r: [[e:catania|Catana]] was known for the laws of [[e:charondas|Charondas]], adopted by other Chalcidian cities in [[e:sicily|Sicily]] and southern [[e:italy|Italy]]. In 476 BCE [[e:hiero-i-of-syracuse|Hieron I of Syracuse]] moved its people to [[s:leontini|Leontini]], resettled it with [[e:dorians|Dorians]] and renamed it [[e:mount-etna|Aetna]], celebrated by [[e:pindar|Pindar]] and [[e:aeschylus|Aeschylus]]; the original citizens returned in 461 BCE. It served as [[e:athens|Athens]]' base during the [[e:sicilian-expedition|Sicilian Expedition]] in 415 BCE. Its farmland and wine benefited from Etna's volcanic soil, though eruptions repeatedly struck it.
catana.e: In 403 BCE [[e:dionysius-i-of-syracuse|Dionysius I]] captured [[e:catania|Catana]] and sold its people into [[e:slavery|slavery]], settling Campanian [[e:mercenary|mercenaries]] there. It recovered under later rulers and in 263 BCE was one of the first Sicilian cities taken by [[e:rome|Rome]], which carried off its sundial. Roman Catina became a prosperous town, today Catania.

chalukyas-of-vemulavada.t: A Chalukya branch in Telangana, vassals of the Rashtrakutas, whose court hosted the great Kannada poet Pampa.
chalukyas-of-vemulavada.o: The [[e:vemulawada|Vemulavada]] [[e:chalukya-dynasty|Chalukyas]] emerged in the 8th century in the [[e:karimnagar|Karimnagar]] region of modern [[e:telangana|Telangana]] as feudatories of the [[s:rashtrakuta-dynasty|Rashtrakuta dynasty]]. They claimed kinship with the [[s:chalukyas-of-badami|Chalukyas of Badami]], and their capital was Vemulavada, with an earlier seat at [[e:bodhan|Bodhan]].
chalukyas-of-vemulavada.r: The family fought in the wars of their Rashtrakuta overlords against the [[s:eastern-chalukyas|Eastern Chalukyas]]. [[e:arikesari-ii|Arikesari II]] was the patron of the poet [[e:adikavi-pampa|Pampa]], who wrote the [[e:kannada|Kannada]] epics [[e:vikramarjuna-vijaya|Vikramarjuna Vijaya]] and [[e:adipurana-pampa|Adipurana]] in 941 and cast Arikesari as the hero [[e:arjuna|Arjuna]]. The Jain scholar [[e:somadeva-suri|Somadeva Suri]] wrote his [[e:sanskrit|Sanskrit]] romance [[e:yashastilaka|Yashastilaka]] at the court of Arikesari's son. The dynasty supported Jain monks and Shaiva temples, such as the [[e:raja-rajeshwara-temple-vemulawada|Rajarajeshvara]] temple at [[e:vemulawada|Vemulavada]].
chalukyas-of-vemulavada.e: The family fell with its Rashtrakuta overlords around 973, when the [[s:western-chalukya-empire|Western Chalukya Empire]] took over their lands.

chanda-kingdom.t: A Gond kingdom of eastern Maharashtra ruled from Chanda (Chandrapur), whose fortified capital and temples survive.
chanda-kingdom.o: [[e:gond-people|Gond]] chiefs built a kingdom in the [[e:wainganga-river|Wainganga]] and [[e:wardha-river|Wardha]] valleys from around the 13th century, traditionally beginning with Kol [[e:bhils|Bhil]] or Bhim Ballal Singh at Sirpur. The capital moved to [[e:ballarpur|Ballarpur]] and then, in the 15th and 16th centuries under [[e:khandkya-ballal-shah|Khandkya Ballal Shah]], to [[e:chandrapur|Chanda]], where a walled city was laid out.
chanda-kingdom.r: The [[e:gond-people|Gond]] kings ruled forested and farming country through Gond and [[e:hinduism|Hindu]] nobles, and gradually adopted Rajput-style kingship and Hindu temple patronage. The Mahakali temple and the walls of [[e:chandrapur|Chandrapur]] date from this period. The kingdom paid tribute at times to the [[s:bahmani-sultanate|Bahmani Sultanate]] and later to the [[s:mughal-empire|Mughal Empire]], while keeping wide local autonomy.
chanda-kingdom.e: In the 18th century the [[e:bhonsles|Bhonsle]] [[e:maratha-empire|Marathas]] of [[e:nagpur|Nagpur]] extended their power over the region, and [[e:chandrapur|Chanda]] was annexed around 1751. It passed with Nagpur to the British in 1853. The [[e:gond-people|Gond]] rulers survive as part of local memory and architecture.

county-of-empuries.t: A Catalan coastal county in the Empordà, ruled from Castelló d'Empúries by its own counts for six centuries.
county-of-empuries.o: The county took its name from the ancient Greek city of [[s:emporion|Emporion]] and was created by the [[s:franks|Franks]] in the early 9th century within the [[s:marca-hispanica|Marca Hispanica]]. From the later 9th century it was held with [[e:roussillon|Roussillon]] by the descendants of Count Sunyer, until the two were separated in 991.
county-of-empuries.r: The counts moved their seat from [[e:sant-marti-dempuries|Sant Martí d'Empúries]] to [[e:castello-d-empuries|Castelló d'Empúries]], where they built a large Gothic church. The county controlled the fertile [[e:emporda|Empordà]] plain and a coastline exposed to [[e:vikings|Viking]] and Saracen raids. Its counts were often in conflict with the counts of [[e:barcelona|Barcelona]] and the [[e:bishop|bishops]] of [[e:girona|Girona]], while remaining [[e:vassal|vassals]] of the [[e:house-of-barcelona|House of Barcelona]].
county-of-empuries.e: After centuries of semi-independence, the county was absorbed into the royal domain of the [[s:crown-of-aragon|Crown of Aragon]] in 1402. The title later passed to branches of the royal family and then to the Dukes of Segorbe and [[e:medinaceli|Medinaceli]].

chhuikhadan-state.t: A small state of Chhattisgarh unusual in being ruled by a line of Vaishnava Bairagi mahants rather than a warrior clan.
chhuikhadan-state.o: Chhuikhadan, also called Kondka, was established around 1750 by a Bairagi religious family, whose heads combined the roles of [[e:vaishnavism|Vaishnava]] mahant and landholder. It held its lands as a zamindari under the [[e:bhonsles|Bhonsles]] of the [[s:nagpur-kingdom|Nagpur Kingdom]].
chhuikhadan-state.r: After the [[s:nagpur-kingdom|Nagpur Kingdom]] was annexed, Chhuikhadan became a feudatory state of the [[e:central-provinces|Central Provinces]], later part of the [[e:chhattisgarh-feudatory-states|Chhattisgarh States]] group of the [[e:eastern-states-agency|Eastern States Agency]]. Its ruler, a Mahant with the title of Raja, governed a small territory of [[e:rice|rice]]-growing villages.
chhuikhadan-state.e: The state acceded to [[e:india|India]] and on 1 January 1948 was merged into the [[e:central-provinces|Central Provinces and Berar]], later [[e:madhya-pradesh|Madhya Pradesh]]. Its territory is now in [[e:chhattisgarh|Chhattisgarh]].

cenel-ngabrain.t: The dominant kindred of Dal Riata in Kintyre, whose kings, from Aedan mac Gabrain onwards, most often held the overkingship of Gaelic Argyll.
cenel-ngabrain.o: Cenel nGabrain traced its descent to [[e:gabran-mac-domangairt|Gabran]], said to be a grandson of [[e:fergus-mor|Fergus Mor]], and held [[e:kintyre|Kintyre]], [[s:caucasian-albania|Arran]] and nearby lands in the 6th century. Its leading king, [[e:aedan-mac-gabrain|Aedan mac Gabrain]], was ordained by [[e:columba|Columba of Iona]] according to [[e:adomnan|Adomnan]], and campaigned widely in northern [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]] before his defeat by [[e:aethelfrith-of-northumbria|Aethelfrith]] of [[s:kingdom-of-bernicia|Bernicia]] at [[e:battle-of-degsastan|Degsastan]] in 603.
cenel-ngabrain.r: The kindred controlled the hillfort of [[e:dunadd|Dunadd]] for much of its history and competed with [[s:cenel-loairn|Cenel Loairn]] for the overkingship. Its rulers patronised [[e:iona|Iona]] and fought both [[e:picts|Picts]] and [[e:britons-celtic-people|Britons]] of [[s:kingdom-of-strathclyde|Alt Clut]]. The [[e:senchus-fer-n-alban|Senchus fer nAlban]] records its houses and duties to supply ships.
cenel-ngabrain.e: Defeat at [[e:battle-of-moira|Mag Rath]] in 637 under [[e:domnall-brecc|Domnall Brecc]], and later Pictish conquest, eroded its standing. [[e:kenneth-macalpin|Kenneth MacAlpin]], founder of the [[s:kingdom-of-scotland|Kingdom of Scotland]] in the 840s, was traditionally counted among its descendants, giving the kindred a central place in Scottish royal genealogy.

commune-of-the-working-people-of-estonia.t: Soviet puppet government proclaimed in Narva in 1918, which tried to take Estonia for the Bolsheviks during the Estonian War of Independence.
commune-of-the-working-people-of-estonia.o: As German troops withdrew after the [[e:armistice-of-11-november-1918|armistice]], the [[e:red-army|Red Army]] invaded [[s:republic-of-estonia|Estonia]] and took [[e:narva|Narva]] on 28 November 1918. The next day Estonian Bolsheviks proclaimed the Commune of the Working People of [[e:estonia|Estonia]] there, with [[e:jaan-anvelt|Jaan Anvelt]] as chairman, and [[s:russian-sfsr|Soviet Russia]] recognised it in December.
commune-of-the-working-people-of-estonia.r: The Commune followed the Bolshevik model: it nationalised manors, factories and banks, and set up revolutionary tribunals that executed opponents, including clergy at [[e:tartu|Tartu]]. Its authority depended on the [[e:red-army|Red Army]], which advanced to within about 30 kilometres of [[s:reval|Tallinn]] by early January 1919.
commune-of-the-working-people-of-estonia.e: The Estonian counter-offensive, aided by Finnish volunteers and the British navy, drove the [[e:red-army|Red Army]] out of most of [[s:republic-of-estonia|Estonia]] by February 1919. The Commune retreated into [[e:russia|Russia]] and dissolved in June 1919. The [[e:treaty-of-tartu-russian-estonian|Treaty of Tartu]] in 1920 recognised the independence of the Republic of [[e:estonia|Estonia]].

crimean-peoples-republic.t: The first democratic republic in the Muslim world, proclaimed by the Crimean Tatars in 1917 and crushed by the Bolsheviks weeks later.
crimean-peoples-republic.o: After the [[e:february-revolution|February Revolution]], [[e:crimean-tatars|Crimean Tatars]] organised to win self-government. In December 1917 an elected national assembly, the [[e:kurultai|Kurultai]], met in the [[e:bakhchysarai-palace|Khan's Palace]] at [[e:bakhchysarai|Bakhchysarai]], adopted a constitution and proclaimed the Crimean People's Republic, with the mufti [[e:noman-celebicihan|Noman Celebicihan]] as its leader.
crimean-peoples-republic.r: The constitution declared equality of all nations living in [[e:crimea|Crimea]] and gave women the vote, unusual for its time. A directorate under [[e:noman-celebicihan|Celebicihan]] and [[e:cafer-seydahmet|Cafer Seydahmet]] formed a government and raised [[e:crimean-tatars|Crimean Tatar]] military units, seeking cooperation with Crimea's other peoples against the advancing Bolsheviks.
crimean-peoples-republic.e: In January 1918 Bolshevik forces and sailors of the [[e:black-sea-fleet|Black Sea Fleet]] overran the [[e:crimea|Crimea]]. [[e:noman-celebicihan|Celebicihan]] was captured and shot in [[e:sevastopol|Sevastopol]] in February 1918, and the [[s:taurida-soviet-socialist-republic|Taurida Soviet Socialist Republic]] was proclaimed. The [[e:kurultai|Kurultai]] remains a symbol of [[e:crimean-tatars|Crimean Tatar]] national self-government.

chatti.t: A disciplined Germanic people of Hesse who resisted Rome for two centuries and are often seen as ancestors of the Hessians.
chatti.o: The Chatti lived in the hill country of the upper [[e:weser|Weser]], [[e:fulda-river|Fulda]] and [[e:eder-river|Eder]], roughly modern northern [[e:hesse|Hesse]]. They appear in Roman sources around 10 BCE, when [[e:nero-claudius-drusus|Drusus]] campaigned against them. [[e:germanicus|Germanicus]] burned their chief centre, [[e:mattium|Mattium]], in 15 CE, but [[e:rome|Rome]] never brought them under lasting control.
chatti.r: [[e:tacitus|Tacitus]] describes the Chatti as unusually well organised for Germans: they chose leaders, kept ranks, entrenched camps and planned campaigns. Young warriors wore an iron ring and left their hair uncut until they had killed an enemy. They farmed the fertile Hessian basins and fought regular wars with the [[s:hermunduri|Hermunduri]] over salt springs.
chatti.e: [[e:domitian|Domitian]] fought the Chatti in 83 to 85 and pushed the frontier forward along the [[e:taunus|Taunus]] and [[e:wetterau|Wetterau]], the line later fortified as the [[e:limes-germanicus|Limes]]. After about 260 they appear among the [[s:franks|Franks]]. Their name is generally linked to the later Hessians, though the connection is debated.

county-of-hoya.t: Lower Saxon county on the middle Weser, ruled from Hoya and Nienburg until its counts died out in 1582 and their lands went to the Guelphs.
county-of-hoya.o: Count Henry, of a noble family from the area, acquired lands on the middle [[e:weser|Weser]] and called himself Count of Hoya from about 1202. His descendants extended their rule along the river between [[s:free-hanseatic-city-of-bremen|Bremen]] and [[e:minden|Minden]], building a county around the towns of Hoya and [[e:nienburg-weser|Nienburg]].
county-of-hoya.r: The county lay in flat farmland and marsh along the [[e:weser|Weser]], with river tolls and grain the main sources of wealth. It was divided at times into upper and lower counties ruled by separate branches. The counts were pressed between the [[e:house-of-welf|Guelph]] dukes of Brunswick-[[e:luneburg|Lüneburg]] and the [[e:bishop|bishops]] of [[e:minden|Minden]] and [[e:verden|Verden]]. [[e:lutheranism|Lutheranism]] was introduced in the 1520s and 1530s.
county-of-hoya.e: When the last count, Otto VIII, died in 1582, the county was divided between branches of the [[e:house-of-welf|Guelph]] house, the [[s:principality-of-luneburg|Principality of Lüneburg]] and the [[s:principality-of-wolfenbuttel|Principality of Wolfenbüttel]]. It later belonged to the [[s:electorate-of-hanover|Electorate of Hanover]] and is now in [[e:lower-saxony|Lower Saxony]].

cenomani.t: Celtic people of the plain around Brescia and Verona who, unlike other Cisalpine Gauls, were usually allies of Rome.
cenomani.o: [[e:livy|Livy]] describes the [[s:aulerci-cenomani|Cenomani]] as [[e:gaul|Gauls]] who crossed the [[e:alps|Alps]] under a leader named Elitovius in the 5th or 4th century BCE and settled in the lands around [[e:brescia|Brixia]] ([[s:commune-of-brescia|Brescia]]) and [[s:commune-of-verona|Verona]], between the [[s:insubres|Insubres]] and the [[s:veneti|Veneti]].
cenomani.r: [[e:brescia|Brixia]] was their main centre. They farmed the plain and traded with the [[s:veneti|Veneti]] and [[e:etruscans|Etruscans]]. Their relations with their Celtic neighbours were often hostile, and in 225 BCE they joined the Veneti in sending troops to help [[e:rome|Rome]] against the [[s:insubres|Insubres]] and [[s:boii|Boii]]. Apart from joining a revolt in 200–197 BCE, they remained Roman allies.
cenomani.e: After 197 BCE the [[s:aulerci-cenomani|Cenomani]] stayed loyal and were gradually Romanised. Their towns received [[e:latin|Latin]] rights in 89 BCE and full citizenship in 49 BCE. [[e:brescia|Brixia]] became a Roman colony and [[s:commune-of-verona|Verona]] a leading town of northern [[e:italy|Italy]].

chalco.t: A confederation of Nahua altepetl in the south-eastern Valley of Mexico that resisted the Mexica for decades before its conquest in 1465.
chalco.o: Chalco developed around the eastern shore of [[e:lake-chalco|Lake Chalco]] and the slopes of the volcanoes [[e:popocatepetl|Popocatépetl]] and [[e:iztaccihuatl|Iztaccíhuatl]]. From the 13th century several groups settled the area, and their altepetl, including [[e:tlalmanalco|Tlalmanalco]] and [[e:amecameca|Amaquemecan]], formed a loose confederation. The chronicler [[e:chimalpahin|Chimalpahin]], a native of Amaquemecan, recorded its history.
chalco.r: The [[e:chalca|Chalca]] confederation was governed by the rulers of its constituent altepetl, each with its own dynasty, who acted together in war and diplomacy. Its fertile lands and [[e:chinampa|chinampas]] produced [[e:maize|maize]] and other crops, and it controlled routes from the [[e:valley-of-mexico|Valley of Mexico]] to [[e:morelos|Morelos]] and Puebla. It fought long wars with the [[e:mexica|Mexica]] and the [[s:tepanec-empire|Tepanec Empire]].
chalco.e: After a war lasting from the 1440s, the [[s:aztec-empire|Aztec Empire]] under [[e:moctezuma-i|Moctezuma I]] conquered Chalco in 1465 and made it a tributary. Its towns later became Spanish colonial jurisdictions in the State of [[s:mexico|Mexico]].

carlist-state.t: The counter-state of the Carlist pretender Carlos VII in the Basque Country and Navarre during the Third Carlist War, with its capital at Estella.
carlist-state.o: In 1872, as the [[s:sexenio-democratico|Sexenio Democrático]] unsettled [[e:spain|Spain]], the traditionalist pretender [[e:carlos-duke-of-madrid|Carlos VII]], Duke of [[e:madrid|Madrid]], launched the [[e:third-carlist-war|Third Carlist War]] under the banner of God, Fatherland and King. His forces took control of much of rural [[e:kingdom-of-navarre|Navarre]], the Basque provinces and parts of [[s:principality-of-catalonia|Catalonia]].
carlist-state.r: The [[e:carlism|Carlists]] organised a real administration from [[e:estella-lizarra|Estella]]: ministries, courts, a postal service with its own stamps, coinage and a university at [[e:onati|Oñati]]. They restored the Basque and Navarrese fueros and enforced strict [[e:catholicism|Catholicism]]. Their armies besieged [[e:bilbao|Bilbao]] in 1874 but never held a major city for long.
carlist-state.e: After the [[s:ile-bourbon|Bourbon]] restoration in [[s:restoration-spain|Restoration Spain]], government armies advanced. [[e:estella-lizarra|Estella]] fell in February 1876, and [[e:carlos-duke-of-madrid|Carlos VII]] crossed into [[e:france|France]]. The Basque fueros were then largely abolished, though [[e:carlism|Carlism]] survived as a political movement.

county-of-maine.t: A county around Le Mans, long fought over by Anjou and Normandy, which became part of the Plantagenet heartland and later a royal appanage.
county-of-maine.o: Counts of Maine appear in the mid-10th century, ruling from [[e:le-mans|Le Mans]] between the stronger principalities of [[s:county-of-anjou|Anjou]], [[s:duchy-of-normandy|Normandy]] and [[s:duchy-of-brittany|Brittany]]. Count [[e:herbert-i-count-of-maine|Herbert I]], known as Wakedog, defended it against [[e:fulk-nerra|Fulk Nerra]] of Anjou in the early 11th century.
county-of-maine.r: Maine was a land of farming and forests, with a strong [[e:bishop|bishop]] and an assertive town: [[e:le-mans|Le Mans]] formed one of the first urban communes in [[e:france|France]] around 1070. [[e:william-the-conqueror|William the Conqueror]] took the county in 1063, but Count [[e:elias-i-count-of-maine|Elias of La Flèche]] recovered it, and his daughter's marriage to [[e:fulk-king-of-jerusalem|Fulk V]] joined it to [[s:county-of-anjou|Anjou]].
county-of-maine.e: After [[e:philip-ii-of-france|Philip II]] seized it in 1204, Maine became part of the royal domain and was granted as an [[e:appanage|appanage]] to the [[s:county-of-anjou|Anjou]] princes. On the death of [[e:charles-iv-duke-of-anjou|Charles of Maine]] in 1481 it returned permanently to the [[s:kingdom-of-france|Kingdom of France]].

county-of-macon.t: Carolingian county in southern Burgundy, the land in which the great abbey of Cluny was founded in 910.
county-of-macon.o: The Mâconnais, around [[e:macon|Mâcon]] on the [[e:saone|Saône]], became a Carolingian county in the 9th century, at the junction of the lands of [[s:west-francia|West Francia]] and the Burgundian kingdoms. Its early counts were linked with the dukes of [[s:duchy-of-aquitaine|Aquitaine]] and [[s:duchy-of-burgundy|Burgundy]].
county-of-macon.r: In 910 Duke [[e:william-i-duke-of-aquitaine|William I of Aquitaine]] founded the abbey of [[e:cluny-abbey|Cluny]] in the county, free from lay and episcopal control, and it became the head of a vast monastic network. From the late 10th century the county was held by a branch of the house of Burgundy-[[e:ivrea|Ivrea]] descended from Otto-William, who also ruled the [[s:free-county-of-burgundy|Free County of Burgundy]].
county-of-macon.e: The last countess, Alix, and her husband John of Dreux sold the county to [[e:louis-ix-of-france|Louis IX of France]] in 1239, and it was attached to the royal domain. The Mâconnais remains known for its wines.

chavda-dynasty.t: The dynasty traditionally said to have founded Anahilavada Patan, the medieval capital of Gujarat.
chavda-dynasty.o: [[e:jainism|Jain]] chronicles of the 13th and 14th centuries tell how [[e:vanraj-chavda|Vanaraja]], a prince whose father had been killed in battle, was raised under the protection of a Jain monk and founded the city of [[e:patan-gujarat|Anahilavada]], modern Patan in northern [[e:gujarat|Gujarat]], around 746. Contemporary records of the dynasty are almost entirely lacking.
chavda-dynasty.r: The chronicles portray the Chavdas as patrons of [[e:jainism|Jainism]], a tradition that shaped later Gujarati culture. They probably ruled a small kingdom in northern [[e:gujarat|Gujarat]], at times under the [[s:gurjara-pratihara|Gurjara-Pratihara]]. Inscriptions mention Chapotkata chiefs in the region, which suggests a historical basis for the chronicles.
chavda-dynasty.e: According to tradition, the last king, Samantasimha, was killed by his nephew [[e:mularaja|Mularaja]] around 942, who founded the [[s:chaulukya-dynasty|Chaulukya dynasty]] and made [[e:patan-gujarat|Anahilavada]] the capital of a far larger kingdom.

canton-of-appenzell.t: An Alpine land of free peasants who threw off the rule of the abbot of Saint Gall in the Appenzell Wars and joined the Swiss in 1513.
canton-of-appenzell.o: The Appenzell districts belonged to the [[s:imperial-abbey-of-saint-gall|Imperial Abbey of Saint Gall]]. From 1401 the peasants rebelled against the abbot's officials and, with help from the [[s:canton-of-schwyz|Canton of Schwyz]], defeated his and [[s:county-of-habsburg|Habsburg]] forces at [[e:battle-of-vogelinsegg|Vögelinsegg]] in 1403 and [[e:battle-of-stoss|Stoss]] in 1405. Their League above the Lake briefly spread across eastern [[s:swiss-confederation|Switzerland]] before its defeat at [[e:bregenz|Bregenz]] in 1408.
canton-of-appenzell.r: Appenzell governed itself through the [[e:landsgemeinde|Landsgemeinde]], the assembly of all men, which elected the [[e:landammann|Landammann]]. It became an associate of the [[s:confederate-states-of-america|Confederacy]] in 1411 and a full member, the thirteenth canton, in 1513. The economy rested on [[e:cattle|cattle]] and dairy farming and later on linen weaving. The [[e:protestant-reformation|Reformation]] split the inner, Catholic districts from the outer, Reformed ones.
canton-of-appenzell.e: To avoid civil war the canton was divided in 1597, with Swiss mediation, into [[s:appenzell-innerrhoden|Appenzell Innerrhoden]], which stayed Catholic, and [[s:appenzell-ausserrhoden|Appenzell Ausserrhoden]], which became Reformed. The two half-cantons still exist.

caucasian-imamate.t: The Islamic state of Imam Shamil in Dagestan and Chechnya, which fought the Russian Empire for three decades before surrendering at Gunib in 1859.
caucasian-imamate.o: In the 1820s [[e:sufism|Sufi]] teachers of the Naqshbandi order preached holy war and strict [[e:sharia|sharia]] against both Russian rule and local customary law. [[e:ghazi-muhammad|Ghazi Muhammad]] was proclaimed [[e:imam|imam]] around 1828-1829 and led the first campaigns until he was killed at [[e:gimry|Gimry]] in 1832. His successor [[e:hamzat-bek|Hamzat Bek]] was assassinated in 1834, and [[e:imam-shamil|Shamil]] became imam.
caucasian-imamate.r: [[e:imam-shamil|Shamil]] built a centralised theocracy across mountainous [[e:dagestan|Dagestan]] and [[e:chechnya|Chechnya]], dividing it into districts under naibs, levying taxes, raising a standing army and replacing customary law with [[e:sharia|sharia]]. He survived the Russian siege of [[e:siege-of-akhulgo|Akhulgo]] in 1839 and defeated a large Russian expedition at [[e:battle-of-dargo|Dargo]] in 1845. The capital moved, settling at [[e:vedeno|Vedeno]].
caucasian-imamate.e: Exhausted by war and Russian advances through the forests, the [[e:imamate|imamate]] collapsed. In 1859 [[e:imam-shamil|Shamil]] surrendered at [[e:gunib|Gunib]] and lived in honourable exile in [[e:russia|Russia]], dying in [[e:medina|Medina]] in 1871. The [[s:russian-empire|Russian Empire]] annexed the region.

cr.a: Mega programmer at English Wikipedia, Takhirgeran Umar

comalcalco.t: The westernmost major Classic Maya city, in the Tabasco plain, unique for being built of fired brick rather than stone.
comalcalco.o: Comalcalco grew in the alluvial lowlands of [[e:tabasco|Tabasco]], close to the [[e:gulf-coast-of-mexico|Gulf Coast]], where there was no building stone. It became a significant centre from about 600 CE Its ancient name was Joy Chan, and in 649 it was conquered by [[e:tortuguero|Tortuguero]], whose kings used the same [[s:palenque|B'aakal]] emblem as Palenque.
comalcalco.r: Builders made fired clay bricks, many incised or stamped with drawings, glyphs and marks, and used lime from burnt oyster shells for mortar. The city's acropolis held palaces and a tomb decorated with stucco figures. Its economy rested on fertile plains well suited to [[e:cacao|cacao]], a crop that is still important in [[e:tabasco|Tabasco]].
comalcalco.e: Comalcalco declined around 900 CE during the wider collapse of lowland Maya kingdoms. Its brick architecture remains unique in the Maya world.

county-of-forcalquier.t: A county of upper Provence that broke away from the main comital line and was reunited with Provence in 1209.
county-of-forcalquier.o: The county arose from the division of the inheritance of the counts of [[s:county-of-provence|Provence]] in the mid-11th century, when one branch kept rights in the north-east around [[e:forcalquier|Forcalquier]], [[e:sisteron|Sisteron]] and the [[e:durance|Durance]] valley. In the 12th century it passed to the counts of Urgell, who ruled it as a separate principality.
county-of-forcalquier.r: [[e:forcalquier|Forcalquier]] was a land of hill towns and pasture along the [[e:durance|Durance]], controlling routes between [[s:county-of-provence|Provence]] and the [[e:alps|Alps]]. Count [[e:william-iv-of-forcalquier|William IV]], the most prominent ruler, held out against the Catalan counts of Provence and the emperors for decades.
county-of-forcalquier.e: In 1193 [[e:william-iv-of-forcalquier|William IV]]'s granddaughter [[e:garsenda-of-forcalquier|Garsenda]] married [[e:alfonso-ii-count-of-provence|Alfonso II of Provence]], and on William's death in 1209 [[e:forcalquier|Forcalquier]] was reunited with the [[s:county-of-provence|County of Provence]]. Their son [[e:ramon-berenguer-iv-count-of-provence|Raymond Berengar IV]] ruled both.

caral-supe.t: The oldest known civilisation of the Americas, whose monumental pyramids and plazas in Peru's coastal valleys rose at the same time as those of Egypt and Mesopotamia.
caral-supe.o: From around 3000 BCE communities in the Supe, Pativilca and Fortaleza valleys north of [[e:lima|Lima]] began building large platform mounds and sunken circular plazas. [[e:caral|Caral]], about 23 km inland in the Supe valley, became the largest of some twenty related sites. The culture emerged without pottery, which is why archaeologists also call this the Late Preceramic period.
caral-supe.r: Little is known of government, but the scale of building implies an elite able to organise labour and redistribute goods. The economy linked inland farmers, who grew [[e:cotton|cotton]], squash and beans by irrigation, with coastal fishing villages such as [[e:aspero|Áspero]] that traded anchovies and shellfish. Cotton fishing nets were a key product. A knotted-string device found at [[e:caral|Caral]] may be an early ancestor of the khipu. Flutes of condor and pelican bone suggest a rich ritual life.
caral-supe.e: Building at [[e:caral|Caral]] slowed and the valley settlements were largely abandoned around 1800 BCE, perhaps after earthquakes, floods and climatic change. Excavations led by [[e:ruth-shady|Ruth Shady]] from 1994 revealed its age. Caral was declared a [[e:unesco-world-heritage-site|UNESCO World Heritage Site]] in 2009.

county-of-nassau.t: The county on the Lahn whose division in 1255 produced the Walram and Otto lines of Nassau, ancestors of the royal houses of the Netherlands and Luxembourg.
county-of-nassau.o: The counts of Laurenburg, who held lands on the [[e:lahn|Lahn]], built [[e:nassau-castle|Nassau Castle]] around 1125 on land claimed by the [[e:bishopric-of-worms|Bishopric of Worms]]. Around 1160 they began to call themselves counts of Nassau. They extended their territory in the [[e:westerwald|Westerwald]], the [[e:taunus|Taunus]] and the [[e:siegerland|Siegerland]].
county-of-nassau.r: The county lay in hilly, wooded country with mining and iron working, especially around [[e:siegen|Siegen]]. Its counts were mostly modest regional lords, often in dispute with the archbishops of [[e:trier|Trier]] and [[e:mainz|Mainz]]. Its Count [[e:walram-ii-count-of-nassau|Walram II]] and his brother [[e:otto-i-duke-of-bavaria|Otto I]] jointly ruled it in the mid 13th century.
county-of-nassau.e: In 1255 [[e:walram-ii-count-of-nassau|Walram II]] and Otto I divided Nassau along the [[e:lahn|Lahn]]. Walram's line produced [[e:adolf-of-nassau|King Adolf of Nassau]], elected in 1292, and later the grand dukes of [[s:county-of-luxembourg|Luxembourg]]; Otto's line produced [[e:william-the-silent|William the Silent]] and the house of [[e:house-of-orange-nassau|Orange-Nassau]], today's [[e:dutch|Dutch]] royal family.

commonwealth-of-australia.t: A federation of six former British colonies founded in 1901, now a parliamentary democracy spanning an entire continent.
commonwealth-of-australia.o: From the 1880s the colonies debated federation to manage defence, tariffs and immigration. Conventions in the 1890s drafted a constitution, approved by referendums, and the Commonwealth was proclaimed on 1 January 1901, uniting [[s:colony-of-new-south-wales|New South Wales]], [[s:colony-of-victoria|Victoria]], [[s:colony-of-queensland|Queensland]], [[s:province-of-south-australia|South Australia]], [[s:colony-of-western-australia|Western Australia]] and [[s:colony-of-tasmania|Tasmania]]. [[e:edmund-barton|Edmund Barton]] became the first prime minister, and Parliament met in [[e:melbourne|Melbourne]] until [[e:canberra|Canberra]] opened in 1927.
commonwealth-of-australia.r: The federation combined British-style responsible government with an American-style senate and [[e:high-court-of-australia|High Court]]. Early laws created the [[e:white-australia-policy|White Australia policy]] and, in 1902, votes for women, though most [[e:aboriginal-australians|Aboriginal]] people were excluded. The [[e:gallipoli-campaign|Gallipoli]] landing of 1915 became a founding national memory. During the [[e:second-world-war|Second World War]] [[e:john-curtin|John Curtin]] turned to the [[s:united-states|United States]] for defence, and [[e:robert-menzies|Robert Menzies]] led the long post-war boom with mass migration from [[e:europe|Europe]].
commonwealth-of-australia.e: The 1967 referendum included [[e:aboriginal-australians|Aboriginal]] people in the [[e:census|census]], [[e:white-australia-policy|White Australia]] was dismantled by 1973, and the [[e:australia|Australia]] Act of 1986 ended British legal ties. The [[e:mabo-v-queensland-no-2|Mabo decision]] of 1992 recognised native title. Republic and Indigenous Voice referendums failed in 1999 and 2023.
