colony-of-mayotte-and-dependencies.t: France's first foothold in the Comoros, bought in 1841, from which it extended control over the whole archipelago.
colony-of-mayotte-and-dependencies.o: [[e:andriantsoly|Andriantsoly]], a former [[e:sakalava|Sakalava]] king from [[e:madagascar|Madagascar]] who had become ruler of Mayotte, ceded the island to [[e:france|France]] in 1841 in return for a pension and protection from rival Comoran sultans. France took formal possession in 1843 and fortified the islet of [[e:dzaoudzi|Dzaoudzi]] as its seat.
colony-of-mayotte-and-dependencies.r: French administrators abolished [[e:slavery|slavery]] in 1846 and promoted [[e:sugar-plantation|sugar]] plantations worked by contract labourers, though the industry later declined. The population remained Muslim, speaking [[e:shimaore|Shimaore]] and [[e:kibushi|Kibushi]]. In 1886 [[e:france|France]] placed the [[s:sultanate-of-anjouan|Sultanate of Anjouan]], the [[s:sultanate-of-moheli|Sultanate of Moheli]] and [[e:grande-comore|Grande Comore]] under [[e:protectorate|protectorates]] administered from Mayotte.
colony-of-mayotte-and-dependencies.e: The other islands were annexed in the early 20th century and the whole group was attached to [[s:french-madagascar|French Madagascar]] in 1912. In 1946 the archipelago became the separate [[s:territory-of-the-comoros|Territory of the Comoros]].

commune-of-alessandria.t: A new city founded by the Lombard League in 1168 and named after Pope Alexander III, which held out against Frederick Barbarossa's siege.
commune-of-alessandria.o: The [[s:lombard-league|Lombard League]] founded Alessandria in 1168 at the confluence of the [[e:tanaro|Tanaro]] and [[e:bormida|Bormida]], settling people from nearby villages to block imperial allies such as [[s:commune-of-pavia|Pavia]] and the [[s:march-of-montferrat|March of Montferrat]]. The city was named in honour of [[e:pope-alexander-iii|Pope Alexander III]].
commune-of-alessandria.r: Hastily fortified, Alessandria withstood a six-month siege by [[e:frederick-barbarossa|Frederick Barbarossa]] in 1174–1175, a key blow to the emperor before [[e:battle-of-legnano|Legnano]]. In 1183 the city made peace with the emperor and was briefly renamed [[s:lordship-of-caesarea|Caesarea]]. Governed by consuls and later a podestà, it fought its neighbours, especially the marquises of [[e:montferrat|Montferrat]], for control of the surrounding plain.
commune-of-alessandria.e: After periods under [[e:montferrat|Montferrat]] and other lords, Alessandria passed in 1348 to [[e:luchino-visconti-lord-of-milan|Luchino Visconti]] and became part of the [[s:lordship-of-milan|Lordship of Milan]]. It passed to the [[s:duchy-of-savoy|Duchy of Savoy]] in 1707, a transfer confirmed in 1713.

canton-of-zurich.t: Guild-ruled city-republic on Lake Zürich that joined the Swiss Confederacy in 1351 and became the cradle of Zwingli's Reformation.
canton-of-zurich.o: Zürich grew from the Roman customs post of [[e:turicum|Turicum]] and the royal abbey of the [[e:fraumunster|Fraumünster]]. Under [[e:house-of-zahringen|Zähringen]] protection the town flourished, and when their line died out in 1218 it became an imperial city. In 1336 [[e:rudolf-brun|Rudolf Brun]] overthrew the old council and introduced a [[e:guild|guild]] constitution, and in 1351 Zürich joined the [[s:old-swiss-confederacy|Old Swiss Confederacy]].
canton-of-zurich.r: The burgomaster, councils and [[e:guild|guilds]] ruled the city and a growing rural territory. The ambitious mayor [[e:hans-waldmann|Hans Waldmann]] was executed in 1489 after a revolt. From 1519 [[e:huldrych-zwingli|Huldrych Zwingli]] led a [[e:protestant-reformation|Reformation]] that made Zürich a centre of [[e:calvinism|Reformed Protestantism]]; Zwingli died at [[e:battle-of-kappel|Kappel]] in 1531. [[e:silk|Silk]] and [[e:cotton|cotton]] manufacturing later made the city prosperous. Its claims to [[s:county-of-toggenburg|Toggenburg]] caused the [[e:old-zurich-war|Old Zürich War]] in the 1440s.
canton-of-zurich.e: The French invasion of 1798 ended the old regime, and Zürich became part of the [[s:helvetic-republic|Helvetic Republic]]. It returned as a canton in 1803, became [[e:switzerland|Switzerland's]] largest city and financial centre, and remains a canton.

creones.t: People of the west Highland coast of Scotland, named only in Ptolemy's 2nd-century Geography.
creones.o: The Creones are known solely from [[e:geography-ptolemy|Ptolemy's Geography]] of about 150, which places them on the western seaboard of [[e:scotland|Scotland]] north of the [[s:epidii|Epidii]], usually located somewhere between [[e:lorn|Lorn]], [[e:ardnamurchan|Ardnamurchan]] and [[e:knoydart|Knoydart]]. Their name has no clear meaning, and some editors read it as a corrupted form.
creones.r: Nothing is recorded of their rulers or society. The rugged coast and sea lochs of this region were settled in small communities living in duns, crannogs and roundhouses, relying on fishing, herding and limited farming. Ptolemy's information probably came from sailors who passed along the coast, perhaps during [[e:gnaeus-julius-agricola|Agricola's]] fleet operations.
creones.e: The Creones are not mentioned again. Their region was later divided between the Gaelic kingdom of [[s:dal-riata|Dál Riata]] in the south and the [[e:picts|Picts]] further north.

county-of-diepholz.t: A small Lower Saxon county of moors and lakes south of Bremen, held by the noble lords of Diepholz until their line died out in 1585.
county-of-diepholz.o: The lords of Diepholz are first recorded around 1085 as noble lords on the [[e:hunte|Hunte]] river, between [[e:osnabruck|Osnabrück]] and [[s:free-hanseatic-city-of-bremen|Bremen]]. Their territory lay among moors around the [[e:dummer|Dümmer]] lake, with a castle at Diepholz controlling a route across the marshes.
county-of-diepholz.r: The lords, later counts from 1531, ruled a small, poor territory of moorland villages. They were [[e:vassal|vassals]] of several overlords and balanced between the [[e:bishop|bishops]] of [[e:minden|Minden]] and [[e:osnabruck|Osnabrück]] and the dukes of Brunswick-[[e:luneburg|Lüneburg]]. The [[e:protestant-reformation|Reformation]] was introduced in the 16th century.
county-of-diepholz.e: When Count Friedrich II died without heirs in 1585, Diepholz passed by feudal right to the Brunswick-[[e:luneburg|Lüneburg]] dukes of [[e:celle|Celle]], and later to the [[s:electorate-of-hanover|Electorate of Hanover]]. It is now part of the district of Diepholz in [[e:lower-saxony|Lower Saxony]].

commune-of-verona.t: A city-republic on the Adige that led resistance to Frederick Barbarossa and then fell under the tyrant Ezzelino da Romano.
commune-of-verona.o: Verona, guarding the route from the [[e:brenner-pass|Brenner Pass]] into [[e:italy|Italy]], had consuls by 1136. It led the [[s:veronese-league|Veronese League]] of 1164 against [[e:frederick-barbarossa|Frederick Barbarossa's]] officials and then joined the wider [[s:lombard-league|Lombard League]].
commune-of-verona.r: [[e:consul|Consuls]] and later a podestà governed the city, whose wealth came from the [[e:adige|Adige]] trade and the road to [[e:germany|Germany]]. The Romanesque basilica of [[e:basilica-of-san-zeno|San Zeno]] was rebuilt in the 12th century. From the 1220s the city was dominated by [[e:ezzelino-iii-da-romano|Ezzelino III da Romano]], a Ghibelline ally of Frederick II whose harsh rule over Verona, [[s:commune-of-vicenza|Vicenza]] and [[s:commune-of-padua|Padua]] made him a byword for tyranny.
commune-of-verona.e: After [[e:ezzelino-iii-da-romano|Ezzelino]]'s death in 1259 the city chose [[e:mastino-i-della-scala|Mastino I della Scala]] as its leader, and by 1262 communal government had given way to the [[s:lordship-of-verona|Lordship of Verona]] of the [[e:scaliger|Scaliger]] family.

condrusi.t: One of the Germani Cisrhenani of the Belgian uplands, remembered in the name of the Condroz.
condrusi.o: Caesar names the Condrusi with the [[s:eburones|Eburones]], [[s:caeroesi|Caeroesi]] and [[s:paemani|Paemani]] as Germani living west of the [[e:rhine|Rhine]], and calls them clients of the [[s:treveri|Treveri]]. They lived south of the [[e:meuse|Meuse]] in the region still called the [[e:condroz|Condroz]], between [[s:county-of-namur|Namur]] and [[s:prince-bishopric-of-liege|Liège]].
condrusi.r: Nothing is known of their rulers or settlements.
condrusi.e: They joined the Belgic league in 57 BCE. In 53 BCE they asked Caesar to spare them from his war on the [[s:eburones|Eburones]]. Under [[e:rome|Rome]] they were absorbed into the civitas of the [[s:tungri|Tungri]].

cacaxtla.t: A hilltop palace-city in Tlaxcala, seat of the Olmeca-Xicalanca, whose brilliant murals blend Maya and central Mexican styles.
cacaxtla.o: After Teotihuacan's decline, Cacaxtla rose around 650 on a fortified hill in southern [[s:tlaxcala|Tlaxcala]], alongside the neighbouring ceremonial centre of [[e:xochitecatl|Xochitécatl]]. Later chronicles attribute it to the [[e:olmeca-xicalanca|Olmeca-Xicalanca]], a people with [[e:gulf-coast-of-mexico|Gulf Coast]] connections who controlled the [[e:puebla-tlaxcala-valley|Puebla-Tlaxcala valley]] in this period.
cacaxtla.r: Cacaxtla's Great Platform held palaces, plazas and shrines protected by ditches and walls. Its murals, painted between about 650 and 900, show a battle between jaguar and bird warriors and richly dressed figures with symbols of trade, in a style strongly influenced by the Maya. They suggest a cosmopolitan elite tied to long-distance trade between the highlands and the Gulf.
cacaxtla.e: Cacaxtla was abandoned around 950, and the [[e:olmeca-xicalanca|Olmeca-Xicalanca]] were displaced by incoming groups, later including the founders of [[s:tlaxcala|Tlaxcala]]. Its murals were discovered in 1975 and are among the best preserved in [[e:mesoamerica|Mesoamerica]].

canton-of-schwyz.t: Alpine valley community that gave Switzerland its name and flag, a founding member of the Confederacy and victor over the Habsburgs at Morgarten.
canton-of-schwyz.o: The free peasants of Schwyz, at the foot of the [[e:mythen|Mythen]], gained a charter of imperial immediacy from Frederick II at [[s:lordship-of-faenza|Faenza]] in 1240. In 1291 they joined Uri and [[s:canton-of-unterwalden|Unterwalden]] in the [[e:federal-charter-of-1291|Federal Charter]], and in 1315 they defeated a [[s:county-of-habsburg|Habsburg]] army at [[e:battle-of-morgarten|Morgarten]], securing their independence and lending their name to the whole [[s:old-swiss-confederacy|Swiss Confederacy]].
canton-of-schwyz.r: The [[e:landsgemeinde|Landsgemeinde]] of all free men elected the [[e:landammann|Landammann]], and leading families dominated politics. [[e:cattle|Cattle]], transit trade and [[e:mercenary|mercenary]] service supported the canton. Schwyz quarrelled with [[e:einsiedeln-abbey|Einsiedeln Abbey]] over pasture, expanded into the March and [[e:hofe-district|Höfe]], and fought [[s:canton-of-zurich|Zürich]] in the [[e:old-zurich-war|Old Zürich War]]. It stayed firmly Catholic and led the Catholic cantons after the [[e:protestant-reformation|Reformation]].
canton-of-schwyz.e: In 1798 Schwyz resisted the French under [[e:alois-von-reding|Alois von Reding]] but was absorbed into the [[s:helvetic-republic|Helvetic Republic]]. It was restored as a canton in 1803 and remains one today; the [[e:federal-charter-of-1291|Federal Charter]] is kept in its archive.

county-of-castile.t: The frontier county of the Kingdom of León, made autonomous by Fernán González, that grew into the Kingdom of Castile.
county-of-castile.o: [[s:kingdom-of-castile|Castile]], 'land of castles', began in the 9th century as a frontier district of the [[s:kingdom-of-asturias|Kingdom of Asturias]] in the upper [[e:ebro-river|Ebro]] and [[e:burgos|Burgos]] region. Its first known count, [[e:rodrigo-of-castile|Rodrigo]], governed from around 850, and his son [[e:diego-rodriguez-porcelos|Diego Rodríguez Porcelos]] founded Burgos in 884. Several local counts governed until the territory was united.
county-of-castile.r: Count [[e:fernan-gonzalez-of-castile|Fernán González]], from about 931 to 970, gathered the Castilian counties and made his office hereditary, largely independent of León. [[s:kingdom-of-castile|Castile]] was a society of free peasant-soldiers and frontier towns, with its own customary law and a Romance dialect that became Castilian. [[e:sancho-garcia-of-castile|Sancho García]] granted fueros to frontier settlers, and the counts fought [[e:almanzor|Almanzor]] and his successors.
county-of-castile.e: The murder of the young Count [[e:garcia-sanchez-of-castile|García Sánchez]] in 1029 brought [[s:kingdom-of-castile|Castile]] under [[e:sancho-iii-of-navarre|Sancho III of Navarre]], whose son [[e:ferdinand-i-of-leon|Ferdinand I]] ruled it and became king of León in 1037. From 1065 [[e:kingdom-of-castile|Castile]] was a kingdom in its own right under [[e:sancho-ii-of-castile|Sancho II]].

canton-of-solothurn.t: Catholic city-republic on the Aare, a Swiss confederate from 1481 and for over two centuries the residence of the French ambassadors to Switzerland.
canton-of-solothurn.o: Solothurn grew from the Roman settlement of [[e:salodurum|Salodurum]] and the shrine of the martyrs [[e:ursus-of-solothurn|Ursus]] and Victor. Under the [[e:house-of-zahringen|Zähringen]] dukes it was a town of growing importance, and when their line died out in 1218 it became an imperial city. It built a rural territory and allied closely with neighbouring Bern.
canton-of-solothurn.r: Solothurn was ruled by patrician families through councils. It fought with the Swiss in the [[e:burgundian-wars|Burgundian Wars]] and was admitted to the [[s:old-swiss-confederacy|Old Swiss Confederacy]] with [[s:canton-of-fribourg|Fribourg]] in 1481. After a brief period of division, it remained Catholic during the [[e:protestant-reformation|Reformation]]. From 1530 to 1792 it was the seat of the French ambassadors, whose presence brought money, French culture and baroque buildings, including [[e:st-ursus-cathedral|St. Ursus Cathedral]].
canton-of-solothurn.e: French troops occupied Solothurn in 1798 and it became part of the [[s:helvetic-republic|Helvetic Republic]]. Restored as a canton under the [[e:act-of-mediation|Act of Mediation]] in 1803, it remains a canton of [[s:swiss-confederation|Switzerland]].

county-of-kyburg.t: A powerful noble lordship in north-eastern Switzerland whose extinction in 1264 handed its lands to the Habsburgs.
county-of-kyburg.o: The castle of Kyburg near [[e:winterthur|Winterthur]] belonged to the counts of Winterthur in the early 11th century; in 1027 it was besieged by [[e:conrad-ii-holy-roman-emperor|Emperor Conrad II]] during the revolt of Duke [[e:ernest-ii-duke-of-swabia|Ernest II of Swabia]]. Around 1080 it passed to the counts of Dillingen, whose branch took the name Kyburg in the 12th century.
county-of-kyburg.r: The [[e:house-of-kyburg|Kyburgs]] inherited part of the lands of the [[e:house-of-zahringen|Zähringen]] dukes in 1218, gaining [[e:burgdorf|Burgdorf]], [[e:thun|Thun]] and [[s:canton-of-fribourg|Fribourg]], which made them one of the largest landholders in the Swiss plateau. They founded towns such as [[e:winterthur|Winterthur]], [[e:diessenhofen|Diessenhofen]] and [[e:frauenfeld|Frauenfeld]] and governed through castles and stewards.
county-of-kyburg.e: Hartmann IV and his nephew Hartmann V died without male heirs in 1263 and 1264. [[e:rudolf-i-of-germany|Rudolf of Habsburg]], Hartmann IV's nephew, seized the inheritance, nearly doubling the [[s:county-of-habsburg|County of Habsburg]]'s lands. Kyburg castle later belonged to Zurich from 1424.

colony-of-barbados.t: England's richest early colony, where the sugar revolution and its slave society took shape, governed by Britain until independence in 1966.
colony-of-barbados.o: English settlers financed by the merchant [[e:william-courteen|William Courteen]] landed at [[e:holetown|Holetown]] in 1627 on the uninhabited island. Early colonists grew tobacco and [[e:cotton|cotton]] with indentured servants, and an elected [[e:house-of-assembly-of-barbados|House of Assembly]] was established in 1639, one of the oldest legislatures in the [[e:americas|Americas]].
colony-of-barbados.r: In the 1640s planters turned to [[e:sugar-plantation|sugar]], and [[s:barbados|Barbados]] became the model plantation colony, with enslaved Africans soon forming the large majority. The [[e:barbados-slave-code|Barbados Slave Code]] of 1661 influenced other English colonies. After Bussa's rebellion in 1816 and emancipation in 1834-38, a planter elite still dominated. The 1937 riots led to labour reforms under [[e:grantley-adams|Grantley Adams]].
colony-of-barbados.e: [[s:barbados|Barbados]] gained universal suffrage in 1951, joined the [[s:west-indies-federation|West Indies Federation]] in 1958-62 and became the independent state of Barbados on 30 November 1966 under [[e:errol-barrow|Errol Barrow]].

commonwealth-of-dominica.t: Mountainous, forested island republic between Guadeloupe and Martinique, independent since 1978 and home to the Kalinago Territory.
commonwealth-of-dominica.o: The [[s:colony-of-dominica|Colony of Dominica]] became independent on 3 November 1978 as a republic within the Commonwealth, with a president elected by parliament and [[e:patrick-john|Patrick John]] as prime minister.
commonwealth-of-dominica.r: [[e:hurricane-david|Hurricane David]] devastated the island in 1979, and John's government fell amid scandal. [[e:eugenia-charles|Eugenia Charles]] of the [[e:dominica-freedom-party|Dominica Freedom Party]], prime minister from 1980 to 1995, was the first woman to lead a [[e:caribbean|Caribbean]] government; she survived coup plots in 1981, one involving John and foreign [[e:mercenary|mercenaries]], and backed the US intervention in [[s:grenada|Grenada]] in 1983. Bananas were the main export until European preferences ended. The [[e:kalinago-territory|Kalinago Territory]] preserves the region's largest indigenous community.
commonwealth-of-dominica.e: [[e:roosevelt-skerrit|Roosevelt Skerrit]] has been prime minister since 2004. [[e:hurricane-maria|Hurricane Maria]] caused enormous damage in 2017, and Dominica, which funds much of its development through citizenship by investment, aims to become a climate-resilient nation.

county-of-alava.t: A Basque frontier county of the Kingdom of Asturias, defending the upper Ebro against the Banu Qasi before merging with Castile.
county-of-alava.o: Álava appears in the 9th-century Asturian chronicles as an eastern frontier district of the [[s:kingdom-of-asturias|Kingdom of Asturias]], facing Muslim raids up the [[e:ebro-river|Ebro]]. Counts are recorded from the 860s, among them [[e:vela-jimenez|Vela Jiménez]], who held the castle of Cellorigo against [[e:cordoba|Córdoba]] in 882 and 883.
county-of-alava.r: Its society was largely Basque-speaking and rural, organised in valleys and villages, with the counts acting as military governors for the kings of [[e:asturias|Asturias]] and León. The 1025 [[e:reja-de-san-millan|Reja de San Millán]], a list of Álava villages paying iron to the monastery of [[e:san-millan-de-la-cogolla|San Millán]], shows a dense pattern of settlements.
county-of-alava.e: [[e:fernan-gonzalez-of-castile|Fernán González]] brought Álava under his control in the 930s, linking it to the [[s:county-of-castile|County of Castile]]. In the 11th century it passed between [[s:kingdom-of-castile|Castile]] and [[e:kingdom-of-navarre|Navarre]], before being integrated permanently into [[e:kingdom-of-castile|Castile]] in 1200.

county-of-anjou.t: The Loire Valley county whose aggressive counts built the power base of the Plantagenets and later passed to a line of French royal princes.
county-of-anjou.o: Anjou emerged in the late 9th century, when the Frankish crown entrusted the region around [[e:angers|Angers]] to local [[e:magnates|magnates]] facing Breton and [[e:vikings|Viking]] raids. [[e:ingelger|Ingelger]] held authority there, and his son [[e:fulk-i-count-of-anjou|Fulk the Red]] was styled count by about 930, founding a dynasty that turned a frontier command into a hereditary principality.
county-of-anjou.r: The counts ruled from [[e:angers|Angers]] with a dense network of stone castles, many built by [[e:fulk-nerra|Fulk Nerra]] (987–1040), which let them push into [[e:touraine|Touraine]] and [[s:county-of-maine|Maine]]. Anjou was a wine and river-trade region with powerful abbeys. [[e:geoffrey-plantagenet-count-of-anjou|Geoffrey Plantagenet]] conquered [[s:duchy-of-normandy|Normandy]] in the 1140s, and his son [[e:henry-ii-of-england|Henry II]] joined Anjou to [[e:england|England]] and [[s:duchy-of-aquitaine|Aquitaine]] in the [[s:angevin-empire|Angevin Empire]].
county-of-anjou.e: [[e:philip-ii-of-france|Philip II of France]] seized Anjou in 1204. It was granted as an [[e:appanage|appanage]] to [[e:charles-i-of-anjou|Charles of Anjou]] in 1246, became a duchy in 1360 for Louis I, and its last great duke, [[e:rene-of-anjou|René of Anjou]], died in 1480. [[e:louis-xi|Louis XI]] then annexed it to the [[s:kingdom-of-france|Kingdom of France]].

cr.a: FDRMRZUSA. See also the sourced file for original author.

chi-tu.t: The 'Red Earth Kingdom' of Chinese sources, a Buddhist state on the Malay Peninsula visited by a Sui embassy in 607.
chi-tu.o: Chi Tu is known almost entirely from the [[e:sui-dynasty|Sui]] shu, which describes a mission sent by [[e:emperor-yang-of-sui|Emperor Yang of Sui]] in 607 under [[e:chang-jun|Chang Jun]]. The account calls it a branch of [[s:funan|Funan]] and places it on the [[e:malay-peninsula|Malay Peninsula]], probably in the region of [[s:kelantan-sultanate|Kelantan]], [[s:pattani-kingdom|Pattani]] or [[e:songkhla|Songkhla]], but its location has never been confirmed.
chi-tu.r: The Chinese envoys described a king of the Qutan (Gautama) family who lived in a palace with three-storeyed gates, and a court where [[e:buddhism|Buddhism]] and [[e:brahmins|Brahmin]] rites were practised. They were received with ceremony, gifts of food served on leaves and a gold-leaf letter. The kingdom traded local products along the peninsular coast.
chi-tu.e: After [[e:chang-jun|Chang Jun's]] visit and a return mission to [[e:china|China]] in 610, Chi Tu vanishes from the record. It was probably absorbed into the expanding [[e:srivijaya|Srivijaya]] network or neighbouring peninsular states such as [[s:langkasuka|Langkasuka]]. Its name survives mainly as an example of early Chinese ethnography of [[e:southeast-asia|Southeast Asia]].

caristii.t: A small people of Bizkaia and Álava between the Deba and Nervión rivers, whose Roman town Veleia lay on the road to Gaul.
caristii.o: The Caristii lived in the later [[e:iron-age|Iron Age]] between the [[e:deba-river|Deba]] and [[e:nervion|Nervión]] rivers, in modern [[s:lordship-of-biscay|Bizkaia]] and northern Álava, flanked by the [[s:autrigones|Autrigones]] and [[s:varduli|Varduli]]. Their language is unknown.
caristii.r: Their society of hillfort communities is little documented. Ptolemy names their towns as Suessatium, Tullica and [[e:iruna-veleia|Veleia]], the last of which grew into the Roman town of Iruña-Veleia.
caristii.e: They came under Roman control as the conquest of the north was completed in 19 BCE and were absorbed into [[s:hispania-tarraconensis|Hispania Tarraconensis]].

colony-of-nevis.t: English sugar colony on a small volcanic island in the Leewards, once among the richest in the Caribbean and birthplace of Alexander Hamilton.
colony-of-nevis.o: English settlers led by [[e:anthony-hilton|Anthony Hilton]] crossed from neighbouring [[s:colony-of-saint-christopher|Saint Kitts]] in 1628 and founded a settlement on the leeward coast of Nevis. Tobacco gave way to [[e:sugar-plantation|sugar]] from the mid-17th century, and the island grew quickly despite raids from the Spanish in 1629 and the French, who briefly captured it in 1706.
colony-of-nevis.r: A governor or lieutenant governor ruled with an elected assembly of planters and an appointed council. By the 18th century the island was a plantation economy worked by enslaved Africans, who formed the great majority of the population. [[e:charlestown-saint-kitts-and-nevis|Charlestown]] was a busy port, and the hot springs at the [[e:bath|Bath]] Hotel drew wealthy visitors. [[e:horatio-nelson|Horatio Nelson]] married the Nevisian widow [[e:frances-nelson-viscountess-nelson|Frances Nisbet]] here in 1787. The [[e:church-of-england|Church of England]] was the established church.
colony-of-nevis.e: [[e:sugar-plantation|Sugar]] declined after emancipation in 1834 and the collapse of prices. Nevis lost its separate assembly and in 1882 was joined with [[s:colony-of-saint-christopher|Saint Kitts]] and [[e:anguilla|Anguilla]] in the colony of [[s:saint-christopher-nevis-anguilla|Saint Christopher-Nevis-Anguilla]], the forerunner of today's [[s:saint-kitts-and-nevis|Saint Kitts and Nevis]].

colony-of-tasmania.t: Australia's island colony, notorious for its convict stations and the near-destruction of its Aboriginal people, before it joined the federation in 1901.
colony-of-tasmania.o: [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]] settled Van Diemen's Land in 1803 to forestall the French, and [[e:hobart|Hobart]] was founded in 1804. Administered at first from the [[s:colony-of-new-south-wales|Colony of New South Wales]], it became a separate colony in 1825, under Lieutenant Governor [[e:george-arthur|George Arthur]].
colony-of-tasmania.r: The island received around 75,000 convicts, held at stations such as [[e:port-arthur-tasmania|Port Arthur]] and [[e:macquarie-harbour|Macquarie Harbour]], and became a disciplined penal society that also exported wool and whale oil. During the [[e:black-war|Black War]] of the 1820s colonists and soldiers killed many [[e:aboriginal-tasmanians|Aboriginal Tasmanians]], and the survivors were removed to [[e:wybalenna|Wybalenna]] on [[e:flinders-island|Flinders Island]] in the 1830s. [[e:penal-transportation|Transportation]] ended in 1853, and in 1856 the colony won self-government and adopted the name Tasmania.
colony-of-tasmania.e: Tasmania stayed small, with mining at [[e:mount-bischoff|Mount Bischoff]] and [[e:mount-lyell|Mount Lyell]] later in the century. It voted for federation and became a state of the [[s:commonwealth-of-australia|Commonwealth of Australia]] in 1901. [[e:andrew-inglis-clark|Andrew Inglis Clark]], its attorney general, was a key drafter of the Australian Constitution.

cr.a: Unknown author (Proclaimed by Sir Frederick Weld)

county-of-loon.t: A Limburg county around Borgloon and Hasselt that remained independent for three centuries before being absorbed by the prince-bishops of Liège.
county-of-loon.o: Counts of [[e:borgloon|Loon]] appear around 1015, when Giselbert held lands around Borgloon in the [[e:hesbaye|Hesbaye]]. They expanded north into the [[e:campine|Kempen]] heathlands, and the county became one of the middle-ranking principalities of [[e:duchy-of-lower-lorraine|Lower Lorraine]].
county-of-loon.r: [[e:borgloon|Loon]] was largely rural, with small towns such as [[e:hasselt|Hasselt]] and Borgloon. From the late 12th century the counts were [[e:vassal|vassals]] of the prince-[[e:bishop|bishops]] of [[s:prince-bishopric-of-liege|Liège]]. The poet [[e:henric-van-veldeke|Henric van Veldeke]], a founder of literature in [[e:dutch|Dutch]] and German, came from the county and wrote for its court circles.
county-of-loon.e: After Count Louis IV died childless in 1336, his inheritance was disputed between his heirs and the [[e:bishop|bishops]] of [[s:prince-bishopric-of-liege|Liège]]. In 1366 the Prince-Bishopric of Liège annexed the county, and it remained part of the principality until 1795; it corresponds roughly to Belgian [[s:duchy-of-limburg|Limburg]].

coba.t: A large Maya city among lakes in north-eastern Yucatán, hub of the longest known Maya causeway network.
coba.o: Cobá developed around a group of lakes in the north-east of the [[e:yucatan-peninsula|Yucatán]] peninsula, whose water supported a large population. It became a major centre in the Classic period, from about 600 CE, with stelae showing southern Maya influence.
coba.r: More than 50 raised white causeways (sakbeob) radiate from Cobá. One runs about 100 kilometres west to [[e:yaxuna|Yaxuná]], perhaps to secure control of territory against rivals in the centre of the peninsula. The [[e:nohoch-mul|Nohoch Mul]] pyramid is among the tallest in northern [[e:yucatan-peninsula|Yucatán]]. Stelae depict rulers standing on captives, and some royal women are also recorded.
coba.e: Cobá lost power to [[s:chichen-itza|Chichen Itza]] in the 10th and 11th centuries and was largely abandoned by about 1100, though Postclassic shrines were later added. It is now a popular archaeological site in [[e:quintana-roo|Quintana Roo]].

confederation-of-shan-states.t: An alliance of Shan principalities led by Mohnyin that conquered Ava in 1527 and ruled Upper Burma until Bayinnaung's conquest.
confederation-of-shan-states.o: Shan saophas had raided the [[s:ava-kingdom|Ava Kingdom]] for decades. Under [[e:sawlon|Sawlon of Mohnyin]], a coalition of Shan states including [[s:mohnyin|Mohnyin]], [[s:mogaung|Mogaung]], [[e:bhamo|Bhamo]], [[s:momeik-state|Momeik]] and Kale attacked Ava and in 1527 captured it, killing King [[e:shwenankyawshin|Shwenankyawshin]]. Sawlon placed his son [[e:thohanbwa|Thohanbwa]] on the throne.
confederation-of-shan-states.r: The confederation ruled [[e:upper-burma|Upper Burma]] from Ava but remained a loose alliance of Shan rulers with their own interests. [[e:thohanbwa|Thohanbwa]] distrusted the Burmese Buddhist establishment and is remembered in the chronicles for killing monks and destroying pagodas, though this may be exaggerated. The confederation allied with the [[s:prome-kingdom|Prome Kingdom]] against the rising Toungoo.
confederation-of-shan-states.e: [[e:thohanbwa|Thohanbwa]] was assassinated in 1542, and Ava passed to other Shan and Burman nobles. Internal quarrels weakened the alliance, and in 1555 [[e:bayinnaung|Bayinnaung]] of the [[s:first-toungoo-empire|First Toungoo Empire]] captured Ava, then subdued the northern Shan states one by one.

chen-han.t: The Yangtze river empire of Chen Youliang, whose great fleet was destroyed by Zhu Yuanzhang at Lake Poyang in 1363, one of the largest naval battles in history.
chen-han.o: [[e:chen-youliang|Chen Youliang]], the son of a fisherman, rose as an officer in the southern [[e:red-turban-rebellion|Red Turban]] regime of [[e:xu-shouhui|Xu Shouhui]] on the middle [[e:yangtze-river|Yangtze]]. In 1360 he murdered Xu and proclaimed himself emperor of Han, ruling first from Jiangzhou and later from [[e:wuchang|Wuchang]].
chen-han.r: Chen Han controlled [[e:jiangxi|Jiangxi]] and [[e:huguang|Huguang]] and was at first the strongest of the rebel states against the [[s:yuan-dynasty|Yuan Dynasty]]. Its power rested on a large river fleet of towering warships. Chen ruled by force rather than by building institutions, and the murder of [[e:xu-shouhui|Xu Shouhui]] led commanders such as [[e:ming-yuzhen|Ming Yuzhen]] in [[e:sichuan|Sichuan]] to break away.
chen-han.e: An attack on [[e:nanjing|Nanjing]] failed in 1360. In 1363 Chen besieged [[e:nanchang|Nanchang]] and then met [[e:hongwu-emperor|Zhu Yuanzhang]] on [[e:lake-poyang|Lake Poyang]]; after weeks of fighting, including fire-ships, Chen was killed by an arrow. His son [[e:chen-li-chen-han|Chen Li]] surrendered [[e:wuchang|Wuchang]] in 1364, and his lands became part of the future [[s:ming-empire|Ming Empire]].

condo-confederation.t: A confederation of Mande, Gola and Vai peoples in north-western Liberia, built by the warrior-trader Sao Boso around the town of Bopolu.
condo-confederation.o: In the early 19th century [[e:sao-boso|Sao Boso]], a [[e:mandinka|Mandingo]] warrior and trader known to Europeans as King Boatswain, built a coalition around [[e:bopolu|Bopolu]] in the hinterland of what is now north-western [[s:liberia|Liberia]]. Linking [[e:gola-people|Gola]], Vai, Dei and other communities, the Condo Confederation aimed to keep the trade routes between the interior and the coast open and safe.
condo-confederation.r: [[e:bopolu|Bopolu]] was a market town where caravans exchanged slaves, [[e:cattle|cattle]], cloth and [[e:ivory-trade|ivory]] for salt and European goods from the coast at [[e:cape-mount|Cape Mount]] and [[e:monrovia|Monrovia]]. [[e:sao-boso|Sao Boso]] and his Muslim [[e:mandinka|Mandingo]] allies dominated the confederation, though its members kept their own chiefs. Its relations with the settlers of the [[s:colony-of-liberia|Colony of Liberia]] mixed trade with occasional conflict.
condo-confederation.e: After [[e:sao-boso|Sao Boso's]] death in 1836 the confederation was weakened by succession quarrels among its leaders and wars between member peoples. By the 1870s its lands came under the claims of [[s:liberia|Liberia]], which absorbed them into the republic's interior.

childir-eyalet.t: The Ottoman province of Akhaltsikhe in the south-west Caucasus, governed by Islamised Georgian pashas for two centuries.
childir-eyalet.o: After decades of [[e:ottoman-safavid-wars|Ottoman-Safavid wars]] over [[e:samtskhe|Samtskhe]], the [[e:ottoman-empire|Ottomans]] turned the [[s:principality-of-samtskhe|Principality of Samtskhe]] into a province in 1628. Its first governor was [[e:safar-pasha|Safar Pasha]], a member of the Georgian Jaqeli family who had converted to [[e:islam|Islam]], and the post remained largely hereditary in his house.
childir-eyalet.r: Governed from [[e:akhaltsikhe|Akhaltsikhe]], the eyalet included [[e:ardahan|Ardahan]], [[e:artvin|Artvin]] and the upper [[e:kura-river|Kura]] valleys. Much of the population, Georgian-speaking Meskhetians, gradually adopted [[e:islam|Islam]], while Armenian and Jewish merchants lived in the towns. Akhaltsikhe had a notorious slave market fed by raids into [[s:georgia|Georgia]]. Its pashas, often semi-independent, intervened in the politics of [[s:kingdom-of-kartli|Kartli]] and [[s:kingdom-of-imereti|Imereti]].
childir-eyalet.e: During the [[e:russo-turkish-war-1828-1829|Russo-Turkish War]] Russian forces under [[e:ivan-paskevich|Paskevich]] stormed [[e:akhaltsikhe|Akhaltsikhe]] in 1828, and the [[e:treaty-of-adrianople-1829|Treaty of Adrianople]] in 1829 gave the northern part to the [[s:russian-empire|Russian Empire]]. The remainder stayed Ottoman until 1878. Many [[e:meskhetian-turks|Meskhetian Turks]] descend from its Muslim population.
childir-eyalet.re: Sunni Islam; Georgian and Armenian Christianity

county-of-ortenburg.t: A tiny Bavarian county near Passau that survived as an imperial Protestant enclave surrounded by Catholic Bavaria until 1805.
county-of-ortenburg.o: The counts of Ortenburg descend from the [[e:house-of-sponheim|Spanheim]] family; around 1120 Count Rapoto I built Ortenburg castle in [[e:lower-bavaria|Lower Bavaria]] near [[e:vilshofen-an-der-donau|Vilshofen]]. His descendants briefly held the office of count palatine of [[e:bavaria|Bavaria]] in the 13th century before losing most of their lands to the [[e:house-of-wittelsbach|Wittelsbachs]].
county-of-ortenburg.r: The counts long disputed with [[e:bavaria|Bavaria]] whether Ortenburg was an imperial county or a Bavarian fief; the [[e:imperial-chamber-court|Imperial Chamber Court]] confirmed its imperial status in 1573. In 1563 Count Joachim introduced [[e:lutheranism|Lutheranism]], making Ortenburg a Protestant island surrounded by Catholic Bavaria. Its castle is noted for a [[e:renaissance|Renaissance]] wooden ceiling.
county-of-ortenburg.e: In 1805 the count exchanged Ortenburg with [[e:bavaria|Bavaria]] for the territory of Tambach in [[e:franconia|Franconia]], and Ortenburg became part of the [[s:kingdom-of-bavaria|Kingdom of Bavaria]]. The count's family still owns Tambach.

cumae.t: The oldest Greek colony on the Italian mainland, home of the Sibyl, which passed the Greek alphabet to the Etruscans and Latins.
cumae.o: Euboean [[e:greeks|Greeks]] from [[s:chalcis|Chalcis]] and [[s:eretria|Eretria]] founded Cumae around 740 BCE on the Campanian coast north of the [[e:bay-of-naples|Bay of Naples]], having first settled the island of [[e:pithekoussai|Pithekoussai]] ([[e:ischia|Ischia]]). The site, a steep acropolis above the sea, controlled the fertile [[e:campi-flegrei|Phlegraean Fields]] and gave access to Etruscan and native trade.
cumae.r: Cumae was an aristocratic city that became a major power in the Tyrrhenian world. Its version of the Greek alphabet was adopted by the [[e:etruscans|Etruscans]] and, through them, by [[e:rome|Rome]]. The cave of the [[e:cumaean-sibyl|Sibyl]] and the temple of [[e:apollo|Apollo]] made it a famous oracle. The tyrant [[e:aristodemus-of-cumae|Aristodemus]] defeated the Etruscans at [[e:aricia|Aricia]] around 504 BCE, and in 474 BCE Cumae and [[e:hiero-i-of-syracuse|Hieron I of Syracuse]] destroyed an Etruscan fleet off the city. Cumae also founded [[s:neapolis|Neapolis]].
cumae.e: Around 421 BCE Samnite-speaking Campanians captured Cumae, and it became an [[e:oscan-language|Oscan]] town. It received Roman citizenship without the vote in 338 BCE, later became a Roman municipium and declined as nearby [[e:pozzuoli|Puteoli]] grew. A Byzantine fortress in the 6th century CE, it was finally destroyed by [[e:naples|Naples]] in 1207.

cornovii.t: Iron Age people of the West Midlands and Welsh borders, centred on the Wrekin, whose Roman town of Viroconium became one of the largest in Britain.
cornovii.o: The Cornovii occupied [[e:shropshire|Shropshire]], [[e:cheshire|Cheshire]] and parts of [[e:staffordshire|Staffordshire]] and the Welsh borderland in the late [[e:iron-age|Iron Age]]. Their landscape was dominated by hillforts such as the [[e:the-wrekin|Wrekin]], [[e:titterstone-clee-hill|Titterstone Clee]] and the [[e:breiddin|Breiddin]], many of which had been occupied for centuries before the Roman period.
cornovii.r: They issued no coins and used very little pottery, so their society is known mainly from hillforts and farmsteads. Livestock farming was central, and the brine springs of [[e:cheshire|Cheshire]] supplied salt that was traded in distinctive clay containers. No rulers are named in any source, suggesting power was held by local chiefs.
cornovii.e: The Roman army advanced into the region in the 50s, and around 55 to 60 a [[e:legion|legionary]] fortress was built at [[e:viroconium-cornoviorum|Wroxeter]] below the [[e:the-wrekin|Wrekin]], which seems to have been abandoned. When the army left, the site became Viroconium Cornoviorum, capital of their civitas in [[s:roman-britain|Roman Britain]] and later the seat of post-Roman rulers in what became the [[s:kingdom-of-powys|Kingdom of Powys]].

county-of-perche.t: A hilly county between Normandy and Maine whose crusading counts fought in Spain and the Holy Land before it lapsed to the French crown.
county-of-perche.o: The lords of [[e:mortagne-au-perche|Mortagne]] and [[e:nogent-le-rotrou|Nogent]] gathered the forested hill country of the Perche in the 11th century, and around 1079 Geoffrey II was styled count of Perche. The county lay on the frontier between [[s:duchy-of-normandy|Normandy]], [[s:county-of-maine|Maine]] and the royal domain, and its counts balanced between the Anglo-Norman kings and the [[e:capetian-dynasty|Capetians]].
county-of-perche.r: Perche was a land of forests, iron and [[e:horse-breeding|horse breeding]], later famous for the [[e:percheron|Percheron]]. Count [[e:rotrou-iii-count-of-perche|Rotrou III]] fought in the [[e:first-crusade|First Crusade]] and in Aragon's wars against the [[e:almoravid-empire|Almoravids]], and married a daughter of Henry I of [[e:england|England]]. Count Thomas was killed fighting for the French prince Louis at [[e:lincoln-england|Lincoln]] in 1217.
county-of-perche.e: The last count, William, [[e:bishop|bishop]] of [[e:chalons-en-champagne|Châlons]], died in 1226, and [[e:louis-viii-of-france|Louis VIII]] and [[e:louis-ix-of-france|Louis IX]] absorbed the county into the royal domain of the [[s:kingdom-of-france|Kingdom of France]]. It was later granted as an [[e:appanage|appanage]] to royal princes.

county-of-holland.t: The coastal county that grew from Frisian marshland into the richest province of the Low Countries and the core of the later Dutch Republic.
county-of-holland.o: The dynasty began with Gerulf, a Frisian lord granted lands by the [[e:carolingian-empire|Carolingians]] in the 880s, and [[e:dirk-i-count-of-holland|Dirk I]], who received the land around Egmond in 922. The counts were first known as counts of [[e:west-frisia|West Frisia]], and the name Holland ('wood land') came into use around 1100.
county-of-holland.r: The counts drained peat bogs, built dykes and founded towns such as [[e:haarlem|Haarlem]], [[e:delft|Delft]], [[e:leiden|Leiden]] and [[e:dordrecht|Dordrecht]]. [[e:dirk-iii-count-of-holland|Dirk III]] defeated an imperial army at [[e:battle-of-vlaardingen|Vlaardingen]] in 1018; [[e:william-ii-of-holland|William II]] was elected King of the [[e:roman-empire|Romans]] in 1247 and began the [[e:binnenhof|Binnenhof]] at [[e:the-hague|The Hague]]. Under [[e:floris-v-count-of-holland|Floris V]] the towns, fishing and cloth trade grew rapidly, and water boards became a hallmark of local government.
county-of-holland.e: Holland passed to the [[e:house-of-avesnes|Avesnes]] counts of [[s:county-of-hainaut|Hainaut]] in 1299, the [[e:house-of-wittelsbach|Wittelsbachs]] in 1345 and the [[s:burgundian-state|Burgundian State]] in 1433, amid the [[e:hook-and-cod-wars|Hook and Cod wars]]. Under the [[s:habsburg-netherlands|Habsburg Netherlands]] it led the revolt against [[e:spain|Spain]], and after the [[e:act-of-abjuration|Act of Abjuration]] of 1581 it became the dominant province of the [[s:dutch-republic|Dutch Republic]].

chahamanas-of-naddula.t: A Chauhan branch of Marwar ruling from Nadol, offshoot of the Ajmer dynasty and forerunner of the Chauhans of Jalor.
chahamanas-of-naddula.o: Around 950 Lakshmana, a younger member of the [[s:chahamanas-of-shakambhari|Chahamanas of Shakambhari]], carved out a kingdom at [[e:nadol|Naddula]], modern Nadol in the Pali district of [[e:rajasthan|Rajasthan]]. Inscriptions and later bardic tradition, where he appears as Rao Lakhan, record the founding.
chahamanas-of-naddula.r: The [[e:nadol|Naddula]] [[e:chauhan|Chahamanas]] held the southern [[s:jodhpur-state|Marwar]] plains and the routes between [[e:gujarat|Gujarat]] and the north. They fought the [[s:paramara-dynasty|Paramara dynasty]] and the [[s:chaulukya-dynasty|Chaulukya dynasty]], and from the 12th century often served the [[e:chaulukya-dynasty|Chaulukyas]] as feudatories; [[e:alhana|Alhana]] and his son [[e:kelhana|Kelhana]] fought in Chaulukya campaigns. The kings and their nobles supported both Shaiva and Jain temples, and Nadol has many Jain shrines.
chahamanas-of-naddula.e: [[e:qutb-ud-din-aibak|Qutb al-Din Aibak]] attacked [[e:nadol|Nadol]] in 1197, ending the main line. A branch founded by [[e:kirtipala|Kirtipala]], son of [[e:alhana|Alhana]], moved to [[e:jalore|Jalor]], where the [[s:chahamanas-of-jalor|Songara Chauhans]] ruled until [[e:alauddin-khalji|Alauddin Khalji]] took the fort in 1311.

chahamanas-of-jalor.t: A Chauhan Rajput dynasty of Jalor in Marwar, famous for its last stand against the armies of Alauddin Khalji.
chahamanas-of-jalor.o: The [[e:jalore|Jalor]] branch of the [[e:chauhan|Chahamanas]] (Chauhans) descended from the [[s:chahamanas-of-naddula|Chahamanas of Naddula]]. [[e:kirtipala|Kirtipala]], a son of the [[e:nadol|Naddula]] king [[e:alhana|Alhana]], captured the hill fort of Jalor from the Paramaras around 1160 and founded a separate line, known as the Songara Chauhans after the fort's Sonagiri hill.
chahamanas-of-jalor.r: The kings held a strong fort controlling routes between [[e:gujarat|Gujarat]] and the Indo-Gangetic plain, and acted at times as allies or [[e:vassal|vassals]] of the [[e:chaulukya-dynasty|Chaulukyas of Gujarat]] and later the [[s:delhi-sultanate|Delhi Sultanate]]. [[e:udayasimha-of-jalor|Udayasimha]] extended the kingdom and repelled [[e:iltutmish|Iltutmish]]. Jain temples and inscriptions at [[e:jalore|Jalor]] record the patronage of merchants and rulers alike.
chahamanas-of-jalor.e: [[e:kanhadadeva|Kanhadadeva]] resisted [[e:alauddin-khalji|Alauddin Khalji]], who took [[e:siwana|Siwana]] and then besieged [[e:jalore|Jalor]], capturing it in 1311; the king and his son Viramadeva were killed. The story became the subject of the 15th-century epic [[e:kanhadade-prabandha|Kanhadade Prabandha]]. Jalor passed to the [[s:delhi-sultanate|Delhi Sultanate]].

cuzcatlan.t: The kingdom of the Nahua-speaking Pipil in western and central El Salvador, which resisted Spanish conquest from 1524 to 1528.
cuzcatlan.o: The [[e:pipil|Pipil]] descended from Nahua-speaking migrants from central [[s:mexico|Mexico]] who reached the Pacific lowlands of [[e:central-america|Central America]] in waves between about 900 and 1200. They settled what is now [[s:republic-of-el-salvador|El Salvador]] and founded a number of lordships, with Cuzcatlan, near modern [[e:antiguo-cuscatlan|Antiguo Cuscatlán]], the most powerful.
cuzcatlan.r: Cuzcatlan was ruled by a lord and nobles, with priests and warriors at the top of society. Its rich volcanic soils produced [[e:cacao|cacao]], the most valuable trade crop in the region, along with [[e:maize|maize]], [[e:cotton|cotton]] and balsam, traded widely across [[e:mesoamerica|Mesoamerica]]. [[e:pipil|Pipil]] religion and calendar resembled those of central [[s:mexico|Mexico]].
cuzcatlan.e: In 1524 [[e:pedro-de-alvarado|Pedro de Alvarado]] invaded and fought the [[e:pipil|Pipil]] at [[e:acajutla|Acajutla]] and Tacuzcalco, but they resisted for years; [[e:san-salvador|San Salvador]], first founded in 1525, was re-established in 1528. The territory became part of the [[s:captaincy-general-of-guatemala|Captaincy General of Guatemala]].

caereni.t: People of the far north-west of Scotland, named only by Ptolemy, living on the Atlantic coast of Sutherland.
caereni.o: The Caereni appear in [[e:geography-ptolemy|Ptolemy's Geography]] of about 150 on the north-western mainland of [[e:scotland|Scotland]], north of the [[s:carnonacae|Carnonacae]], usually located in western [[e:sutherland|Sutherland]] around [[e:assynt|Assynt]] and Kinlochbervie. Their name has been interpreted as meaning 'sheep folk', though this is uncertain.
caereni.r: Nothing is recorded of their rulers or institutions. The Atlantic coast of [[e:sutherland|Sutherland]] was a thinly peopled land of rock, bog and sea lochs, and its inhabitants lived in roundhouses and brochs, herding livestock, fishing and farming small patches of better land.
caereni.e: The Caereni are not mentioned again. Their region later formed part of the lands of the [[e:picts|Picts]] and from the 9th century came under the control of Norse settlers and the earls of [[e:orkney|Orkney]].

captaincy-of-minas-gerais.t: The gold and diamond region of colonial Brazil, whose wealth funded Portugal's 18th century and whose baroque towns are among the finest in the Americas.
captaincy-of-minas-gerais.o: Gold was discovered in the highlands of [[e:minas-gerais|Minas Gerais]] in the 1690s, starting the largest gold rush in the colonial [[e:americas|Americas]]. After a tax revolt at [[e:ouro-preto|Vila Rica]] in 1720 led by [[e:filipe-dos-santos|Filipe dos Santos]], the crown separated the mining region from the [[s:captaincy-of-sao-paulo|Captaincy of São Paulo]] as its own captaincy, with Vila Rica, now Ouro Preto, as capital.
captaincy-of-minas-gerais.r: The crown taxed gold through the royal fifth and strictly controlled the region. Diamonds were found around [[e:diamantina|Tijuco]], now Diamantina, in the 1720s and became a royal monopoly. Hundreds of thousands of enslaved Africans worked the mines. Wealthy brotherhoods built baroque churches decorated by the sculptor [[e:aleijadinho|Aleijadinho]]. As gold declined, a conspiracy, the [[e:inconfidencia-mineira|Inconfidência Mineira]], plotted independence in 1789; its leader [[e:tiradentes|Tiradentes]] was hanged in 1792.
captaincy-of-minas-gerais.e: After the gold ran low, [[e:minas-gerais|Minas]] turned to farming and [[e:cattle|cattle]]. In 1821 it became a province of [[s:new-republic-brazil|Brazil]], and later one of its most populous states. [[e:ouro-preto|Ouro Preto]] became a [[e:unesco-world-heritage-site|UNESCO World Heritage Site]] in 1980.

colony-of-rhode-island-and-providence-pl.t: The New England colony founded by Roger Williams on the principle of religious liberty, the first to separate church and state in law.
colony-of-rhode-island-and-providence-pl.o: Banished from the [[s:massachusetts-bay-colony|Massachusetts Bay Colony]], [[e:roger-williams|Roger Williams]] founded [[e:providence-rhode-island|Providence]] in 1636 on land obtained from the [[e:narragansett-people|Narragansett]]. [[e:anne-hutchinson|Anne Hutchinson's]] followers founded [[e:portsmouth-rhode-island|Portsmouth]] in 1638, a group split off to found [[e:newport-rhode-island|Newport]] in 1639, and [[e:samuel-gorton|Samuel Gorton]] founded [[e:warwick-rhode-island|Warwick]] in 1642. Williams won a parliamentary patent uniting the towns in 1644.
colony-of-rhode-island-and-providence-pl.r: The royal charter of 1663, obtained by [[e:john-clarke-baptist-minister|John Clarke]], guaranteed full liberty in religious concerns, and the colony became a home for [[e:baptists|Baptists]], [[e:quakers|Quakers]] and [[e:jews|Jews]], whose [[e:touro-synagogue|Touro Synagogue]] at [[e:newport-rhode-island|Newport]] opened in 1763. [[s:rhode|Rhode]] Islanders elected their own governors and assembly. Newport grew rich on [[e:atlantic-slave-trade|Atlantic trade]], including a large share of the colonial slave trade, while farms in [[e:narragansett-people|Narragansett]] Country used enslaved labour.
colony-of-rhode-island-and-providence-pl.e: [[s:rhode|Rhode]] Islanders burned the British customs ship [[e:gaspee-affair|Gaspee]] in 1772, and on 4 May 1776 the colony became the first to renounce allegiance to the Crown. It joined the [[s:united-states|United States]], and its 1663 charter served as the state constitution until 1843.

crown-colony-of-north-borneo.t: British colony formed from the war-ravaged territory of the North Borneo Company, which became the Malaysian state of Sabah.
crown-colony-of-north-borneo.o: The [[e:british-north-borneo-company|British North Borneo Company]], unable to finance rebuilding after the [[s:japanese-occupation-of-british-borneo|Japanese occupation of British Borneo]], transferred [[s:north-borneo|North Borneo]] to the crown on 15 July 1946. [[s:crown-colony-of-labuan|Labuan]] was added to the new colony. Because [[e:sandakan|Sandakan]] had been destroyed, the capital moved to [[e:kota-kinabalu|Jesselton]], today Kota Kinabalu.
crown-colony-of-north-borneo.r: A British governor ruled with advisory and legislative councils. The colonial government rebuilt towns and ports and expanded [[e:timber|timber]], [[e:rubber|rubber]] and copra exports, while education and health services grew slowly. Local political leaders emerged in the early 1960s, among them [[e:fuad-stephens|Donald Stephens]] of the Kadazan community and [[e:mustapha-harun|Mustapha Harun]].
crown-colony-of-north-borneo.e: [[s:north-borneo|North Borneo]] became self-governing in August 1963 and joined [[s:malaysia|Malaysia]] on 16 September 1963 as the state of [[e:sabah|Sabah]], despite a Philippine claim based on the old rights of the [[s:sulu-sultanate|Sulu Sultanate]], a dispute that persists.
