consoranni.t: Pyrenean people of the upper Salat valley who gave their name to the Couserans district of the Ariège.
consoranni.o: Known from [[e:pliny-the-elder|Pliny]] and later Roman sources, the Consoranni lived in the central [[e:pyrenees|Pyrenees]] in the modern [[e:ariege-department|Ariège]], between the [[s:convenae|Convenae]] and the [[s:volcae-tectosages|Volcae Tectosages]]. Little else is recorded of them before the Roman conquest.
consoranni.r: No rulers or institutions are known.
consoranni.e: Their land came under Roman control during the conquest of [[e:gallia-aquitania|Aquitania]]. Their chief town, [[e:saint-lizier|Lugdunum Consoranorum]], later took the name of a [[e:bishop|bishop]], Saint-Lizier, and the region kept the name [[e:couserans|Couserans]].

chandela-dynasty.t: The Rajput dynasty of Bundelkhand that built the temples of Khajuraho, famous for their carved sculpture.
chandela-dynasty.o: [[e:nannuka|Nannuka]] founded the Chandela line around 831 as a feudatory of the [[s:gurjara-pratihara|Gurjara-Pratihara]] in [[e:jejakabhukti|Jejakabhukti]], modern [[e:bundelkhand|Bundelkhand]]. [[e:yashovarman-chandela|Yashovarman]] made the dynasty a regional power in the mid-10th century, capturing the fortress of [[e:kalinjar-fort|Kalinjar]], and his son [[e:dhanga|Dhanga]] became fully independent.
chandela-dynasty.r: The Chandelas built some 85 temples at [[e:khajuraho|Khajuraho]] between about 950 and 1050, of which about 25 survive, among them the [[e:lakshmana-temple-khajuraho|Lakshmana temple]] of [[e:yashovarman-chandela|Yashovarman]] and the [[e:kandariya-mahadeva-temple|Kandariya Mahadeva]]. They were [[e:hinduism|Hindu]] but also supported Jain temples. Their kingdom was held by great [[e:hill-fort|hill forts]] at [[e:kalinjar-fort|Kalinjar]], [[e:ajaigarh|Ajaygarh]] and [[e:mahoba|Mahoba]] and watered by large artificial lakes. [[e:vidyadhara-chandela-dynasty|Vidyadhara]] resisted [[e:mahmud-of-ghazni|Mahmud of Ghazni]] in the early 11th century.
chandela-dynasty.e: [[e:prithviraj-chauhan|Prithviraja III]] of the [[s:chahamanas-of-shakambhari|Chahamanas of Shakambhari]] defeated [[e:paramardi|Paramardi]] in 1182, and in 1203 [[e:qutb-ud-din-aibak|Qutb al-Din Aibak]] took [[e:kalinjar-fort|Kalinjar]]. The Chandelas survived as a local power until about 1315.

ceh-pech.t: A Maya province of north-western Yucatán ruled by the Pech lineage from Motul, an early ally of the Spanish conquerors.
ceh-pech.o: Ceh Pech emerged after the collapse of the [[s:league-of-mayapan|League of Mayapan]] around 1441, under the Pech lineage, which had been prominent at Mayapan. Its territory lay along the northern coast between [[s:chakan|Chakan]] and [[s:ah-kin-chel|Ah Kin Chel]], with its capital at Motul.
ceh-pech.r: The province was ruled by lords of the Pech lineage over towns such as Conkal, Chicxulub and Motul. Coastal salt production and [[e:maize|maize]] farming supported it. The Pech chose to ally with [[e:francisco-de-montejo-the-younger|Francisco de Montejo the Younger]] in 1541, and one of its nobles, Nakuk Pech, later wrote the [[e:chronicle-of-chicxulub|Chronicle of Chicxulub]], a Maya account of the conquest.
ceh-pech.e: In return for their alliance, Pech nobles kept privileges under Spanish rule, and the province was absorbed into the [[s:province-of-yucatan|Province of Yucatán]]. Motul became a Franciscan centre.

corcu-loigde.t: Kingdom of the Érainn in south-west Cork, ancestral to the O'Driscolls, which tradition remembers as rulers of Munster before the Eóganachta.
corcu-loigde.o: The Corcu Loigde were a people of the [[s:iverni|Érainn]], the old population group of [[s:kingdom-of-munster|Munster]] linked with the [[e:iverni|Iverni]] of Ptolemy. In Irish tradition they held the kingship of Munster before the rise of the [[e:eoganacht-chaisil|Eóganachta of Cashel]] around the 5th century, and afterwards kept a respected place as a free subject kingdom in south-west [[e:county-cork|Cork]].
corcu-loigde.r: Their kingdom covered the coast and hinterland from around [[e:clonakilty|Clonakilty]] to [[e:baltimore-county-cork|Baltimore]] and inland toward [[e:skibbereen|Skibbereen]]. St [[e:ciaran-of-saighir|Ciarán of Saigir]], among the earliest Irish saints, was claimed as one of their kin, and a genealogical text on the Corcu Loigde preserves their lineages. The ruling family became known as [[e:odriscoll|Ó hEidirsceoil]], later O'Driscoll, with power based on [[e:cattle|cattle]], farmland and the sea.
corcu-loigde.e: From the 12th century the [[e:charles-maccarthy|MacCarthys]] of Desmond and then the [[e:anglo-normans|Anglo-Normans]] pushed the Corcu Loigde to the coast. The [[e:odriscoll|O'Driscolls]] survived as lords of Collymore around [[e:baltimore-county-cork|Baltimore]] and its islands until the early 17th century.

county-of-forez.t: A county of the upper Loire, ruled from Montbrison, that separated from Lyon in 1173 and passed to the dukes of Bourbon.
county-of-forez.o: In the 10th and 11th centuries a single family held the counties of [[e:lyon|Lyon]] and Forez, contesting control of Lyon with its archbishops. The register dates the county from around 1000. By the 1173 agreement known as the Permutatio, Count Guy II gave up his rights in Lyon to the archbishop and kept Forez.
county-of-forez.r: The counts ruled from [[e:montbrison|Montbrison]] over a land of plains and hills on the upper [[e:loire|Loire]], founding towns and abbeys. They cultivated close ties with the French crown and with the lords of [[e:beaujeu|Beaujeu]]. The county's customs and archives are unusually well preserved, including the 15th-century Armorial of Forez.
county-of-forez.e: In 1371 the heiress [[e:anne-of-forez|Anne of Forez]] married [[e:louis-ii-duke-of-bourbon|Louis II, Duke of Bourbon]], and the county joined the [[s:duchy-of-bourbon|Duchy of Bourbon]]. After [[e:francis-i|Francis I]] confiscated the lands of [[e:charles-iii-duke-of-bourbon|Constable Charles of Bourbon]], Forez was united with the [[s:kingdom-of-france|Kingdom of France]] in 1531.

caere.t: Coastal Etruscan city, now Cerveteri, famed for its vast tomb-city of the Banditaccia and its ports open to Greek and Phoenician traders.
caere.o: Caere, Etruscan Caisra, Greek Agylla, rose on a tufa plateau near the Tyrrhenian coast north-west of [[e:rome|Rome]]. Villanovan villages united into a city during the 8th century BCE, and by the 7th century the princely [[e:regolini-galassi-tomb|Regolini-Galassi tomb]] shows great wealth from metals and long-distance trade.
caere.r: Caere looked to the sea through its ports, [[e:pyrgi|Pyrgi]], [[e:alsium|Alsium]] and Punicum. At Pyrgi the gold tablets of about 500 BCE, written in Etruscan and Phoenician, record king [[e:thefarie-velianas|Thefarie Velianas]] dedicating a shrine to the goddess Uni-[[e:astarte|Astarte]]. Caere joined [[e:carthage|Carthage]] against the [[e:phocaeans|Phocaean Greeks]] at [[e:alalia|Alalia]] around 540 BCE, kept a treasury at [[s:delphi|Delphi]] and produced painted Caeretan hydriae and the famous [[e:sarcophagus-of-the-spouses|Sarcophagus of the Spouses]].
caere.e: Caere was long on friendly terms with [[e:rome|Rome]], sheltering Roman sacred objects during the Gallic sack of 390 BCE and receiving a form of citizenship without the vote. After a brief revolt it lost half its territory in 273 BCE and became a Roman town. Its necropolises are a [[e:unesco-world-heritage-site|UNESCO World Heritage Site]].

caeroesi.t: One of the Germani Cisrhenani of the Ardennes and Eifel, who joined the Belgic coalition against Caesar in 57 BCE.
caeroesi.o: Caesar names the Caeroesi with the [[s:condrusi|Condrusi]], [[s:eburones|Eburones]] and [[s:paemani|Paemani]] as peoples called Germani living west of the [[e:rhine|Rhine]]. They are usually placed in the [[e:eifel|Eifel]], between the [[s:treveri|Treveri]] and the Eburones.
caeroesi.r: Nothing is known of their rulers or settlements.
caeroesi.e: In 57 BCE they promised, together with the other [[e:germani-cisrhenani|Germani Cisrhenani]], some forty thousand warriors to the Belgic league against Caesar. After the conquest they vanish from the record, their land probably absorbed by the [[s:treveri|Treveri]] or the [[s:tungri|Tungri]].

county-of-toggenburg.t: East Swiss county of the upper Thur valley whose last count's death in 1436 set off the Old Zürich War between Swiss confederates.
county-of-toggenburg.o: The lords of Toggenburg appear in the 11th century and are documented as counts by the early 13th century, holding the upper [[e:thur|Thur]] valley from castles near [[e:lichtensteig|Lichtensteig]]. Through marriage and purchase they gained wide lands in the eastern [[e:alps|Alps]], including the [[e:prattigau|Prättigau]] and [[e:davos|Davos]].
county-of-toggenburg.r: The counts ruled a valley of farmers and herders and fought frequently with the [[s:imperial-abbey-of-saint-gall|Imperial Abbey of Saint Gall]] and with [[s:county-of-habsburg|Habsburg]] [[e:austria|Austria]]. Count [[e:frederick-vii-count-of-toggenburg|Frederick VII]] became one of the most powerful lords in the region, allying with both [[s:canton-of-zurich|Zürich]] and [[s:canton-of-schwyz|Schwyz]]. Communities in his Rhaetian lands formed the [[s:league-of-the-ten-jurisdictions|League of the Ten Jurisdictions]] after his death in 1436.
county-of-toggenburg.e: [[e:frederick-vii-count-of-toggenburg|Frederick VII]] died childless in 1436, and the rival claims of [[s:canton-of-zurich|Zürich]] and [[s:canton-of-schwyz|Schwyz]] to his lands caused the [[e:old-zurich-war|Old Zürich War]] of 1440 to 1446. The core county passed to the barons of [[e:raron|Raron]], who sold it to the [[s:imperial-abbey-of-saint-gall|Imperial Abbey of Saint Gall]] in 1468.

cao-wei.t: The strongest of the Three Kingdoms, founded on Cao Cao's conquest of the north, which ended the Han in 220 and was itself taken over by the Sima family.
cao-wei.o: [[e:cao-cao|Cao Cao]], holding the last Han emperor, [[e:emperor-xian-of-han|Emperor Xian]], in his power, reunified northern [[e:china|China]] after defeating [[e:yuan-shao|Yuan Shao]] at [[e:battle-of-guandu|Guandu]] in 200, and became King of Wei in 216. After his death in early 220 his son [[e:cao-pi|Cao Pi]] forced Emperor Xian to abdicate and proclaimed the Wei dynasty, with its capital at [[e:luoyang|Luoyang]].
cao-wei.r: Wei controlled the populous north. Military agricultural colonies, the tuntian, fed its armies, and the [[e:nine-rank-system|Nine-Rank system]] for recommending officials entrenched great families. The court of the Cao family fostered the [[e:jian-an-poetry|Jian'an]] poets. Wei fought [[s:shu-han|Shu Han]] and [[s:eastern-wu|Eastern Wu]], absorbed [[s:gongsun-yan|Gongsun Yan]] in 238 and received envoys from Queen [[e:himiko|Himiko]] of the Wa in [[e:japan|Japan]].
cao-wei.e: In 249 [[e:sima-yi|Sima Yi]] seized power in the [[e:incident-at-the-gaoping-tombs|Gaoping Tombs incident]], and the Sima family ruled through puppet emperors. Wei conquered [[s:shu-han|Shu Han]] in 263, and in 266 [[e:emperor-wu-of-jin|Sima Yan]] forced [[e:cao-huan|Cao Huan]] to abdicate, founding the [[s:western-jin|Western Jin]].

commune-of-piacenza.t: A Po crossing city-republic whose merchants and bankers traded across Europe and whose Gothic town hall still dominates its main square.
commune-of-piacenza.o: Piacenza, an old Roman colony where the [[e:via-aemilia|Via Emilia]] meets the Po, had consuls by 1126. Its citizens took over the [[e:bishop|bishop]]'s powers and controlled the river crossings and the road to [[s:republic-of-genoa|Genoa]].
commune-of-piacenza.r: Governed by consuls and later a podestà, Piacenza joined the [[s:lombard-league|Lombard League]], and the preliminary talks for the [[e:peace-of-constance|Peace of Constance]] were held there in 1183. Its merchants and money-changers were active at the [[s:county-of-champagne|Champagne]] fairs and in papal finance. The [[e:palazzo-gotico|Palazzo Gotico]], the town hall, was begun in 1281. Ghibelline lords such as [[e:uberto-pallavicino|Uberto Pallavicino]] and later [[e:alberto-scotti|Alberto Scotti]] held power in the 13th century.
commune-of-piacenza.e: Rival families repeatedly invited outside lords, and in 1336 [[e:azzone-visconti|Azzone Visconti]] took the city into the [[s:lordship-of-milan|Lordship of Milan]]. Piacenza later became part of the [[s:duchy-of-parma-and-piacenza|Duchy of Parma and Piacenza]].

county-of-tusculum.t: Lordship of the Counts of Tusculum, a Roman noble family who controlled the papacy in the early 11th century and fought the commune of Rome.
county-of-tusculum.o: The counts of [[s:tusculum|Tusculum]] descended from the [[e:theophylacti|Theophylacti]], the family that dominated [[e:rome|Rome]] in the 10th century. Around 999 Gregory I of Tusculum held the fortified hill town of Tusculum in the [[e:alban-hills|Alban Hills]], and from there his family built a lordship over the countryside south-east of Rome.
county-of-tusculum.r: The Tusculani controlled papal elections for decades: Gregory's sons became Popes [[e:pope-benedict-viii|Benedict VIII]] (1012–1024) and [[e:pope-john-xix|John XIX]] (1024–1032), and his grandson [[e:pope-benedict-ix|Benedict IX]] was pope three times before being removed. Their power declined after the reform [[e:papacy|papacy]] and the Roman commune emerged, but in 1167 Tusculan troops and imperial forces routed a Roman army at [[e:battle-of-monte-porzio|Monte Porzio]].
county-of-tusculum.e: Squeezed between [[e:rome|Rome]] and the [[e:papacy|papacy]], the counts placed [[s:tusculum|Tusculum]] under papal and imperial protection in the 12th century. In 1191 the [[e:roman-empire|Romans]], with [[e:henry-vi-holy-roman-emperor|Emperor Henry VI]]'s consent, destroyed the town. Survivors are said to have founded nearby [[e:frascati|Frascati]].

cheng-han.t: A refugee-founded kingdom in Sichuan, one of the first states established in the collapse of the Western Jin, noted for its light taxes and Daoist influence.
cheng-han.o: Li Te led Ba and Di refugees from famine in [[e:gansu|Gansu]] into [[e:sichuan|Sichuan]] around 298 and rebelled against Jin officials. After his death his son [[e:li-xiong|Li Xiong]] took [[e:chengdu|Chengdu]] in 304, styling himself King of Chengdu, and in 306 proclaimed himself emperor of Cheng.
cheng-han.r: [[e:li-xiong|Li Xiong]] governed leniently, with simple laws and low taxes, and appointed the [[e:taoism|Daoist]] master [[e:fan-changsheng|Fan Changsheng]] as chancellor, reflecting the strong presence of the [[e:way-of-the-five-pecks-of-rice|Celestial Masters]] tradition among his followers. Later rulers were less able: [[e:li-shou|Li Shou]] seized the throne in 338, renamed the state Han and built extravagant palaces.
cheng-han.e: In 347 the [[s:eastern-jin|Eastern Jin]] general [[e:huan-wen|Huan Wen]] marched up the [[e:yangtze-river|Yangtze]], captured [[e:chengdu|Chengdu]] and accepted the surrender of [[e:li-shi-cheng-han|Li Shi]], restoring [[e:sichuan|Sichuan]] to Chinese dynastic rule.

ce.t: A Pictish province named in the legend of the seven sons of Cruithne, probably in Mar and Buchan in north-east Scotland.
ce.o: Ce is listed among the seven Pictish provinces, named after the sons of [[e:cruithne-legendary-king|Cruithne]]. It is usually placed in [[e:aberdeenshire|Aberdeenshire]], around [[e:mar-scotland|Mar]] and Buchan, partly because the hill [[e:bennachie|Bennachie]] may preserve its name.
ce.r: Nothing is known of its rulers or institutions. The area is rich in Pictish symbol stones and hillforts, such as [[e:bennachie|Bennachie's]] Mither Tap, suggesting an organised society within the wider Pictish kingdom.
ce.e: Ce disappeared as a distinct unit when [[s:kingdom-of-the-picts|Pictland]] became part of the [[s:kingdom-of-scotland|Kingdom of Scotland]]. The later mormaerdoms or earldoms of [[e:mar-scotland|Mar]] and Buchan may continue its territory.

county-of-mark.t: Westphalian county around Hamm and the later Ruhr, whose counts beat Cologne at Worringen and whose iron trades made it an industrial heartland.
county-of-mark.o: A branch of the counts of Altena acquired the castle of Mark near [[e:hamm|Hamm]] and from about 1198 called themselves counts of the Mark. Adolf I founded Hamm in 1226. Their county lay between the [[e:ruhr|Ruhr]] and the [[e:lippe-river|Lippe]], and they long fought the archbishops of [[s:free-imperial-city-of-cologne|Cologne]] for dominance in [[e:westphalia|Westphalia]].
county-of-mark.r: Count [[e:eberhard-ii-count-of-the-mark|Eberhard II]] helped defeat [[s:free-imperial-city-of-cologne|Cologne]] at the [[e:battle-of-worringen|Battle of Worringen]] in 1288, securing the county's independence. Small towns such as [[e:hamm|Hamm]], [[e:unna|Unna]], [[e:iserlohn|Iserlohn]] and [[e:ludenscheid|Lüdenscheid]] grew from metalworking and wire-drawing. In 1368 the counts also inherited [[e:kleve|Cleves]], and from 1398 Cleves and Mark were ruled together. [[e:soest|Soest]] joined Mark after the [[e:soest-feud|Soest Feud]] of 1444 to 1449.
county-of-mark.e: Joined with Jülich-Berg in 1521, Mark was inherited by [[e:brandenburg|Brandenburg]] in 1614 after the Jülich succession dispute. It was part of the [[s:grand-duchy-of-berg|Grand Duchy of Berg]] from 1807, then [[e:kingdom-of-prussia|Prussia's]] [[e:province-of-westphalia|Province of Westphalia]], and its [[e:ruhr|Ruhr]] towns industrialised in the 19th century.

county-of-castell.t: Tiny Franconian county in the Steigerwald, held by one of Germany's oldest comital families, whose bank founded in 1774 still operates.
county-of-castell.o: The lords of Castell, named after a castle on the western edge of the [[e:steigerwald|Steigerwald]], appear as counts around 1200. Their family is among the oldest noble houses in [[e:franconia|Franconia]], and they held lands between [[e:wurzburg|Würzburg]] and [[e:bamberg|Bamberg]], often as [[e:vassal|vassals]] of the [[s:prince-bishopric-of-wurzburg|Prince-Bishopric of Würzburg]], while claiming imperial immediacy.
county-of-castell.r: The county was small, rural and divided among branches of the family, with vineyards on the [[e:steigerwald|Steigerwald]] slopes a key source of income. The counts adopted [[e:lutheranism|Lutheranism]] in the 16th century and maintained it in the face of their powerful Catholic neighbours. In 1774 they founded a bank to manage the county's finances, the [[e:castell-bank|Castell Bank]].
county-of-castell.e: Castell was mediatised in 1806 and absorbed into the [[s:kingdom-of-bavaria|Kingdom of Bavaria]], its counts becoming landowners. The family still lives at Castell and Rüdenhausen, and the [[e:castell-bank|Castell Bank]] remains one of [[e:germany|Germany's]] oldest banks.

chancay.t: A culture of Peru's central coast known for its black-on-white pottery, gauze-like textiles and doll-like figurines.
chancay.o: The Chancay culture emerged around 1000 in the Chancay, [[e:chillon-river|Chillón]] and Huaura valleys north of modern [[e:lima|Lima]], filling the space left by the decline of Wari influence. Large centres with adobe pyramids and residential compounds developed at sites such as Lauri and Pisquillo Chico.
chancay.r: Chancay was a group of local lordships rather than a single state. Its economy combined irrigation farming with fishing and trade along the coast. Its people produced vast quantities of pottery with a matte black-on-white finish, including large egg-shaped jars and figures called cuchimilcos. Their weavers made fine gauze, painted [[e:cotton|cotton]] cloth and figurines of cloth. Large cemeteries have preserved these goods.
chancay.e: The [[e:inca-empire|Incas]] incorporated the Chancay valleys into their empire around 1470. Spanish colonisation followed in the 1530s. Many Chancay cemeteries were later looted, which is why their pottery is widely found in museums. Chancay is also known today for its deep-water port opened in 2024.

county-of-perigord.t: Medieval county of the Dordogne valley around Périgueux, the land of the ancient Petrocorii.
county-of-perigord.o: In 866 [[e:charles-the-bald|Charles the Bald]] entrusted the counties of Périgord and [[e:angouleme|Angoulême]] to [[e:vulgrin-i-count-of-angouleme|Vulgrin]], a kinsman, to resist [[e:vikings|Viking]] raids along the rivers of western [[e:france|France]]. After his death the two counties were divided between his sons, and Périgord passed to a line of counts from whom the later [[e:charles-maurice-de-talleyrand|Talleyrand-Périgord]] family claimed descent.
county-of-perigord.r: The counts were [[e:vassal|vassals]] of the [[s:duchy-of-aquitaine|Duchy of Aquitaine]] and held a land of castles and abbeys on the frontier between English and French power. Their authority was contested by the [[e:burghers|burghers]] of [[e:perigueux|Périgueux]], whose town of Puy-Saint-Front won wide privileges.
county-of-perigord.e: During the [[e:hundred-years-war|Hundred Years' War]] the counts changed sides repeatedly. In 1399 Count Archambaud VI was condemned for treason and his county confiscated; [[e:charles-vi-of-france|Charles VI]] gave it in 1400 to his brother [[e:louis-i-duke-of-orleans|Louis of Orléans]]. It later passed to the [[e:house-of-albret|Albret]] family and was united with the crown under [[e:henry-iv-of-france|Henry IV]].

county-of-rietberg.t: Tiny Westphalian county on the upper Ems that survived from 1237 to the Napoleonic era, last held by the Austrian statesman Kaunitz.
county-of-rietberg.o: A branch of the counts of [[e:arnsberg|Arnsberg]] established itself at Rietberg on the upper Ems around 1237, founding a small county in the marshy lowlands between the territories of Münster, [[e:paderborn|Paderborn]] and [[s:county-of-ravensberg|Ravensberg]]. The counts held it as an imperial fief.
county-of-rietberg.r: The county was small and agricultural, with Rietberg as its only town. Through marriage it passed in the 16th century to the East Frisian [[e:house-of-cirksena|Cirksena]] family and then, in 1699, to the Kaunitz family, whose most famous member, [[e:wenzel-anton-von-kaunitz-rietberg|Wenzel Anton von Kaunitz-Rietberg]], became Austrian state chancellor under [[e:maria-theresa|Maria Theresa]]. After a period of [[e:lutheranism|Lutheranism]], the county was restored to [[e:catholicism|Catholicism]].
county-of-rietberg.e: Rietberg was absorbed into the [[s:kingdom-of-westphalia|Kingdom of Westphalia]] in 1807 and passed to [[e:kingdom-of-prussia|Prussia]] in 1815, becoming part of the [[e:province-of-westphalia|Province of Westphalia]]. The town of Rietberg is now in [[e:north-rhine-westphalia|North Rhine-Westphalia]].

colony-of-cape-breton-island.t: A separate British colony created for Loyalist refugees on Cape Breton Island, later reabsorbed into Nova Scotia.
colony-of-cape-breton-island.o: Formerly the French colony of [[s:ile-royale|Ile Royale]] with its fortress at [[e:louisbourg|Louisbourg]], Cape Breton passed to [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]] in 1763 and was joined to [[s:colony-of-nova-scotia|Nova Scotia]]. In 1784, as Loyalists arrived after the [[e:american-revolution|American Revolution]], [[e:britain|Britain]] made it a separate colony. Its first lieutenant governor, [[e:joseph-frederick-wallet-desbarres|Joseph Frederick Wallet DesBarres]], founded [[e:sydney-nova-scotia|Sydney]] as the capital in 1785.
colony-of-cape-breton-island.r: The colony was governed by a lieutenant governor and appointed council and never received an elected assembly, which left it unable to levy taxes legally and fed constant quarrels among officials. Its population grew mainly through Scottish Highland immigrants after 1800, along with [[e:acadians|Acadians]] and [[e:mikmaq|Mi'kmaq]]. [[e:coal|Coal]] mines near [[e:sydney-nova-scotia|Sydney]], leased by the Crown, provided much of the revenue.
colony-of-cape-breton-island.e: Political paralysis and doubts about the legality of its taxes led [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]] to reannex Cape Breton to the [[s:colony-of-nova-scotia|Colony of Nova Scotia]] in 1820, despite local protests. It remains part of [[e:nova-scotia|Nova Scotia]] within [[s:province-of-canada|Canada]].

carnonacae.t: People of north-west Scotland named in Ptolemy's Geography, usually placed on the coast of Wester Ross.
carnonacae.o: The Carnonacae appear in [[e:geography-ptolemy|Ptolemy's Geography]] of about 150 on the western coast of the [[e:scottish-highlands|Scottish Highlands]], north of the [[s:creones|Creones]] and south of the [[s:caereni|Caereni]], roughly in modern [[e:wester-ross|Wester Ross]]. Their name may contain a Celtic element meaning cairn or horn, perhaps referring to rocky headlands.
carnonacae.r: Nothing is recorded of their rulers or institutions. The coast of [[e:wester-ross|Wester Ross]] supported small populations living in roundhouses and duns, with brochs appearing along the Atlantic seaboard in the last centuries BCE. These tall drystone towers suggest local elites able to organise considerable labour.
carnonacae.e: The Carnonacae do not appear in any later source. Their territory later formed part of the lands of the [[e:picts|Picts]] and, from the 9th century, came under strong Norse influence.

county-of-nevers.t: A Loire county in Burgundy's orbit that passed through Flemish, Burgundian and Cleves hands before becoming a duchy in 1539.
county-of-nevers.o: Around 990 Otto-William, count of [[s:duchy-of-burgundy|Burgundy]], gave the county of Nevers to his son-in-law [[e:landry-count-of-nevers|Landry]], who founded its first dynasty. Landry's descendants also held [[e:auxerre|Auxerre]] and [[e:tonnerre|Tonnerre]], giving the counts a large lordship along the upper [[e:loire|Loire]] and the [[e:yonne-river|Yonne]].
county-of-nevers.r: Nevers lay on the [[e:loire|Loire]] between the royal domain and the [[s:duchy-of-burgundy|Duchy of Burgundy]], with forests, ironworks and river trade. Several counts went on [[e:crusade|crusade]], and [[e:william-iii-count-of-nevers|Count William III]] joined the [[e:second-crusade|Second Crusade]]. In the 13th and 14th centuries the county passed by marriage to the Flemish counts, including [[e:louis-i-count-of-flanders|Louis of Nevers]], and then to a younger branch of the [[e:house-of-valois|Valois]] dukes of [[e:burgundy|Burgundy]].
county-of-nevers.e: In 1491 it passed to the house of [[e:kleve|Cleves]], and in 1539 [[e:francis-i-duke-of-nevers|Francis I]] raised it to a duchy-peerage for François de Clèves. The Duchy of Nevers later went to the [[e:house-of-gonzaga|Gonzagas]] and the Mazarins, and lost its last rights in the Revolution.

county-of-gorizia.t: A county on the Isonzo, at the meeting point of the Italian, Slovene and German worlds, whose counts once ruled Tyrol and Carinthia.
county-of-gorizia.o: The counts of [[e:gorizia|Gorizia]] (Görz) appear around 1090 as advocates of the [[s:patriarchate-of-aquileia|Patriarchate of Aquileia]], with lands in [[e:friuli|Friuli]], [[e:carinthia|Carinthia]] and the [[e:puster-valley|Puster valley]]. They took their name from the castle of Gorizia on the [[e:soca|Isonzo]] river, and in 1253 inherited the [[s:county-of-tyrol|County of Tyrol]].
county-of-gorizia.r: In 1271 the family split: [[e:meinhard-ii-of-gorizia-tyrol|Meinhard II]] took [[e:tyrol|Tyrol]] and became Duke of [[e:carinthia|Carinthia]], while his brother Albert kept [[e:gorizia|Gorizia]] and the [[e:puster-valley|Puster valley]]. The county combined Italian, Friulian, Slovene and German populations. Its counts held lands in [[s:histria|Istria]] and on the Karst and built the castle that still dominates Gorizia.
county-of-gorizia.e: The last count, [[e:leonhard-count-of-gorizia|Leonhard]], died in 1500, and [[e:gorizia|Gorizia]] passed to [[e:maximilian-i-holy-roman-emperor|Emperor Maximilian I]] and the [[e:habsburg-dynasty|Habsburgs]]. Joined with Gradisca in 1754, it remained an Austrian crown land until 1918. The area was then divided between [[e:italy|Italy]] and, after 1947, [[e:yugoslavia|Yugoslavia]], which created [[e:nova-gorica|Nova Gorica]].

callatis.t: Dorian colony of Heraclea Pontica on the Dobruja coast, a grain-trading city that defied Lysimachus and later allied with Rome, at modern Mangalia.
callatis.o: Callatis was founded by colonists from [[s:heraclea-pontica|Heraclea Pontica]] on the western [[e:black-sea|Black Sea]] coast, probably in the late 6th century BCE, though some sources place the foundation later. Its fertile hinterland in southern [[e:dobruja|Dobruja]] made it a natural centre for grain exports, and it grew alongside the Milesian colonies of [[s:histria|Histria]], [[s:tomis|Tomis]] and [[s:odessos|Odessos]].
callatis.r: Callatis kept the Doric dialect and institutions of its mother city, with cults of [[e:apollo|Apollo]], [[e:dionysus|Dionysus]] and [[e:heracles|Heracles]]. It traded grain, wine and craft goods with the [[s:getae|Getae]] of the interior and struck its own coinage. In 313 BCE it led the Pontic cities in revolt against [[e:lysimachus|Lysimachus]], withstanding a long siege that ended around 309 BCE.
callatis.e: In the 1st century BCE Callatis concluded a formal treaty with [[e:rome|Rome]], a rare surviving text of its kind. After the campaign of [[e:marcus-terentius-varro-lucullus|Marcus Terentius Varro Lucullus]] in 72-71 BCE it lay within the Roman sphere and later in the province of [[e:moesia|Moesia]]. The site is the modern Romanian town of Mangalia.

colony-of-queensland.t: The northeastern Australian colony that grew from a penal station into a land of sugar, gold and cattle, and elected the world's first Labour government.
colony-of-queensland.o: A penal settlement for reoffending convicts was set up at [[e:moreton-bay|Moreton Bay]] in 1824 and moved to the site of [[e:brisbane|Brisbane]] in 1825. The district opened to free settlement in 1842 and was part of the [[s:colony-of-new-south-wales|Colony of New South Wales]] until 6 June 1859, when it became a separate colony with [[e:george-bowen|George Bowen]] as governor and Brisbane as capital.
colony-of-queensland.r: Pastoralists spread across [[e:aboriginal-australians|Aboriginal]] lands, with frontier violence carried out by settlers and the Native Police. Gold rushes at [[e:gympie|Gympie]], Charters Towers and [[e:mount-morgan-queensland|Mount Morgan]] brought wealth. [[e:sugar-plantation|Sugar plantations]] used some 62,000 Pacific Islanders, many recruited by deception in the trade known as blackbirding. The shearers' strike of 1891 helped found the Labour Party, and in 1899 [[e:anderson-dawson|Anderson Dawson]] briefly led the world's first Labour government.
colony-of-queensland.e: Queensland voted for federation in 1899 and became a state of the [[s:commonwealth-of-australia|Commonwealth of Australia]] in 1901. Most Pacific Islander labourers were deported under the new federation's [[e:white-australia-policy|White Australia policy]].

chickasaw-nation.t: A formidable south-eastern nation, allies of the British and enemies of the French, who after removal built a self-governing republic in Indian Territory.
chickasaw-nation.o: The Chickasaw descended from Mississippian chiefdoms of northern [[e:mississippi-river|Mississippi]]; the Spanish of [[e:hernando-de-soto|Hernando de Soto's]] expedition met them, as Chicaza, in 1540 to 1541, and were attacked in their winter camp. By around 1700 they lived in a cluster of towns near modern [[e:tupelo-mississippi|Tupelo]] and had become key partners of English traders from [[s:province-of-carolina|Carolina]].
chickasaw-nation.r: Towns were led by hereditary chiefs, the minko, and war leaders, within matrilineal clans. Chickasaw warriors raided neighbours for captives sold to the English and traded deerskins for guns and cloth. They defeated [[s:french-louisiana|French Louisiana]] and its allies at [[e:battle-of-ackia|Ackia]] in 1736. Under leaders such as [[e:piomingo|Piomingo]] they allied with the [[s:united-states|United States]] after 1783, and some families became planters owning enslaved Africans.
chickasaw-nation.e: Under the [[e:treaty-of-pontotoc-creek|Treaty of Pontotoc Creek]] of 1832 the Chickasaw sold their [[e:bantustan|homeland]] and moved to [[e:indian-territory|Indian Territory]] in 1837. They adopted a constitution in 1856 with its capital at [[e:tishomingo-oklahoma|Tishomingo]]. Allotment ended their government in 1907, but the Chickasaw Nation has since been revived in [[e:oklahoma|Oklahoma]].

caucasian-albania.t: An ancient kingdom of the eastern Caucasus, roughly modern Azerbaijan, with its own alphabet and church, long a buffer between Rome and Persia.
caucasian-albania.o: Greek and Roman writers describe the [[e:albanians|Albanians]] as a union of 26 tribes speaking different languages in the plains of the [[e:kura-river|Kura]] river. By the 1st century BCE they had a king; [[e:oroeses|Oroeses]] fought [[e:pompey|Pompey]] in 65 BCE. The early capital was [[e:qabala|Kabala]], near modern Qabala, later moved to [[e:barda|Partav]].
caucasian-albania.r: The country was farmed and herded, and its kings depended on great noble families. It was a client of the [[s:roman-empire|Roman Empire]] and then of the [[s:sasanian-empire|Sasanian Empire]], whose cavalry it supplied. King [[e:urnayr|Urnayr]] adopted [[e:christianity|Christianity]] in the 4th century, and an alphabet for the Caucasian Albanian language was created in the 5th century, attested in palimpsests from Sinai.
caucasian-albania.e: [[e:vachagan-iii|Vachagan III]] issued church canons around 488, but in about 510 the [[e:sasanian-empire|Sasanians]] abolished the Albanian kingship and governed through [[e:marzban|marzbans]]. The [[s:mihranid-principality-of-albania|Mihranid Principality of Albania]] later revived local rule; the Albanian church and language faded after the Arab conquest, absorbed into Armenian and later Turkic culture.

chinese-soviet-republic.t: The Communist state founded in the hills of Jiangxi in 1931, where Mao Zedong and the Red Army learned to govern before the Long March.
chinese-soviet-republic.o: After the [[s:nationalist-government|Nationalist government]] turned on its Communist allies in 1927, Communist forces under [[e:mao-zedong|Mao Zedong]] and Zhu De built rural bases in the mountains between [[e:jiangxi|Jiangxi]] and [[e:fujian|Fujian]]. On 7 November 1931 a congress at [[e:ruijin|Ruijin]] proclaimed the Chinese Soviet Republic, with Mao as chairman of its central executive committee.
chinese-soviet-republic.r: The republic redistributed land from landlords to poor peasants, issued its own currency, stamps and laws on marriage and labour, and mobilised villagers for the [[e:chinese-red-army|Red Army]]. It was linked to other soviet base areas across central [[e:china|China]]. Its policies were shaped by [[e:communist-international|Comintern]]-trained leaders, who sidelined [[e:mao-zedong|Mao]] after 1932, and by constant encirclement campaigns launched by [[e:chiang-kai-shek|Chiang Kai-shek]].
chinese-soviet-republic.e: The fifth encirclement campaign, using blockhouses and [[e:naval-blockade|blockade]], broke the [[e:jiangxi|Jiangxi]] base, and in October 1934 the [[e:chinese-red-army|Red Army]] began the [[e:long-march|Long March]], reaching northern [[e:shaanxi|Shaanxi]] in 1935. Under the [[e:second-united-front|Second United Front]] in 1937 the remaining soviet became the [[e:shaan-gan-ning-border-region|Shaan-Gan-Ning Border Region]].

cayor.t: Wolof kingdom of the coast between Dakar and Saint-Louis, whose last great ruler Lat Dior fought the French railway.
cayor.o: Cayor was a province of the [[s:jolof-empire|Jolof Empire]] until 1549, when its governor [[e:amari-ngone-sobel-fall|Amari Ngoone Sobel Fall]] defeated the [[e:buurba-jolof|Buurba Jolof]] at [[e:battle-of-danki|Danki]] and became the first independent [[e:damel|Damel]]. The capital was later fixed at Mboul. Cayor controlled the coast between the [[e:cap-vert|Cap-Vert]] peninsula and the [[e:senegal|Senegal]] river.
cayor.r: The [[e:damel|Damel]] was elected from the Fall royal lineage by a council of great [[e:prince-elector|electors]], and ruled with an army of crown slaves, the tyeddo. Cayor traded slaves, hides and [[e:groundnut|groundnuts]] with the French at [[s:goree|Gorée]] and [[e:saint-louis-senegal|Saint-Louis]]. Kings often also ruled the [[s:kingdom-of-baol|Kingdom of Baol]], and tension grew between the tyeddo and Muslim clerics.
cayor.e: In the 1860s the French began to annex Cayor. [[e:damel|Damel]] [[e:lat-dior|Lat Dior Diop]] opposed the [[e:dakar-senegal|Dakar]] to [[e:saint-louis-senegal|Saint-Louis]] railway and was killed at [[e:battle-of-dekhele|Dekhle]] in 1886, after which [[e:france|France]] absorbed the kingdom into [[s:french-senegal|French Senegal]]. Lat Dior is a national hero in [[e:senegal|Senegal]].

crimean-regional-government.t: Two successive governments of the Crimea in 1918 and 1919, first under German protection and then under Allied and White support.
crimean-regional-government.o: After German troops occupied the [[e:crimea|Crimea]] in spring 1918 and ended the [[s:taurida-soviet-socialist-republic|Taurida Soviet Socialist Republic]], they backed a regional government led by General [[e:maciej-sulkiewicz|Maciej Sulkiewicz]], a Lithuanian [[e:tatars|Tatar]] former Russian officer, formed in June 1918.
crimean-regional-government.r: [[e:maciej-sulkiewicz|Sulkiewicz]]'s government claimed autonomy and refused to accept rule by the [[s:ukrainian-state|Ukrainian State]], which blockaded the peninsula. When [[e:germany|Germany]] withdrew in November 1918, a liberal second government under [[e:solomon-krym|Solomon Krym]], a Karaite agronomist, took over, relying on Allied warships and the White [[e:volunteer-army|Volunteer Army]]. Both governments had little control over their own security or economy.
crimean-regional-government.e: In April 1919 the [[e:red-army|Red Army]] broke into the [[e:crimea|Crimea]], the [[e:allies|Allies]] evacuated and the Krym government left by sea. The Bolsheviks then set up the [[s:crimean-socialist-soviet-republic|Crimean Socialist Soviet Republic]].

county-of-rodez.t: The county of the Rouergue around Rodez, held by the Millau and Armagnac families, which shared its hilltop city with a powerful bishop.
county-of-rodez.o: The county of Rouergue had belonged to the counts of [[s:county-of-toulouse|Toulouse]]. In 1112 the viscount of [[e:millau|Millau]], Richard, acquired the county of [[e:rodez|Rodez]], founding a local line that ruled the comital part of the city, the Bourg, while the [[e:bishop|bishop]] governed the Cité around the cathedral.
county-of-rodez.r: The Rouergue was a land of uplands, sheep and pilgrim routes to [[e:santiago-de-compostela|Compostela]], with [[e:conques|Conques]] nearby. Count [[e:henry-ii-count-of-rodez|Henry II of Rodez]] was a patron of troubadours in the late 13th century. In 1302 his daughter Cécile brought [[e:rodez|Rodez]] to [[e:bernard-vi-of-armagnac|Bernard VI of Armagnac]], and the county became one of the [[e:house-of-armagnac|Armagnacs]]' chief holdings.
county-of-rodez.e: After the [[s:county-of-armagnac|Armagnac]] line ended, [[e:rodez|Rodez]] passed to the Alençon and [[e:house-of-albret|Albret]] families and so to [[e:henry-iv-of-france|Henry of Navarre]]. When he became Henry IV in 1589, the county joined the [[s:kingdom-of-france|Kingdom of France]]; his personal lands were formally united with the crown in 1607.

cupul.t: A large Maya province of eastern Yucatán, including Chichen Itza, whose people led the Great Maya Revolt against Spanish rule in 1546.
cupul.o: Cupul formed after the collapse of the [[s:league-of-mayapan|League of Mayapan]] around 1441 under the Cupul lineage. It covered a large area of east-central Yucatán, including the ruins of [[s:chichen-itza|Chichen Itza]], with its main town at Saci, where [[e:valladolid-yucatan|Valladolid]] now stands.
cupul.r: The province was governed by lords of the Cupul lineage, who appear to have shared power among several branches rather than recognising one supreme ruler. Its people farmed [[e:maize|maize]], [[e:cotton|cotton]] and honey. The Cupul resisted [[e:francisco-de-montejo|Montejo]]'s first invasions in the late 1520s and early 1530s, forcing him to abandon a base at [[s:chichen-itza|Chichen Itza]].
cupul.e: In 1545 the Spanish founded [[e:valladolid-yucatan|Valladolid]] at Saci. In 1546 the Cupul rose with [[s:sotuta|Sotuta]] in the [[e:great-maya-revolt|Great Maya Revolt]], killing Spaniards and their allies, but were crushed in 1547. The province became part of the [[s:province-of-yucatan|Province of Yucatán]].

commune-of-como.t: A lakeside city-republic that Milan destroyed in 1127 and Frederick Barbarossa rebuilt, home of the master builders known as the Comacine masters.
commune-of-como.o: Como, at the southern tip of [[e:lake-como|Lake Como]] on the route to the Alpine passes, had consuls by 1109. Its quarrel with [[s:duchy-of-milan|Milan]] over the bishopric and lake trade led to the [[e:ten-years-war-1118-1127|Ten Years' War]] of 1118–1127, which ended with Como's destruction.
commune-of-como.r: Como was ruled by consuls and later a podestà. Allied with [[e:frederick-barbarossa|Frederick Barbarossa]], it was rebuilt with imperial support in 1159 and remained largely Ghibelline. Its builders and stonemasons, the magistri comacini, worked across northern [[e:italy|Italy]], and the city controlled lake shipping and Alpine traffic. In the 13th and 14th centuries the Ghibelline Rusca and Guelph Vittani families fought for control.
commune-of-como.e: In 1335 [[e:franchino-rusca|Franchino Rusca]] surrendered the city to [[e:azzone-visconti|Azzone Visconti]], and Como became part of the [[s:lordship-of-milan|Lordship of Milan]], later the [[s:duchy-of-milan|Duchy of Milan]].

cacicazgo-of-jaragua.t: The largest Taíno chiefdom of Hispaniola, in the south-west, ruled by Bohechío and his sister Anacaona until a Spanish massacre in 1503.
cacicazgo-of-jaragua.o: Jaragua (Xaraguá) occupied south-western [[e:hispaniola|Hispaniola]], including much of today's southern [[s:first-empire-of-haiti|Haiti]]. It was one of the five principal chiefdoms that the Spanish found in 1492, formed during the growth of [[e:taino|Taíno]] society over the preceding centuries.
cacicazgo-of-jaragua.r: Its paramount cacique [[e:bohechio|Bohechío]] ruled from a town near modern [[e:leogane|Léogâne]], receiving tribute from many lesser chiefs. Jaragua was noted for its elaborate court, [[e:cotton|cotton]] cloth and wooden ceremonial seats (duhos). After the death of her husband [[e:caonabo|Caonabo of Maguana]], [[e:anacaona|Anacaona]] returned to Jaragua and, on Bohechío's death, became its ruler; she was celebrated for her poetry and areítos (songs and dances).
cacicazgo-of-jaragua.e: In 1503 Governor [[e:nicolas-de-ovando|Nicolás de Ovando]] invited Jaragua's chiefs to a feast, then had them burnt and [[e:anacaona|Anacaona]] hanged. The chiefdom ended, and Anacaona became a symbol of indigenous resistance in [[s:first-empire-of-haiti|Haiti]] and the [[s:first-dominican-republic|Dominican Republic]].

cantona.t: A huge fortified city in the eastern Puebla highlands, notable for its many ballcourts and its control of the Oyameles-Zaragoza obsidian source.
cantona.o: Cantona grew from about 600 BCE on a rough lava field in eastern [[e:puebla-state|Puebla]]. Its position near the Oyameles-[[e:zaragoza|Zaragoza]] obsidian deposits and on routes between the central highlands and the [[e:gulf-coast-of-mexico|Gulf Coast]] made it an important manufacturing and trading centre.
cantona.r: The city was densely built of unmortared stone, with walled residential compounds, raised causeways and controlled entrances that suggest strong concern with defence. It has more than twenty ballcourts, the most known from any Mesoamerican site, pointing to the political and ritual importance of the game. Obsidian tools were produced on a large scale. Cantona seems to have remained independent of [[s:teotihuacan|Teotihuacan]].
cantona.e: Cantona reached its height after Teotihuacan's decline, between about 600 and 900 CE, then lost population and was abandoned by about 1050. Rediscovered in modern times, it was opened to visitors in 1994.

county-of-armagnac.t: A Gascon county whose counts gave their name to a faction in France's civil war and fought Louis XI to the bitter end.
county-of-armagnac.o: Armagnac was carved out of the duchy of [[e:gascony|Gascony]] around 960 for [[e:bernard-i-of-armagnac|Bernard the Squinter]], a younger son of the Gascon ducal house. His descendants ruled the hill country around [[e:auch|Auch]] and [[e:lectoure|Lectoure]] and gradually gathered neighbouring counties such as [[e:fezensac|Fezensac]] and [[e:rodez|Rodez]].
county-of-armagnac.r: The counts were among the greatest lords of the south-west, shifting between the English in [[s:duchy-of-aquitaine|Guyenne]] and the French crown. [[e:bernard-vii-count-of-armagnac|Bernard VII]] became constable of [[e:france|France]] and led the Armagnac party against the [[e:burgundians|Burgundians]] in the civil war of the 1410s until his murder in [[e:paris|Paris]] in 1418. The land was known for wine and its brandy, later named after it.
county-of-armagnac.e: Count John V defied [[e:louis-xi|Louis XI]] and was killed when royal troops took [[e:lectoure|Lectoure]] in 1473. The last count, Charles I, died in 1497, and the county passed to the duke of Alençon and later to the house of [[e:house-of-albret|Albret]] before returning to the [[s:kingdom-of-france|Kingdom of France]].

county-of-ribagorza.t: A Pyrenean county between Aragon and Catalonia, with its bishopric at Roda de Isábena, later absorbed into the Kingdom of Aragon.
county-of-ribagorza.o: [[e:ribagorza|Ribagorza]], the valleys of the [[e:isabena|Isábena]] and [[e:noguera-ribagorzana|Noguera Ribagorzana]], was part of the Frankish [[s:county-of-toulouse|County of Toulouse]] until around 872, when [[e:ramon-i-of-pallars-and-ribagorza|Ramon I]] established himself as count of [[e:pallars|Pallars]] and Ribagorza. After his death Ribagorza went to one of his sons.
county-of-ribagorza.r: The counts ruled a mountain society of herders and farmers, defended by castles against the Muslim lords of [[e:lleida|Lleida]] and [[e:barbastro|Barbastro]]. They founded a bishopric at [[e:roda-de-isabena|Roda de Isábena]], whose cathedral was consecrated in 956, making it the county's religious centre. The county shared its culture and language with both Aragon and [[s:principality-of-catalonia|Catalonia]].
county-of-ribagorza.e: [[e:almanzor|Almanzor's]] raids weakened the county around 1000. [[e:sancho-iii-of-navarre|Sancho III of Navarre]] took control in the 1010s and 1020s, and in 1035 [[e:ribagorza|Ribagorza]] passed with [[s:county-of-sobrarbe|Sobrarbe]] to his son Gonzalo. After Gonzalo's death around 1045 it went to [[e:ramiro-i-of-aragon|Ramiro I]], joining the [[s:kingdom-of-aragon|Kingdom of Aragon]].

county-of-east-frisia.t: The North Sea county of the Cirksena family, whose powerful estates and Calvinist port of Emden kept their rulers in check.
county-of-east-frisia.o: After a century of feuds among Frisian chieftains, [[e:ulrich-i-count-of-east-frisia|Ulrich Cirksena]] united most of [[e:east-frisia|East Frisia]], and in 1464 [[e:frederick-iii-holy-roman-emperor|Emperor Frederick III]] made him an imperial count. His descendants extended their rule over neighbouring chieftaincies, though they failed to win the [[s:lordship-of-jever|Lordship of Jever]].
county-of-east-frisia.r: The [[e:house-of-cirksena|Cirksena]], raised to princes in the 17th century, ruled from [[e:aurich|Aurich]], but the estates, above all the town of [[e:emden|Emden]], held great power. Emden became a Calvinist stronghold, the '[[s:republic-of-geneva|Geneva]] of the North', and in 1595 rebelled against the Lutheran counts, after which the estates leaned on the [[s:dutch-republic|Dutch Republic]]. The economy rested on [[e:cattle|cattle]], grain and shipping.
county-of-east-frisia.e: When [[e:charles-edzard-prince-of-east-frisia|Charles Edzard]], the last [[e:house-of-cirksena|Cirksena]], died in 1744, [[e:frederick-the-great|Frederick II of Prussia]] occupied [[e:east-frisia|East Frisia]] under an inheritance claim. It passed to the [[s:kingdom-of-hanover|Kingdom of Hanover]] in 1815 and back to [[e:kingdom-of-prussia|Prussia]] in 1866, and is now part of [[e:lower-saxony|Lower Saxony]].

county-of-ravensberg.t: A Westphalian county around Bielefeld that joined the Jülich-Cleves inheritance and became a Prussian linen-weaving region.
county-of-ravensberg.o: The counts of Ravensberg appear around 1140, named after a castle near [[e:borgholzhausen|Borgholzhausen]]. Their territory grew between the [[e:teutoburg-forest|Teutoburg Forest]] and the [[e:weser|Weser]] hills, and around 1214 Count Hermann IV founded the town of [[e:bielefeld|Bielefeld]] beneath the [[e:sparrenburg|Sparrenburg]] castle.
county-of-ravensberg.r: Ravensberg became known for linen weaving, which made [[e:bielefeld|Bielefeld]] a centre of the trade. In 1346 the county passed by marriage to the counts of Berg and later formed part of the united territory of Jülich, [[e:kleve|Cleves]] and Berg. Its estates kept local institutions.
county-of-ravensberg.e: After the [[e:war-of-the-julich-succession|Jülich succession crisis]], the [[e:treaty-of-xanten|Treaty of Xanten]] of 1614 assigned Ravensberg to [[e:brandenburg|Brandenburg]], confirmed in 1666. It remained Prussian, was briefly part of the [[s:kingdom-of-westphalia|Kingdom of Westphalia]] from 1807, and then joined the Prussian province of [[e:westphalia|Westphalia]].

cr.a: Willem Janszoon Blaeu and Joan Blaeu

convenae.t: Mixed community gathered by Pompey in the central Pyrenees, whose town became Saint-Bertrand-de-Comminges.
convenae.o: Their name means those who came together. According to [[e:jerome|Jerome]], around 72 BCE [[e:pompey|Pompey]], returning from his war against [[e:quintus-sertorius|Sertorius]] in [[e:hispania|Hispania]], settled defeated fighters and mountain people at [[e:lugdunum-convenarum|Lugdunum]] in the upper [[e:garonne|Garonne]] valley.
convenae.r: The community mixed Iberian, Aquitanian and Roman elements and quickly adopted Roman ways. Its town had a forum, temple, baths and [[e:theatre|theatre]].
convenae.e: Their land was absorbed into [[e:gallia-aquitania|Roman Aquitania]]; Caesar's legate [[e:marcus-licinius-crassus|Crassus]] campaigned in the region in 56 BCE. [[e:lugdunum-convenarum|Lugdunum Convenarum]] became Saint-Bertrand-de-Comminges, with its [[e:romanesque-architecture|Romanesque]] cathedral, and the region kept the name [[s:county-of-comminges|Comminges]].

county-of-pallars-sobira.t: A remote Pyrenean county around Sort whose counts kept a degree of independence until 1491, the last of the old Catalan counties to be extinguished.
county-of-pallars-sobira.o: It was formed in 1011 when Count Sunyer of [[e:pallars|Pallars]] divided his lands between his sons. [[e:guillem-ii-of-pallars-sobira|Guillem II]] received the high valleys of the [[e:noguera-pallaresa|Noguera Pallaresa]] around [[e:sort|Sort]] and the [[e:valls-daneu|Àneu valleys]], while his brother [[e:ramon-iii-of-pallars-jussa|Ramon III]] took the lower [[s:county-of-pallars-jussa|County of Pallars Jussà]].
county-of-pallars-sobira.r: A mountain land of pastures, iron and small villages, [[e:pallars|Pallars]] Sobirà was ruled by a line of counts from [[e:sort|Sort]] and the castle of [[e:valencia|Valencia]] d'[[e:valls-daneu|Àneu]]. They became [[e:vassal|vassals]] of the [[e:house-of-barcelona|Counts of Barcelona]] and later the [[s:crown-of-aragon|Crown of Aragon]], but kept wide local powers. Many bore the names Artau and Hug Roger.
county-of-pallars-sobira.e: Count [[e:hug-roger-iii-of-pallars-sobira|Hug Roger III]] sided against [[e:john-ii-of-aragon|King John II]] in the Catalan civil war of 1462-1472 and later resisted [[e:ferdinand-ii-of-aragon|Ferdinand II]]. Defeated in 1487, he lost his county, which was confiscated in 1491 and given to the [[e:house-of-cardona|Cardona]] family as the Marquisate of [[e:pallars|Pallars]].

choctaw-nation.t: The largest nation of the Mississippi region, long allied with France, and the first of the south-eastern peoples forced west on the Trail of Tears.
choctaw-nation.o: The Choctaw formed from the merging of [[e:mississippian-culture|Mississippian]]-descended communities in central and southern [[e:mississippi-river|Mississippi]] in the 16th and 17th centuries. Their tradition places their origin at [[e:nanih-waiya|Nanih Waiya]], a great mound in [[e:winston-county-mississippi|Winston County]]. By around 1700 they lived in some 50 towns grouped in western, eastern and southern divisions.
choctaw-nation.r: Chiefs of the three divisions met in council, and matrilineal clans structured society. The Choctaw were skilled farmers and ballplayers. As the main allies of [[s:french-louisiana|French Louisiana]] they fought the [[s:chickasaw-nation|Chickasaw Nation]] and the [[s:natchez-chiefdom|Natchez chiefdom]], though a pro-British faction under [[e:red-shoe|Red Shoe]] sparked a civil war in 1747 to 1750. After 1783 they dealt with the [[s:united-states|United States]], and [[e:pushmataha|Pushmataha]] led warriors against the [[e:red-sticks|Red Sticks]] in the [[e:creek-war|Creek War]].
choctaw-nation.e: By the [[e:treaty-of-dancing-rabbit-creek|Treaty of Dancing Rabbit Creek]] in 1830 the Choctaw ceded their [[e:bantustan|homeland]] and were removed to [[e:indian-territory|Indian Territory]] in 1831 to 1833. Their government, seated at [[e:tuskahoma-oklahoma|Tuskahoma]], was dissolved by 1907 but later restored; the [[e:mississippi-band-of-choctaw-indians|Mississippi Band of Choctaw]] stayed in the east.

cr.a: Unknown author, commissioned by the Choctaw Nation [3]

chedi.t: An ancient kingdom of Bundelkhand, known from the Rigveda and the Mahabharata, whose royal name was later claimed by kings of Kalinga.
chedi.o: The Chedis are already mentioned in the [[e:rigveda|Rigveda]], where a king [[e:kashu-chaidya|Kashu Chaidya]] is praised for generous gifts to priests. Their country lay south of the [[e:yamuna|Yamuna]] in [[e:bundelkhand|Bundelkhand]], with its capital at Suktimati, probably near modern [[s:kingdom-of-banda|Banda]]. By the 6th century BCE they were counted among the sixteen mahajanapadas.
chedi.r: Little is known of Chedi government or society from contemporary sources. In the [[e:mahabharata|Mahabharata]] its king [[e:shishupala|Shishupala]] is killed by [[e:krishna|Krishna]] at the royal sacrifice of [[e:yudhishthira|Yudhishthira]]. The kingdom lay on routes leading from the [[e:ganges-plain|Ganges plain]] towards the [[e:narmada-river|Narmada]] and the [[e:deccan|Deccan]].
chedi.e: Chedi was absorbed by [[s:kingdom-of-magadha|Magadha]], probably by the [[s:nanda-empire|Nandas]] in the 4th century BCE. Branches of the Chedi line were claimed by later dynasties, notably the [[s:mahameghavahana-dynasty|Mahameghavahana dynasty]] of [[s:kingdom-of-kalinga|Kalinga]], and medieval Kalachuris called their realm Chedi.

commune-of-mantua.t: A lake-ringed city-republic of the Po plain that emerged after Matilda of Canossa's death and ended when the Bonacolsi seized power in 1272.
commune-of-mantua.o: [[s:duchy-of-mantua|Mantua]] had been a centre of [[e:matilda-of-tuscany|Matilda of Canossa's]] lands. After her death in 1115 its citizens organised a commune under consuls, taking control of the city and the countryside from the old feudal lords and the [[e:bishop|bishop]].
commune-of-mantua.r: The commune was governed by consuls and later a podestà. [[s:duchy-of-mantua|Mantua]] joined the [[s:lombard-league|Lombard League]] against [[e:frederick-barbarossa|Frederick Barbarossa]] and in the late 12th century engineer [[e:alberto-pitentino|Alberto Pitentino]] regulated the [[e:mincio|Mincio]] to form the lakes that still surround the city. Mantua traded along the Po and the Mincio and fought neighbours such as [[s:commune-of-verona|Verona]] and [[s:commune-of-cremona|Cremona]]. The troubadour poet [[e:sordello|Sordello]] came from its territory.
commune-of-mantua.e: In 1272 [[e:pinamonte-bonacolsi|Pinamonte Bonacolsi]] made himself captain of the people and ruled as lord, ending communal government. The [[e:house-of-gonzaga|Gonzaga]] overthrew the Bonacolsi in 1328, founding what became the [[s:duchy-of-mantua|Duchy of Mantua]].

chutia-kingdom.t: A kingdom of the upper Brahmaputra valley centred on Sadiya, the main rival of the Ahom kingdom until its conquest in 1524.
chutia-kingdom.o: The Chutia kingdom took shape in the far east of the [[e:brahmaputra|Brahmaputra]] valley, around [[e:sadiya|Sadiya]] in modern [[e:assam|Assam]] and [[e:arunachal-pradesh|Arunachal Pradesh]]. Its traditional founding is dated to 1187 under a ruler remembered as Birpal, though the early history rests mainly on later chronicles. By the 14th century it was a significant power north of the river.
chutia-kingdom.r: The [[e:chutia-people|Chutias]] were a [[e:bodo-kachari-peoples|Bodo-Kachari]] people whose rulers adopted [[e:hinduism|Hindu]] forms of kingship, patronising [[e:shaktism|Shakta]] worship, notably the Tamreswari temple near [[e:sadiya|Sadiya]]. [[e:copper|Copper]]-plate inscriptions of the 14th and 15th centuries record land grants and use [[e:sanskrit|Sanskrit]] and early Assamese. The kingdom was known for metalwork, including the manufacture of guns and [[e:field-artillery|cannon]], and for its control of trade routes to the hills.
chutia-kingdom.e: After a long series of wars, the Ahom king [[e:suhungmung|Suhungmung]] defeated the [[e:chutia-people|Chutias]] and annexed their kingdom in 1523 to 1524. [[e:sadiya|Sadiya]] became the seat of an Ahom frontier governor, the Sadiya-khowa Gohain, and many Chutia nobles and artisans were absorbed into Ahom society.

county-of-wertheim.t: A Franconian county at the meeting of the Main and the Tauber, whose castle still dominates the town, inherited by the Löwenstein family in 1556.
county-of-wertheim.o: The counts of Wertheim appear in 1132, with their castle on a hill at the confluence of the Main and [[e:tauber|Tauber]]. They held lands in the [[e:spessart|Spessart]] and the Main valley as [[e:vassal|vassals]] of the [[e:bishop|bishops]] of [[e:wurzburg|Würzburg]] and gradually built a small territory.
county-of-wertheim.r: The town of Wertheim developed as a river port with trade along the Main. The counts adopted the [[e:protestant-reformation|Reformation]] in the 1520s. Their castle, one of the largest in southern [[e:germany|Germany]], was expanded in the [[e:renaissance|Renaissance]]. The counts held offices at the courts of the [[s:electoral-palatinate|Palatinate]] and the Empire.
county-of-wertheim.e: Count Michael III died in 1556, the last of his line, and after disputes the county passed to Count Ludwig of [[s:county-of-stolberg|Stolberg]] and then, through marriage, to the [[e:house-of-lowenstein-wertheim|Löwenstein]] family, founding [[s:county-of-lowenstein-wertheim|Löwenstein-Wertheim]]. It was mediatised in 1806 and divided between [[e:baden|Baden]] and [[e:bavaria|Bavaria]].

congress-poland.t: The Kingdom of Poland created at Vienna under the Russian tsar, scene of two great uprisings and of Poland's industrial revolution.
congress-poland.o: The [[e:congress-of-vienna|Congress of Vienna]] in 1815 turned most of the [[s:duchy-of-warsaw|Duchy of Warsaw]] into a [[s:kingdom-of-poland-1916-1918|Kingdom of Poland]] joined to the [[s:russian-empire|Russian Empire]] by personal union, with [[e:alexander-i-of-russia|Tsar Alexander I]] as king. It received a liberal constitution, its own [[e:sejm|Sejm]], army, currency and administration, with [[e:warsaw|Warsaw]] as capital.
congress-poland.r: In practice the tsar's brother [[e:grand-duke-konstantin-pavlovich-of-russia|Grand Duke Constantine]] commanded the army and disregarded the constitution. The [[e:november-uprising|November Uprising]] of 1830 was crushed, and Marshal [[e:ivan-paskevich|Ivan Paskevich]] governed as [[e:viceroy-of-india|viceroy]] for decades. After the [[e:january-uprising|January Uprising]] of 1863 the kingdom lost its remaining autonomy and was renamed the [[e:vistula|Vistula]] Land, with Russian imposed in schools. At the same time [[e:lodz|Lodz]] grew into a great textile city.
congress-poland.e: During the [[e:first-world-war|First World War]] German and Austro-Hungarian armies drove the Russians out in 1915. The occupiers proclaimed the [[s:kingdom-of-poland-1916-1918|Kingdom of Poland]] (1916-1918), and its lands became the core of the [[s:second-polish-republic|Second Polish Republic]].

carausian-empire.t: Breakaway Roman regime in Britain and northern Gaul, founded by the admiral Carausius in 286, the first time Britain was ruled as a separate realm.
carausian-empire.o: [[e:carausius|Carausius]], a Menapian from the [[e:low-countries|Low Countries]], commanded the Roman fleet charged with clearing Frankish and [[e:saxons|Saxon]] [[e:piracy|pirates]] from the [[e:english-channel|Channel]]. Accused of keeping captured plunder for himself and sentenced to death by [[e:maximian|Maximian]], he declared himself emperor in 286, taking control of [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]] and part of northern [[e:gaul|Gaul]] with his fleet.
carausian-empire.r: [[e:carausius|Carausius]] ruled from [[e:london|London]] and [[s:county-of-boulogne|Boulogne]], presenting himself as a legitimate colleague of [[e:diocletian|Diocletian]] and [[e:maximian|Maximian]]. His coins, minted at London and another British mint, carried slogans such as RESTITVTOR BRITANNIAE and EXPECTATE VENI, quoting [[e:virgil|Virgil]]. He kept a strong fleet, repelled Maximian's attempted invasion in 289 and may have begun forts of the [[e:saxons|Saxon]] Shore.
carausian-empire.e: In 293 [[e:constantius-i|Constantius Chlorus]] captured [[s:county-of-boulogne|Boulogne]], and [[e:carausius|Carausius]] was murdered by his finance minister [[e:allectus|Allectus]], who took power. In 296 Constantius invaded; his prefect [[e:julius-asclepiodotus|Asclepiodotus]] defeated and killed Allectus, and Constantius entered [[e:london|London]], as the [[e:arras|Arras]] medallion celebrates. [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]] returned to [[s:roman-britain|Roman Britain]].

callaeci.t: The hillfort peoples of north-western Iberia, whose castro culture shaped Galicia and northern Portugal and who held out against Rome until 19 BCE.
callaeci.o: The Callaeci, or Gallaeci, occupied the north-west of [[e:iberia|Iberia]] north of the [[e:douro|Douro]], in modern [[s:kingdom-of-galicia-and-lodomeria|Galicia]] and northern Portugal. Their culture grew from the [[e:late-bronze-age|Late Bronze Age]] into the [[e:iron-age|Iron Age]] castro culture, marked by hundreds of fortified hilltop settlements of round stone houses.
callaeci.r: They were divided into many small communities rather than one state, each based on a castro such as [[e:citania-de-briteiros|Citânia de Briteiros]] or [[e:castro-of-santa-trega|Santa Tecla]]. They mined gold and [[e:tin|tin]], worked bronze and gold into torcs, and built sauna-like bathhouses with carved stones. They spoke a Celtic language, worshipped gods such as [[e:bandua|Bandua]], and erected stone warrior statues.
callaeci.e: [[e:decimus-junius-brutus-callaicus|Decimus Junius Brutus]] campaigned among them in 137 BCE and took the name Callaicus, but conquest was completed only in Augustus' [[e:cantabrian-wars|Cantabrian Wars]], ending in 19 BCE. Their land became the Roman region and later province of [[s:gallaecia|Gallaecia]].

county-of-schwerin.t: A county created by Henry the Lion in Obotrite lands around Schwerin, whose count once kidnapped the King of Denmark.
county-of-schwerin.o: After conquering the [[s:obotrite-confederation|Obotrites]], [[e:henry-the-lion|Henry the Lion]] founded a German town and bishopric at Schwerin and in 1167 created a county there for [[e:gunzelin-of-hagen|Gunzelin of Hagen]], one of his [[e:vassal|vassals]]. The county lay in western [[s:lordship-of-mecklenburg|Mecklenburg]], separate from the lands restored to the native Lordship of Mecklenburg.
county-of-schwerin.r: In 1223 Count Henry I of Schwerin captured King [[e:valdemar-ii-of-denmark|Valdemar II of Denmark]] and his son on the island of Lyø, holding them for two years; this helped to end Danish dominance in northern [[e:germany|Germany]], sealed by the [[e:battle-of-bornhoved|Battle of Bornhöved]] in 1227. The counts later split into lines at Schwerin, [[e:wittenburg|Wittenburg]] and [[e:boizenburg|Boizenburg]].
county-of-schwerin.e: As the comital lines died out, Duke [[e:albert-ii-duke-of-mecklenburg|Albert II of Mecklenburg]] bought the county in 1358 for 20,000 [[e:silver|silver]] marks. Schwerin became the capital of the [[s:lordship-of-mecklenburg|Mecklenburg]] dukes and later of the [[s:duchy-of-mecklenburg-schwerin|Grand Duchy of Mecklenburg-Schwerin]], and is today the capital of [[e:mecklenburg-vorpommern|Mecklenburg-Vorpommern]].

carpatho-ukraine.t: An autonomous Ukrainian region of Czechoslovakia that declared independence on 15 March 1939 and was conquered by Hungary the same week.
carpatho-ukraine.o: After the [[e:munich-agreement|Munich Agreement]] of 1938 weakened [[s:czechoslovakia|Czechoslovakia]], [[e:carpathian-ruthenia|Subcarpathian Ruthenia]] received autonomy in October 1938, first under [[e:andriy-brodiy|Andriy Brodiy]] and then the Greek Catholic priest [[e:avgustyn-voloshyn|Avgustyn Voloshyn]]. When the [[e:first-vienna-award|First Vienna Award]] gave [[e:uzhhorod|Uzhhorod]] and the southern lowlands to the [[s:kingdom-of-hungary-1920-1946|Kingdom of Hungary]] (1920-1946), the government moved to [[e:khust|Khust]].
carpatho-ukraine.r: The autonomous government renamed the region Carpatho-[[e:ukraine|Ukraine]], promoted Ukrainian language and culture and formed a paramilitary force, the [[e:carpathian-sich|Carpathian Sich]], which attracted volunteers from [[s:kingdom-of-galicia-and-lodomeria|Galicia]]. Elections in February 1939 gave [[e:avgustyn-voloshyn|Voloshyn]]'s Ukrainian National Union a large majority. The region was poor, mountainous and dependent on [[e:prague|Prague]].
carpatho-ukraine.e: As [[e:germany|Germany]] destroyed [[s:czechoslovakia|Czechoslovakia]], the Carpatho-Ukrainian diet declared independence on 15 March 1939 and elected [[e:avgustyn-voloshyn|Voloshyn]] president. Hungarian troops invaded the same day and occupied the region within days. It was annexed to the Soviet [[s:ukrainian-ssr|Ukrainian SSR]] in 1945.

cook-islands-federation.t: A British protectorate uniting the chiefly governments of the Cook Islands under a federal parliament, before annexation by New Zealand in 1901.
cook-islands-federation.o: Fearing French expansion from [[s:kingdom-of-tahiti|Tahiti]], the ariki of [[s:kingdom-of-rarotonga|Rarotonga]] and other islands accepted a British [[e:protectorate|protectorate]] in 1888. The [[s:new-zealand|New Zealand]] politician [[e:frederick-moss|Frederick Moss]], appointed British Resident in 1891, persuaded the chiefs to form a federal government in the early 1890s, bringing the Kingdom of Rarotonga, [[e:aitutaki|Aitutaki]], [[e:mangaia|Mangaia]] and other islands under one parliament.
cook-islands-federation.r: [[e:makea-takau-ariki|Makea Takau Ariki]] of [[s:kingdom-of-rarotonga|Rarotonga]] was chief of the federation, presiding over a federal council and parliament of ariki and elected members, while the islands kept their own councils. [[e:frederick-moss|Moss]] pushed land and legal reforms but clashed with traders and [[s:new-zealand|New Zealand]] interests, and he was replaced in 1898 by [[e:walter-gudgeon|Walter Gudgeon]]. The economy relied on fruit and copra exports.
cook-islands-federation.e: [[e:richard-seddon|Richard Seddon's]] [[s:new-zealand|New Zealand]] government sought to expand in the Pacific. With the agreement of Makea and other ariki, the islands, together with [[e:niue|Niue]], were annexed to [[e:new-zealand|New Zealand]] on 11 June 1901, becoming the [[s:cook-islands|Cook Islands]].

colony-of-prince-edward-island.t: A small Gulf of St Lawrence colony shaped by its absentee landlord system, and later the birthplace of talks that led to Canadian Confederation.
colony-of-prince-edward-island.o: Known to the French as [[e:prince-edward-island|Île Saint-Jean]], the island passed to [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]] in 1763 and was attached to [[s:colony-of-nova-scotia|Nova Scotia]]. In 1767 it was divided by lottery into 67 lots granted to absentee proprietors in [[e:britain|Britain]], and in 1769 it was made a separate colony with [[e:walter-patterson|Walter Patterson]] as governor. It was renamed Prince Edward Island in 1799.
colony-of-prince-edward-island.r: The colony had an elected assembly from 1773 and responsible government from 1851. Its central problem was the land question: most farmers were tenants paying rent to proprietors overseas, and agitation by the Escheat movement and the Tenant League dominated politics. The economy rested on farming, fishing and shipbuilding, with many settlers from the [[e:scottish-highlands|Scottish Highlands]], Ireland and [[s:acadia|Acadia]].
colony-of-prince-edward-island.e: The [[e:charlottetown-conference|Charlottetown Conference]] of 1864 launched Confederation, but the island at first stayed out of [[s:province-of-canada|Canada]]. Debt from a costly railway, and [[e:ottawa|Ottawa's]] promise to buy out the absentee landlords, brought it into [[e:canada|Canada]] as a province in 1873.

chaulukya-dynasty.t: The Solanki dynasty of Gujarat, whose patronage produced the Modhera Sun temple, the Rani ki Vav stepwell and the marble temples of Mount Abu.
chaulukya-dynasty.o: Around 942 [[e:mularaja|Mularaja]], according to tradition the nephew of the last [[s:chavda-dynasty|Chavda dynasty]] king, seized [[e:patan-gujarat|Anahilavada]] and founded the dynasty. He and his successors expanded across [[e:gujarat|Gujarat]], [[s:cutch-state|Kutch]] and [[e:kathiawar|Saurashtra]], fighting the [[s:chahamanas-of-shakambhari|Chahamanas of Shakambhari]], the [[s:paramara-dynasty|Paramara dynasty]] and the [[s:western-chalukya-empire|Western Chalukya Empire]].
chaulukya-dynasty.r: Under [[e:bhima-i-chaulukya-dynasty|Bhima I]], [[e:mahmud-of-ghazni|Mahmud of Ghazni]] sacked the [[e:somnath-temple|Somnath temple]] in 1025, but the kingdom recovered quickly: the [[e:modhera-sun-temple|Modhera Sun temple]] and the [[s:rani|Rani]] ki Vav stepwell, built by Bhima's queen [[e:udayamati|Udayamati]], date from his reign, and his minister [[e:vimal-shah|Vimala]] built the first [[e:dilwara-temples|Dilwara]] temple at [[e:mount-abu|Mount Abu]]. [[e:jayasimha-siddharaja|Jayasimha Siddharaja]] and [[e:kumarapala-chaulukya-dynasty|Kumarapala]] ruled at the height of Chaulukya power; the Jain scholar [[e:hemachandra|Hemachandra]] served their courts, and Kumarapala became a patron of [[e:jainism|Jainism]]. Maritime trade made [[e:gujarat|Gujarat]] wealthy.
chaulukya-dynasty.e: [[e:mularaja-ii|Mularaja II]] defeated [[e:muhammad-of-ghor|Muhammad of Ghor]] in 1178, but [[e:qutb-ud-din-aibak|Qutb al-Din Aibak]] sacked [[e:patan-gujarat|Anahilavada]] in 1197. The dynasty weakened, and around 1244 the [[e:baghel|Vaghela]] branch took the throne.
