chalcedon.t: Megarian colony on the Asian shore of the Bosporus, mocked as the 'city of the blind' for overlooking the better site of Byzantium opposite.
chalcedon.o: Settlers from [[s:megara|Megara]] founded Chalcedon c. 685 BCE on the Asian side of the [[s:bosporan-kingdom|Bosporus]], opposite the later site of [[s:byzantium|Byzantium]]. [[e:herodotus|Herodotus]] reports the Persian [[e:megabazus|Megabazus]] calling its founders blind for choosing the poorer site when the better one lay across the strait.
chalcedon.r: Chalcedon lived from farming, fishing and [[s:bosporan-kingdom|Bosporus]] traffic, though [[s:byzantium|Byzantium]] controlled the main currents. It came under the [[s:achaemenid-empire|Achaemenid Empire]], then paid tribute in the [[s:delian-league|Delian League]]. The sophist [[e:thrasymachus|Thrasymachus]] came from Chalcedon. In the [[e:hellenistic-period|Hellenistic period]] it was closely tied to [[e:byzantine-empire|Byzantium]] and pressed by the [[s:kingdom-of-bithynia|Kingdom of Bithynia]].
chalcedon.e: When [[e:nicomedes-iv|Nicomedes IV]] left [[s:kingdom-of-bithynia|Bithynia]] to [[e:rome|Rome]] in 74 BCE, Chalcedon passed under Roman rule; [[e:mithridates-vi-of-pontus|Mithridates]] defeated a Roman force there that year. It later hosted the [[e:council-of-chalcedon|Council of Chalcedon]] of 451 CE and is now [[e:kad-koy|Kadıköy]] in [[e:istanbul|Istanbul]].

carvetii.t: People of the Eden valley in Cumbria, known almost entirely from Roman inscriptions naming their self-governing civitas at Carlisle.
carvetii.o: The Carvetii lived in the [[e:river-eden-cumbria|Eden]] valley and around [[e:carlisle|Carlisle]] in what is now [[e:cumbria|Cumbria]]. They are not named by any ancient historian, and they may originally have been a section of the [[s:brigantes|Brigantes]] that the [[e:roman-empire|Romans]] recognised as a separate community after the conquest of the north in the 70s.
carvetii.r: Their existence is known from inscriptions: a 3rd-century milestone from near [[e:brougham|Brougham]] names the civitas Carvetiorum, and a tombstone from Old [[e:penrith|Penrith]] records a councillor of the Carvetii. These show a self-governing community with a council, administered from [[e:carlisle|Luguvalium]], Carlisle, close to [[e:hadrians-wall|Hadrian's Wall]]. The countryside was farmed by native communities living in enclosed settlements.
carvetii.e: As one of the northernmost civitates of [[s:roman-britain|Roman Britain]], the community lasted until Roman rule ended around 410. [[e:carlisle|Carlisle]] remained an important centre afterwards, and the area later formed part of British kingdoms such as [[s:kingdom-of-rheged|Rheged]].

chiefdom-of-kauai.t: The kingdom of Kauaʻi and Niʻihau, the only Hawaiian realm never conquered by Kamehameha I, which joined the Kingdom of Hawaii by agreement in 1810.
chiefdom-of-kauai.o: [[e:kauai|Kauaʻi]] was settled early in Hawaiian history, and by around 1400 its districts were united under a single aliʻi nui, the paramount chief or mōʻī, ruling from [[e:waimea-kauai|Waimea]] on the south-west coast. Island genealogies trace a long line of rulers, though dates before the 18th century rest on oral tradition.
chiefdom-of-kauai.r: Chiefs governed through the kapu system of sacred restrictions and a hierarchy of district and land-section chiefs; commoners farmed irrigated taro and tended fishponds. The wide [[e:kaieiewaho-channel|Kaʻieʻiewaho Channel]] protected [[e:kauai|Kauaʻi]] from invasion. [[e:james-cook|James Cook]] landed at [[e:waimea-kauai|Waimea]] in January 1778, the first European contact with [[e:hawaii|Hawaii]]. [[e:kaeokulani|Kaʻeokulani]], who ruled Kauaʻi and for a time [[e:maui|Maui]], died in 1794, leaving the island to his young son Kaʻumualiʻi.
chiefdom-of-kauai.e: [[e:kamehameha-i|Kamehameha I]] twice prepared invasions, in 1796 and 1804, but storms and epidemic stopped him. In 1810 Kaʻumualiʻi agreed to become his [[e:vassal|vassal]]. After a Russian adventure in 1816 to 1817, Kaʻumualiʻi was taken to [[e:honolulu|Honolulu]] in 1821 and died there in 1824; his son's revolt that year failed.

curonians.t: Seafaring Baltic people of the coast of Courland, feared as pirates across the Baltic, who resisted the Livonian crusade until 1267.
curonians.o: The Curonians lived along the Baltic coast of what is now western [[s:republic-of-latvia|Latvia]] and [[s:grand-duchy-of-lithuania|Lithuania]]. [[e:rimbert|Rimbert's]] life of [[e:ansgar|Ansgar]] describes a Swedish king attacking their stronghold at [[e:apuole|Apuolė]] in 854, and they appear in Norse sagas as both trading partners and raiders. Their land was divided into several districts, each with its own hillforts and leaders.
curonians.r: They combined farming and fishing with seaborne trade and plunder, raiding Danish and Swedish coasts in the 11th to 13th centuries. Their cremation burials and weapons resemble those of Scandinavians. In 1230 a ruler called [[e:lamekins|Lamekins]] made a treaty with the papal legate [[e:baldwin-of-alna|Baldwin of Alna]], accepting baptism in return for keeping his lands.
curonians.e: The [[s:livonian-order|Livonian Order]] and the [[s:bishopric-of-courland|Bishopric of Courland]] conquered them between 1240 and 1267, despite a great uprising after the Order's defeat at [[e:battle-of-durbe|Durbe]] in 1260. A small group of Curonian freemen, the 'Curonian kings', kept a special status into modern times, and the people merged into the [[e:latvians|Latvians]] and [[e:lithuanians|Lithuanians]].

courland-gambia.t: Colony of the small Baltic Duchy of Courland on an island in the Gambia River, part of Duke Jacob Kettler's bold overseas venture.
courland-gambia.o: [[e:jacob-kettler|Duke Jacob Kettler]] of the [[s:duchy-of-courland-and-semigallia|Duchy of Courland and Semigallia]], who built a merchant fleet, acquired [[e:kunta-kinteh-island|St Andrew's Island]] in the [[e:the-gambia|Gambia]] River from local rulers in 1651. His men built Fort Jacob on the island and trading posts on the river banks.
courland-gambia.r: The colony was a small garrisoned trading station dealing in [[e:ivory-trade|ivory]], gold, beeswax, hides and enslaved people. It depended on supplies from [[e:courland|Courland]] and on agreements with the kings of Kombo and [[s:kingdom-of-niumi|Niumi]]. Its distance from [[e:europe|Europe]] and the small size of Courland made it hard to sustain.
courland-gambia.e: While [[e:jacob-kettler|Duke Jacob]] was held prisoner by the Swedes, the [[e:dutch|Dutch]] seized the fort in 1659, and in 1661 the English took it and renamed it [[e:kunta-kinteh-island|James Island]] after the [[e:james-ii-of-england|Duke of York]]. The island, now Kunta Kinteh Island, is a [[e:unesco-world-heritage-site|World Heritage Site]] in [[e:the-gambia|The Gambia]].
courland-gambia.re: Lutheran Christianity, Islam, African traditional religion

canada.t: A federation founded in 1867 from four British colonies that grew into the world's second-largest country and a parliamentary democracy under the Crown.
canada.o: Political deadlock in the [[s:province-of-canada|Province of Canada]], fear of the [[s:united-states|United States]] after its Civil War and the wish for a railway to the Atlantic led to the conferences at [[e:charlottetown-conference|Charlottetown]] and [[s:province-of-quebec|Quebec]] in 1864. The [[e:constitution-act-1867|British North America Act]] united [[e:ontario|Ontario]], [[e:quebec|Quebec]], [[s:colony-of-nova-scotia|Nova Scotia]] and [[s:colony-of-new-brunswick|New Brunswick]] as the [[e:dominion|Dominion]] of Canada on 1 July 1867, with [[e:john-a-macdonald|John A. Macdonald]] as first prime minister.
canada.r: [[s:province-of-canada|Canada]] bought [[s:ruperts-land|Rupert's Land]] in 1870, creating [[e:manitoba|Manitoba]], and added [[e:british-columbia|British Columbia]] in 1871 and [[s:colony-of-prince-edward-island|Prince Edward Island]] in 1873. The Canadian Pacific Railway, finished in 1885, tied the country together, while the numbered treaties and residential schools dispossessed [[e:first-nations-in-canada|First Nations]]. Immigration settled the prairies, and [[e:alberta|Alberta]] and [[e:saskatchewan|Saskatchewan]] became provinces in 1905. Tension between English and [[e:french-canadians|French Canada]] recurred, notably over conscription in both world wars.
canada.e: The [[e:statute-of-westminster-1931|Statute of Westminster]] of 1931 confirmed full independence, [[s:dominion-of-newfoundland|Newfoundland]] joined in 1949, and the constitution was patriated with a Charter of Rights in 1982. [[s:province-of-quebec|Quebec]] voted against [[e:sovereignty|sovereignty]] in 1980 and, by a very narrow margin, in 1995. [[e:nunavut|Nunavut]] was created in 1999 as an Inuit-majority territory.

chengjia.t: The Sichuan empire of Gongsun Shu, the self-styled White Emperor, who held out against the restored Han for eleven years.
chengjia.o: [[e:gongsun-shu|Gongsun Shu]] was a governor in Shu ([[e:sichuan|Sichuan]]) under [[e:wang-mang|Wang Mang's]] [[s:xin-dynasty|Xin dynasty]]. As the [[e:xin-dynasty|Xin]] collapsed he seized the region, took the title King of Shu and in 25 proclaimed himself emperor of Chengjia, with his capital at [[e:chengdu|Chengdu]], the same year [[e:emperor-guangwu-of-han|Liu Xiu]] restored the Han.
chengjia.r: Protected by mountains and supplied by the fertile [[e:chengdu|Chengdu]] plain, Chengjia attracted officials fleeing the chaos in the north. [[e:gongsun-shu|Gongsun Shu]] called himself the White Emperor, after the element of metal, which gave the name to [[e:baidicheng|Baidicheng]] in the [[e:three-gorges|Three Gorges]], and issued iron coins. His rule was cautious and defensive.
chengjia.e: Having conquered the north-west, [[e:emperor-guangwu-of-han|Emperor Guangwu]] turned on Shu: 'having got Long, one longs for Shu.' His generals [[e:cen-peng|Cen Peng]] and [[e:wu-han-general|Wu Han]] advanced up the [[e:yangtze-river|Yangtze]], and in 36 [[e:gongsun-shu|Gongsun Shu]] was mortally wounded outside [[e:chengdu|Chengdu]], which Wu Han then sacked.

canton-of-unterwalden.t: One of the three founding cantons of the Swiss Confederacy, a mountain community on Lake Lucerne that was always split into two self-governing halves.
canton-of-unterwalden.o: The valleys south of [[e:lake-lucerne|Lake Lucerne]], [[e:obwalden|Obwalden]] around [[e:sarnen|Sarnen]] and [[e:nidwalden|Nidwalden]] around [[e:stans|Stans]], were rural communities under scattered lordships, including the [[e:habsburg-dynasty|Habsburgs]]. Nidwalden swore the [[e:federal-charter-of-1291|Federal Charter of 1291]] with the [[s:canton-of-uri|Canton of Uri]] and the [[s:canton-of-schwyz|Canton of Schwyz]], and Obwalden soon joined, so Unterwalden counted among the three original forest cantons of the [[s:old-swiss-confederacy|Old Swiss Confederacy]].
canton-of-unterwalden.r: Each half held its own [[e:landsgemeinde|Landsgemeinde]], an open-air assembly of free men that elected officials and passed laws, and the two shared a single seat at the federal [[e:tagsatzung|Diet]]. The economy rested on [[e:cattle|cattle]], cheese and [[e:mercenary|mercenary]] service abroad. Unterwalden remained firmly Catholic during the [[e:protestant-reformation|Reformation]] and stood with the other inner cantons against [[s:canton-of-zurich|Zürich]] and Bern.
canton-of-unterwalden.e: When [[e:france|France]] imposed the [[s:helvetic-republic|Helvetic Republic]] in 1798, [[e:nidwalden|Nidwalden]] resisted and was crushed in September 1798 with heavy loss of civilian life. After 1803 the two halves re-emerged and today survive as the separate cantons of [[e:obwalden|Obwalden]] and Nidwalden.

cancuen.t: A Maya trading kingdom at the head of navigation on the Pasión river, rich from jade and obsidian, which ended in a massacre of its royal court around 800.
cancuen.o: Cancuén lay where the [[e:pasion-river|Pasión]] river becomes navigable, at the gateway between the Guatemalan highlands and the [[e:peten|Petén]] lowlands. It rose to prominence in the 7th century, around 650, under the patronage of the [[s:kingdom-of-kaan|Kingdom of Kaan]], whose overlord oversaw the accession of a local king in 656.
cancuen.r: Instead of a great temple pyramid, Cancuén's core was a vast palace of some 170 rooms. The city worked jade, pyrite and obsidian brought from the highlands, and controlled river trade. Its greatest king, [[e:taj-chan-ahk|Taj Chan Ahk]], who reigned from 757 to about 795, built much of the palace and a ballcourt.
cancuen.e: Around 800 the last king, [[e:kan-maax|Kan Maax]], his queen and some 30 nobles were killed and their bodies placed in a cistern, and the city was abandoned. The massacre, found in 2005, is vivid evidence of the violence of the Classic collapse.

county-of-delmenhorst.t: North German county of a branch of the Oldenburg counts, seized by the Bishop of Münster for 65 years and reunited with Oldenburg in 1647.
county-of-delmenhorst.o: The counts of [[s:county-of-oldenburg|Oldenburg]] divided their lands in the 13th century, and around 1281 a separate line took Delmenhorst, a castle and town south-west of [[s:free-hanseatic-city-of-bremen|Bremen]], as its seat. The county lay on the lower [[e:weser|Weser]], between the [[s:prince-archbishopric-of-bremen|Prince-Archbishopric of Bremen]] and the Oldenburg lands.
county-of-delmenhorst.r: The county was rural, with marsh and moorland farming. The first Delmenhorst line died out in 1436, and the county returned to [[s:county-of-oldenburg|Oldenburg]]. In 1482 the [[s:prince-bishopric-of-munster|Prince-Bishopric of Münster]] seized it and held it until Count Anton I of Oldenburg recovered it in 1547. The counts introduced [[e:lutheranism|Lutheranism]]. From 1577 a younger Oldenburg branch under [[e:anthony-ii-count-of-delmenhorst|Anton II]] ruled Delmenhorst again.
county-of-delmenhorst.e: When the Delmenhorst line died out in 1647, the county was reunited with the [[s:county-of-oldenburg|County of Oldenburg]]. Both passed to the Danish crown in 1667 and later formed part of the [[s:duchy-of-oldenburg|Duchy of Oldenburg]]. Delmenhorst is now in [[e:lower-saxony|Lower Saxony]].

cr.a: Charlie1965nrw at German Wikipedia (Original text: Charlie1965nrw (Karl-Heinz Meurer))

colony-of-virginia.t: England's first lasting colony in America, founded at Jamestown in 1607, where tobacco, representative government and racial slavery took root together.
colony-of-virginia.o: The [[e:virginia|Virginia]] Company of [[e:london|London]] sent settlers to [[e:jamestown|Jamestown]] on the [[e:james-river|James River]] in 1607, in the heart of the [[s:powhatan-confederacy|Powhatan Confederacy]]. Disease, hunger and conflict killed most early colonists, especially in the [[e:starving-time|Starving Time]] of 1609 to 1610. [[e:john-rolfe|John Rolfe's]] sweet tobacco, first grown around 1612, gave the colony an export crop, and in 1624 the Crown took direct control.
colony-of-virginia.r: In 1619 the House of Burgesses met as the first elected assembly in English America, and the same year the first enslaved Africans arrived at [[e:old-point-comfort|Point Comfort]]. A planter elite grew rich on tobacco worked first by indentured servants and later by enslaved Africans, codified in the slave laws of 1705. The [[e:church-of-england|Church of England]] was established, and the [[e:college-of-william-and-mary|College of William and Mary]] was founded in 1693. Governor [[e:william-berkeley-governor|William Berkeley]]'s rule provoked [[e:bacons-rebellion|Bacon's Rebellion]] in 1676.
colony-of-virginia.e: The capital moved to [[e:williamsburg-virginia|Williamsburg]] in 1699. Virginians such as [[e:patrick-henry|Patrick Henry]], [[e:george-washington|George Washington]] and [[e:thomas-jefferson|Thomas Jefferson]] led resistance to [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]], and in 1776 the colony adopted George Mason's [[e:virginia-declaration-of-rights|Declaration of Rights]] and became an independent commonwealth within the [[s:united-states|United States]].

cr.a: Unknown engraver (from work by Lyon Gardiner Tyler)

county-of-comminges.t: A Pyrenean county around Saint-Bertrand-de-Comminges whose counts fought on the Occitan side in the Albigensian Crusade.
county-of-comminges.o: Counts of Comminges appear in the early 10th century, governing the upper [[e:garonne|Garonne]] valley around the old Roman town of [[e:lugdunum-convenarum|Lugdunum Convenarum]], later Saint-Bertrand-de-Comminges. They were related to the counts of [[e:couserans|Couserans]] and [[e:carcassonne|Carcassonne]] and drifted into the orbit of the counts of [[s:county-of-toulouse|Toulouse]].
county-of-comminges.r: Comminges was a mountainous land of pastoral farming, small towns and pilgrimage, centred on the cathedral of [[e:lugdunum-convenarum|Saint-Bertrand]]. The counts later held Muret near [[s:county-of-toulouse|Toulouse]]. Count [[e:bernard-iv-of-comminges|Bernard IV]] joined [[e:raymond-vi-count-of-toulouse|Raymond VI of Toulouse]] against the crusaders and was present at the battle of Muret in 1213, where [[e:peter-ii-of-aragon|Peter II of Aragon]] was killed.
county-of-comminges.e: The comital line ended with Countess [[e:margaret-countess-of-comminges|Marguerite]], whose disputed inheritance was settled in favour of the crown; [[e:charles-vii-of-france|Charles VII]] annexed Comminges to the [[s:kingdom-of-france|Kingdom of France]] in 1454. The name survives as a region of the [[e:haute-garonne|Haute-Garonne]].

county-of-rantzau.t: Tiny Holstein county that won imperial status for the Rantzau family and ended after a fratricide.
county-of-rantzau.o: [[e:christian-rantzau|Christian zu Rantzau]], a Danish statesman, bought the [[s:county-of-holstein|Holstein]] district of [[e:barmstedt|Barmstedt]] from the Duke of [[s:duchy-of-holstein-gottorp|Holstein-Gottorp]] in 1649. In 1650 [[e:ferdinand-iii-holy-roman-emperor|Emperor Ferdinand III]] raised him to imperial count and made Barmstedt an immediate imperial county, outside the duchy of Holstein.
county-of-rantzau.r: The county covered only a few villages and the market town of [[e:elmshorn|Elmshorn]], governed from [[e:barmstedt|Barmstedt]] and a castle on an island in the Rantzau lake. Its counts enjoyed full jurisdiction but depended on their Danish connections. In 1721 Count Christian Detlev was shot dead, and his brother [[e:wilhelm-adolf-count-of-rantzau|Wilhelm Adolf]] was arrested and convicted of arranging the killing.
county-of-rantzau.e: [[e:wilhelm-adolf-count-of-rantzau|Wilhelm Adolf]] died in prison in 1734, but the Danish king had already occupied the county, and in 1726 it was annexed to [[e:denmark|Denmark]] under a prior agreement, becoming a district of [[s:county-of-holstein|Holstein]]. It later passed to [[e:kingdom-of-prussia|Prussia]] with [[s:provisional-government-of-schleswig-holstein|Schleswig-Holstein]] in 1867.

chitral-state.t: A mountain kingdom of the Hindu Kush ruled by its Mehtars, scene of the famous siege of 1895 and part of Pakistan until 1969.
chitral-state.o: The [[e:katur-dynasty|Katur dynasty]] took power in Chitral in the later 16th century, ruling the high valleys of the [[e:kunar-river|Kunar]] (Chitral) river beneath [[e:tirich-mir|Tirich Mir]]. The rulers took the title Mehtar and contended with neighbouring [[s:principality-of-badakhshan|Badakhshan]], the Kushwaqt rulers of upper Chitral and the [[e:dards|Dards]] of [[e:gilgit|Gilgit]].
chitral-state.r: The Mehtar ruled through a hierarchy of nobles over a population of farmers and herders speaking [[e:khowar-language|Khowar]], with [[e:sunni-islam|Sunni]] and [[e:ismailism|Ismaili]] Muslim communities. Aman ul-Mulk, who died in 1892, united upper and lower Chitral. The succession war after his death led to the siege of the British garrison in Chitral fort in 1895, its relief, and closer British control.
chitral-state.e: Chitral acceded to [[s:islamic-republic-of-pakistan|Pakistan]] in 1947 under Muzaffar ul-Mulk. Its princely status was abolished in 1969, when it became a district of [[e:pakistan|Pakistan's]] [[e:north-west-frontier-province|North-West Frontier Province]], now Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.

county-of-waldburg.t: The upper Swabian territory of the Truchsesses of Waldburg, whose Georg, the 'Bauernjörg', crushed the Peasants' War of 1525.
county-of-waldburg.o: The lords of [[e:house-of-waldburg|Waldburg]] near [[s:free-imperial-city-of-ravensburg|Ravensburg]] served the [[e:hohenstaufen|Hohenstaufen]] as imperial stewards (Truchsess). In the 14th and 15th centuries they acquired lands around [[e:wolfegg|Wolfegg]], [[e:zeil-castle|Zeil]] and [[e:bad-waldsee|Waldsee]], and after a division in 1429 the branches of the family built up a cluster of lordships and counties in upper Swabia.
county-of-waldburg.r: [[e:georg-truchsess-von-waldburg|Georg III, Truchsess of Waldburg]], commanded the army of the [[e:swabian-league|Swabian League]] that crushed the peasant revolt in 1525, earning the nickname 'Bauernjörg'. The family remained Catholic and supplied churchmen such as [[e:otto-truchsess-von-waldburg|Otto Truchsess von Waldburg]], cardinal and [[e:bishop|bishop]] of [[s:free-imperial-city-of-augsburg|Augsburg]]. Repeated partitions created the [[e:house-of-waldburg|Waldburg]]-[[e:wolfegg|Wolfegg]], Waldburg-[[e:zeil-castle|Zeil]] and other lines, which ranked as imperial counts from the 17th century.
county-of-waldburg.e: Mediatised in 1806, the [[e:house-of-waldburg|Waldburg]] lands passed mainly to the [[s:kingdom-of-wurttemberg|Kingdom of Württemberg]], with some under [[e:bavaria|Bavaria]]. The princely families of Waldburg-[[e:zeil-castle|Zeil]] and Waldburg-[[e:wolfegg|Wolfegg]] still own their castles and estates.

county-palatine-of-pembroke.t: A Norman marcher lordship in south-west Wales, base of Strongbow's invasion of Ireland and birthplace of Henry VII.
county-palatine-of-pembroke.o: [[e:arnulf-de-montgomery|Arnulf de Montgomery]] built the first castle at [[e:pembroke-pembrokeshire|Pembroke]] in 1093, and it held out against Welsh counter-attacks. In 1138 [[e:stephen-king-of-england|King Stephen]] made [[e:gilbert-de-clare-1st-earl-of-pembroke|Gilbert de Clare]] Earl of Pembroke, giving the lordship palatine powers. English and Flemish settlers occupied south [[e:pembrokeshire|Pembrokeshire]], creating the 'Little [[e:england|England]] beyond [[e:wales|Wales]]'.
county-palatine-of-pembroke.r: The earls exercised royal-style jurisdiction within the county. [[e:humphrey-gilbert|Gilbert's]] son [[e:richard-de-clare-2nd-earl-of-pembroke|Richard de Clare]], Strongbow, led the invasion of Ireland in 1170 from here. [[e:william-marshal-1st-earl-of-pembroke|William Marshal]], who married Strongbow's heiress, rebuilt [[e:pembroke-castle|Pembroke Castle]] with its great round keep. Later holders included the [[e:valence|Valence]] and Hastings families and [[e:jasper-tudor|Jasper Tudor]], whose nephew [[e:henry-vii-of-england|Henry VII]] was born in the castle in 1457.
county-palatine-of-pembroke.e: The [[e:laws-in-wales-acts-1535-and-1542|Laws in Wales Act]] of 1536 ended its special status, and [[e:pembroke-pembrokeshire|Pembroke]] became the core of [[e:pembrokeshire|Pembrokeshire]]. The earldom title continued in the Herbert family.

county-of-mansfeld.t: A county on the eastern edge of the Harz whose copper mines made it rich and in whose town Martin Luther was born.
county-of-mansfeld.o: Counts of Mansfeld appear around 1069, with their castle above the town of Mansfeld east of the [[e:harz|Harz]]. The original line died out in 1229, and the lands passed to the lords of [[e:querfurt|Querfurt]], who took the name Mansfeld and ruled for the rest of the county's history.
county-of-mansfeld.r: Mansfeld's wealth came from [[e:copper|copper]] shale mining, one of the largest copper industries in medieval [[e:europe|Europe]]. [[e:martin-luther|Martin Luther]] was born in nearby [[e:eisleben|Eisleben]] in 1483 and grew up in Mansfeld, where his father ran smelters. The counts adopted the [[e:protestant-reformation|Reformation]] early, and Luther died in Eisleben in 1546 after mediating a dispute between them.
county-of-mansfeld.e: Heavy debts and repeated divisions among many branches weakened the counts, and from 1570 the [[s:electorate-of-saxony|Electorate of Saxony]] and the [[s:archbishopric-of-magdeburg|Archbishopric of Magdeburg]] took the county into sequestration. The last count died in 1780, and the lands were divided between [[e:saxony|Saxony]] and [[e:kingdom-of-prussia|Prussia]].
county-of-mansfeld.la: Middle and Early New High German

catalan-republic-1641.t: A Catalan republic proclaimed during the Reapers' War, which lasted barely a week before Catalonia placed itself under the French king.
catalan-republic-1641.o: [[s:principality-of-catalonia|Catalonia]] rose against [[e:philip-iv-of-spain|Philip IV]] in 1640 in the [[e:reapers-war|Reapers' War]], provoked by the billeting of royal troops and the [[e:gaspar-de-guzman-count-duke-of-olivares|Count-Duke of Olivares's]] demands. As a royal army advanced on [[e:barcelona|Barcelona]], [[e:pau-claris|Pau Claris]], president of the [[e:generalitat-de-catalunya|Generalitat]], proclaimed a Catalan Republic under French protection in January 1641.
catalan-republic-1641.r: The republic was an emergency regime run by the [[e:generalitat-de-catalunya|Generalitat]] and [[e:barcelona|Barcelona's]] councils, preoccupied with defence. Unable to resist Castilian forces alone, its leaders quickly decided that French support required a monarch.
catalan-republic-1641.e: On 23 January 1641 the Catalan authorities recognised [[e:louis-xiii-of-france|Louis XIII of France]] as Count of [[e:barcelona|Barcelona]], ending the republic. Days later Catalan and French troops defeated the royal army at [[e:battle-of-montjuic-1641|Montjuïc]]. [[e:pau-claris|Claris]] died in February, and [[s:principality-of-catalonia|Catalonia]] returned to [[e:philip-iv-of-spain|Philip IV]]'s rule in 1652, losing [[e:roussillon|Roussillon]] to [[e:france|France]] in 1659.

county-of-roussillon.t: A Catalan county north of the Pyrenees centred on Perpignan, bequeathed to the Crown of Aragon in 1172 and French since 1659.
county-of-roussillon.o: [[e:roussillon|Roussillon]], named after the ancient town of [[e:ruscino|Ruscino]], became a Carolingian county in the early 9th century, part of the [[s:marca-hispanica|Marca Hispanica]]. It was long held with Empúries by a single comital family descended from Sunyer, until the two were divided in 991 and Roussillon got its own line of counts.
county-of-roussillon.r: The counts ruled from [[e:perpignan|Perpignan]], which grew into a prosperous town on the route between [[s:principality-of-catalonia|Catalonia]] and [[e:languedoc|Languedoc]]. The economy rested on the fertile plain of the Têt, cloth making and trade. The county shared the Catalan language and laws, and monasteries such as [[e:sant-genis-de-fontanes|Sant Genís de Fontanes]] and [[e:sant-andreu-de-sureda|Sant Andreu de Sureda]] flourished on its plain and foothills.
county-of-roussillon.e: The last count, [[e:girard-ii-of-roussillon|Girard II]], died without heirs in 1172 and left [[e:roussillon|Roussillon]] to [[e:alfonso-ii-of-aragon|Alfonso II of Aragon]] and [[e:barcelona|Barcelona]]. It later formed part of the [[s:kingdom-of-majorca|Kingdom of Majorca]], and the [[e:treaty-of-the-pyrenees|Treaty of the Pyrenees]] of 1659 gave it to [[e:france|France]].

county-of-tecklenburg.t: A Westphalian hill county north of Münster, often at war with its episcopal neighbours, which Prussia bought in 1707.
county-of-tecklenburg.o: The counts of Tecklenburg appear around 1140, with a castle on the [[e:teutoburg-forest|Teutoburg Forest]] ridge north of Münster. They were advocates of the bishoprics of Münster and [[e:osnabruck|Osnabrück]], which gave them influence and frequent conflicts with the [[e:bishop|bishops]].
county-of-tecklenburg.r: The county was small and rural, ruled from Tecklenburg castle, with linen weaving an important local trade. In the 1260s it passed to the counts of [[s:county-of-bentheim|Bentheim]], and in 1328 to the [[s:county-of-schwerin|Schwerin]] family. Count Conrad introduced the [[e:protestant-reformation|Reformation]] in 1527, and the county later adopted the Reformed faith.
county-of-tecklenburg.e: Inheritance disputes between the [[s:county-of-bentheim|Bentheim-Tecklenburg]] family and the counts of Solms-[[e:braunfels|Braunfels]] led to a long court case. In 1707 [[e:kingdom-of-prussia|Prussia]] bought the [[s:county-of-solms-braunfels|Solms]] claims and took the county. It became part of the Prussian province of [[e:westphalia|Westphalia]] in 1815.

county-of-pallars.t: A remote Pyrenean county in the Noguera Pallaresa valley that broke away from Frankish Toulouse and split in two in 1011.
county-of-pallars.o: [[e:pallars|Pallars]], the mountain valleys of the [[e:noguera-pallaresa|Noguera Pallaresa]] in north-western [[s:principality-of-catalonia|Catalonia]], was a district of the [[s:county-of-toulouse|County of Toulouse]] until around 872, when [[e:ramon-i-of-pallars-and-ribagorza|Ramon I]] made Pallars and [[e:ribagorza|Ribagorza]] a hereditary lordship of his own.
county-of-pallars.r: The county was a land of herders and small farmers in high valleys, with castles guarding against raids from the Muslim lands to the south and monasteries such as Santa Maria de Gerri. Its counts stayed largely independent of both the [[s:franks|Franks]] and [[e:barcelona|Barcelona]], and ruled with little written administration.
county-of-pallars.e: After [[e:ramon-i-of-pallars-and-ribagorza|Ramon I]]'s death [[e:ribagorza|Ribagorza]] separated. In 1011 [[e:pallars|Pallars]] was divided between two brothers into [[e:county-of-pallars-jussa|Pallars Jussà]] and [[e:county-of-pallars-sobira|Pallars Sobirà]]. Pallars Jussà passed to the counts of [[e:barcelona|Barcelona]] in 1192, while Pallars Sobirà survived until it was confiscated by the [[s:crown-of-aragon|Crown of Aragon]] in 1487.

county-of-gruyere.t: A Swiss Alpine county known for cheese and cattle, whose counts went bankrupt and lost their lands to Fribourg and Bern.
county-of-gruyere.o: The first known count of Gruyère, Rudolf, appears around 1073 to 1115 in the [[e:sarine|Saane]] valley of the western Swiss [[e:alps|Alps]]. The counts built their castle above the small town of [[e:gruyeres|Gruyères]] and ruled a territory of pastures and villages on the borderland between French- and German-speaking [[s:swiss-confederation|Switzerland]].
county-of-gruyere.r: The county lived from [[e:cattle|cattle]] and dairying; the hard cheese produced there gave its name to Gruyère cheese. The counts were [[e:vassal|vassals]] of [[s:county-of-savoy|Savoy]] and allied with Bern and [[s:canton-of-fribourg|Fribourg]]. The town and castle of [[e:gruyeres|Gruyères]] were among the most picturesque in the region.
county-of-gruyere.e: Count Michel of Gruyère fell heavily into debt, and in 1554 to 1555 his creditors, the cities of [[s:canton-of-fribourg|Fribourg]] and Bern, divided the county between them. Fribourg kept [[e:gruyeres|Gruyères]] and the lower valley, while Bern took the upper [[e:sarine|Saane]] valley ([[e:saanen|Saanen]]). The castle is now a museum.

commune-of-orvieto.t: A Guelph hill-town republic on a volcanic crag in Umbria, a frequent papal residence and builder of one of Italy's most splendid Gothic cathedrals.
commune-of-orvieto.o: Orvieto, perched on a tufa cliff above the [[e:paglia|Paglia]] valley, had consuls by 1157. The commune extended its rule over much of the surrounding countryside towards [[e:lake-bolsena|Lake Bolsena]] and the [[e:maremma|Tuscan Maremma]].
commune-of-orvieto.r: Orvieto was ruled by consuls, then a podestà and a popular government of the Seven. Strongly Guelph, it often hosted popes in the 13th century, including [[e:pope-urban-iv|Urban IV]], at whose court [[e:thomas-aquinas|Thomas Aquinas]] taught. The cathedral, begun in 1290, was linked to the Eucharistic miracle of [[e:bolsena|Bolsena]] and the feast of [[e:corpus-christi-feast|Corpus Christi]]; [[e:luca-signorelli|Luca Signorelli]] later painted its frescoes. The Guelph Monaldeschi and Ghibelline Filippeschi, both named by [[e:dante-alighieri|Dante]], fought for control.
commune-of-orvieto.e: Weakened by faction and the [[e:black-death|Black Death]], the commune fell to strongmen in the 1340s. In 1354 [[e:gil-alvarez-carrillo-de-albornoz|Cardinal Albornoz]] restored papal authority, and Orvieto remained part of the [[s:papal-states|Papal States]].

colony-of-the-bay-islands.t: Brief British colony on Roatán and the neighbouring islands off Honduras, whose creation clashed with a treaty with the United States.
colony-of-the-bay-islands.o: From the 1830s English-speaking settlers, many from the [[s:cayman-islands|Cayman Islands]] and other British [[e:caribbean|Caribbean]] islands, settled on [[e:roatan|Roatán]], [[e:utila|Utila]] and [[e:guanaja|Guanaja]], where [[e:garifuna|Garifuna]] communities already lived. The superintendent of [[s:belize|Belize]] claimed the islands for [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]], and in 1852 [[e:britain|Britain]] proclaimed them the Colony of the [[e:bay-islands|Bay Islands]], under the oversight of the Jamaican governor.
colony-of-the-bay-islands.r: The colony was small, with a few thousand inhabitants living by fishing, turtling, coconuts and fruit trade with [[e:new-orleans|New Orleans]], and was run by a lieutenant governor and local council at [[e:coxen-hole|Coxen Hole]]. The [[s:united-states|United States]] protested that the colony breached the [[e:clayton-bulwer-treaty|Clayton-Bulwer Treaty]] of 1850, in which both powers had agreed not to colonise [[e:central-america|Central America]]. [[s:republic-of-honduras|Honduras]] also claimed the islands as its own.
colony-of-the-bay-islands.e: Seeking better relations with [[e:washington-dc|Washington]], [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]] signed the [[e:wyke-cruz-treaty|Wyke-Cruz Treaty]] with [[s:republic-of-honduras|Honduras]] in 1859 and handed over the islands in 1860. Their English-speaking, largely Protestant population remained, and the islands are now a [[e:departement|department]] of Honduras.

county-of-provence.t: The Mediterranean county between the Rhône and the Alps that passed from Catalan to Angevin counts and was bequeathed to France in 1481.
county-of-provence.o: Under the kings of [[e:arles|Arles]], Boso of Arles held comital power in Provence around the mid-10th century. His son [[e:william-i-of-provence|William the Liberator]] drove the Saracens from their base at [[e:fraxinetum|Fraxinetum]] in 973 and became effective ruler of the region, founding the first comital dynasty.
county-of-provence.r: In 1112 the heiress [[e:douce-i-countess-of-provence|Douce]] married [[e:ramon-berenguer-iii-of-barcelona|Ramon Berenguer III of Barcelona]], bringing Catalan counts who fostered troubadour culture and [[e:mediterranean|Mediterranean]] trade. [[e:ramon-berenguer-iv-count-of-provence|Raymond Berengar IV]]'s daughter [[e:beatrice-of-provence|Beatrice]] married [[e:charles-i-of-anjou|Charles of Anjou]] in 1246, and the Angevin counts, also kings of [[e:naples|Naples]], ruled from [[e:aix-en-provence|Aix]] and Naples. The popes settled at [[e:avignon|Avignon]], on the county's edge, in the 14th century.
county-of-provence.e: [[e:joanna-i-of-naples|Queen Joanna I]] adopted Louis I of [[s:county-of-anjou|Anjou]], whose line held Provence until 1481. That year [[e:charles-iv-duke-of-anjou|Charles of Maine]], heir of [[e:rene-of-anjou|René of Anjou]], bequeathed it to [[e:louis-xi|Louis XI]], and Provence was united with the [[s:kingdom-of-france|Kingdom of France]], while keeping its own estates and parliament at [[e:aix-en-provence|Aix]].

chad-french-colony.t: France's vast colony around Lake Chad, the first territory in the French empire to rally to de Gaulle in 1940.
chad-french-colony.o: French expeditions converged on the Chari after 1897, and the defeat of [[s:rabih-az-zubayrs-state|Rabih az-Zubayr's state]] at [[e:kousseri|Kousseri]] in 1900 opened the region. It was administered as a military territory, then joined to [[s:ubangi-shari|Ubangi-Shari]], and became a separate colony in 1920 within [[s:french-equatorial-africa|French Equatorial Africa]]. [[e:ndjamena|Fort-Lamy]], now N'Djamena, was its capital.
chad-french-colony.r: French control was weak in the Muslim north, where the [[s:wadai-empire|Wadai Empire]] and Saharan peoples resisted for years. The south, home to the [[e:sara-people|Sara]] and other peoples, was made to grow [[e:cotton|cotton]] for export from the 1920s, and supplied soldiers and forced labour. In August 1940 Governor [[e:felix-eboue|Félix Éboué]] declared for [[s:free-france|Free France]], and [[e:philippe-leclerc-de-hauteclocque|Leclerc]]'s forces struck north from [[e:chad|Chad]] into [[e:libya|Libya]].
chad-french-colony.e: [[e:chad|Chad]] became an autonomous republic in 1958 and independent on 11 August 1960 under [[e:francois-tombalbaye|François Tombalbaye]]. Tensions between north and south inherited from colonial rule soon led to civil war.

clazomenae.t: Ionian city on the Gulf of Smyrna, birthplace of the philosopher Anaxagoras, which moved onto an offshore islet to escape Persian attack.
clazomenae.o: Clazomenae was founded by Ionian settlers, traditionally from [[s:colophon|Colophon]], on the southern shore of the [[e:gulf-of-izmir|Gulf of Smyrna]] c. 1000 BCE. It joined the [[s:ionian-league|Ionian League]] and in the 7th century BCE helped found [[s:abdera|Abdera]], a first attempt later renewed by [[s:teos|Teos]], and traded at [[e:naucratis|Naucratis]] in [[e:egypt|Egypt]].
clazomenae.r: Clazomenae was known for painted terracotta sarcophagi and [[e:olive-oil|olive oil]]. After the [[e:ionian-revolt|Ionian Revolt]] its people moved to an islet just offshore for safety. [[e:anaxagoras|Anaxagoras]], who taught that mind orders the cosmos, was born there c. 500 BCE. It belonged to the [[s:delian-league|Delian League]] and was fought over during the [[e:peloponnesian-war|Peloponnesian War]].
clazomenae.e: The [[e:peace-of-antalcidas|King's Peace]] of 387 BCE named Clazomenae as Persian territory. Alexander linked the island to the mainland by a causeway. Under Hellenistic kings and then [[e:rome|Rome]], from 133 BCE in the province of Asia, it slowly declined.

captaincy-of-pernambuco.t: Brazil's most successful hereditary captaincy, whose sugar plantations made it the world's leading sugar producer in the late 16th century.
captaincy-of-pernambuco.o: In 1534 [[e:john-iii-of-portugal|King John III]] granted [[e:duarte-coelho|Duarte Coelho]] the captaincy of Pernambuco, which he called Nova Lusitânia, on the northeastern coast of [[s:new-republic-brazil|Brazil]]. Coelho arrived in 1535 and founded [[e:olinda|Olinda]], which became the capital. He fought the [[e:caete|Caeté]] and other indigenous groups and established [[e:sugar-plantation|sugar]] mills with financing from [[e:lisbon|Lisbon]] and [[e:antwerp|Antwerp]].
captaincy-of-pernambuco.r: Pernambuco prospered on [[e:sugar-plantation|sugar]] grown on large plantations with mills called engenhos, worked first by enslaved indigenous people and then by enslaved Africans. [[e:olinda|Olinda]] and the port of [[e:recife|Recife]] were among the richest towns in the [[e:americas|Americas]]. From 1630 to 1654 the [[e:dutch|Dutch]] occupied Pernambuco as [[s:dutch-brazil|Dutch Brazil]]. Rivalry between Olinda's planters and Recife's merchants led to the [[e:war-of-the-mascates|War of the Mascates]] in 1710 and 1711.
captaincy-of-pernambuco.e: The crown took direct control in 1654. Pernambuco led the anti-[[s:third-portuguese-republic|Portuguese Republic]] of Pernambuco in 1817, and became a province of the [[e:brazilian-empire|Empire of Brazil]] after independence in 1822. [[e:olinda|Olinda's]] historic centre became a [[e:unesco-world-heritage-site|UNESCO World Heritage Site]] in 1982.

cossack-hetmanate.t: The Cossack state created by Bohdan Khmelnytsky's uprising, which governed central Ukraine under hetmans until Catherine the Great abolished it.
cossack-hetmanate.o: In 1648 [[e:bohdan-khmelnytsky|Bohdan Khmelnytsky]] led the [[e:zaporozhian-cossacks|Zaporozhian Cossacks]] and peasants in a rebellion against the [[s:polish-lithuanian-commonwealth|Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth]]. After victories at [[e:battle-of-zhovti-vody|Zhovti Vody]] and [[s:chersonesus-taurica|Korsun]], the [[e:treaty-of-zboriv|Treaty of Zboriv]] in 1649 recognised a Cossack-ruled territory with its capital at [[e:chyhyryn|Chyhyryn]]. In 1654, at [[e:pereiaslav|Pereiaslav]], Khmelnytsky accepted the protection of the [[s:tsardom-of-russia|Tsardom of Russia]].
cossack-hetmanate.r: The Hetmanate was divided into [[e:cossacks|Cossack]] regiments that served as both military and administrative units, led by an elected [[e:hetman|hetman]] and a council of senior officers. [[e:eastern-orthodox-church|Orthodox]] culture flourished, with the [[e:kyiv-mohyla-academy|Kyiv-Mohyla Academy]] as its intellectual centre. After [[e:bohdan-khmelnytsky|Khmelnytsky]]'s death, the period called the Ruin brought civil war and division along the [[e:dnieper|Dnieper]] by the [[e:truce-of-andrusovo|Truce of Andrusovo]] in 1667.
cossack-hetmanate.e: [[e:hetman|Hetman]] [[e:ivan-mazepa|Ivan Mazepa]] sided with [[e:charles-xii-of-sweden|Charles XII of Sweden]], and after their defeat at [[e:battle-of-poltava|Poltava]] in 1709 [[e:russia|Russia]] steadily reduced the Hetmanate's autonomy. [[e:catherine-the-great|Catherine II]] forced the last hetman, [[e:kyrylo-rozumovsky|Kyrylo Rozumovsky]], to resign in 1764, and the regimental system was abolished by 1781.

captaincy-of-porto-seguro.t: A hereditary captaincy on the coast where Cabral first landed in 1500, whose settlement struggled against indigenous resistance and economic decline.
captaincy-of-porto-seguro.o: In 1534 [[e:john-iii-of-portugal|King John III]] granted the Captaincy of [[e:porto|Porto]] Seguro, in the south of modern [[e:bahia|Bahia]], to [[e:pero-do-campo-tourinho|Pero do Campo Tourinho]]. The coast included the place where [[e:pedro-alvares-cabral|Pedro Álvares Cabral]] had landed in 1500. Tourinho founded the town of Porto Seguro and several villages in 1535.
captaincy-of-porto-seguro.r: The captaincy grew [[e:sugar-plantation|sugar]] and [[e:brazilwood|brazilwood]] but remained small. [[e:pero-do-campo-tourinho|Tourinho]] was denounced by settlers to the [[e:portuguese-inquisition|Inquisition]] and sent to [[e:lisbon|Lisbon]] in 1546. Attacks by the [[e:aimore|Aimoré]] people repeatedly devastated settlements, and [[e:jesuits|Jesuit]] missions were founded among indigenous groups. The captaincy passed through several noble families, including the [[e:duke-of-aveiro|Dukes of Aveiro]], while [[e:salvador|Salvador]] to the north overshadowed it.
captaincy-of-porto-seguro.e: In 1759, as part of [[e:marquis-of-pombal|Pombal]]'s reforms ending private captaincies, the crown took back [[e:porto|Porto]] Seguro, and it was later attached to [[e:bahia|Bahia]]. Its coast is today known as the Discovery Coast, whose Atlantic Forest reserves are a [[e:unesco-world-heritage-site|UNESCO World Heritage Site]].

carnutes.t: Gallic people of the middle Loire, whose land held the annual assembly of the druids and whose massacre at Cenabum began the revolt of 52 BCE.
carnutes.o: The Carnutes lived between the [[e:seine|Seine]] and the [[e:loire|Loire]], around [[e:chartres|Autricum]] (Chartres) and [[e:orleans|Cenabum]] (Orléans). Caesar reports that their territory was considered the centre of all [[e:gaul|Gaul]], where the druids met each year in a sacred place to judge disputes.
carnutes.r: They were ruled by a nobility, and Caesar installed [[e:tasgetius|Tasgetius]] as their king, but he was murdered in 54 BCE. [[e:orleans|Cenabum]], on the [[e:loire|Loire]], was a busy trading town where Roman merchants lived.
carnutes.e: In early 52 BCE the Carnutes killed the Roman traders at [[e:orleans|Cenabum]], the signal for the revolt of [[e:vercingetorix|Vercingetorix]]. Caesar sacked the town and in 51 BCE executed their leader [[e:gutuater|Gutuater]]. Under [[e:rome|Rome]] [[e:chartres|Autricum]] became Chartres and Cenabum was refounded as Aurelianum, later Orléans.

commune-of-treviso.t: The city-republic at the heart of the 'joyful March', whose courtly culture under the da Camino lords was praised by Dante.
commune-of-treviso.o: Treviso, north of [[e:venice|Venice]], had a commune of consuls in the 12th century and joined the [[s:veronese-league|Veronese League]] in 1164 and then the [[s:lombard-league|Lombard League]]. It dominated the [[e:march-of-treviso|March of Treviso]], a region of rivers and fertile plain between the [[e:alps|Alps]] and the lagoon.
commune-of-treviso.r: The commune was governed by consuls and later a podestà. Under [[e:ezzelino-iii-da-romano|Ezzelino III da Romano's]] brother [[e:alberico-da-romano|Alberico]] it suffered harsh rule until 1259. The da Camino family then dominated; [[e:gherardo-da-camino|Gherardo da Camino]], lord from 1283 to 1306, kept a brilliant court that [[e:dante-alighieri|Dante]] praised, and the region's festive life earned it the name Marca gioiosa. Treviso traded with [[e:venice|Venice]] and the Alpine valleys.
commune-of-treviso.e: [[e:cangrande-i-della-scala|Cangrande della Scala]] took Treviso in 1329, joining it to the [[s:lordship-of-verona|Lordship of Verona]]. In 1339 it submitted to the [[s:republic-of-venice|Republic of Venice]], its first major mainland possession, which held it until 1797.

county-of-isenburg-budingen.t: A Wetterau county of the house of Isenburg, centred on Büdingen castle, that sheltered religious dissenters in the 18th century.
county-of-isenburg-budingen.o: The house of Isenburg held lands in the [[e:wetterau|Wetterau]] and around [[e:budingen|Büdingen]] from the 13th century. A division of the family's possessions in 1517 created the Büdingen line alongside the Birstein branch, and further partitions followed in the 17th century.
county-of-isenburg-budingen.r: The counts ruled a hilly, wooded territory from [[e:budingen|Büdingen's]] walled town and castle. They adopted the [[e:protestant-reformation|Reformation]] and later [[e:calvinism|Calvinism]]. Witch trials in the 16th and 17th centuries were severe. In 1712 Count Ernst Casimir issued an edict of tolerance that drew [[e:community-of-true-inspiration|Inspirationists]], [[e:moravian-church|Moravian Brethren]] and other dissenters to the Ronneburg and Marienborn.
county-of-isenburg-budingen.e: In 1806 the county was mediatised and placed under the [[s:principality-of-isenburg|Principality of Isenburg]], and in 1816 it passed to the [[s:grand-duchy-of-hesse|Grand Duchy of Hesse]]. The princes of Ysenburg-[[e:budingen|Büdingen]] still own Büdingen castle.

colony-of-guadeloupe.t: French sugar colony in the Lesser Antilles, where slavery was abolished, restored and abolished again, now an overseas department of France.
colony-of-guadeloupe.o: [[e:charles-lienard-de-lolive|Charles Liénard de l'Olive]] and [[e:jean-du-plessis-dossonville|Jean du Plessis d'Ossonville]] landed in 1635 for the [[e:compagnie-des-iles-de-lamerique|Compagnie des Îles d'Amérique]]. Settlers fought the [[e:kalinago|Kalinago]], who were driven off within a few decades. The colony passed to the [[e:french-west-india-company|French West India Company]] in 1664 and then to the crown in 1674.
colony-of-guadeloupe.r: A royal governor ruled from [[e:basse-terre|Basse-Terre]], and [[e:pointe-a-pitre|Pointe-à-Pitre]] grew into the main commercial port. [[e:sugar-plantation|Sugar plantations]] worked by enslaved Africans dominated the economy, regulated by the [[e:code-noir|Code Noir]] of 1685. [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]] occupied the island in 1759 to 1763 and again in later wars. During the [[e:french-revolution|Revolution]], [[e:victor-hugues|Victor Hugues]] abolished [[e:slavery|slavery]] in 1794, but [[e:napoleon|Napoleon]] restored it in 1802, crushing the resistance of [[e:louis-delgres|Louis Delgrès]].
colony-of-guadeloupe.e: [[e:slavery|Slavery]] was finally abolished in 1848 through [[e:victor-schoelcher|Victor Schoelcher's]] decree, after which indentured workers came from [[e:india|India]]. A law of 19 March 1946 made Guadeloupe an overseas [[e:departement|department]] of [[e:france|France]], ending its colonial status; it remains a French department and region today.

chuda-state.t: A Jhala Rajput state of the Jhalawad district of northern Kathiawar, one of several Jhala branches.
chuda-state.o: Chuda was held by a branch of the [[e:jhala|Jhala Rajputs]] of [[s:wadhwan-state|Wadhwan State]] and emerged as a separate holding in 1707. Its seat was the small town of Chuda in the [[e:cotton|cotton]] country of [[e:jhalawad|Jhalawad]].
chuda-state.r: The Thakor ruled a territory of [[e:cotton|cotton]] and grain villages, paying tribute to the [[e:gaekwads|Gaekwads]] and then coming under British supervision in the [[e:kathiawar-agency|Kathiawar Agency]] after 1807. Few further details of its rulers are widely recorded.
chuda-state.e: Chuda merged into the [[s:saurashtra-state|United State of Saurashtra]] in 1948 and became part of [[e:gujarat|Gujarat]] in 1960, in [[e:surendranagar-district|Surendranagar district]].

county-of-holstein.t: A north German county between the Elbe and the Eider, ruled by the Schauenburg counts, whose union with Schleswig shaped centuries of Danish-German history.
county-of-holstein.o: In 1111 [[e:lothair-iii-holy-roman-emperor|Duke Lothair of Saxony]] granted the County of Holstein and [[e:stormarn|Stormarn]] to Adolf I of [[s:county-of-schaumburg|Schauenburg]]. His successors pushed into Slavic [[e:wagria|Wagria]], and [[e:adolf-ii-of-holstein|Adolf II]] founded [[s:free-and-hanseatic-city-of-lubeck|Lübeck]] in 1143. Holstein was lost to [[e:denmark|Denmark]] in 1201 but regained after the [[e:battle-of-bornhoved|Battle of Bornhöved]] in 1227.
county-of-holstein.r: The county repeatedly divided into lines such as Holstein-[[e:kiel|Kiel]], Holstein-Plön and Holstein-Rendsburg. [[e:gerhard-iii-count-of-holstein-rendsburg|Gerhard III the Great of Holstein-Rendsburg]] dominated [[e:denmark|Denmark]] in the 1330s, ruling [[e:jutland|Jutland]] until his murder in 1340. Holstein's counts gained the [[s:duchy-of-schleswig|Duchy of Schleswig]] in 1386, binding the two lands together.
county-of-holstein.e: The Rendsburg line died out in 1459, and the estates of [[e:schleswig|Schleswig]] and Holstein chose [[e:christian-i-of-denmark|King Christian I of Denmark]] as ruler in 1460 under the [[e:treaty-of-ribe|Treaty of Ribe]]. In 1474 [[e:frederick-iii-holy-roman-emperor|Emperor Frederick III]] raised Holstein to a duchy. The [[s:provisional-government-of-schleswig-holstein|Schleswig-Holstein]] Question later troubled [[e:europe|Europe]] until 1864.

county-of-chiny.t: A small Ardennes county on the Semois, on whose lands the Cistercian abbey of Orval was founded, before it was absorbed by Luxembourg.
county-of-chiny.o: The county emerged in the mid-10th century in the southern [[e:ardennes|Ardennes]], in the frontier region between the Lotharingian duchies and [[e:france|France]]. Its first known count, [[e:otto-of-warcq|Otto of Warcq]], built a castle at Chiny on the [[e:semois|Semois]], and his descendants extended their lands towards [[e:carignan-ardennes|Ivoix]] and [[e:montmedy|Montmédy]].
county-of-chiny.r: Chiny was a wooded, thinly settled county of castles, iron working and abbeys. The counts sponsored the abbey of [[e:orval-abbey|Orval]], founded in 1070 and later Cistercian, which became the county's main religious centre. They were [[e:vassal|vassals]] of the Empire, connected by marriage to Bar, [[s:county-of-namur|Namur]] and [[e:borgloon|Loon]].
county-of-chiny.e: In 1226 Countess Jeanne married Arnold of [[e:borgloon|Loon]], joining Chiny to the [[s:county-of-loon|County of Loon]]. After the Loon line ended, the county was sold in 1364 to Wenceslaus, duke of [[s:county-of-luxembourg|Luxembourg]], and merged into the County of Luxembourg; it lies today in [[s:kingdom-of-belgium|Belgium]].

chakan.t: A Maya province of north-western Yucatán around T'ho, on whose ruins the Spanish founded the city of Mérida in 1542.
chakan.o: Chakan was one of the provinces formed after the collapse of the [[s:league-of-mayapan|League of Mayapan]] around 1441. It covered the area around [[e:tho|T'ho]] (Ichcaansihó), an old centre with large pyramids, in the north-west of the peninsula.
chakan.r: Unlike the more centralised provinces, Chakan appears to have had no single overlord; its towns were governed by batabs of several lineages, including the Canché, who cooperated loosely. Its people farmed [[e:maize|maize]] and kept bees, and the coastal area produced salt. It is known chiefly from Spanish colonial records.
chakan.e: In 1542 [[e:francisco-de-montejo-the-younger|Francisco de Montejo the Younger]] founded [[e:merida-yucatan|Mérida]] on the site of [[e:tho|T'ho]], using its stones for the new buildings, and Chakan became the core of the [[s:province-of-yucatan|Province of Yucatán]].

county-of-hainaut.t: A cloth and coal county of the southern Low Countries, ruled from Mons for nine centuries and long linked by marriage to Flanders and Holland.
county-of-hainaut.o: Hainaut grew out of a Carolingian district on the [[e:scheldt|Scheldt]] and [[e:sambre|Sambre]]. Around 898 [[e:reginar-duke-of-lorraine|Reginar Longneck]], a leading Lotharingian noble, held comital power there, and his descendants, the [[e:reginarids|Reginarids]], struggled with the German kings for control. By the 11th century the county was centred on [[e:mons|Mons]] and [[e:valenciennes|Valenciennes]].
county-of-hainaut.r: Hainaut lay within the [[s:holy-roman-empire|Holy Roman Empire]] but faced [[e:france|France]], and its counts played both sides. The marriage of [[e:richilde-countess-of-hainaut|Richilde]] to [[e:baldwin-vi-count-of-flanders|Baldwin VI]] of [[s:county-of-flanders|Flanders]] in 1051 began a long Flemish link; [[e:baldwin-i-latin-emperor|Baldwin IX of Flanders]], count of Hainaut, became the first [[e:latin|Latin]] emperor of [[e:constantinople|Constantinople]] in 1204. Towns grew rich on cloth, and the countryside later on [[e:coal|coal]].
county-of-hainaut.e: Hainaut was united with Holland under the [[e:house-of-avesnes|Avesnes]] counts from 1299, and [[e:jacqueline-countess-of-hainaut|Jacqueline of Bavaria]] lost both to [[e:philip-the-good|Philip the Good]] of the [[s:burgundian-state|Burgundian State]] in 1433. The [[e:treaties-of-nijmegen|Treaty of Nijmegen]] of 1678 gave its south to [[e:france|France]]; the rest stayed in the [[s:spanish-netherlands|Spanish Netherlands]] and [[s:austrian-netherlands|Austrian Netherlands]] until French annexation in 1795.

colony-of-curacao.t: Dutch island colony that served as the Dutch West India Company's main Caribbean trading hub and slave depot, and later as capital of all Dutch Antillean territories.
colony-of-curacao.o: The [[e:dutch-west-india-company|Dutch West India Company]] captured [[s:curacao|Curaçao]] from [[e:spain|Spain]] in 1634 under [[e:johannes-van-walbeeck|Johannes van Walbeeck]], seeking a naval base, salt and a foothold near the Spanish Main. [[s:aruba|Aruba]] and [[e:bonaire|Bonaire]] were taken soon after. Under [[e:peter-stuyvesant|Peter Stuyvesant]], governor from 1642 before he moved to [[s:new-netherland|New Netherland]], the island became a company stronghold around [[e:willemstad|Willemstad]].
colony-of-curacao.r: The dry soil was poor for plantations, so [[s:curacao|Curaçao]] lived by trade, both legal and smuggled, with [[e:spanish-america|Spanish America]]. It was a main transit market for enslaved Africans in the 17th and 18th centuries. [[e:willemstad|Willemstad's]] merchant community included one of the oldest [[e:sephardic-jews|Sephardic Jewish]] congregations in the [[e:americas|Americas]], [[e:mikve-israel-emanuel-synagogue|Mikvé Israel]]. [[e:papiamento|Papiamentu]] emerged as the common language. A major slave revolt led by Tula broke out in 1795.
colony-of-curacao.e: [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]] occupied the island during the [[e:napoleonic-wars|Napoleonic Wars]], returning it in 1816. From 1845 [[e:willemstad|Willemstad]] governed all six [[e:dutch|Dutch]] islands as Curaçao and Dependencies. The Shell oil refinery, opened in 1918, transformed the economy. In 1954 the colony became the autonomous [[s:netherlands-antilles|Netherlands Antilles]] within the [[s:kingdom-of-the-netherlands|Kingdom of the Netherlands]].
colony-of-curacao.re: Catholicism, Dutch Reformed Church and Judaism

canari-confederation.t: An alliance of chiefdoms in the southern highlands of Ecuador that fiercely resisted the Incas and later sided with the Spanish against them.
canari-confederation.o: The Cañari peoples occupied the southern highlands of [[s:republic-of-ecuador|Ecuador]], around the modern provinces of [[e:azuay-province|Azuay]] and [[e:canar-province|Cañar]], from the first millennium CE. Their chiefdoms formed a loose confederation, with Guapondelig, near modern [[e:cuenca-ecuador|Cuenca]], as a leading centre and [[e:ingapirca|Hatun Cañar]], now Ingapirca, as another.
canari-confederation.r: The Cañari were led by local chiefs who joined forces in war. They farmed [[e:maize|maize]], [[e:potato|potatoes]] and beans and were skilled metalworkers in gold and [[e:copper|copper]]. Their origin myth traced the people to a macaw and a flood, and they revered the moon. Burial sites such as Sigsig have yielded rich gold objects.
canari-confederation.e: Around 1463 the [[e:inca-empire|Inca]] ruler [[e:tupac-inca-yupanqui|Túpac Inca Yupanqui]] conquered the Cañari after hard resistance, and the Incas built [[e:tomebamba|Tomebamba]] on the site of Guapondelig. Many Cañari were resettled as mitmaq. In the Inca civil war they backed [[e:huascar|Huáscar]] and suffered under [[e:atahualpa|Atahualpa]], so they allied with the Spanish in the 1530s.

county-of-hohenzollern.t: Swabian county of the Zollern counts, the Catholic home branch of the dynasty that later ruled Brandenburg, Prussia and Germany.
county-of-hohenzollern.o: The counts of Zollern are first recorded in 1061, with a castle on the Zollern hill in the [[e:swabian-jura|Swabian Jura]]. After the death around 1204 of Count Frederick, who had become [[e:burgraviate-of-nuremberg|Burgrave of Nuremberg]], his sons divided the family lands: Conrad took the burgraviate and founded the Franconian line that later ruled [[e:brandenburg|Brandenburg]], while his brother Frederick kept the Swabian lands as counts of Zollern.
county-of-hohenzollern.r: The Swabian counts held a small territory around [[e:hechingen|Hechingen]], often weakened by divisions and feuds; Zollern castle was destroyed by the Swabian imperial cities in 1423 and rebuilt. Eitel Friedrich II rose as an adviser to [[e:maximilian-i-holy-roman-emperor|Emperor Maximilian I]] and secured new lands. The family remained Catholic and served the [[e:habsburg-dynasty|Habsburgs]], gaining [[e:sigmaringen|Sigmaringen]] and Veringen as Austrian fiefs.
county-of-hohenzollern.e: After Count Charles I died in 1576, the county was divided between his sons into [[s:principality-of-hohenzollern-hechingen|Hohenzollern-Hechingen]], [[s:principality-of-hohenzollern-sigmaringen|Hohenzollern-Sigmaringen]] and Hohenzollern-[[e:haigerloch|Haigerloch]]. Both main lines were sold to [[e:kingdom-of-prussia|Prussia]] in 1850, and [[e:hohenzollern-castle|Hohenzollern Castle]] was rebuilt in its present form.

captaincy-general-of-guatemala.t: The Spanish Kingdom of Guatemala, which governed Central America from Chiapas to Costa Rica for nearly three centuries.
captaincy-general-of-guatemala.o: [[e:pedro-de-alvarado|Pedro de Alvarado]] conquered the highland Maya kingdoms from 1524 and founded [[e:antigua-guatemala|Santiago de los Caballeros]], first at [[s:kaqchikel-kingdom|Iximche]]. The capital moved to the [[e:ciudad-vieja|Almolonga]] valley and, after a mudflow in 1541, to present-day [[s:colony-of-antigua|Antigua]]. An audiencia was established in 1543 and seated in [[s:spanish-jamaica|Santiago]] from 1549.
captaincy-general-of-guatemala.r: The Captaincy General, nominally under [[s:new-spain|New Spain]], governed [[e:chiapas|Chiapas]], [[s:republic-of-guatemala|Guatemala]], [[s:republic-of-el-salvador|El Salvador]], [[s:republic-of-honduras|Honduras]], [[s:republic-of-nicaragua|Nicaragua]] and [[s:republic-of-costa-rica|Costa Rica]]. Its economy rested on indigenous tribute and labour, [[e:cacao|cacao]] and later [[e:indigo|indigo]]. [[e:bartolome-de-las-casas|Bartolomé de las Casas]] led peaceful missions in [[e:verapaz|Verapaz]]. [[s:spanish-jamaica|Santiago]] was a centre of [[e:baroque|Baroque]] architecture and learning until earthquakes in 1773 led to the founding of [[e:guatemala-city|Guatemala City]].
captaincy-general-of-guatemala.e: [[e:central-america|Central America]] declared independence on 15 September 1821, joined the [[s:first-mexican-empire|First Mexican Empire]] briefly, and in 1823 formed the [[s:federal-republic-of-central-america|Federal Republic of Central America]], except [[e:chiapas|Chiapas]], which stayed with [[s:mexico|Mexico]].

captaincy-of-mato-grosso.t: Brazil's far-western frontier captaincy, born of a gold rush at Cuiabá and built to hold the Guaporé river border against Spain.
captaincy-of-mato-grosso.o: Paulista bandeirantes led by [[e:pascoal-moreira-cabral|Pascoal Moreira Cabral]] found gold near [[e:cuiaba|Cuiabá]] in 1718, and miners reached it by long canoe convoys called monções from [[e:sao-paulo|São Paulo]]. To secure the western frontier with Spanish lands, the crown separated Mato Grosso from the [[s:captaincy-of-sao-paulo|Captaincy of São Paulo]] in 1748. Its first governor, [[e:antonio-rolim-de-moura|Antônio Rolim de Moura]], founded the capital [[e:vila-bela-da-santissima-trindade|Vila Bela da Santíssima Trindade]] on the [[e:guapore-river|Guaporé]] river in 1752.
captaincy-of-mato-grosso.r: Mato Grosso was a remote military frontier facing the [[e:jesuits|Jesuit]] missions of [[e:jesuit-missions-of-moxos|Moxos]] and [[e:jesuit-missions-of-chiquitos|Chiquitos]] in Spanish [[e:upper-peru|Charcas]]. Its governors began the massive [[e:fort-principe-da-beira|Real Forte Príncipe da Beira]] on the [[e:guapore-river|Guaporé]] in 1776. Gold mining relied on enslaved Africans, and [[e:vila-bela-da-santissima-trindade|Vila Bela]] had a largely black population. The [[e:treaty-of-madrid-1750|Treaty of Madrid]] of 1750 recognised Portuguese possession of much of the region.
captaincy-of-mato-grosso.e: As gold declined, the population fell. Mato Grosso became a province in 1821, and in 1835 its capital moved to [[e:cuiaba|Cuiabá]]. Its territory was later divided into the states of Mato Grosso, Mato Grosso do Sul and [[e:rondonia|Rondônia]].

city-of-st-gallen.t: A linen-weaving city that freed itself from its famous abbey and became an imperial city and associate of the Swiss Confederacy.
city-of-st-gallen.o: [[e:st-gallen|St. Gallen]] grew around the abbey founded in 719 on the site of [[e:saint-gall|Saint Gall's]] 7th-century hermitage. The townspeople gradually freed themselves from the abbot's lordship, and in 1415 [[e:sigismund-holy-roman-emperor|King Sigismund]] granted the city imperial privileges, making it a free imperial city. In 1454 it allied with six Swiss cantons as an associate ([[e:associates-of-the-swiss-confederacy|zugewandter Ort]]).
city-of-st-gallen.r: [[e:guild|Guild]]-dominated councils ran the city, whose wealth came from linen exported across [[e:europe|Europe]] under strict quality controls. Under its mayor and reformer [[e:joachim-vadian|Joachim Vadian]], [[e:st-gallen|St. Gallen]] adopted the Reformed faith in the 1520s, while the [[s:imperial-abbey-of-saint-gall|Imperial Abbey of Saint Gall]], whose precinct lay within the town, remained Catholic. From 1566 a wall separated city and abbey.
city-of-st-gallen.e: The city lost its independence in 1798 under the [[s:helvetic-republic|Helvetic Republic]]. In 1803 it became the capital of the new canton of [[e:st-gallen|St. Gallen]], which also absorbed the abbey's lands. The abbey precinct is now a [[e:unesco-world-heritage-site|World Heritage Site]].

circassia.t: The land of the Adyghe peoples in the north-western Caucasus, a society of princes and free communities whose long war with Russia ended in mass expulsion in 1864.
circassia.o: The [[e:circassians|Adyghe]], known to [[e:greeks|Greeks]] and Genoese as [[e:zygii|Zygoi]] and Zichians, lived between the [[e:black-sea|Black Sea]] coast and the Kuban river since antiquity. By the 15th century, after the Mongol era, they formed a recognisable country of related principalities and tribal societies, with Genoese trading posts on the coast.
circassia.r: Circassia had no single ruler. Princely tribes such as [[s:principality-of-kabarda|Kabarda]], [[s:principality-of-temirgoy|Temirgoy]] and [[s:principality-of-bzhedugh|Bzhedugh]] had hereditary princes and nobles over free peasants and serfs, while [[s:shapsugs|Shapsugs]], [[s:natukhaj|Natukhaj]] and [[s:abadzekhs|Abadzekhs]] governed themselves through assemblies. A strict code of conduct, [[e:adyghe-khabze|Adyghe Khabze]], shaped society. [[e:circassians|Circassians]] served as [[e:mamluk|Mamluks]] in [[e:egypt|Egypt]], paid tribute to the [[s:crimean-khanate|Crimean Khanate]], and gradually adopted [[e:sunni-islam|Sunni Islam]].
circassia.e: [[e:russia|Russia's]] advance led to the [[e:russo-circassian-war|Russo-Circassian War]], which ended in 1864 when the [[s:russian-empire|Russian Empire]] completed its conquest. Most [[e:circassians|Circassians]] were killed or expelled to the [[s:ottoman-empire|Ottoman Empire]], an event many call the Circassian [[e:genocide|genocide]]; their diaspora remains in [[e:turkey|Turkey]], [[s:hashemite-kingdom-of-jordan|Jordan]] and [[s:syrian-arab-republic|Syria]].
circassia.re: Sunni Islam, earlier Christianity and native beliefs

county-of-sayn.t: A Westerwald county near the Rhine whose counts, at their height in the 13th century, rivalled the archbishops of Cologne.
county-of-sayn.o: The counts of Sayn appear in 1139 with a castle above [[e:bendorf|Bendorf]], near [[e:koblenz|Koblenz]]. Count [[e:henry-iii-count-of-sayn|Henry III of Sayn]], who ruled until 1247, built up a large territory in the [[e:westerwald|Westerwald]] and [[e:siegerland|Siegerland]], and was accused of heresy by [[e:konrad-of-marburg|Konrad of Marburg]] in 1233 but cleared at an [[e:imperial-diet|imperial diet]] in [[e:mainz|Mainz]].
county-of-sayn.r: After Henry III's death the lands passed through his sister to the [[s:county-of-sponheim|Sponheim]] family, forming Sayn and Sayn-[[e:ludwig-wittgenstein|Wittgenstein]] lines. The counts ruled hilly lands with iron mines and abbeys such as [[e:sayn-abbey|Sayn Abbey]] and [[e:marienstatt-abbey|Marienstatt]]. They adopted the [[e:protestant-reformation|Reformation]] in the 16th century.
county-of-sayn.e: With the death of Count Henry IV in 1606 the main line ended, and the county was divided after long disputes between heirs and the [[s:electorate-of-trier|Archbishopric of Trier]]. Sayn-Hachenburg and Sayn-Altenkirchen later passed to [[s:county-of-nassau|Nassau]] and [[e:kingdom-of-prussia|Prussia]]. The Sayn-[[e:ludwig-wittgenstein|Wittgenstein]] princes survive.

commune-of-viterbo.t: A papal city-commune north of Rome that hosted popes in the 13th century and gave the Church the longest papal election in its history.
commune-of-viterbo.o: Viterbo grew on the [[e:via-cassia|Via Cassia]] in northern [[e:lazio|Lazio]], and consuls governing the town are recorded by 1095. It expanded by subduing neighbouring towns and fought a long rivalry with the [[s:commune-of-rome|Commune of Rome]], while recognising the distant overlordship of the [[s:papal-states|Papal States]].
commune-of-viterbo.r: The commune was ruled by consuls, then a podestà, while rival clans such as the Gatti and the [[e:prefect|prefects]] of Vico fought for control. From the mid-13th century popes often lived there, and the [[e:palazzo-dei-papi-viterbo|Palazzo dei Papi]] was built for them. The election of 1268–1271 dragged on for almost three years until the townspeople locked the cardinals in and removed the roof, leading to the conclave rules of Gregory X.
commune-of-viterbo.e: In the 14th century [[e:giovanni-di-vico|Giovanni di Vico]] made himself lord of the city until [[e:gil-alvarez-carrillo-de-albornoz|Cardinal Albornoz]] restored papal authority in 1354. After further strife the town came under direct papal government at the end of the century and remained part of the [[s:papal-states|Papal States]] until 1870.

cirebon-sultanate.t: A Muslim kingdom on the north coast of Java, founded with Sunan Gunung Jati, one of the Nine Saints who spread Islam on the island.
cirebon-sultanate.o: [[e:cirebon|Cirebon]] grew as a port on the border between Javanese and Sundanese lands. Tradition says Prince [[e:walangsungsang|Walangsungsang]], son of the [[e:sunda-strait|Sunda]] king, founded a settlement there around 1430 and embraced [[e:islam|Islam]]. His nephew [[e:sunan-gunung-jati|Syarif Hidayatullah]], known as Sunan Gunung Jati, ruled from the late 15th century and broke away from the [[s:sunda-kingdom|Sunda Kingdom]].
cirebon-sultanate.r: [[e:sunan-gunung-jati|Sunan Gunung Jati]], one of the [[e:wali-songo|Wali Songo]], allied with [[s:demak-sultanate|Demak]] and helped take [[e:banten|Banten]] and [[e:sunda-kelapa|Sunda Kalapa]] from [[e:sunda-strait|Sunda]]. [[e:cirebon|Cirebon's]] courts blended Javanese, Sundanese, Chinese and Islamic culture, visible in the [[s:kasepuhan-sultanate|Kasepuhan]] palace and its batik with cloud motifs. The port traded [[e:rice|rice]], [[e:timber|timber]] and textiles.
cirebon-sultanate.e: In the 17th century [[e:cirebon|Cirebon]] fell under the influence of the [[s:mataram-sultanate|Mataram Sultanate]]. In 1677, with [[e:banten|Banten's]] help, the realm was split between princes into the courts of [[s:kasepuhan-sultanate|Kasepuhan]] and [[s:kanoman-sultanate|Kanoman]], which soon accepted [[e:dutch|Dutch]] protection. The palaces and their sultans survive as cultural institutions today.

county-of-besalu.t: A small Catalan county of the Garrotxa whose fortified bridge and Jewish quarter still mark the medieval town of Besalú.
county-of-besalu.o: [[e:besalu|Besalú]] emerged as a county in the later 9th century, carved out of the lands of [[e:girona|Girona]] and linked to the family of [[e:wilfred-the-hairy|Wilfred the Hairy]]. For much of the 10th century it was held together with [[e:cerdanya|Cerdanya]] by Wilfred's descendants, before acquiring its own line of counts.
county-of-besalu.r: Its best-known count, [[e:bernat-i-count-of-besalu|Bernat I Tallaferro]], from 988 to 1020, was a brother of [[e:oliba|Abbot Oliba]] and briefly obtained a bishopric for [[e:besalu|Besalú]] from the pope in 1017. The town grew around its castle, monasteries such as [[e:sant-pere-de-besalu|Sant Pere de Besalú]], a fortified bridge over the [[e:fluvia|Fluvià]] and a Jewish community whose ritual bath survives. The economy was rural, with markets on the routes to [[e:roussillon|Roussillon]].
county-of-besalu.e: Count [[e:bernat-iii-of-besalu|Bernat III]] married a daughter of [[e:ramon-berenguer-iii-of-barcelona|Ramon Berenguer III of Barcelona]] and died without heirs in 1111, so the county passed to [[e:barcelona|Barcelona]]. It became part of [[s:principality-of-catalonia|Catalonia]] and the [[s:crown-of-aragon|Crown of Aragon]].

chera-perumals-of-makotai.t: The kingdom of the Chera Perumals of Kerala, ruling from Kodungallur, whose copper plates record grants to Christian and Jewish merchants.
chera-perumals-of-makotai.o: In the early 9th century a [[e:chera-dynasty|Chera]] kingdom re-emerged on the [[e:kerala|Kerala]] coast, claiming the legacy of the [[s:early-cheras|Early Cheras]]. Its capital was [[e:mahodayapuram|Mahodayapuram]], also called Makotai, near modern [[e:kodungallur|Kodungallur]]. Tradition identifies its early kings with the [[e:vaishnavism|Vaishnava]] poet-saint [[e:kulashekhara-alvar|Kulashekhara Alvar]] and the Shaiva saint [[e:cheraman-perumal-nayanar|Cheraman Perumal Nayanar]].
chera-perumals-of-makotai.r: The Perumals ruled through local chiefs, the naduvazhis, and temple councils of [[e:brahmins|Brahmins]]. [[e:kodungallur|Kodungallur]] and [[e:kollam|Kollam]] were major ports for the spice trade with [[e:arabia|Arabia]] and [[e:china|China]]. The Tharisapalli plates of 849, issued under [[e:sthanu-ravi|Sthanu Ravi]], granted privileges to a [[e:saint-thomas-christians|Syrian Christian]] church in Kollam, and the Jewish [[e:copper|copper]] plates of [[e:bhaskara-ravi-varman|Bhaskara Ravi]] gave rights to a Jewish merchant. [[e:malayalam-language|Malayalam]] began to emerge as a distinct language.
chera-perumals-of-makotai.e: Long wars with the [[s:chola-empire|Chola Empire]] in the 11th century weakened the kingdom. After the last ruler, [[e:rama-kulashekhara|Rama Kulashekhara]], around 1124, [[e:kerala|Kerala]] divided into principalities such as [[s:kingdom-of-venad|Venad]] and [[e:calicut|Kozhikode]], later ruled by the [[e:zamorin|Zamorin]].

company-rule-in-india.t: The century in which a trading corporation, the East India Company, ruled most of the Indian subcontinent until the rebellion of 1857.
company-rule-in-india.o: The [[e:east-india-company|English East India Company]] traded in [[e:india|India]] from 1600. [[e:robert-clive|Robert Clive's]] victory at [[e:battle-of-plassey|Plassey]] in 1757 over the [[s:nawabate-of-bengal|Nawabate of Bengal]] made the Company the power behind the nawabs, and the [[e:battle-of-buxar|Battle of Buxar]] in 1764 led to the grant of the diwani of [[e:bengal|Bengal]], [[e:bihar|Bihar]] and [[e:odisha|Odisha]] by the Mughal emperor in 1765.
company-rule-in-india.r: The Company governed through the [[s:bengal-presidency|Bengal Presidency]], the [[s:madras-presidency|Madras Presidency]] and the [[s:bombay-presidency|Bombay Presidency]] under a governor-general, overseen by Parliament from the [[e:regulating-act-of-1773|Regulating Act of 1773]]. It defeated the [[s:kingdom-of-mysore-1399-1799|Kingdom of Mysore]], the [[e:maratha-empire|Marathas]] and the [[s:sikh-empire|Sikh Empire]], bound [[e:princely-state|princely states]] by subsidiary alliances, imposed the Permanent Settlement of 1793, abolished sati in 1829 and introduced English education. Revenue extraction and famine marked rural life.
company-rule-in-india.e: Discontent over annexations and army grievances erupted in the rebellion of 1857. The [[e:government-of-india|Government of India]] Act of 1858 transferred power from the Company to the Crown, beginning the [[s:british-raj|British Raj]], and the Company was dissolved in 1874.

chalukyas-of-badami.t: The Deccan dynasty that defeated Harsha and created the temple architecture of Badami, Aihole and Pattadakal.
chalukyas-of-badami.o: [[e:pulakeshin-i|Pulakeshin I]] founded the dynasty around 543 by fortifying [[e:badami|Vatapi]], modern Badami in northern [[e:karnataka|Karnataka]], and performing a horse sacrifice. His sons [[e:kirtivarman-i|Kirtivarman I]] and [[e:mangalesha|Mangalesha]] conquered the [[s:kadamba-dynasty|Kadamba dynasty]], the [[s:kalachuris-of-mahishmati|Kalachuris of Mahishmati]] and the [[e:konkan-coast|Konkan coast]], and Mangalesha carved the cave temples of Badami.
chalukyas-of-badami.r: [[e:pulakeshin-ii|Pulakeshin II]] defeated [[e:harsha|Harsha]] of the [[s:pushyabhuti-dynasty|Pushyabhuti dynasty]] on the [[e:narmada-river|Narmada]], and the [[e:aihole|Aihole]] inscription of 634 by the poet Ravikirti celebrates his conquests. He gave [[e:vengi|Vengi]] to his brother, founder of the [[s:eastern-chalukyas|Eastern Chalukyas]]. The [[e:chalukya-dynasty|Chalukyas]] ruled through feudatories and patronised Vedic ritual, [[e:jainism|Jainism]] and temple building; the temples at Aihole and [[e:pattadakal|Pattadakal]], such as the [[e:virupaksha-temple-pattadakal|Virupaksha]] built by Queen [[e:lokamahadevi|Lokamahadevi]], mix northern and southern styles.
chalukyas-of-badami.e: In 642 [[e:narasimhavarman-i|Narasimhavarman I]] of the [[s:pallava-dynasty|Pallava dynasty]] sacked [[e:badami|Vatapi]] and [[e:pulakeshin-ii|Pulakeshin II]] died. [[e:vikramaditya-i|Vikramaditya I]] restored the kingdom, and [[e:vikramaditya-ii|Vikramaditya II]] later occupied [[e:kanchipuram|Kanchipuram]]. In 753 [[e:dantidurga|Dantidurga]], a feudatory, overthrew [[e:kirtivarman-ii|Kirtivarman II]] and founded the [[s:rashtrakuta-dynasty|Rashtrakuta dynasty]].
